Do not harm others and/or their property.
They who creates a thing controls a thing.

-

Equity will never come to the aid of a volunteer.
Equity sees that as done what ought to be done
Equity will not suffer a wrong to be without a remedy
Equity delights in equality
One who seeks equity must do equity
Equity aids the vigilant, not those who slumber on their rights
Equity imputes an intent to fulfill an obligation
Equity acts in personam or persons
Equity abhors a forfeiture
Equity does not require an idle gesture
They who comes into equity must come with clean hands
Equity delights to do justice and not by halves
Equity will take jurisdiction to avoid a multiplicity of suits
Equity follows the law
Equity will not aid a volunteer
Where equities are equal, the law will prevail
Between equal equities the first in order of time shall prevail
Equity will not complete an imperfect gift
Equity will not allow a trust to fail for want of a trustee
Equity regards the beneficiary as the true owner.

It concerns the commonwealth and the hardiness of our Republic that crimes do not remain un-punished, unless no true remedy, and perhaps only detriment, may be reached by such punishment.

It concerns the commonwealth and the hardiness of our Republic that things adjudged be not rescinded, and Stare Decisis remain intact as far as no critical error or fatal flaw in a prior judgment is made, such that in such case it should then require appeal and/or repairation.

It concerns the commonwealth and the hardiness of our Republic that prisons be secure.

It concerns the commonwealth and the hardiness of our Republic that there be an end of law suits.

SECTION. 1.

The judicial power of Pacifica shall be vested in the Courts of Pacifica.

The Courts of Pacifica shall consist of the Civil Court, Criminal Court and the Supreme Court.

The Courts of Pacifica shall first and foremost protect the Rights of Citizens and other Residents of Pacifica by upholding the Constitution and any laws passed in accordance therewith. It shall be the duty of the Judiciary to strike down as void and unlawful any laws in conflict with the Constitution, and to elaborate upon the decision for the benefit of the People.

In all cases of law, justice, and equity, they shall be settled according to the principles and rules of Roman Civil Law, except as may be directed otherwise by this Constitution, or if neither, prescribe a course or remedy, as according to the customs of Common Law, or Contract law (under Pacifican Principles), or in none such case, as according the legal customs of United States law as under to the Articles of Confederation except as may be provided otherwise by the 1787CE Constitution of the United States, and additionally through the Bill of Rights of 1789CE, as it was originally proposed. This rule of law shall be followed in every case where it is not repugnant to the Constitutions of Pacifica’s, and the several States beneath it.

The Judges, both of the supreme and inferior Courts, shall hold their Offices during good Behavior for a non-renewable term of twelve years.

A retention referendum shall be cast every two years, whereby a judge is subject to a referendum held at the same time as a general election; The judge shall be removed from office if a majority of votes are cast against retention.

We the People of Pacifica, reserve to our State Legislatures and Courts, as well as to ourselves as Electors by the ballot, and as members of the Jury, the Power to nullify and strike down unconstitutional and unjust Federal, Territorial, State, or Local laws, acts, and orders, as well as the power to grant amnesty and exoneration to Individuals trapped under their crushing weight, and provide pardon, expungement, exoneration, and restitution, through the public instrument under the People's control and will.

SECTION. 2.

The Judges of the Courts of Pacifica shall regulate their own affairs within the Secretariat of the Judiciary of Pacifica:
(1) The Secretariat of the Judiciary shall be headed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
(2) The Secretariat of the Judiciary shall supervise, but not command, all Agents of the judicial branch of the Public Administration.
(3) No Agent of Law Enforcement shall enter the premises of any Court of Pacifica unless with the express and informed consent of the Secretariat of the Judiciary or pursuant to the Supreme Warrant.

The Judges of the Courts of Pacifica shall be independent and shall not be removable by any other branch of the Public Administration:
(1) The re-muneration of the Judges shall not be lowered without the express and informed consent of either the Secretariat of the Judiciary of Pacifica, or the Citizens of the several States.
(2) No Judge of any Court of Pacifica shall be arrested for any period whatsoever unless pursuant to the Supreme Warrant or under exigent circumstances where there is a direct threat to others whom are non-aggressors or where vital evidence may be destroyed.
(3) Where a Judge is placed under arrest without the Supreme Warrant, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall be immediately notified about the detainment and shall have the power to order immediate release of the detained Judge.
(4) Should the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court be the Judge arrested, the most senior Justice of the Supreme Court shall have the power to order the immediate release of him or her.
(5) The Supreme Warrant shall be issued by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or by at least three Justices of the Supreme Court acting together, upon request by the Office of the Public Prosecutor supported by clear and convincing evidence of an alleged offense.

The Judicial Appointment Commission shall have the power to inquire into alleged misconduct of any Judge of the Civil Court or the Criminal Court:
(1) The Judicial Appointment Commission shall have the power to subpoena Judges of the Civil Court and the Criminal Court and Agents of the Public Administration to hear testimonies given under oath.
(2) The Judicial Appointment Commission may remove any Judge of the Civil Court or the Criminal Court from the office upon a proven case of gross misconduct or intentional procurement of the miscarriage of justice.
(3) Should there be suspicion that any Judge of the Civil Court or the Criminal Court issues Warrants or Orders too leniently, the Judicial Appointment Commission shall have the power to inquire into the justifiability of such Warrants or Orders, and may remove such a Judge from his or her office upon proving that is the case.
(4) Should the Judicial Appointment Commission find evidence of any criminal conduct, it shall be passed to the Office of the Chief Public Prosecutor; testimonies given in breach of oath shall be prosecuted in a regular manner in the Criminal Court.
(5) The Judicial Appointment Commission shall have the power to declare any Judge of any Court of Pacifica to be unable to continue to hold his or her office due to very poor health or old age but not before the age of seventy-two.

The Supreme Court shall be composed of four Justices of the Supreme Court and the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court who shall preside over the Court:
(1) The Supreme Court shall at all times give hearing en banc and reach its decisions with a simple majority unless required otherwise in this Constitution.
(2) All verdicts of the Supreme Court shall be binding upon the parties to the proceedings and the Civil Court and the Criminal Court on the point of law in all future proceedings where applicable.
(3) Should the office of any of the Justices of the Supreme Court become vacant, the President shall appoint a current or former Judge of the Criminal Court or the Civil Court for the position for eighteen years.
(4) Should the office of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court become vacant, a special election referendum will be held to appoint the most senior Justice of the Supreme Court by a vote of the Citizenry for the position for eighteen years.
(5) The Chief Justice or any Justice of the Supreme Court shall nevertheless be removable from their position by the Citizens of Pacifica with a majority of two-thirds vote in a referendum called by 5.555555555555 percent of the overall number of Citizens registered to vote at the time of the last General Election or by the Judicial Appointment Commission as described in this Constitution.
(6) Should any Justice or the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court have any personal interest in a case before the Court, he or she shall recuse him or herself from the proceedings, in which case, his place shall be temporary taken by the most senior of Judges of the Civil Court and the Criminal Court who has not been involved in the case before it is heard by the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court shall have compulsory appellate and inherent jurisdiction as prescribed in this Constitution and powers to issue warrants, injunctions and other orders as prescribed by law:
(1) The Supreme Court shall hear appeals from the Civil Court and the Criminal Court on the point of law, material procedural irregularity or severity of sentence.
(2) The Supreme Court shall have inherent jurisdiction to issue declarations as to the law and Constitution of Pacifica upon request by the Attorney General of Pacifica.
(3) The Supreme Court shall have inherent jurisdiction to review the prima facie constitutionality of all Bills and legislation passed in accordance with Article III which shall take place within ninety days and no Bill shall become the law of Pacifica unless the Supreme Court, in no less than two-thirds majority, declares the Bill to be constitutional.
(4) Upon reviewing the prima facie constitutionality of a Bill, the Supreme Court shall hear submissions, which are of relevance for the outcome of the determination, from the Congress and any association composed of no fewer than thirty Citizens in the form of amicus curiae briefs.
(5) Should a Bill be declared un-constitutional by reason only of parts of the Bill which may reasonably be excised from the whole, the Supreme Court shall send the remainder of such Bill to the Congress which may pass a resolution authorizing the remainder of the Bill proceed for consideration of Citizens.
(6) The Supreme Court shall retain the power to strike down any provision of any Act passed in accordance with Article III  as un-constitutional at any criminal or civil proceedings notwithstanding the declaration of the prima facie constitutionality; such provision shall be dis-applied on the appeal in question and shall be deemed no longer in force at the time the verdict is given.
(7) The Supreme Court shall have inherent jurisdiction to review the constitutionality of all international treaties the Congress intends to sign and no international treaty shall be signed unless the Supreme Court, unanimously, declares the treaty to be constitutional.
(8) The Supreme Court shall have inherent jurisdiction to review the validity of any election or referendum upon the request of one-quarter of the overall number of Congressional Representatives or 3.333333333333 percent of the overall number of Citizens registered to vote at the time of the last General Election. This shall not be the power to decide a winner, only simply to audit and/or verify the results.
(9) The Supreme Court shall have inherent jurisdiction to rule on the President’s ability to perform his or her duties upon request by a simple majority of all Members of the Congress or the Vice-President.

The Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate all disputes concerning contracts which were made under, and civil wrongs which took place within, the jurisdiction of Pacifica.
(1) The jurisdiction of the Civil Court shall not be ousted by any contract unless fair arbitration proceedings are envisaged in case of dispute.
(2) The fairness of arbitration proceedings shall be judged in reference to proceedings taking place before the Civil Court and, if questioned, may be subject to a challenge in this Court.
(3) Contracts may require parties to attempt mediation before the jurisdiction of the Court becomes exercisable.
(4) The Civil Court
shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate all disputes between Citizens or other Residents of Pacifica and any body of the Public Administration.
(5) The Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate all disputes between two or more bodies of the Public Administration.
(6) The Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to hear cases concerned with the well-being of Minors and Persons lacking mental capacity.
(7) The Civil Court may adjudicate civil disputes concerning contracts made outside the jurisdiction of Pacifica provided such jurisdiction has been conferred upon it by law.
(8) All disputes concerning subject matter of small value as prescribed by law shall be adjudicated by one Judge whereas all other disputes shall be adjudicated by a panel of three Judges reaching a decision with a simple majority.
(9) The Civil Court shall have the power to issue Publication Orders and other Orders in accordance with this Constitution and warrants, injunctions and other orders as prescribed by law.

All administrative decisions of any branch of the Public Administration, and actions undertaken by its Agents, which are capable of directly affecting any Person, may be subject to challenge in the Civil Court by such a Person:
(1) All Executive Orders or Directives issued by the Congress may be subject to challenge in the Civil Court by a Person affected thereby or, in the absence of such a Person, by any association composed of no fewer than thirty-two Citizens.
(2) Without prejudice to the appeal procedures, such challenge shall be admissible once only unless the original challenge was not genuine but brought in order to shield the defendant from liability or where a new challenge raises a different point of law.
(3) The right described in this provision shall be exercisable once all administrative appeals have been exhausted.

Should an alleged criminal offense leave no Victim or Proxy capable of instituting a Private Prosecution, the Office of the Public Prosecutor shall have the power to institute a Public Prosecution on behalf of the Citizens of Pacifica:
(1) Should a criminal offense be allegedly committed by a Member or Agent of the Public Administration in the course of his or her official duties, and no Public Prosecution has been brought within a reasonable period of time, a Private Prosecution may be brought by any association composed of no fewer than thirty Citizens.
(2) Where a Private Prosecution is instituted in place of a Public Prosecution, the Office of the Public Prosecutor shall fully cooperate with the association in charge of the proceedings.

All civil and criminal offenses, for which Pacifica shall have jurisdiction, shall be tried in the civil and criminal Courts of Pacifica, held before a Judge with a panel of Jury to give a verdict of “Guilty” or “Not guilty”:
(1) The Jury shall be composed of twelve impartial Citizens drawn randomly from the Electoral Register.
(2) The Jury shall determine the facts and render the verdict according to the law under the direction of the Judge.
(3) The Jury shall deliberate in camera and shall not be required to disclose reasons behind the verdict or be reprimanded for it.
(4) The Jury shall, under all circumstances, retain the unequivocal right to acquit and shall be informed of this right; such acquittal shall be final.
(5) The Jury shall reach its decisions unanimously with the whole of twelve votes.
(6) Should the Jury not be able to render a verdict with all twelve votes within reasonable time, the Judge shall order retrial with a newly appointed Jury; such retrial shall be considered to be a continuation of the original proceedings.
(7) The Jury shall render the verdict free from any form of coercion, compulsion, or extortion; the Judge may order sequestration of the Jurors should it be required for the independence of the Jury.
(8) All defendants who have been convicted by the Jury shall be sentenced by the Judge as prescribed by law.
(9) The Criminal Court may exercise jurisdiction over international crimes provided it has been conferred upon it by law and only if the accused is within the jurisdiction of Pacifica.
(10) The Criminal Court shall have the power to issue Warrants as prescribed by this Constitution and injunctions and other orders as prescribed by law.

Any civil and criminal proceedings shall be preceded by a Preliminary Hearing held by one Judge of the relevant Court:
(1) A defendant at a Preliminary Hearing shall enter his or her positions in relation to the claim or prosecution brought against him or her.
(2) The Judge at a Preliminary Hearing shall have the power to issue preliminary Warrants and Orders within the powers of the relevant Court which shall be re-viewable at a full trial.
(3) The Judge at a Preliminary Hearing shall review the prima facie validity of the claim or prosecution and shall dismiss the case before it proceeds to a full trial where:
(a) no modicum of credible evidence has been proven to the satisfaction of the Courts;
(b) he or she is satisfied that the claim or prosecution would be contrary to the Constitution;
(c) defendant’s procedural rights as laid down in the Constitution or any laws passed in accordance therewith have been violated and such a violation has prejudiced his or her case.
(4) Should a claim or a prosecution be dismissed as frivolous at a Preliminary Hearing, the plaintiff or the prosecutor shall ordinarily be ordered to cover all reasonable expenses of the defendant connected to his or her legal defense as well as all court fees unless there is compelling and rational reason otherwise.

No special commission, tribunal or court not recognized by this Constitution shall be established by the Public Administration.

All powers, and restrictions placed thereon, of the Civil Court and the Criminal Court shall equally apply to the Supreme Court upon appeals from such Courts.

All parties to any trial before any Court of Pacifica shall be given a fair hearing in accordance with the rules of natural justice before a verdict is rendered.

Access to any Court of Pacifica shall not be impeded by any excessive formal, financial or other requirements. No rule or procedure of the Courts may unduly burden the Acquisition of Justice.

SECTION. 3.

No court shall be secret, but justice shall be administered, openly and without purchase, completely and without delay, and every man shall have remedy by due course of law for injury done to him in his person, property, or reputation. No person, entity, or government within Pacifica shall require, enforce, or give legal effect to any pre-dispute agreement mandating arbitration of claims arising under Pacifican law, including employment, consumer, civil rights, labor, environmental, and contractual disputes, with all such clauses declared void ab initio as violations of the inherent right to access public courts; every resident and enterprise retains the unqualified right to seek redress in open, impartial courts with full procedural safeguards, jury trials where applicable, class and collective actions, discovery, appeals, and public proceedings, while private arbitration may only be agreed upon post-dispute voluntarily without coercion or economic duress and with equal bargaining power; Pacifican courts shall sever and disregard any conflicting arbitration provision, preserving other contract terms, with no law, treaty, or federal overlay preempting this sovereign protection of due process and equal justice, and violations constituting unlawful restraint of rights subject to injunction, damages, and attorney fees for prevailing parties.

The Federal Judicial power shall extend to all cases in law and equity arising under this Constitution, and the laws which shall be made by its authority; and to all treaties, rules, interpretations, guidances, bulletins, circulars, or other administrative statement or action of any type or form, made, or which shall be made, under their authority; to all cases of admiralty and maritime jurisdiction; to controversies between two or more States; The Judicial Power shall also extend to Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of Pacifica.

The Citizen’s Judicial power shall extend to all cases in law and equity arising under this Constitution, and the laws which shall be made by its authority, which rulings may impair the rights of an Individual; to all cases affecting Ambassadors, other public Ministers, or Consuls; to all cases of admiralty and maritime jurisdiction; to controversies to which Pacifica shall be a party; between a State and citizens of another State; between the citizens of different States; between the citizens of the same State claiming under grants of different States; and between a State or the citizens thereof and foreign States, citizens, or subjects;

The Judicial power of Pacifica shall not be construed to extend to any suit in law or equity, commenced or prosecuted against one of Pacifica by Citizens of another State, or by Citizens or Subjects of any Foreign State.

The District Courts of each State shall have original jurisdiction over all cases occurring within the limits of their respective districts, with such exceptions, and under such regulations, as the Congress may make.

In all Cases affecting Ambassadors, other public Ministers and Consuls, and those in which a State shall be Party, the supreme Court shall have original Jurisdiction. In all the other Cases before mentioned, the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact, with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make, but lower courts are allowed to have original jurisdiction for cases in which a state is a party.

Appeals may be made from the District Courts of the States to the Supreme Courts of the States, and from the Supreme Courts of the States to the Supreme Court of Pacifica, in all cases where the Supreme Courts of the States are not a unit, under such rules and regulations as shall be prescribed by Congress.

At each level of appeal a case shall first be heard by a randomly selected panel of three, appealable to a randomly selected panel of nine, and thence appealable to either a randomly selected or en banc panel of twenty-seven, depending on the number of judges assigned to that court.

No appeal to the Supreme Court of Pacifica shall be allowed, where the value in controversy shall not amount to at least one thousand dollars, or to which there is no criminal sanction; nor shall any fact triable by a jury according to the course of Common Law, be otherwise re-examinable, than according to the rules of Common Law.

Judges settle all disputes regarding the competence of the authorities. No one seeking a ruling thereon can, however, temporarily evade obeying a lawful order from the authorities by submitting the matter for a judicial decision.

Every proposed law must include a citation of the Constitutional clause that empowers government to engage in or order the action of said law.

The judicial decisions in every court of Pacifica and of every State shall be made according to the principles and rules of under Roman Civil Law, except as may be directed otherwise by this Constitution, or if neither prescribe a course or remedy, as according to the customs of Common Law, then Contract law (under Pacifican Principles), or in none such case, as according the legal customs of United States law as under to the Articles of Confederation except as may be provided otherwise by the 1787CE Constitution of the United States, and additionally through the Bill of Rights of 1789CE, as it was originally proposed, and to the terms and rules of due process and construction in effect in Pacifica that do not conflict with this Constitution or statutes enacted within its authority.

In any case or controversy arising under the Constitution, statutes, or treaties of Pacifica, of which a court of Pacifica or of any State has jurisdiction, the rules of decision shall be supplied by the relevant texts of the Constitution, statutes, or treaties of Pacifica, taken in context and understood according to the original public meaning of the language used at the time of the adoption, enactment, or ratification of the provision(s) involved.

The Courts may declare Statutes void for being inconsistent with the Constitution. The supreme Court may declare a federal Statute void only if three-fourths or more of the Justices concur.

Only Pacifican citizens or those arrested or detained under Pacifican jurisdiction [or under the direction of Pacifica] have the right for their case to be heard in Pacifican civilian courts. Unlawful enemy combatants fall under the jurisdiction of military tribunals, and can never have access to the civilian courts. No citizen shall be denied the right of access to the courts.

National and State laws passed under this Constitution shall also provide for the education, hiring, and budgets for a pro bono bar of legal representatives who shall specialize in and provide free confidential assistance for each area of the law, being available through material and electronic means, for answering the queries of the People for legal aid, to communicate appeals and petitions, and to assist those asking for advice or consultation.

Judicial officers shall consist of all Persons sworn to duty in a court of Pacifica or subdivisions thereof, including but not limited to court presidents, judges, magistrates, clerks, bailiffs, lawyers and attorneys, witnesses, trial jurors, or recorders.

A Public lawyer cannot abandon a case for a personal reason due to simply a disagreement with a client, a personality conflict, or philosophical compatibility, though a client may fire their lawyer, including a public defender, for any reason. Exceptions will be carved out by law for issues like relocation to another area or familial personal issues that occupy their time so that they are unavailable to the client.

There will be developed by each Jurisdiction, through their legislative powers and/or ‘the People’, a standard set of Rules of Professional Conduct for lawyers.

Subsequently appointed presidents, judges, magistrates, and clerks shall not be appointed permanently to a particular court, but periodically reassigned to courts and cases by sortition, with presidents or judges reassigned at random to courts every six months, and at random to cases, other officials other than jurors assigned to courts for up to two years, and trial jurors selected at random to each case.

Intervenors in cases who argue in defense of the Constitution shall not be excluded or impeded, in trial or appeal, in the courtroom or outside it, or in presenting legal arguments to juries.

Any multi-member judicial panel must be unanimous to sustain a claimed power of government against the claim of a citizen that the government lacks such power. If there is any doubt concerning whether an official has a delegated power, the presumption shall be that they do not. Courts shall not defer to the judgment of legislative or executive officials, but shall require strict proof of their findings or authority, with a presumption of non-authority.

Opinions of all courts, majority, concurring, or dissenting, shall be signed by each judicial officer participating, and all decisions and opinions shall be published except for State secrets. The summary, findings, orders, and commentary shall be clearly separated and labeled as such.

No court shall be secret, but justice shall be administered, openly and without purchase, completely and without delay, without need of elevation for timely process, and every Person shall have remedy by due course of law for injury done to them in their Person, property, or reputation.

No governmental Representative shall be precluded from taking part in any legislative vote by virtue of being detained prior to their trial; no judge of any Court of Pacifica shall be detained on suspicion of any criminal offense unless with an express consent of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or if unable to reach or incapacitated, any other Justice of the Supreme Court.

A crime, whether under the laws of Pacifica or a State, shall be considered to have been committed at the point in space and time where mens rea and actus reus concur, not where the harm is caused. Territorial jurisdiction for treason, piracy, and offenses against the Law of Nations is not confined to the territory of Pacifica, but personal jurisdiction for treason is confined to Pacifican citizens.

The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury; and such Trial shall be held in the State where the said Crimes shall have been committed; but when not committed within any State, the Trial shall be at such Place or Places as the Congress may by Law have directed. The People shall be entitled to “Judices judicatus cum jus judex” or “[the] Jury deciding as [the] presiding Judge”.

A Person charged in any State with Treason, Felony, or other Crime, who shall flee from Justice, and be found in another State, shall on Demand of the executive Authority of the State from which they fled, be delivered up, to be removed to the State having Jurisdiction of the Crime.

No citizen of Pacifica shall be deported, expelled, or otherwise transferred to any foreign country, government, or jurisdiction for the purpose of serving a criminal sentence or as punishment for any crime. No law or executive action of Pacifica, or of any State, shall authorize or permit the removal of a Pacifican citizen to a foreign country for the purpose of imprisonment, detention, or penal servitude. Congress and the several States shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.

SECTION. 4.

In times of disaster or invasion, where the public courts may be unable to [react] or fully meet their duties for these reasons, the General Citizenry shall under like procedure and rules to the calling of jurors, be vested with ‘Power of the Bench’. The “Citizen’s Bench” shall also be the judge in instances where the government is a party to the cases or controversies in question.

The suspension of aggressor’s rights as a protective measure for the People against aggressing individuals must be authorized by an independent citizen’s court which abides by due process, that will act as the impartial arbiter of decision over the request by the government courts over the suspension of any right of a duly convicted offender, as may be set forth under this Constitution. rights may only be suspended proportionately to an actual act of aggression against another, or in other words, as an equal reaction to a violation of the mutual non-aggression principle, if it is suspected that suspension of the right is a reasonably efficient and meaningfully effective measure of achieving their victim’s, and in extension. neighboring People’s safety, so long as such restrictions are to the least degree necessary as possible to reach such ends. The lengths of time in which a right may “be removed” must be limited to two years, though they may be renewed upon the ruling of a subsequent new citizen’s court composed of a citizen consulate of three judges serving as one in unanimous consensus, and a jury composed of eighteen Citizens of Pacifica.

No court within Pacifica shall enter a default judgment against any party in any civil or criminal proceeding. All parties shall be afforded the right to notice, due process, and a fair opportunity to be heard before any judgment is rendered. This provision guarantees that judgments may only be issued upon the merits of the case, following actual participation or a meaningful opportunity for participation by all parties, consistent with the principles of individual liberty and justice. Legislative bodies within Pacifica shall enact no law permitting default judgments, and any such law in effect at the time of this Constitution's adoption shall be null and void.

SECTION. 5.

The Citizens Court is a voluntary, decentralized judicial body composed of Jurial peers, established to resolve disputes, protect individual rights, and uphold contracts, operating strictly within the bounds of consent and without expanding state power beyond the protection of liberty, property, and personal autonomy.

The Citizens Court shall derive its authority solely from this Constitution and the laws made in accordance therewith, with all proceedings open, transparent, and based on mutual agreement to participate or the pursuit of Justice in criminal cases.

Jurisdiction is limited to the protection of individual rights, enforcement of contracts, and resolution of disputes where no party’s health, liberty, or property is infringed.

All decisions must be rendered by a jury of peers or mutually agreed-upon arbiters, with each party retaining the right to select or challenge jurors to ensure impartiality.

The Citizens Court may not impose penalties, obligations, or remedies beyond those necessary to restore violated rights or enforce voluntary agreements, and may not create or interpret rights beyond those explicitly recognized in this Constitution or by mutual contract.

Participation in the Citizens Court is voluntary except to enforce natural rights; no individual may be compelled to submit to its authority, except as provided by prior, freely entered contract, unless they breach the rights of another as according to this constitution.

All orders and judgments must respect the principle of individual liberty, be narrowly tailored to the dispute at hand, and be subject to appeal or review by higher courts or arbitration panels, as agreed by the parties.

The Citizens Court shall not serve as an instrument for expanding state power, but as a means for individuals to peacefully resolve disputes and protect their rights without coercion.

SECTION. 5.

Trial by jury is an inviolate right and shall be secured to all, but in a civil cause three-fourths of the jury may render a verdict. A jury may be waived in a criminal cause, by the consent of both parties to the case, expressed in open court by the defendant and the defendant’s counsel, in accordance with the common law; In a civil cause a jury may be waived by the consent of the parties expressed as prescribed by statute, in accordance with the common law.

In civil causes the jury shall consist of twelve persons or a lesser number agreed on by the parties in open court. In civil causes other than causes within the appellate jurisdiction of the court of appeal the Legislature may provide that the jury shall consist of eight persons or a lesser number agreed on by the parties in open court.

In criminal actions in which a felony is charged, the jury shall consist of twelve persons. In criminal actions in which a misdemeanor is charged, the jury shall consist of twelve persons or a lesser number agreed on by the parties in open court.

    All jurors summoned for actual service in trials of law and equity, must be mutually approved by all parties being represented, having met the impartiality criteria of those interests by all parties being represented. One criteria of their impartiality must be to uphold all of the natural and constitutional rights of Persons & Pacificans, as prescribed in part by this Constitution.

In all criminal cases whatever, the Jury shall have the right to grant a new trial, as in civil cases.

It is the natural right of every citizen of Pacifica, when serving on a civil-trial or criminal-trial jury, to judge both the law and the facts pertaining to the case before the jury, in order to determine whether justice will be served by applying the law to the defendant. It is mandatory that all jurors be informed of this right. Before the jury hears a case, and again before jury deliberation begins, the court shall inform jurors of their rights in these words: “As jurors, your first responsibility is to decide whether the prosecution has proven beyond a reasonable doubt every element of the civil/criminal liability/charge. If you decide that the prosecution has proven beyond a reasonable doubt every element of the civil/criminal liability/charge but you cannot in good conscience support a liable/guilty verdict, you are not required to do so. To reach a verdict which you believe is just, each of you has the right to consider to what extent the defendant’s actions have actually caused harm or otherwise violated your sense of right and wrong. If you believe justice requires it, you may also judge both the merits of the law under which the defendant has been [held] liable/charged and the wisdom of applying that law to the defendant. Accordingly, for each charge against the defendant, even if review of the evidence strictly in terms of the law would indicate a liable/guilty verdict, you have the right to find the defendant not liable/guilty. The court cautions that with the exercise of this right comes the full moral responsibility for the verdict you bring in.” As part of their oath, the jurors shall affirm that they understand the information concerning their rights which this section requires the court to give them, and that no party to the trial may be prevented from encouraging jurors to exercise this right. For the jurors to be so informed is declared to be part of the defendant’s fundamental right to a fair trial by jury, and failure to conduct any criminal trial in accordance with this section shall not constitute harmless error, and shall be grounds for a mistrial. No potential juror may be disqualified from serving on a jury because they express willingness to judge the law or its application, or to vote according to their conscience.

Juries decide Sentencing Severity and Length, not Government Judges, except upon Bench Trial at Consent of the Accused upon consultation with their Attorney; Both Judges and Jurors have the Power to show leniency to criminal defendants, and to reduce or drop charges based on their good conscience, even if the evidence is indisputable, that the accused had committed the crime, if either the Judge or Jury thinks and can articulate that the law is unjust, unfairly applied, or any other reason they believe is just.

The Jury shall be the decider in all cases of fact and law before them, unless the defendant shall choose a bench trial of their own volition, and no case shall be settled by plea bargain, but any reduction in charges or sentence length or substance which the prosecutor, Judge, or Jury, see to be suitable to meet the ends of Justice, shall be applied to Jury or Bench convicted individuals.

The primary obligation of a Juror is to serve Justice, whether this is in line with or despite the law as written.

Jurors are free to consider materials outside of what is furnished in the trial process for the purposes of fully informing themselves further in their legal knowledge and jurial position.

The jury shall have the right to nullify enforcement of un-constitutional or otherwise unjust laws and penalties in all cases brought before them. Jurors shall be explicitly informed of their right to nullify laws they find unjust during all criminal and civil trials.

Juries retain the right to vote their conscience, and the power to strike down as void and unlawful any laws in conflict with the constitution, with the duty to elaborate upon the decision for the benefit of the People, and the responsibility to do so mindfully and only upon serious consideration through their deliberations.

Grand juries:
1) Screen out and dismiss cases against defendants with procedural defects, issue counter claims against corrupt officials or other conspiring parties upon preliminary remediation of nullification in the case of the falsely accused or those victim to corrupted process
2) Liable for allowing cases to go through that have obvious procedural defects
3) Their job is to keep a person out of jail in the first place, like if the accused were falsely arrested
4) Jurially appointed position upon good behavior lasting a term of one year renewable twice, maybe rotate based on maximal degrees of separation with minimal re-use.

Juries should be “periodically” randomly selected, so that juries cycle through, and do not constantly remain the same members, as some may manipulate the interpretation of the constitution into. In this case, when citizens review the constitutionality of a bill or other legislation/initiatives, then they will be periodically cycled out and fresh jurors are randomly selected from the lottery pool, including their name re-entered for random selection (odds of successive selections diminish by powers of odds or exponentials, so there is little risk of multiple members serving as a ‘supreme/immortal council’).

All forms of Juries must pass a legal knowledge exam with high marks exceeding 8-out-of-10 score, and pass a problem analysis and solution test without using a single logical fallacy, when the conundrum is designed to confound an illogical person into for example, special pleading their position is correct, when it requires them deliver a full standard of a burden of proof, in other words, in addition to the cognitive exam that includes IQ and world perception skills, such as a WAIS examination and evaluation, and the requisite to demonstrate an understanding of the rights of another and when objectionable exercise is still the less legal and not strictly offensive in the legal and criminal sense, they will also be required to demonstrate an understanding of logical fallacies and not use them themself, and may even be required to solve logical puzzles other than a few mazes as according to the rules decided by their State.

Grand Juries will be selected and exercise the People’s Authority in like manner to all other military/maritime, criminal, civil Juries, and be equally answerable before the People and those who are falsely accused or victims unrightfully deprived remedy.

Prosecutors, Judges, and Juries are criminally and civilly liable for any false convictions rendered under their position of trust, authority, and power; Juries which produce improper indictment, or impart false convictions, which are later overturned by a habeas Corpus, Appeal, State Supreme Citizen’s Court, proper jurisdictional District of the Federal Supreme Citizen’s Court, or the Supreme Citizen’s High Court ruling, shall be guilty of corruption of the legal process as well as conspiracy to deprive rights, and will be tried in criminal court, with long and harsh sentences if they are convicted, and be directly open and responsible for any Civil liabilities and criminal charges that may stem from their victim/[‘]s[‘] rights being deprived.

Jury instructions must allow the entertainment of any defense supported by law by which the defendant could seek relief. Juries may be screened out based on failure to properly distinguish lawful actions or speech from unlawful conduct, and juries shall be instructed on the nuances of areas such as obstruction of justice versus defense against unlawful arrest, and legitimate threats versus protected speech. Juries will be required to take a [state-paid] legal orientation course unless they test out on examination.

Juries shall retain the right to vote their conscience, and the power to strike down as void and unlawful any laws in conflict with the constitution, with the duty to elaborate upon the decision for the benefit of the People, and the responsibility to do so mindfully and only upon serious consideration through their deliberation.

Juries shall retain the right to refuse to convict an accused individual on the basis that the interpretation of the law put forth by prosecutors, if adopted, would result in violating the individual’s rights.

Jury and victim decide punishment, not judges; Judges are referees; Judges may only reverse a conviction if it is plainly evident that no reasonable Jury could possibly have arrived at the conclusion of guilt given the facts provided, and must clearly explain the reasons or counter-proofs that show that such conviction is contrary to the purposes of Justice (This is customary judicial power in the United States of America).

Jury duty is also reprimandable by exonerating evidence presented later that proves beyond a reasonable doubt the innocence of the accused, contrary to the burden of proof, and thereby constituting a second violation upon the defendant; Courts which deliver false edicts even without malice may result in the constituent body losing their ability to serve in public office.

SECTION. 6.

Law enforcement have a duty to protect the People and secure the natural rights of the People and visitors to Pacifica.

Law enforcement have explicit duties and obligations to investigate complaints, guard and protect as well as serve the People, preserve safety and promote the welfare of all people, and to enforce all laws within their jurisdiction. They must take an oath affirming their duty “to guard and protect as well as serve their community”, which includes protecting individuals from the criminal acts of others (without the need for a special relationship of care to exist), as well as, “to uphold the laws of their jurisdiction”, and “to preserve and defend the constitution”, and at all times they as individuals retain liability for failing to perform any of these duties while actually in service to the public. The motto of law enforcement is “To protect, serve, maintain peace, and preserve liberty”. Their mission is “To provide a safe and secure environment for all residents and visitors; to seek, understand, and address the underlying issues that lead to calls for service, and to provide answers to questions and solutions to problems as far as they are capable; To accomplish these goals through community involvement policing along with an aggressive enforcement of the laws within their jurisdiction using the minimal amount of force necessary to secure the accused, as prescribed in this Constitution and as may additionally be laid down by law; Collaborative efforts and enhanced problem solving techniques to improve the quality of life for residents and enhancing the experience of visitors; Law enforcement will fulfill their mission by protecting and serving in a compassionate, patient, courteous, and helpful manner with integrity, honesty, accountability, loyalty, and usefulness to the People, in which they serve”.

All approachments of law enforcement towards a Person or Persons in question must proceed in a professional, polite, respectful, and compassionate manner, where law enforcement are required to adequately identify themselves including by verbal and affixed text articulation of their name and of their personnel ID, in addition to their articulating their purpose for the interaction, and to provide facts related to their jurisdiction or lawful justification for any action which impairs the rights of the people.

Law enforcement must take active charge and exercise independent judgment in dealing with unusual, serious, or dangerous situations, exercising safety practices and procedures. They must be able to work under stressful, high risk conditions. It is their duty to protect the citizens they are meant to be serving, and their own safety should always come second to that. The Job of Law Enforcement is to stand the line between the civilians and the initiators of aggression; Sometimes that means taking a bullet because Law Enforcement are bound to the Rules of Engagement and are not allowed to shoot first; Lethal force should only be used after the life of Law Enforcement, or the life of an/other Citizen/s or other Person/s, has been placed in direct jeopardy.

Law enforcement may patrol public areas for the purpose of observing possible criminal activity or other conditions that could endanger public safety. They shall investigate and report fires or other related events; keep bystanders out of danger; and safeguard persons as well as property.

Law enforcement shall watch for wanted or missing persons and lost minors, and report stray animals as necessary.

Law enforcement are expected to answer questions asked by the People and refer the public to people or agencies which can provide further assistance as required.

Law enforcement must attend required periodic training sessions and seminars for the interests, service, protection, and defending there of the whole public [and ensure the best interests {through this republic, by the means administered en/in Populii, for and of the People, as in "We the People"} of the People through appropriate use of discretion are furthermore upheld], including true offenders: Law enforcement must take basic life preservation training including first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the use of automated external defibrillators, and be educated on human anatomy in order to try to save lives, including but not limited to that of the accused; Law enforcement are supposed to within their ability, save lives, such as rendering first aid to the injured or aiding in the Public defense for emergency situations; Law enforcement will be trained in self-defense and weapons safety. They must maintain a required level of proficiency in the use of weapons, and evasive action along with driving skills. They must maintain weapons and equipment in functional and presentable condition. Law enforcement shall be required to receive de-escalation training. Law enforcement shall be trained on their duty to intervene when another officer uses excessive force. Law enforcement’s otherwise reasonable (and lawful) defensive use of force is unreasonable as a matter of law, if their agent/s intentionally or recklessly provokes a forceful response, and, that provocation is an independent constitutional violation.

Law enforcement must participate in required physical fitness activities.

Law enforcement shall record information concerning events that took place during tour of duty, and record such activity in the manner as prescribed by the department in accordance with the legislature.

There shall be produced a law enforcement misconduct registry that departments will have to use when hiring, and the database on each individual will be maintained for thirty years from their last incident and at all times will be open to public inquiry.

Law enforcement may transport criminal mental patients and other prisoners to prescribed locations as necessary, as according to law in this Constitution, and of any other Constitution or law made in accordance therewith in any other jurisdiction in which they engaged in a criminal act. They shall account for and transport evidence coming into custody.

The primary power of arrest shall lie with Agents of Law Enforcement; in the absence of any such Agent, in exigent circumstances or pursuant to a public arrest warrant, a Person may be arrested by any Citizen or other Resident of Pacifica for so long as reasonably necessary to allow an Agent of Law Enforcement to take custody of the detainee.

All officers entrusted with the enforcement of law within the Commonwealth of Pacifica, whether serving under federal or state authority, shall exercise their powers not merely in obedience to statute but in steadfast pursuit of Justice as the supreme end of law, guided by conscience, fairness, and the preservation of human dignity. Each officer shall retain discretion in determining the manner and necessity of detention, citation, or arrest, favoring warnings, mediation, and restorative measures where such actions more fully serve peace, equity, and the welfare of the community than punitive enforcement. Officers owe their highest allegiance to the Constitution and to the enduring principles of liberty, equality, and the protection of the innocent and vulnerable; no statute, decree, or order shall compel them to act in violation of these principles. Every officer has both the right and the duty to refrain from enforcing any law or command that would contravene constitutional rights or offend the true aims of Justice, and no officer shall face penalty or reprisal for acts of just disobedience undertaken in good conscience and fidelity to the Constitution, subject to transparent review by an independent and impartial tribunal. Law enforcement throughout Pacifica shall be grounded in restorative and human-centered practice, holding that confinement and restraint of liberty are justified only in response to a legitimate violation of the rights of another, and shall never be employed as instruments of coercion, retribution, or social control. The legitimacy of law and its guardians shall rest upon the trust and consent of the governed, for Justice arises not from the power to command obedience but from the moral duty to harmonize right, mercy, equality, and the preservation of public order in service to the common good.

All law enforcement must work in a region local to their active residence; Officers of the law are specifically prohibited from policing areas of which they are not local residents. Law enforcement must be locally accountable to the areas they patrol, and preferably be a part of that community.

The powers of arrest in Pacifica shall not be exercised arbitrarily but solely upon a warrant issued only under a modicum of credible evidence for which it is apparent that the accused has likely committed or is committing a/n [criminal] offense against the rights of another, or that they have been made, or are soon to be made, a subject of a Court Order regarding an institutionalization in a mental health facility, deportation proceedings, or committal to prison for a breach of a Court order, and as such, is to be brought to trial or to the disposition of the appropriate authorities or the Court respectively.

Law enforcement have the duty to petition for the release of any Person they reasonably believe to be falsely imprisoned, and to submit any evidence that to their knowledge may exist to support this finding, to first the attorney general of their Jurisdiction, and if upon there shall be a failure for a release to happen, their Gubernor; This provision shall not obstruct the right of the People to petition for a writ of habeas Corpus upon demand, and to appeal on demand any finding under such writ.

In all cases involving mental or behavioral health crises, the default response shall be a Behavioral Health Unit, Crisis Response Team, or Crisis Outreach Team composed of trained professionals, rather than armed police, except where there is a clear and immediate threat to public safety that requires law enforcement intervention. Law enforcement agencies shall establish protocols to ensure that crisis response teams are the primary responders for nonviolent behavioral health emergencies, and shall collaborate with health care providers to facilitate effective, humane, and de-escalatory interventions. All police reports shall be written clearly and consistently, using standardized language to accurately describe incidents, especially those involving behavioral health crises, to ensure transparency, accountability, and effective communication across agencies. The legislature shall enact laws and provide resources necessary to implement these provisions, ensuring that communities throughout Pacifica have timely access to behavioral health crisis response services and that law enforcement receives appropriate training to support these initiatives.

Every law enforcement officer is bound to execute the penal warrants given to them to execute. They may summon to their assistance, either in writing or orally, any of the citizens of the neighborhood or county to assist in the execution of such warrants, so long as the summoned individuals consent to participate. The acts of the citizens formed as a posse by such officer shall be subject to the same protection and consequences as official acts.

Agents of Law Enforcement executing arrests shall act openly and shall inform the detainee about the relevant rights they enjoy under this Constitution and any laws passed in accordance therewith; where a Person is placed under arrest, Agents of Law Enforcement shall immediately inform their close ones as prescribed by law about the detention.

Officers are required to state the essential specific evidentiary elements in providing the officer with the required and unassailable real and reasonable suspicion or probable cause to allow short term detention while awaiting a warrant [or which supports a warrant itself], as part of their official report on and before levying the charge in the first place so as to prima facially validate the warranted seizure, search, and arrest of the individual being accused, and officers are required to immediately inform the Accused of these specific elements in order to lawfully and legally establish the officer’s legal authority to act against them in this matter.

Law enforcement who fail to meet these criteria will be subject to penalties including fines and/or criminal charges, and be open to Civil suit/s.

Where appropriate in accordance to the following criteria, citations should be issued in lieu of arrest in certain cases where there is no credible threat to the public for the suspect to remain outside of the confines of an institution, such as a jail or mental ward. Officers must weigh he severity of the crime at issue; whether the suspect poses an immediate threat to the safety of officers or others, whether the suspect is trying to evade arrest by flight, whether the citation is likely to cease the criminal activity, and whether they have an existing warrant for their arrest that must be executed. An arrest versus a citation must be justified in the totality of all circumstances, without the benefit of retrospect.

Citizens are naturally endowed with the Just power of Citizen’s Police Authority, and are subject to the same limitations as to the powers of government and the rules of Due Process, including but not limited to abiding by the warrant requirement for all Searches and Seizures, including following all rules regarding Detentions to serve such warrants and in placing Arrests or transferring custody. This power includes but is not limited to the lawful authority to issue warning/s against trespassing or intimidation/coercion, and the right to place a Citizen’s arrest for any violation of Rights.

The Highest Obligations of Law Enforcement are both, Firstly and most importantly, to protect and serve the Health and Lives, Liberty, and Happiness Citizens, and secondarily, to enforce and defend, the Constitution of both Pacifica as well as their State if there be any, in that order.

All law enforcement incidents where deadly force is used, whether or not someone is killed, will be investigated, and ruled Justified or Unjustified, by an impartial Citizen’s review board and Citizen’s bench;

Officers of the law, while on active duty, such as issuing and executing a warrant or placing an arrest, shall need to wear a reasonably affixed body mounted camera, when available, and there shall be a microphone present as well, which shall continuously record audio and video simultaneously using a redundant system and also a live stream over the cellular networks of their locality, and are to never be turned off while they are required by law; nothing in this provision shall be construed as to allow for general surveillance by the Public Administration. Body-cams must live stream and record such streams offsite, and contain two separate fixed/non-removable redundant password-protected-erasure-protected recording-memory banks, as well as furnish an exact copy of the local data to a removable medium for backup, and furnish a secured/protected read-only serial interface for copying the data; Additionally, they must also capture GPS data and seamlessly work in pitch-black and low-light ambient conditions alongside ambient lighting in the regular course of normal usage; Their resolution must be no lower than 1440p and their frames per second must be no less than one-hundred-and-twenty per instant/second.

Members of government, including law enforcement, shall be open to civil and criminal liability for any violation of law, process, or rights they may commit upon any person/android, animal/robot, or towards [the] nature/environment.

Law enforcement exist to serve the public by responding to reported crimes, investigating offenses supported by lawful evidence, protecting people from imminent harm, and enforcing laws within constitutional limits. They must not operate as a roving force that treats the public as presumptive suspects or seeks pretexts to discover wrongdoing. Intervention by Law Enforcement must be grounded in a complaint, direct observation, a warrant, an emergency, or particularized probable cause supported by specific and articulable facts.
