There shall be no semi/quasi/para-militarization or militarization of law enforcement, other than the militia itself. Law enforcement [other than than the militia] is barred from militarization for any conceivable purpose whatsoever; Militarizing law enforcement [except for militia] is a felony, similar to a Posse Comitatus.

Members of Law Enforcement cannot lawfully make arrests without them first showing identification of who they are and what Agency they are from.

Officers of the Law shall have the duty to inform any of those whom they work under explicit consent with, or detain under [unassailable] probable cause with a real and reasonable suspicion, that which is they the Officer’s: Full name and Public Work Identification Number. They must, beyond declaring their name and cause, cite their evidence in favor of any stop, search, seizure, or arrest, to the detained and suspected.

Members of public law enforcement do not have the exclusive monopoly of enforcing the law, but this power of the public may be freely exercised in right by the People as well.

Plainclothes and undercover officers alike may not operate without a clearly defined and limited warrant authorizing each one of their activities while operating under color of law within the scope of their official duties, with any/all of their additional requests for leniency must be specifically authorized by the presiding justice over the police case; Their permitted hours of operation must be stipulated within the warrant and any changes in operative parameters must be approved by the presiding judge whom may then alter the warrant in accordance with the public record.

There must be a reasonability and believability in police reports, so that the average person who is schooled in civics included but not limited to this constitution, and receiving the report, would believe there was the need to send assistance of Law Enforcement and not proceed in some other manner, such as sending a Mental Health Crisis team, Social Worker mediator, or some other department of Public service such as Firefighters or Emergency Medical Technicians.

Law enforcement must have liability insurance for not less than One hundred thousand dollars Pacifican money and be liable for all the rest after insurance pays, if any remains unpaid to victim

The right of the People to organize, maintain, and operate community-based security and policing organizations, hereafter “Sheriffia”, shall not be reduced. These units, akin to citizen militias, are composed of voluntary members of the community and are empowered to maintain peace, protect property, and uphold justice according to the freely chosen norms and agreements of their locality. Citizen police power is the inherent authority of individuals, acting collectively or independently, to prevent, deter, and respond to violations of person or property, provided such actions respect due process and the rights of all parties. This power is not a grant from the state but a natural extension of the right to self-defense and mutual aid. Sheriffia may operate independently or in cooperation with other local or regional entities, always subject to the consent of the governed. The People retain the right to form, join, or contract with multiple, overlapping legal and security systems within any given jurisdiction, fostering a polycentric legal order. No single authority shall monopolize the provision of law enforcement or dispute resolution. Instead, legal services-including policing, arbitration, and adjudication-may be provided by competing or federated entities, each accountable to those who voluntarily choose their services. All Sheriffs and legal service providers operate by the express consent of the communities they serve. Their authority derives from mutual agreement, historical custom, or explicit contract, not from coercive state mandate. Disputes between individuals, communities, or policing units shall be settled through mutually agreed-upon arbitration or customary law, with the aim of restitution and restoration rather than punishment. No government at any level shall prohibit, restrict, or monopolize the formation and operation of Sheriffia or alternative legal systems, except where such groups violate the fundamental rights of others. All policing and legal entities must operate with transparency and be subject to public oversight within their communities.

[Agents] [or] Officers of the law are required to report each time they engage in the use of injurious or deadly force, and to submit to a full battery-arrayed assay drug test, except for spinal tap, after all applications of deadly force or misbehavior or investigation for unnecessary or over use of force.

It is unlawful for law enforcement to perform sexual acts with their captives, this also extends to prison guards and other personnel.

Law enforcement are borrowed from performing choke-holds unless the use of deadly force is otherwise authorized.

The falsification or omission in and of reports by law enforcement shall be a felony.

If law enforcement are held liable for excessive use of force and/or while operating outside national plus state guidelines, then any monetary judgments are paid out of police retirement funds, or directly out of the offending officer’s pocket, they shall not be made up with State sector business funds.

Individual police are required to carry insurance in case of judgments against them. same as for bad drivers, the bad cops will simply price themselves out of a joblessness

Any law enforcement official caught planting incriminating evidence and/or withholding exculpatory evidence shall face the same penalties (fines & jail time) as the crimes they attempted to frame.

No person, whether acting in a governmental, corporate, or private capacity, shall enjoy qualified immunity, civil immunity, sovereign immunity, or any other form of special exemption from civil or criminal liability for their actions. All individuals and entities shall be fully accountable under the law for violations of the rights, property, or person of others. Every individual whose rights have been infringed by another, including by agents or employees of the government, shall have full and equal access to seek redress and remedy in a court of law or through any mutually agreed-upon dispute resolution process. No law, decree, or policy shall shield any person or entity from legal responsibility for their conduct. Holding public office, employment by the state, or acting under color of law shall not confer any special legal protections or immunities. All government officials, employees, contractors, and agents, and those cooperating with any of them, are subject to the same laws and liabilities as any private citizen. No legislative or executive act shall grant retroactive immunity or pardon for actions that violated the rights of others, except as may be determined by a jury of peers in accordance with due process and the principles of justice.

No law or rule shall shield a member of the Public Body or a Private citizen from culpability or criminal liability, nor from civil suit, for any crime they may commit upon the rights of another, or absolve them for any harm they may perpetrate or allow to occur under their ‘supervision’. Public Servants of Pacifica, acting beyond the reasonable discharge of their constitutionally enumerated duties, enjoy no immunity from civil or criminal prosecution by the Courts of the several States and Territories, Localities, or Federal authority.

All officers and agents of the law required to show proof of identity, position, and authority to order/direct or act, including citing the exact section of law in violation or in real and reasonable suspicion of being violated

The use of robotic law enforcement is barred from the Public Instrument, hereby, there shall only be allowed Citizens of Pacifica, which includes [true] androids, to work as officers of the law, as they abide by this constitution and the laws made in accordance therewith.

Law enforcement shall not be quartered in any place in time of Peace nor in time of war, except in manner to be prescribed by law consistent with the rights of the people.

No agent of the state, nor any person acting under color of law, shall initiate force against any individual except in direct response to an act of aggression that threatens the life, liberty, or property of another. The use of force shall be governed strictly by the principle: “Do not fire unless fired upon.” Law enforcement and community defense actions must always be reactive, never preemptive, except where there is clear and imminent threat evidenced by overt acts of aggression. In all circumstances, the minimum amount of force necessary to secure the safety of non-aggressors and to prevent further harm shall be used. Escalation of force is permitted only when lesser means have failed or are clearly inadequate to stop an ongoing rights violation. All actions must prioritize the preservation of life, liberty, and property of peaceful individuals. Any use of force must be documented, subject to immediate public review, and open to independent investigation. Officers and agents are individually liable for violations of these rules and shall not be shielded by any form of special immunity. Communities retain the right to set and enforce their own standards for rules of engagement and escalation, consistent with the non-aggression principle and the protection of civil liberties. Law enforcement authority shall be decentralized and accountable to the people it serves, not to distant bureaucracies or centralized power structures.

A[n] [stocked] ambulance with EMTs nearby on standby is needed when law enforcement are executing their duties and could possibly use force; It further goes without saying, though the trope of government is to perform intentional negligence and malice and claim ignorance and accident, it shall be proclaimed that if any party [for which law enforcement are responding to] are injured, or if there are victims, prompt and adequate medical care shall be rendered as soon as humanly possible.

In order to reduce the likelihood of State violence against our people, priorities shall be to use social workers for domestic disputes and minor kid and youth protection investigations, and for seeking alternative people to arbitrate disputes. Law enforcement shall, upon discovery of its appropriate need, to provide social workers or mental health specialist staff as additional members of the reconciliation of disputes and to detain offenders.

All members of law enforcement are required to release any falsely held or charged or sentenced detainee/s, arrested, and those imprisoned for any term, in so far as such release promotes the integrity of Universal Law in the interest of Natural Justice and Rights.

"Contempt Against the People" shall refer to any action, expression, or behavior by a law enforcement officer or government official directed at an individual, where the officer's or official’s response, such as detention, investigation, arrest, or the initiation of criminal charges, is based solely on a perceived lack of respect, deference, or challenge to the official’s authority, and not on any objectively unlawful conduct. The mere exercise of constitutional rights, including but not limited to freedom of speech and expression, the right to petition, and the right to record public officials, shall not be construed as grounds for detention or arrest under the guise of contempt of cop. Any attempt to penalize individuals for asserting these rights constitutes Contempt Against the People and an abuse of governmental authority.

Public entities such as members of law enforcement, are fully liable for any damages, injuries, or deaths caused by failure to enforce an enactment [of law], failure to arrest somebody who is violating the law, or through any negligence in using insufficient force to keep [a] prisoner/s in custody. All use of force by law enforcement must be objectively reasonable along with proportionate force [under civilian oversight].

Predictive policing, AI-driven behavior scoring, and neural or health data mining shall be banned within Pacifica. No AI crime prediction nor autonomous surveillance drones shall be deployed to profile or preemptively detain any Person. No authority shall use predictive-index algorithms, pre-crime profiling, automated risk-scoring, or incapacitation/neutralization probability metrics as grounds for arrest, detention, or restriction of movement or rights.

AI‑facilitated crime reporting along with AI‑based threat detection and reporting are hereby prohibited to the Government and their contractors, as well as those cooperating with either, in all cases.

All policing must be human-led, transparent, accountable, and subject to community oversight boards comprised solely of local Citizens. No artificial intelligence, synthetic entity, or autonomous algorithm implemented or used by the government or any of the contractors beneath them, or those cooperating with either, shall ever be endowed with authority over any natural person, except where narrowly constrained to purely mechanical tasks under direct human supervision.

All law enforcement personnel exercising Authority within a Jurisdiction must be locally appointed, and accountable to the People for which they serve. Exceptions for state level law enforcement only exist to the degree at which local appointment is impossible and there must be a broader Commonwealth appointment, and in all cases whether elected or appointed law enforcement shall be accountable to the People.

SECTION. 6.

The duties of the sheriff's office are constitutionally defined by each State, and by this constitution.

Among the duties of the sheriff are to serve three square meals a day from the sheriff station to people in the general Public who are in need of food such as the homeless/unsheltered and those of zero or low income. Each one of the meals will include coffee or tea and donuts or muffins available with natural sweetener and milk or real juice. Coffee and tea shall be served all throughout the day including between meal times, and there shall be access to running water and a microwave at all times.

The sheriff may also serve to arm and equip the people separately from the statewide Citizen's armament and equipping program. The terms for which the Sheriffs shall arm and equip the people shall be set by each county.

It is the sacred duty of every freeborn man to defend the common and civil laws and his own liberty before and over every obligation, even through natural law, and an obligation of the state and the rulers. All persons who are the victims of a crime are expected to raise their “hue and cry” and apprehend the criminal; and upon hearing their cry, every able-bodied man in the community is expected to do the “utmost in his power” (pro toto posse suo) to chase and apprehend the accused as a “posse”. Every man is thereby personally responsible for the law and for the safety of the entire community.

Sheriffs are to be elected and employed by the People, and  are the Spark that will inspire many to stand up for their rights and freedoms.

Before taking on the duties and responsibilities of a Sheriff, it is essential that they learn about common law and they are trained how to apply the law to protect the people, and arrest criminals. The community expects its Sheriffs to be well versed in the law so that they can not only uphold it to benefit the community, but also to enable them to make educated judgments about employing it lawfully.

As well, all Sheriffs should complete a course in basic Common Law based on the book “A common Law Training Manual” available from commonlaw.earth .

As Sheriffs train for their task, they become the spark that will inspire and train many other patriots. And by doing so, Sheriffs play a very important part of a great movement, to reclaim Pacifica for all its people, under our Constitution.

Their job as a Sheriff will be to act as the primary peace officers, as the people reassert our common law roots through local Sovereign Peoples’ Assemblies.

Common Law Sheriffs have the power to convene citizen juries and Common Law courts, deputize anyone to perform arrests, and to form and train Citizen Militias, win over the police and other agents of the old regime to act according to common law, and reclaim the land, and the wealth, of the nation for all its people.

In the hands of the Sheriff rests the security of our Nation. Only the most devoted and courageous among them should assume this sacred responsibility. The mission of a Sheriff will not be easy, or safe, but it is necessary to protect our liberty and for our personal safety.

All Sheriffs must be elected by the people after they are vetted by the Chartered members of an Assembly or by 'the People', for which whom they are sworn and empowered by the Public Instrument to protect.

This is the procedure they must follow:
1) Training in the Common Law, available through the online legal education law library platform of their State. A Sheriff candidate must complete a course and produce their completion certificates to their assembly meeting when they stand for election.
2) A Sheriff candidate stands before an Assembly and explains why they want to be a Sheriff and the skills they would bring to the job. To be a Sheriff, we need men and women who are fit, healthy, able to run fast, and who have a working knowledge of Common Law. If they have martial arts training, that is preferable, but not required. All Sheriffs must agree to undergo training. The assembly will judge them on these skills, and then vote accordingly as to whether or not they are eligible for election.
3) Once a Sheriff is elected by the assembly, the Convener, or another Sheriff, will swear in the candidate before the assembly. Each Sheriff must swear on their own honor to act lawfully and honorably in a manner adherent to their good conscience.
4) After a Sheriff has been sworn in, their first duty is to fill out the Oath of Office form and submit it to their county clerk.
5) After filling in the Oath form from the county clerk, the Sheriff will immediately receive a digital copy of their Sheriff Oath of Office which they must then present to the assembly convener to sign. Only after they have done this is their Sheriff appointment valid.
6) On producing the Oath to the Assembly Convener, the Sheriff will be issued with a numbered badge. The cost of the badge is five Pacifican dollars. The Sheriff is also responsible for the costs of their training and uniform. However, the Sheriff may apply to the assembly to reimburse these costs after being sworn in. It is up to each assembly to decide on whether or not to pay the costs back to the Sheriff.
7) Sheriffs must commit to a regular exercise schedule to ensure that they are in peak physical condition at all times.

SECTION. 7.333.

The right of every person to be free from arbitrary surveillance, detention, intimidation, violence, and all forms of secret or politically motivated enforcement by any organ, agent, or auxiliary of the government of Pacifica, or by any entity acting under color of law or authority, is inviolable. No branch, office, department, subdivision, official, or agent of the government of Pacifica, nor any contracted or deputized third party, shall establish, authorize, fund, support, operate, or condone any system, unit, or agency that engages in, enables, or tolerates: Surveillance, investigation, penalization, or any form of interference absent individualized suspicion of criminal wrongdoing and oversight by an independent judiciary; Arrest, detention, interrogation, confinement, or physical or psychological coercion, except pursuant to publicly established law, with full transparency, due process, and immediate independent review; Maintenance of secret dossiers, the use of undisclosed informants, or reliance on anonymous accusations as a basis for enforcement action against persons; Any act or policy intended to suppress dissent, inhibit association, or chill the free exercise of conscience, belief, assembly, speech, or political participation. For the purpose of this provision, “Gestapo” is defined universally as any mechanism, official or unofficial, direct or indirect, that enables a state or its agents to engage in or facilitate secret or arbitrary enforcement, surveillance, or suppression beyond the reach of independent and impartial judicial scrutiny. This applies regardless of the ideological, political, or administrative context, and irrespective of the form, name, scale, or purported necessity invoked. The rights and prohibitions outlined shall not be suspended, displaced, or overridden by any emergency, executive order, delegated power, legislation, or treaty. Any attempt to create or invoke a form of secret or extrajudicial policing is null and void ab initio. All persons within Pacifica, and all sovereign persons subject to Pacifican law, shall have direct standing to challenge any alleged violation of this provision in a court of law or other independent tribunal, and shall be guaranteed the right to immediate public hearing and effective remedies.

SECTION. 7.666.

Jailers and prison guards shall receive training in minimal level of force control techniques and non-lethal self-defense techniques, in addition to any other training normally required by law and elsewhere under this constitution for law enforcement in general.

Security and facility guards in state institutions should be composed of equal numbers of Sheriff’s deputies from each county.

SECTION. 8.

The office of District Attorney shall be filled by election of the People. The District Attorney shall have no authority to judge, determine guilt or fault of any defendant, or rule on the rightfulness of any governmental action. The District Attorney’s role shall be strictly administrative and clerical, serving as a public officer accountable to the People. The primary duty of the District Attorney shall be to receive and process complaints from individuals, including in-person filings at their office, and to facilitate the fair and impartial administration of justice.

Any individual shall have the right to prosecute an alleged offense themselves or to appoint any other person as their proxy to execute prosecution functions on their behalf. Such prosecutions shall proceed as may be justly determined and mutually agreed to by the parties, subject to the rules of due process and oversight by a court of competent jurisdiction.

SECTION. 9.

A person cannot become a ward of court without having first under due process of law been ruled by a jury of twelve in a court of proper jurisdiction, to be either a danger to others or have caused harm to another, or those without a caretaker and in need of special assistance either due to incompetence of minorship or remediality;

All individuals who are wards of state shall be allowed access to their families, to choose if they would like to work on continuing their educations, and to be preserved from exposure to trauma and violence during their custody, as to promote their development as People and in creating and sustaining lifelong positive outcomes upon their release [if and when].

No Person shall be declared to be lacking mental capacity unless by an Order issued by the Civil Court on application of a psychological practitioner under relevant law; all Persons declared to be lacking mental capacity shall be appointed [a] Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s by the Court, unless they are still under the care of their Parent/s or Legal Guardian/s, and, should they pose a threat to others who are non-aggressors, may be committed to a mental health institution pursuant to a Court Order; any Order declaring a Person to be lacking mental capacity shall automatically expire within two years; after the expiration such a Person shall be deemed to have regained mental capacity unless the Court renews its order; the relevance of any Order in such matter may be challenged by the Person concerned or their Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s, once in every six months before it expires, in Habeas Corpus proceedings. No court order deeming somebody as being lacking capacity may authorize the forcing of medications against their will; [and]- furthermore, that it is only through explicit voluntary revocable consent through which may a therapy or prescription may then there be so be administered in the interests of the Patient in counseling; This clause applies to all patients, including minors capable by law of providing a form of consent willingly with Parent or Legal/Revered Guardian or authorization.

Any Person under real and reasonable suspicion by law enforcement or a psychological practitioner of being mentally ill as well as additionally posing an obvious, compelling, and directly demonstrable danger, along with a serious and imminent threat to other [non-aggressing] Individuals, shall be subject to psychological evaluation and potentially detainment or institutionalization in a mental health facility pursuant to an Order of the Civil Court for such time as they remain a serious and imminent threat to the safety or life of others [whom are non-aggressors], due to their illness. No Person shall be declared to be mentally ill as well as to pose an obvious, compelling, and directly demonstrable danger to other [non-aggressing] Individuals unless by an Order issued by the Criminal Court on the application of and/or in conjunction with the testimony of a psychological practitioner under relevant law; all Persons declared to be mentally ill and posing an obvious, compelling, and directly demonstrable danger to other [non-aggressing] Individuals, shall be appointed a Legal Guardian or Caregiving Custodian by the Court, unless they are still under the care of their Parent/s, and may be committed to a mental health institution pursuant to a Court Order; any Order declaring a Person to be mentally ill as well as additionally posing an obvious, compelling, and directly demonstrable danger to society shall automatically expire within two years; after the expiration such a Person shall be deemed to have regained their mental health unless the Court renews its order; the relevance of any Order in such matter may be challenged by the concerned person at hand, or, Parent/s if they do exist, next of kin, or Legal Guardian/s, have there not be a parent or next of kin, or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s, if there be none of these before, once in every six months before it expires, in Habeas Corpus proceedings.

No person accused of a crime shall be deprived of liberty on the grounds of readiness to stand trial on psychiatric grounds for longer than strictly necessary to determine and restore their ability to aid and assist in their own defense. The following principles shall apply: Any individual found unable to aid and assist must be transferred from detention to appropriate mental health care within seven days of such a finding. The maximum duration of involuntary commitment for the purpose of restoring trial competency shall not exceed: Ninety days for misdemeanor charges; Six months for non-violent felony charges; One year for violent felony charges. If, at any point, a less restrictive alternative is sufficient to meet the individual's needs, they shall be released from institutional care without delay. All proceedings and detentions under this section shall be subject to prompt judicial review and the right to independent legal counsel, as well as to Have us Corpus Ex Populii that they be examined by a Jurial body to ensure their pre-trial detention is lawful and not secret. No person shall be held in state custody solely for lack of access to mental health services or due to administrative delay.

SECTION. 10.

Neither Pacifica nor any State shall deny to any person Due Process, nor the equal protection of the law. For every injury, the Law shall provide remedy. That every freeman restrained of his liberty is entitled to a remedy, to enquire into the lawfulness thereof and for others to do likewise, and to remove the same, if unlawful, and that such remedy ought not to be denied nor delayed.

We Recognize that Being an Authority [on] and Mediator of Liberty and Justice is a personal duty of all People. A Victim, or their Trustee/s, is/are required to pursue all reasonable courses of lawful Private action seeking to provide “Just Remedy” from the Injurer, for restoration of Injury to any of the Victim’s rights, before they may rightfully utilize the Courts to pursue restoration of their Life or Health, Liberty or Freedom, ability to secure and defend themselves and whatever willing others, Property, or pursuit of Happiness; a complaint to the Courts by a Victim, or their Trustee/s, otherwise, excepting exigent cases of immediate danger or irrepairable harm, without them first reasonably attempting to seek a “Just Remedy” directly from the Injurer (when possible) through lawful Private means, is invalid.

The rights of victims of violent crime, being capable of protection without denying the constitutional rights of those accused of victimizing them, are hereby established and shall not be denied by any State or Pacifica, nor by any Territory, or Forts/Installations beneath them, or other Jurisdiction under their dominion, and may be restricted only as provided in this provision. A victim of violent crime shall have the right to reasonable and timely notice of any public proceeding involving the crime and of any release or escape of the accused; the rights not to be excluded from such public proceeding and reasonably to be heard at public release, plea, sentencing, reprieve, and pardon proceedings; and the right to adjudicative decisions that duly consider the victim’s safety, interest in avoiding unreasonable delay, and just and timely claims to restitution from the offender. These rights shall not be restricted except when and to the degree dictated by a substantial interest in public safety or the administration of criminal justice, or by compelling necessity guided under a rational-basis. Nothing in this provision shall be construed to provide grounds for a new trial or to authorize any claim for damages. Only the victim or the victim’s lawful representative may assert the rights established by this provision, and no Person accused of the crime may obtain any form of relief hereunder. Congress and each State shall have power to enforce by appropriate legislation the provisions of this article. Nothing in this article shall affect the President’s authority to grant reprieves or pardons.

The Victim of an alleged civil violation or criminal offense shall have the inherent right to file charges and institute a Private Prosecution of an accused Person:
(1) The Private Prosecution may be instituted by the Victim in person or by appointed Proxy on their behalf.
(2) Proxy may be any legal entity or natural Person expressly appointed by the Victim, whether inter vivos or in a last will, to be in charge of the prosecution in question.
(3) Should the Victim be a Minor or a Person lacking mental capacity, their Legal Guardian/s or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s shall be deemed to be a Proxy unless they are involved in the commission of the relevant offense in which case a Public Prosecution may be instituted.
(4) The Victim or appointed Proxy may request the Office of the Public Prosecutor to institute a Public Prosecution free of charge on their behalf in which case the Office of the Public Prosecutor shall be under obligation to institute such prosecution where evidence is sufficient, and in the event that they fail to do so, the victim shall not be barred from performing the prosecution themself or through a designated proxy.
(5) Where a Public Prosecution is instituted on behalf of the Victim or the Proxy, they shall have the right:
(a) to be notified about the schedule of the judicial proceedings;
(b) to receive a copy of all properly submitted discovery.
(c) to address the Civil or Criminal Court before the sentence is determined;
(b) to be advised of release from custody or escape of the defendant.

(1) To preserve and protect the right of crime victims to justice, to ensure crime victims a meaningful role in the criminal and juvenile justice systems, to accord crime victims due dignity and respect and to ensure that criminal and juvenile court delinquency proceedings are conducted to seek the truth as to the defendant's innocence or guilt, and also to ensure that a fair balance is struck between the rights of crime victims and the rights of criminal defendants in the course and conduct of criminal and juvenile court delinquency proceedings, the following rights are hereby granted to victims in all prosecutions for crimes and in juvenile court delinquency proceedings:
(a) The right to be present at and, upon specific request, to be informed in advance of any critical stage of the proceedings held in open court when the defendant will be present, and to be heard at the pretrial release hearing and the sentencing or juvenile court delinquency disposition;
(b) The right, upon request, to obtain information about the conviction, sentence, imprisonment, criminal history and future release from physical custody of the criminal defendant or convicted criminal and equivalent information regarding the alleged youth offender or youth offender;
(c) The right to refuse an interview, deposition or other discovery request by the criminal defendant or other person acting on behalf of the criminal defendant provided, however, that nothing in this paragraph shall restrict any other constitutional right of the defendant to discovery against the state;
(d) The right to receive prompt restitution from the convicted criminal who caused the victim's loss or injury;
(e) The right to have a copy of a transcript of any court proceeding in open court, if one is otherwise prepared;
(f) The right to be consulted, upon request, regarding plea negotiations involving any violent felony; and
(g) The right to be informed of these rights as soon as practicable.
(2) This Provision applies to all criminal and juvenile court delinquency proceedings pending or commenced on or after the effective date of this section. Nothing in this Provision reduces a criminal defendant's rights under the Constitution of Pacifica. Except as otherwise specifically provided, this Provision supersedes any conflicting section of this Constitution. Nothing in this section is intended to create any cause of action for compensation or damages nor may this section be used to invalidate an accusatory instrument, conviction or adjudication or otherwise terminate any criminal or juvenile delinquency proceedings at any point after the case is commenced or on appeal. Except as otherwise provided in subsections (3) and (4) of this Provision, nothing in this section may be used to invalidate a ruling of a court or to suspend any criminal or juvenile delinquency proceedings at any point after the case is commenced.
(3)(a) Every victim described in paragraph (c) of subsection (6) of this Provision shall have remedy by due course of law for violation of a right established in this section.
(b) A victim may assert a claim for a right established in this section in a pending case, by a mandamus proceeding if no case is pending or as otherwise provided by law.
(c) The Legislative Assembly may provide by law for further effectuation of the provisions of this subsection, including authorization for expedited and interlocutory consideration of claims for relief and the establishment of reasonable limitations on the time allowed for bringing such claims.
(d) No claim for a right established in this Provision shall suspend a criminal or juvenile delinquency proceeding if such a suspension would violate a right of a criminal defendant guaranteed by this Constitution or the Constitution of the United States.
(4) Upon the victim's request, the prosecuting attorney, in the attorney's discretion, may assert and enforce a right established in this Provision.
(5) Upon the filing by the prosecuting attorney of an affidavit setting forth cause, a court shall suspend the rights established in this Provision in any case involving organized crime.
(6) As used in this Provision:
(a) “Convicted criminal” includes a youth offender in juvenile court delinquency proceedings.
(b) “Criminal defendant” includes an alleged youth offender in juvenile court delinquency proceedings.
(c) “Victim” means any person determined by the prosecuting attorney or the court to have suffered direct financial, psychological or physical harm as a result of a crime and, in the case of a victim who is a minor, the legal guardian of the minor.
(d) “Violent felony” means a felony in which there was actual or threatened serious physical injury to a victim or a felony sexual offense.
(7) In the event that no individual person or number of them has been determined to be a [sole] victim of the crime, the people of Pacifica, represented by the prosecuting attorney, are considered to be the victims, so far as it meetes the criteria of natural Justice. In no event is it intended that the criminal defendant be considered the victim unless exonerating evidence of their innocence or which rightfully justifies their actions, and such accusation or procedure against the defendant caused measurable real damages to rights.

The judicial consulate presiding over a civil suit or criminal case is required to hear from the victim or their representative about what they think is an appropriate punishment, as is within the bounds of the limits of the law regarding the maximum penalty that may be prescribed, and it shall be a supreme consideration in the determination of sentencing handed down to the convicted upon their proper conviction by such judge of a court of proper jurisdiction by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve in accordance with due process under this Constitution.

A claimant alleging theft may file a civil action for damages based on the greater of the value of the stolen property at the time of taking, or the value at the time of report or filing, adjusted for inflation or deflation where the property stolen is money or other monetary value, and the filing or pendency of any criminal complaint, information, indictment, or prosecution shall not be required as a condition precedent to such civil action; likewise, the filing or pendency of any civil action shall not be required as a condition precedent to the initiation, investigation, charging, or prosecution of any criminal offense arising from the same conduct, and neither remedy shall be deemed to borrow, toll, suspend, or limit the other except as expressly provided by law.

Section. 10.15.

The Nation of Pacifica hereby recognizes that certain persons exist at heightened risk of harm, exploitation, coercion, neglect, or abuse by reason of age, disability, health condition, social marginalization, economic dependence, or structural power imbalance, and therefore affirms as a foundational duty of ordered liberty that the Nation shall enact and enforce laws to protect such persons from crime, to punish offenses committed against them with elevated penalties reflecting the gravity of the breach of trust and asymmetry of power involved, and to safeguard persons who, acting in good faith, reasonably and proportionately intervene to defend vulnerable persons from crimes including force, theft, fraud, or threats thereof, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this provision and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.

[]
For the purposes of this Section, a “vulnerable person” shall include, without limitation and in a non-exhaustive and inclusive construction: Children and young people, defined as persons under the age of majority and [?]those subject to State-supervised care or guardianship[?]; older adults and seniors, defined by statutory age threshold or by conditions of frailty, dependency, or social isolation; persons with physical disabilities, including impairments of mobility, vision, hearing, or chronic illness; persons with intellectual or developmental disabilities, including intellectual disability, autism, or cognitive impairment; persons with moderate to serious mental health conditions, including but not limited to delusional disorder, depersonalization in addition to derealization, disassociation, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depression, severe anxiety, or substance dependency disorders; persons who are homeless or experiencing unstable housing; persons who are economically disadvantaged, including those living in poverty or subject to economic dependence upon another; persons belonging to marginalized racial, ethnic, religious, or linguistic minorities, including Indigenous Peoples, or those subjected to hate crimes by them or for supporting them; migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, or displaced persons, those who assist them, and those oppressed or harmed by them; victims or survivors of violence, abuse, exploitation, or trafficking; persons who identify as []successful, apache helicopter, stable,[] HGTVBLTQAI+ or Straight/Hetero-Normative, either subjected to a hate crime or victimized for their support, both being recognized in the interest of equal protection in the law and no special rights or promoted classes; persons confined within institutions including prisoners, residents of psychiatric facilities, or persons in care homes; persons with remedial or low-levels of education, literacy, or significant language barriers; pregnant persons and unborn children; persons subject to material power imbalance including students, employees, or patients in relation to authority figures; and any other person who is demonstrably unable, whether temporarily or permanently, to adequately protect themselves from harm or exploitation, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this Section and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.
[]

Any offense committed against a vulnerable person, whether such vulnerability is actual or reasonably believed by the offender to exist, shall constitute an aggravating circumstance subjecting the offender to elevated penalties as prescribed by law, including enhanced terms of imprisonment, increased fines, and expanded civil remedies proportionate to the nature of the offense and the degree of vulnerability, and in determining sentence the courts shall consider the extent of the victim’s vulnerability, whether such vulnerability was knowingly targeted or exploited, the existence of any position of trust or authority, and any pattern or history of similar conduct, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this Section and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.

Recognition of vulnerability under this Section shall never be construed to justify discrimination, segregation, denial of equal protection of the laws, or diminution of equal dignity, autonomy, or personhood, and the Nation shall promote respectful language, inclusive policies, and protective practices in the Public Instrument that affirm the agency of vulnerable persons while ensuring their safety, all while not imposing standards of regular conduct upon Private parties, and no person acting in good faith and with necessary and sufficient means to defend a vulnerable person from imminent harm shall incur criminal or civil liability solely by reason of such protective action, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this Section and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.

The State Legislatures shall have power and duty to enact laws, and the Executive shall implement policies, necessary and proper to carry this Section into execution, including measures for risk identification, prevention, reporting, investigation, victim services, and remedies, including explicit statutory protections for persons who in good faith defend vulnerable persons, and the Nation shall establish or maintain independent bodies, including an ombudsperson or human rights authority, empowered to receive complaints, conduct investigations, and recommend corrective action, and shall further provide education, training, and public awareness programs concerning rights, obligations, consequences of offenses, and lawful protections afforded under this Provision, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this provision and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.

This Section shall be construed broadly and liberally in favor of the protection of vulnerable persons and those who lawfully and in good faith act to defend them, and nothing in this Section shall be construed to limit, deny, or impair any other right, remedy, or protection guaranteed by this Constitution, by the laws of the Nation, or by applicable principles of international human rights, provided that persons who have committed criminal acts shall not be shielded from liability through this Section and at no time shall the perpetrator be considered a victim based on these criteria.

Section 10.25

The criminal justice system shall practice restorative justice in criminal justice processes; Practices and programs reflecting restorative purposes shall respond to crime by identifying and taking steps to repair harm, involving all stakeholders, and, transforming the relationship between communities and their governments in responding to crime. The main focus of incarceration should be the rehabilitation of inmates, not releasing them before they are ready to be re-integrated to society.

Laws for the punishment of crime shall be founded on these principles: Protection of Civil Society, Personal Responsibility, Accountability for one’s Actions, Restoration for harm/s done, and Reformation.

Any person may file and/or Prosecute legitimate charges on behalf of themself, or with justification, for another [party], upon the presentation of sworn testimony and/or material evidence, without obstruction or delay.

No person shall be restricted in their liberty, nor deprived of any property, without first being at fault for the deprivation of another’s rights, or, a member of government in violation of the civil social compact of the constitution of their territory or state and/or this Constitution, and they must be tried before a civil or criminal court, and no court may proceed in secret, nor without right to writ of habeas corpus before a jury, neither without a jury trial available to the accused or defendant with the benefit of civil or legal counsel or a team of council as the accused/defendant needs and with the right to privacy under attorney-client privilege; No Person shall be convicted, sentenced, or imprisoned, under law, without first being presumed innocent [without inherent bias or deprivation of right at any point in trial], and thereafter be irrefragably proven through supplementation by irrefutable evidence to have denied or intended to deprive the equal right/s of another Person or other Persons, and only through due process of law, non-absentia, by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve. Sentences need not be excessive, but should be proportional and reflect upon the specific needs of protection for the public against criminal transgressors.
That no freeman ought to be taken, imprisoned, or disseized of his freehold, liberties, privileges, or franchises, or outlawed, or exiled, or in any manner destroyed or deprived of his life, liberty or property, but by the law of the land.

That every freeman ought to find a certain remedy, by recourse to the laws, for all injuries and wrongs he may receive in his person, property or character. He ought to obtain right and justice freely, without sale, completely and without denial, promptly and without delay; and that all establishments or regulations contravening these rights are oppressive and unjust.

Every individual shall have the right to receive prompt and adequate legal notification if any judicial order affecting their rights, responsibilities, or property has been re-instated, modified, or otherwise reactivated by any court or judicial authority. No judicial order shall bar the rightful owner from access to, use of, or possession of their property, except upon a finding by a court of competent jurisdiction, after due process and notice, that such restriction is necessary to prevent imminent harm or to enforce a lawful judgment. Any such restriction must be narrowly tailored and temporary, subject to regular judicial review. Failure to provide timely legal notification as required by this provision shall render any such judicial order unenforceable against the affected party until proper notice is given.

Section 10.5

Legislators must provide evidence establishing that lesser punishments will not satisfy penological objectives. Mandatory punishments are prohibited, except as may be directed by this Constitution. Courts must have discretion to alter punishments based on individual circumstances, except as may be repugnant to this Constitution. Crimes committed with the intention to violate or deprive another’s rights shall always be [punished] as felonies, otherwise, where evil intention is lacking as a mens rea, the crime shall be classified as a misdemeanor, except that which causes or results in death or serious physical injury, or as is laid forth otherwise by this Constitution and the statutes made in accordance therewith.

Federal, Territorial, State, or Local legislation shall set forth time frames whose periods prescribed consist a statute of limitations where affected parties must take action to enforce rights, seek penalties under law and seek redress after injury or damage; There shall be no statute of limitations on manslaughter, murder, treason, or terrorism, nor the attempts thereof, within Pacifica, but Ex Post Facto protections shall exist in all cases.

Federal, territorial, state, and local legislation shall establish defined statute of liability time periods within which an injured party must initiate action to enforce rights, seek restitution, and obtain redress for harm or damage. The liability period shall be unlimited in cases regarding injuries or damages caused by a public body or its agents. The period of liability shall begin at the moment of discovery in the [civil] injury or damage. Liability periods shall not be tolled on the basis that either the injured party or the alleged injuring party is unable to obtain legal representation. All prescribed periods shall be reasonable in duration and structured to ensure fair opportunity for redress while promoting timely resolution of claims. Retroactive protection from civil liability shall not exist for statutes of liability prescribed [in the time frame of the injury or damage caused] before the adoption of this Constitution.

The age of criminal responsibility in Pacifica shall be ten years old. Any Minor, defined as a person under eighteen years of age, who intentionally commits criminal homicide at age ten or older, may be charged as an adult, regardless of Minor Class Citizenship; In all cases, any person twelve years of age or older who intentionally commits criminal homicide shall be tried as an adult. Any Minor fourteen years of age or older who commits a felony may be charged as an adult; In all cases, any person sixteen years of age or older who commits a felony shall be tried as an adult. No statutory or customary minimum age shall bar the prosecution of an emancipated Minor as an adult, where such Minor has been lawfully granted full or partial emancipation; once emancipated, a Minor shall be held to legal accountability equivalent to that of any free and sovereign Person, without prejudice of age. Juvenile court has jurisdiction over offenses alleged to have been committed prior to a Minor’s eighteenth birthday; after age eighteen, the youth shall be charged in adult court. Juvenile court may retain jurisdiction over a youth until their eighteenth birthday, provided the offense occurred before turning eighteen. Minors of any age may be convicted of a crime, subject to the discretion of the victim or their lawful proxy to pursue prosecution. Every Minor accused of a crime has the right to a jury trial, to the assistance of counsel, and to have their parents or legal guardians and close family present and heard at all stages of the proceedings. A Minor convicted as an adult shall remain in juvenile justicial custody until their eighteenth birthday; Any remainder of sentence shall be served in an adult justicial facility until the sentence is fully served as handed down by the presiding judge. Death-in-prison sentences (life imprisonment without parole) may be imposed on Minor Class Citizens convicted of murder, provided they are above the minimum age of criminal responsibility for such offense. Mental deficiency shall not constitute an affirmative defense for relief from such sentence. Upon transfer to and conviction in adult criminal court, the jurisdiction of the juvenile court over any and all delinquent acts with which the Minor may then or thereafter be charged shall be relinquished; Priorly minor inmate or patient shall thereafter be treated as an adult for all pending and subsequent criminal charges. No law, regulation, or executive act shall infringe upon the unalienable rights of the People, including Minors, to due process including to Natural Justice, Jury trial, assistance of counsel, adherence to Corpus Delicti rule, legal process free from bias, and the right to be heard. All proceedings shall be conducted in accordance with the principles of common law and natural justice, with the presumption of innocence, right to confront accusers, right to challenge evidence, and the right to speedy and public trial guaranteed to all, regardless of age.

No Person shall have their physical liberty restricted unless pursuant to a decision of the Courts of Pacifica of the several States thereof, in the following circumstances:
(1) Upon a conviction in the Criminal Court by the Jury;
(2) Upon an Order of the Civil Court committing a violently offending Person lacking mental capacity to a mental health institution;
(3) Upon an Order of the Civil Court providing for further detention of a Resident Alien or Illegal Immigrant pending deportation proceedings;
(4) Upon a decision of any Court to commit any Person to jail for no more than seven days for a contempt of court committed either by disruption of judicial proceedings or by disobeying a Court order.
(5) Should such Person disobey the same order of a Court more than once, he or she shall be tried in a regular manner for a criminal offense as regulated by law and not limited to a seven-day imprisonment in jail.
(6) Nothing in this provision shall affect the powers of arrest, short-term detention of a Resident pending deportation proceedings, or sequestration of Jurors as enumerated in this Constitution.

The government is entirely prohibited from using medical/psychological treatments as a punishment, or as a condition of release, but this shall not prohibit the government from using psychological motivators and rewards based upon contingency to improve attitudes and outcomes of prisoners while held, nor from providing mechanisms of negative feedback to correct misbehavior by prisoners.

No Individual shall be compelled to identify theirself to any Agent of the Public Administration, unless upon valid arrest under warrant, detention under unassailable probable cause of a violation of the law, or, pursuant to enforcing a lawfully derived Civil or Criminal Court order or subpoena. Anybody providing ID for lawful verification purposes need only exhibit them to meet the criteria of compliance, and not be required that a copy be made.

[]
A lawful frisk or pat down is constitutionally limited to circumstances where there is reasonable and specifically articulable and sufficient detailed basis necessary to believe the person is armed and dangerous to non-aggressors, or within confinement inside an institution under lawful process to intercept unlawful contraband and prevent assault upon workers, inmates, and visitors or guests.
[]

Law enforcement are prohibited from expanding the scope of lawful interactions into matters unrelated to the lawful purpose of the interaction, including but not limited to probing whether the defendant possesses contraband, as well as their origin or destination.

All warrants and arrests shall be executed in a non-violent manner as is reasonably possible, using the minimum amount of force necessary, in preservation of health, bodily integrity, and life, and shall not injure People or animals, nor damage property, as much as humanly possible, in accordance with the mutual non-aggression principle.

No Person shall be detained without trial for more than twenty-four hours otherwise than in pursuit of a Warrant and no Warrants shall be issued, but upon [unassailable] probable cause, supported by appropriate order and unless it is absolutely necessary for the protection of others [whom are non-aggressors], and no detention in pursuit of such a Warrant shall be longer than it is absolutely necessary to bring an accused to trial.

No free man shall be taken or imprisoned, or be disseized of his Freehold, or Liberties, or free Customs, or be outlawed, or exiled, or any other wise destroyed, neither will we pass upon him, nor condemn him, but by lawful judgment of their countrymen, under the Law of the land as prescribed by this Constitution; No legal officer shall start proceedings against anyone on their own mere say-so, without reliable witnesses having been brought for the purpose; a person may not be subjected to any legal proceeding, such as arrest and imprisonment, without sufficient evidence having already been collected to show that there is a prima facie case to answer; This evidence must be collected beforehand, because it must be available to be exhibited in a public hearing within hours, or at the most days, after arrest, not months or longer as may happen in other jurisdictions that apply Napoleonic-inquisitorial criminal laws where evidence is commonly sought after a suspect’s incarceration; Any charge leveled at the hearing thus must be based on evidence already collected, and an arrest and incarceration order is not lawful if not supported by sufficient evidence.

All Warrants for the purposes of criminal proceedings shall be issued by a Judge of the Criminal Court upon request by an Agent of Law Enforcement and shall be supported by evidence of [unassailable] probable cause; such Warrants shall be as detailed as possible and shall refer to one Person only; every Warrant granted for a continuous action shall expire no later than after six months and may only be renewed by another Judge in accordance with ordinary procedure; any Person subject to a Warrant shall be informed without delay of its execution or, in case of a Warrant for a continuous action, once such Warrant has expired and is not renewed.

People have the right to be secure in their Persons, Personal and Private information/records which include but are not limited to medical and psychological information/records, papers, articles, properties and premises/homes, effects, location as well as network information, electronic and radio data (including but not limited to: Meta-data) as well as private communications, from [any and all] un-reasonable and un-warranted searches, seizures and storage; Nor shall any person be stopped or detained unreasonably, neither but upon unassailable probable cause, for the sole purpose of temporarily retaining them while a warrant may be secured to proceed in search or seizure; and no warrant to search any place, seize any person or thing, or access electronic/radio data or communications, shall issue without particularly describing the place to be searched, the person or thing to be seized, tracked, or put under surveillance, or the data or communication to be accessed or stored, as nearly as may be; nor without a modicum of credible evidence for which it is apparent that the accused has likely committed an offense against the rights of another person or against Pacifica and/or the [several] States (which evidence may include or be the statement of a witness sworn under oath by pain and penalty of law for its falsification by any measure or degree), which shall be presented to a judge of competent jurisdiction to provide authorization. Neither Congress nor the several States shall pass any law abridging or infringing the right of the People to encrypt their documents, effects, data, and communications. The People retain the Constitutional right to choose their own method/s of encryption and obscufication.
(mention "blanket search warrant" and "general warrant" as specifically delineated as prohibited to court power?)

No information pursued in an investigation or otherwise obtained through due process, may request access to and/or scan or search and/or seize, the neural pathways; which include but are not limited to the biological or electronic brain along with neuronal apparatus of an Individual; No warrant may be issued granting the government power to access, scan, search, seize, or otherwise interact with a personal (private) neuronet or Artificial Intelligence directly trained by the brain-machine interface, neuronal-machine interface, or electro/magneto/electromagnetic-physiological apparatus of an Individual.

10.666

Herein lie constitutionally dictated terms of warrant Search and Seizure provisions of the constitution, which even apply to all persons, including upon searching and Seizing from law enforcement or the Government at large, by will of the many or few who are so ass according to the interests of the Natural and Constitutional Laws, defend the Public from corruption:

No warrant is required for a search or seizure if consent is given by a person reasonably believed by an officer to have authority to give such consent upon the production of credible evidence proving such. Law enforcement may stop a suspect so long as there is a real and reasonable suspicion of a criminal act and the officer can articulate facts leading to that unassailable probable cause supported by a modicum of measurable evidence that a violation of the rights of another or a violation of due process has occurred, against the suspect before placing arrest, and be capable of and actually present such articulation before the Person whose rights are at risk of arrest upon the defendant’s request, with such evidence documented in a sufficiently non-tamperable and integrity verifiable manner, unless explanation is considered demonstrably unreasonable by unanimous agreement of the Jury due to exigent circumstance; If there is reason to believe that the person may be armed and demonstrably dangerous to Innocent Individuals, law enforcement can also frisk the suspect for detecting and removing weapons on their Person until they shall be returned to the rightful owner at a later time, as according to this Constitution and prescribed by law therewith. A search incident to lawful arrest under warrant does not require issuance of a search warrant in order to search the suspect’s person and immediate vicinity; If someone is lawfully arrested, the law enforcement may search their person and any area surrounding the person that is within reach (within their “wingspan”). No warrant is required to seize credible evidence in plain view if law enforcement are legitimately in the location from which the credible evidence can be viewed, except for that evidence which may be obtained from aerial- or space- -crafts, which itself in all cases requires a warrant to be lawfully photographed and/or searched by such device, but no time-craft may be deployed for any purpose whatsoever. A warrant is not required to search vehicles/crafts if law enforcement have unassailable probable cause, supported by a modicum of evidence, sworn in testimony or by an official statement under penalty of Death for Purgery, to believe the vehicle contains evidence of a crime, the instrumentalities of crime, contraband, or the fruits of a crime, whether the vehicle/craft is moving or already stopped. Evidence that can be easily moved, destroyed or otherwise made to disappear which is found while executing a lawful arrest warrant, before a search warrant can be issued, may be seized without a warrant, under [unassailable] probable cause for the necessity of the seizure alone, sworn in testimony or by an official statement, under penalty of Death for Purgery; Furthermore, if a suspect for a Felony enters private property other than their own lands and the domicile thereon, if while in hot pursuit by officers during a valid arrest, no warrant is required to enter that other property in order to continue pursuit, even if the suspect is in no way connected with the property owner, but absolute care and caution as well as clear and open communication must be provided for the occupants of that land, unless they are found to be accomplices to the crime/s.

Warrants can only be used to attain the fruits and instrumentalities of a crime, and to present them as evidence in a public prosecution against the accused, not as a dragnet surveillance tool, nor as a way to usurp [legitimate] property rights.

No warrant may be rightfully executed without presentation to the accused party and their given proper time to peacefully surrender to the authorities before they may forcefully arrest them as well as execute searches and seizures. This also means that "no knock" warrant executions are explicitly barred from execution.

A warrant is required for all searches and seizures, regardless of who or what is doing the search.

No level of government may introduce quotas to arrest individuals.

The People are to be protected by law and through the public process against/from surveillance of emanations from electric, magnetic, or electromagnetic sources, and against sweeping or scanning of homes, vehicles/craft, property, or person without a valid warrant being issued for the same.

There shall be no GPS tracking of Pacifican citizens without a warrant or lawfully-valid pre-trial release agreement for a fixed term.

No public or private person, corporation, partnership, association, or agent shall engage in dragnet surveillance of any person or class of persons, or in the mass collection, correlation, inference, retention, indexing, sale, licensing, transfer, sharing, querying, or use of location data, license-plate data, vehicle characteristics, device identifiers, radio-frequency data, Bluetooth data, Wi-Fi data, RFID data, telematics, cellular and network data, metadata, electronic emissions, association data, co-location data, convoy data, pattern-of-life data, or any aggregation, derivative, or functional equivalent thereof, whether by automatic license plate or biometric recognition, signal-intelligence augmentation, or any present or future analogous sensing, correlation, or inference system, except pursuant to a warrant issued upon unassailable probable cause, supported by oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the person, place, thing, data, communication, or class of narrowly identified targets to be searched, tracked, accessed, seized, stored, or surveilled; no warrant shall authorize general or blanket surveillance, retrospective mass querying, indefinite retention, or the collection of data concerning persons not individually suspected of an offense, and no private actor shall do indirectly, by contract, delegation, cooperation, resale, or technological architecture, that which the government may not do directly; provided, however, that systems which activate only upon an objectively dangerous and externally verifiable threshold, such as a speed-detection camera triggered solely by excessive speed creating actual danger, shall not be deemed prohibited by this section, so long as their use, disclosure, retention, and deletion comply with this Constitution; nothing herein shall prohibit lawful scientific experimentation, security testing, proof-of-concept attacks, or similar research conducted without trespass, fraud, unauthorized access, destruction, circumvention of justice, or other violation of the rights of others, and nothing herein shall be construed to authorize or excuse the abuse of such systems for political retribution, public shaming, discriminatory targeting, guilt by association, selective enforcement, or any other purpose contrary to the pursuit and aims of justice.
