The government may not, without a warrant obtained and limited as specified in this Constitution, purchase or otherwise obtain information about Pacifican Citizens from any non-government entities; Domestic electronic surveillance of any kind without a warrant (issued through onerous Due Process) is prohibited;

Occupants who have less than full rights over the premises can, through consent, give police the legal justification they need to search parts of a residence. For example, a roommate can give consent that allows the police to search her room, the living room, and the kitchen. But if she doesn’t have access to or control over her roommate’s separate bedroom, she can’t provide proper authorization for the police to search it. A primary resident of a home can give valid consent to a search that might implicate a guest who is temporarily staying there. But if the resident doesn’t have access to or use of the place or item to be searched, the consent is probably invalid. A person who doesn’t live in a home but who uses and has joint access to or control over parts of it can authorize the police to search those parts. But someone who is a mere guest generally doesn’t have authority to let the police snoop around. The question is whether police officers reasonably believe that someone who provides consent has normal access to and use of the parts of the house to be searched. consent to search a home that a housekeeper gives is invalid, because the housekeeper isn’t a resident of the home, they don’t use the home for their own purposes, and they have access to it only at the discretion of the homeowner. If the housekeeper lives in the home and authorizes the police to search only those parts of it that he or she has access to, then the search might be legitimate. In_General/On_Average, the more authority over the home or other domicile someone has, the greater the weight in their ability to admit somebody on the principle of good faith and trust between all parties lawfully-worthy of administering such permission to grant.

No Agent of the Public Administration shall operate undercover without a Warrant, and such Warrant shall specify the purposes for which it was issued; no Agent whilst executing a Warrant shall exceed the scope of the authority expressly granted therein, nor shall any Agent acting undercover use any method of entrapment to obtain evidence incriminating any Person; once the function for which the Warrant was issued has been carried into effect or abandoned, the Agent shall disclose to the Court issuing the Warrant a full report of all actions undertaken and evidence gathered whilst acting undercover; no evidence obtained pursuant to a Warrant permitting an Agent to act undercover shall be admissible against any Person unless the aforementioned report and all evidence is disclosed to that Person and to the Court.

10.75

Defendants may motion, and judges may grant such motions, or [judges] may decide upon themself, when it is without an abuse of discretion, that some or all charges against an individual or civil commitment action, to have the entire case be dismissed in the interests of justice (Ex Merito Justitiae), with such interest principally derived from the prerogatives of Society in their needs and interests for protection and the enjoyment of rights, when it is thought a defendant is otherwise to excessively or unfairly/unjustly charged; Or if the punishment does not meete the alleged or actually committed crime for which one faces a criminal or civil verdict. The conditions and terms by which one may be dismissed Ex Merito Justitiae shall be set by the Jurisdiction of the People, as in "We the People", having lawful authority over the court.

No person accused or accuser in any criminal proceeding shall be deprived of liberty without being provided the benefit of a trauma‑informed jury, duly instructed in the scientific understanding of trauma, including its neurobiological effects such as hypervigilance, post‑traumatic stress, and battered person syndrome; and juries shall be required to evaluate all acts alleged as aggression or self‑defense in the full context of the individual’s lived experience of threat, coercion, discrimination, or rights intimidation, wherein it shall be recognized that defendants may in truth be victims of prior or continuing aggression, repression, or injustice, and that the protection of self, others, or inherent rights against violation shall not be construed as criminal. Courts shall therefore admit evidence of trauma and relational threat patterns as prima facie justification where relevant, and any conviction rendered without observance of these standards shall be presumptively invalid, subject to immediate review and restoration of rights; and justice under this Constitution shall be understood to be restorative in nature, grounded in the factual equity of circumstances rather than abstraction or presumption.

The accused awaiting trial and those convicted of criminal charge, or those awaiting or condemned by civil action on account of their mental illness, have the rights to access media such as print, CD-ROM, flash drive; to write, to the press; to print; to entertainment; and to free communicate, including but not limited to paper and pen, by radio, and through the internet/interwebs and computer programs. This right includes the right to word processing and image manipulation,

There shall be a “5 strikes, indeterminate sentence automatically without deference” applying to “person felonies”.

Body camera recordings become public information at the conclusion of any trial or any resolution by the court. Courts are ordered through this constitution to release case discovery to the general public at least 14 business days before the Trial is scheduled to begin, after all hearings and evidentiary suppression reviews by the citizen's court. Body cams are not subject to censoring, and must be revealed after a case concludes, no matter the verdict of not guilty (innocent/blameless), guilty (injurer/liable), or no contest (neither accepting blame nor rejecting guilt), or the suppression of evidence for a trial. Information properly classified which is made available through body camera footage at time of criminal, civil, or familial/parental-custody/kid-protection court proceedings by a citizen’s bench and citizen’s jury must not be censored for the purpose of State security or other ends.

The defendant has the right to opt for their trial to be recorded in Audio+Video, and documents scanned as well as downloads or cloud-files made available, and to receive all discovery, hearings, trials, habeas corpus, appeals, and any other court matters, provided in a long-term-storage format, such as upon LTO-tape/s or Millennium-Disk/s, at the end of court proceedings.

Judges shall have the discretion to set conditions for pretrial release, including monetary bail or release on personal recognizance, based on an individualized assessment of each case. In exercising this discretion, judges may consider the seriousness of the offense charged, the defendant’s criminal history, the risk of flight, and the potential risk to public safety. No condition of pretrial release shall be imposed more restrictively than necessary to reasonably ensure the defendant’s appearance in court and the safety of the community, consistent with the presumption of innocence and the right to liberty. All decisions regarding pretrial release shall be subject to prompt judicial review upon request by the defendant or their counsel. All pretrial release decisions are subject to habeas corpus upon the request of the defendant or their legal counsel.

Probates and Parolees shall be afforded with reasonable accommodations, as needed, such as if there is an exigent circumstance that prevents them from making it to work on time or keeping their job, et cetera.

Inmates shall be segregated by criminal conviction, behavior, as well as previous institutional behavior and more recent history as well, and be granted privileges based on the level and length of good or bad behavior. Inmates have the right to be protected from assault or other forms of abuse by fellow wards. The purpose of segregation is to ensure the safety and security of all inmates and of detention staff.

Both defendants and prosecutors shall have the opportunity for equal time to be given for questioning and to present arguments, and to not be denied time on account of the other party choosing not to use theirs.

Evidence must conform to a number of rules and restrictions to be admissible, or disposed of after trial, as to be prescribed by law.

The fabrication of evidence presented to a court of law shall be a high crime. Preparing, planting, or presenting fabricated evidence shall, in all circumstances, be felonious.

A plaintiff who makes false accusatory statements to an official or otherwise manufactures charges, shall be held criminally liable, for equal to or more than the penalty that would have been handed down otherwise had the accused actually been found guilty and given the maximum punishment, and the [victimized] defendant shall be eligible for the charges against them to be dropped, expunged, or pardoned. An individual giving testimony who knowingly makes false statements to an official or otherwise gives false information or produces ‘manufactured’-evidence, shall be held criminally liable, for equal to or more than the penalty that would have been handed down otherwise. In both cases, the penalty for either shall be the same, and as shall be proscribed by law.

No Person shall be subject to the determination of guilt based on the testimony of another Person’s feelings, religious/spiritual convictions, or dreams.

Where evidence is found to be illegally obtained, those who obtained such evidence shall be subjected to criminal prosecution.

Investigations and trials shall be limited to the relevant facts and related evidence surrounding each individual case.

In civil and criminal cases, the burden of proof lies upon him who affirms an injury, not upon him who denies one; since, by the nature of things, he who denies a fact cannot produce any proof.

The prosecution is required to disclose to a criminal defendant at their request all evidence that is material to guilt or to punishment; Prosecutors have a constitutional duty to disclose to the court and to the defendant “all significant evidence suggestive of innocence or mitigation,” both during a trial and after conviction; Exculpatory evidence found by witnesses, law enforcement, or the court, must be presented, documented, and examined, and the defendant exonerated.

No person shall be denied standing to privately prosecute a public right for at least declaratory or injunctive relief, even if he or she has not incurred, or does not expect, personal injury resulting from the failure to grant such relief.

No Person shall be held to answer for a capital, or otherwise infamous crime, unless on a presentment or indictment of a Grand Jury, except in cases arising in the Military, when in actual service in time of War or public danger.

Absent evidence of a defendant’s misconduct affecting the integrity of the initial judicial process, a defendant will have double jeopardy protection against a particular charge whenever a Jury deliberates and is unable to agree upon conviction unanimously.

All Persons held by any Agent or any body of the Public Administration against their will under any circumstances whatsoever shall have the right to petition the Criminal Court for a writ of habeas corpus.

An accused who does not speak the language in which the civil or criminal proceedings are conducted shall be provided without expense with the services of an interpreter.

A Defendant may choose to be forwarded to another attorney of their choice if necessary for an alternative legal opinion or course of legal defense.

An attorney’s first duty is toward their client/s, and not to the courts and the public, with exception of the Attorney General, whose highest duty is to the People [as their client]. The commencement and continuance of a Person with an Attorney to counsel, guide, or represent them, shall not [in itself] render the client a ward of the court.

Legal professional privilege and common interest doctrine shall be prescribed by law.

Work-product doctrine shall be prescribed by law.

The ability of an inmate to communicate to an attorney in confidence/privilege, appeal, petition, and their right to vote, shall not be restricted, denied, suspended, abridged, obstructed, infringed/impacted/impaired, or otherwise compromised.

The right to appeal never ends, nor may it be denied, though it may be moderated to ensure all other interested appealing Persons get their cases weighed; and though Appeals may fail, another may always follow after.

The law shall define and ensure adequate protection of the secrecy of legal proceedings, in the interest of protecting Victims as well as Offenders from defamation and threats against them.

In order to guarantee the principle of equity, the law shall regulate the cases when justice shall be free of cost.

The law shall establish a procedure so that the detained may request the court to decide about the lawfulness of the detention. Likewise the law shall establish the procedure to restore the impaired fundamental rights of any Person under detention.

Prosecutors may not seek higher Penalties, nor may Judges impose higher Penalties, when Defendants exercise their Right to a jury Trial.

It is considered a form of genocide, and unlawful, for a ward to tamper with sexual reproductivity or to maim or injure the gonadic functions of prisoners.

There shall be co-ed, consensual romantic relationship compatible, and conjugal housing for inmates/patients, with family options for [their] kids up to the age of 14 (fourteen), then they must either be transferred to a relative or legal guardian, or curator over their pupilship [as according to the Roman civil and Familial law otherwise in conformity to this constitution and interoperating with the laws made underneath it in accordance to its principles], unless they are emancipated at or before that time.

No law shall retroactively change the legal consequences or status of actions or omissions that have been already committed, or relationships that already existed, before the enactment of said law.

No Person shall be subject for the same offense to be twice put in jeopardy of a penalty.

Any question of which court, National, State, or Local, shall have jurisdiction, shall be decided by a grand jury of citizens selected at random, if possible, from outside the jurisdictions of the courts in contention.

In all suits of law, the right of trial by jury shall be preserved, and no fact tried by a jury, shall be otherwise re-examined in any Court of Pacifica, than according to the principles and rules under this Constitution, and of the Roman Civil Law except as may be directed otherwise by this Constitution, or if neither, prescribe a course or remedy, as according to the customs of Common Law, Contract law (under Pacifican Principles), or in none such case, as according the legal customs of United States law as under to the Articles of Confederation except as may be provided otherwise by the 1787CE Constitution of the United States, and additionally through the Bill of Rights of 1789CE, as it was originally proposed.

No Person shall be unreasonably impeded from access to a randomly selected grand jury of twenty-four, who, if they should return an indictment or presentment, may appoint that Person, ‘the accuser’, or any other to prosecute the case, and shall decide which court, if any, has jurisdiction, and whether any Person shall have official immunity from suit.

In all trials in which there are mixed questions of law and fact, including all criminal jury trials, and all jury trials in which government officials or agents, whether general, State, or Local, shall be a party, parties shall have the right not to have decisions by the bench on questions of law made before all arguments can be made before the jury, excepting only arguments on defense motions in limine that cannot be made without disclosing evidence properly excluded. Jurors shall receive copies of all applicable constitutions, statutes, court precedents, and legal arguments, including those of Intervenors and amici curiae, and access to an adequate law library in which they can do research with available training, and legal assistant attorneys on select days of the week.

All defendants in civil and criminal proceedings shall have the right to attend Court proceedings, to be informed of the civil liabilities or criminal charges and of their rights, to compel accusors and witnesses to appear in Court for examination, and to examine all evidence gathered against them, including any information which has been classified as a State secret should the Prosecution wish to employ such evidence; in such cases, the proceedings shall take place in camera and all Persons involved shall take an oath of secrecy for the period the relevant information remains [justifyably] classified.

All defendants in civil or criminal or any other innovational-category [in pursuit of Justice] proceedings shall have the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty and to not be compelled to be a witness against himself or herself, or such other Persons as may be prescribed by law, without any negative inference; the Prosecution shall at all times carry the legal burden of proof, discharged beyond reasonable doubt, in relation to the defendant’s liability or guilt, including disproving any defense envisaged by the law which they might raise; nothing in this provision shall prevent the creation of defenses which require the defendant to discharge the evidential burden of proof by raising the issue of defense available to them. The accused have the right at all times [including after conviction] to attain and present exonerating evidence where available and to subpoena for evidence when it is not immediately available to them, without obstruction or delay;-and be it said that exhausting available evidence of innocence is not in itself proof of guilt.

The right to release from custody, prior to conviction through irrefragable proof supplemented by irrefutable evidence, is a clear and important liberty interest. Pre-trial detention is permitted only upon the government showing, by clear and convincing [objective] evidence, that the defendant poses a serious risk of flight or threat of substantial criminal wrongdoing. Pre-trial release conditions shall be narrowly tailored to secure attendance at trial or the prevention of crime. Only State agents may assess and administer financial sureties; and counsel for the indigent shall be available prior to any determination of pre-trial detention.

A defendant’s lack of knowledge shall be a reasonable excuse to pardon them from their behavior when the infraction, violation, or crime in question, was “malum prohibitum”, or “bad because its prohibited”, in such cases where an infraction, violation, or crime has no direct victim or harmed individual, as may be permitted by law for the government to establish under this Constitution, such as for violations surrounding the rules of the road.

All accusations must be possible to be proved through irrefragable proof supplemented by irrefutable evidence, and must be proven so in a court of law to have any effect or ordinance, and false accusations which as a direct result lead to the deprivation of any rights in another, shall always be punished as a felony; failure to prove an accusation irrefragably with irrefutable proof, before a court shall be evidence enough of its falsehood, and unless it can be proven at a later date to in fact be true through evidence directly tangential to the facts the accusation is based upon, it shall be upheld as inference of innocence and absolve the accused of punishment.

No person shall be subjected to a legal proceeding that is designed or used as a tool for political retribution, public shaming, or to suppress dissenting speech. All trials must be conducted with impartiality, ensuring the defendant’s right to a fair hearing free from bias, political pressure, or public spectacle. The imposition of damages or penalties intended to punish speech or suppress unpopular opinions rather than remedy actual, demonstrable harm shall be prohibited. The right of every individual to express opinions, including critical, unpopular, or even offensive views about public events, government narratives, or official accounts, shall be inviolable. Expression questioning or disputing any narrative shall not be grounds for civil or criminal penalties absent direct incitement to violence or unlawful action. The state shall not impose liability or damages as a tool for silencing or financially debilitating such expression, no matter how distressing or controversial. No court shall award damages or impose penalties that function as a tool of political or ideological suppression, including punitive damages disproportionately exceeding actual harm. Remedies in civil litigation shall be limited to compensatory damages strictly correlated to verified harm. Trials and judgments must not be weaponized to bankrupt, censor, or silence individuals for their protected speech or beliefs. The liberty to speak, question, and pursue truth in conscience constitutes a natural right independent of government sanction. The state shall never abridge these rights on grounds of national emergency, public sensitivity, or political expediency. The pursuit of justice demands protecting both popular and unpopular speech equally. Any person subjected to unfair or politicized legal actions under these protections shall have assured access to independent courts to seek immediate relief, including injunctions to halt such proceedings and remedies for wrongful punitive action. Courts found to violate these principles shall face appropriate sanction to uphold rule of law and justice.

No person accused of a crime shall be compelled, whether by warrant, court order, or otherwise, to disclose any mental health or psychiatric records without the voluntary, informed, and explicit consent of the accused. Any attempt by the government to obtain mental health or psychiatric records of an accused without such consent shall be presumed unconstitutional and inadmissible as evidence in any civil or criminal proceeding. The accused shall have the exclusive right to waive or assert this protection, and no waiver shall be implied or presumed by silence or failure to disclose. Exceptions to this protection may only be established by a clear and convincing standard of judicial review, ensuring strict scrutiny, and shall require that any compelled disclosure is narrowly tailored, strictly necessary, and the least intrusive means to serve a compelling state interest such as immediate threat to life or public safety. Any violation of this Provision by law enforcement, prosecutors, or courts shall result in the exclusion of the improperly obtained mental health evidence and may expose responsible parties to civil and criminal penalties, including damages and professional disciplinary actions, in addition to charges related to the violation of the defendant's rights.

In all things/cases, whether or not they are punitive damages, it will be: [that] Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor excessive terms of incarceration, nor any other excessive form of criminal punishment, nor torturous, cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing, or unusual treatments or punishments inflicted. No person arrested, or confined in jail/prison/asylum, shall be treated with unnecessary rigor.

Offences, except murder, and treason, shall be bailable by sufficient sureties or releasable upon personal recognizance. Murder or treason, shall not be bailable or releasable upon personal recognizance, when the proof is evident, or the presumption strong.

All penalties shall be proportioned to the offense. In all criminal cases whatever, the jury shall have the right to determine the law and whether or not a compelling interest of Justice is being served by the law, and the facts under the direction of the Court as to the law, and the right of new trial, as in civil cases.

Forfeiture of property or estate, indefinite imprisonment, and un-reasonable detention of accusers and witnesses are forbidden.

There shall be proportionality of punishment for a crime and in the severity of forfeiture of property or estate for the magnitude of a felony, weighing on an individual basis given the facts and circumstances under which a crime took place, fitting a specific punishment to serve the needs of the community for protection against recidivism while at the same time without applying excessive punishments, et cetera…, to achieve reasonable outcomes for the equal interests of both the convicted and their victims. No person charged with a crime shall be compelled to pay costs before a judgment of conviction has become final. A person not found guilty of a crime shall not be assessed fees or costs to recover property seized as evidence or otherwise held, impounded, or stored by the government.

No torturous, cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing, excessive, or unusual treatment or punishment shall be inflicted by any Agent or Member of any branch of the Public Administration or under the supervision or approval thereof against any Person; nor shall any Person be rendered to any State or group should there be a reasonable suspicion that the aforementioned may inflict such treatment on such Person; nor shall any experiments, medical or otherwise, be conducted against any Person without their express and informed consent; no Individual shall be medically examined or otherwise tested unless pursuant to a Warrant or with the Individual’s express and informed consent.

The prohibition on the torturous, cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing, excessive, or unusual treatment or punishment requires that neither the State nor the National government shall impose the death penalty, except upon members of the Government who violate the limitations imposed upon them by the constitution, or commence in some other form of treason; nor place individuals in prolonged solitary confinement. Furthermore, no person, whether citizen or not, and whether held awaiting trial, convicted, or in detention for other reasons, shall be subjected to cruel, unusual, excessive, or degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing treatment that violates human dignity or is degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing to mental health. When determining whether such a breach is or has taken place, all branches of the government shall consider continually improving [and procedurally-evolving] standards, both national and international, of human decency.

The death penalty shall be abolished throughout Pacifica, except in cases of treason by the government of Pacifica, any State, Territory, or other Jurisdiction therein, including, but not limited to abuses of expressed Authority and exercised powers, as well as them violating any provision or precept espoused within it, even when solely in error or directed by misinformation. Members of the government shall, in all cases of treason, such as violating any clause of the constitution, such as but not limited to when they unjustly injure or kill another by their or the direction of someother’s actions, then they shall be put to death by execution, there through either, or a combination of, hanging, death by firing squad, lethal injection, or DC electric chair. executions of governmental members for treason shall be public and broadcast on live TV. The executions will be made available on parental content-control locked over-the-air radio digital TV, internet streaming public-access cable and public-access satellite TV as free offerings.

In civil and criminal cases, the People shall have the right to the following:
(1) to a speedy and public case and fair trial;
(2) to fair trial by an impartial jury composed of twelve Citizens; In all criminal prosecutions, the accused shall enjoy the right to a speedy and public case and fair trial, by an impartial jury of the State and district wherein the crime shall have been committed, which district shall have been previously ascertained by law; in any event, no Person shall be convicted of a criminal offense later than a year after a Warrant permitting the detention of such Person was executed in connection with that offense; should said Person escape or allegedly commit any subsequent criminal offense, a new Warrant for custody may be issued.
(3) to be informed of nature and cause of the accusation. No Person shall be arrested or detained without being at once informed of the charges against him or without the immediate privilege of counsel; nor shall they be detained without adequate cause; and upon demand of any Person such cause must be immediately shown in open court in their presence and the presence of their counsel;
(4) to confront accusors and witnesses and to compel accusors and witnesses to appear in court;
(5) to the assistance of legal counsel free of charge where appropriate. All Persons held against their will by the Public Administration under any circumstances whatsoever shall have the right to be assisted by effective legal counsel and an interpreter, should they not speak the language of interrogation or court proceedings, and in case of trial, to have reasonable time for the preparation of their case; services of a counsel and an interpreter shall be contracted personally or, in criminal proceedings where a Person is not able to afford it, they shall be provided by the Secretary of the Judiciary with the possibility to subsequently recover reasonable expenses should a defendant be convicted and the verdict not be overturned by the Supreme Court.;
(6) to be presumed innocent until proven guilty;
(7) not to be compelled to be a witness against himself or herself;
(8) not to be disabled in the exercise, or deprived, of Life and Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security and Self-defense, Privacy, Property, or the pursuit of Happiness, without first being irrefragably proven through supplementation of irrefutable evidence to have denied or intended to deprive the equal right/s of another Person or other Persons, and only through due process of law.
(9) In all prosecutions, the accused shall have the right to public case and fair trial by an impartial jury in the county in which the offense shall have been committed; to be heard by himself and counsel; to demand the nature and cause of the accusation against him, and to have a copy thereof; to meet the witnesses face to face, and to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in his favor; provided, however, that any accused person, in other than capital cases, and with the consent of the trial judge, may elect to waive trial by jury and consent to be tried by the judge of the court alone, such election to be in writing; provided however, that they shall only be found guilty by unanimous verdict, and not otherwise; provided further, that the existing laws and constitutional provisions relative to prosecutions shall be continued and remain in effect as to all prosecutions for crimes committed before the taking effect of this amendment.
(10) In all prosecutions, the accused shall have the right to fair public trial by an impartial jury in the county in which the offense shall have been committed; to be heard by himself and counsel; to demand the nature and cause of the accusation against him, and to have a copy thereof; to meet the witnesses face to face, and to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in his favor; provided, however, that any accused person, in other than capital cases, and with the consent of the trial judge, may elect to waive trial by jury and consent to be tried by the judge of the court alone, such election to be in writing; provided however, that they shall only be found guilty by unanimous verdict, and not otherwise; provided further, that the existing laws and constitutional provisions relative to prosecutions shall be continued and remain in effect as to all prosecutions for crimes committed at any time.
(11) Defendants have the right to be served justice by a fully informed jury, who know all of their Rights, Powers, Duties, and Responsibilities, as well as who are learned and understand all basic legal rules and procedures as well as definitions, and whom know all relevant laws and case rulings, as they are applicable to the case at hand.

(a) Personalized detention & treatment plan for prisoners;
(b) Communicate freely in person and by reasonable access to telephones;
(c) Send and receive sealed mail and packages, except that this right may be limited for security reasons in state institutions as prescribed by law through the Legislature of the Relevant Jurisdiction;
(d) Wear the clothing of the person;

(j) Be represented by counsel whenever the rights of the inmate/patient may be affected;
(k) Petition for a writ of habeas corpus in addition to Jurial inquestry and Jurial review;
(l) Not be required to perform routine labor tasks of the facility except those essential for treatment;
(m) Be given reasonable compensation for all work performed other than personal housekeeping duties;
(n) Daily access to fresh air and the outdoors, except that this right may be limited when it would create significant risk of harm to the person or others;
(o) Reasonable privacy and security in resting, sleeping, dressing, bathing, personal hygiene and toileting, except that this right may be limited when it would create significant risk of harm to the person or others;
(p) Such other rights as may be specified by rule; and
(q) Exercise all civil rights in the same manner and with the same effect as one not admitted to the facility, including, but not limited to, the right to dispose of real property, execute instruments, make purchases, enter contractual relationships, and vote, unless the person has been adjudicated incompetent and has not been restored to legal capacity. Disposal of personal property in possession of the person in a state institution is subject to limitation for security reasons.

(2) A person must be immediately informed, orally and in writing, of any limitation:
(A) Of the right to send or receive sealed mail, after security screening;
(B) Regarding the disposal of personal property;
(C) Of the right to reasonable privacy and security in resting, sleeping, dressing, bathing, personal hygiene and toileting under subsection (1)(o) of this provision; and
(D) Of the right to daily access to fresh air and the outdoors under subsection (1)(n) of this provision.
(E) Any limitation under this provision and the reasons for the limitation must be stated in the person’s written punishment or treatment plan.
(F) The person has the right to challenge any limitation under this provision pursuant to rules adopted by the institutional authority. The person must be informed, orally and in writing, of this right.
(G) An incarcerated person shall have the right to be free from potentially unusual or hazardous treatment procedures, including convulsive therapy, unless the person has given express and informed consent. An incarcerated person may not be subjected to psychosurgery.

Upon the lawful release of any individual from detention, whether from a county jail, prison, penal institution, or mental health asylum within Pacifica or the several states, that person shall cease to be an inmate and shall be restored to full liberty without delay, and it shall be the duty of the Sheriff and the Sheriff’s Deputies to prepare the person for discharge, permit the person, at the person’s election, to consume the last available meal of the day provided through the sheriff’s station or the institution’s kitchen before departure, or to be discharged immediately upon request, and, at the moment of release, to ensure that all lawful personal belongings, earned wages for labor performed, and official discharge documents are delivered in full. We say all this because we are the government [!], and we are here to help!”

Convicted criminals shall not have their liberty restricted except so far as is necessary for the protection of others [whom are non-aggressors], nor their lawfully derived property seized, except so far as it is necessary to make restitution to the victim and/or to pay the costs of the criminal’s capture, trial, and housing, or, if it was procured through, or is the gains from, criminal activity or enterprise, but only in the case that they are convicted of a crime through due process of law, by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve in a court of law of proper jurisdiction. Limitations or restrictions on the exercise of any of a Person’s rights can only be lawfully enacted and enforced if the Individual is currently [lawfully] incarcerated, on parole or probation, or is subject to a court order restricting specific rights or their modalities for the protection of others [whom are non-aggressors].

All confined persons, whether held for psychiatric treatment or criminal confinement, shall retain their inherent human dignity, individual autonomy, and full measure of rights except where a restriction is demonstrably necessary, narrowly tailored, and supported by a specific clinical, custodial, or security justification, and the default rule shall be liberty rather than institutional control. Every confined person shall have a constitutional right to participate, through a democratic and participatory process, in the planning, scheduling, administration, and fair distribution of unit activities and shared resources, and the institution shall maintain regular meetings between residents and staff for the purpose of developing and revising an activity plan that is orderly, transparent, therapeutically or developmentally appropriate, and safe. Every confined person shall have access, as reasonably available, to a broad range of lawful recreational, educational, social, restorative, and health-promoting activities, including exercise, physical recreation, music listening or making/mixing/mashing, education, home economics, cooking groups, structured leisure, video games, shared movies, shared television time, radio, computer time, and other approved individual or group activities, including private sensory-room or equivalent individualized sessions when clinically or operationally appropriate. The institution shall maintain an advance sign-up system for approved activities, and confined persons shall have the right to reserve slots up to ten days in advance, with the list administered by a designated staff member and subject to supervisory approval in accordance with a democratically developed unit agreement. Access to shared activities and equipment shall be allocated fairly in proportion to the population served by each unit, and no person shall be favored or disfavored on the basis of conformity, social proximity to staff, perceived cooperativeness, or informal status. No confined person shall be coerced into participating in any activity, nor punished, stigmatized, or subjected to adverse documentation for declining, requesting, or pursuing a lawful therapeutic or recreational activity, provided the conduct remains reasonable and non-disruptive. Clinical notes, disciplinary processes, and institutional records shall not be used as instruments of retaliation, compulsion, or behavioral punishment, but only for legitimate clinical, custodial, and safety/security purposes. No confined person shall be subjected to collective punishment, generalized sanctions, or group-based retaliation for the conduct, dispute, complaint, or alleged misconduct of any other individual, and accountability shall remain strictly personal, not collective, except to the extent that a specific and individualized security necessity plainly requires otherwise. Any limitation, postponement, or suspension of an activity shall be individualized, temporary, and no broader than necessary to address a concrete risk to safety, security, or orderly administration, and temporary staffing shortages may justify restriction only when they are genuine, documented, and not employed as a recurring pretext for denying ordinary liberties. Every confined person shall have the right to assert grievances, challenge restrictions, complain about staff conduct, and seek review of denials or retaliation without reprisal, and the institution shall provide a prompt, neutral, and meaningful review process for such claims. This Provision shall be construed in favor of individual liberty, equal treatment, free exercise of ordinary human behavior, and the least possible institutional interference compatible with legitimate safety and security requirements.

Felons or Misdemeanants, upon completion of their sentence, and the mentally ill, upon completion of the term of their Civil Commitment, are to be fully respected in all of their rights/immunities, and restored in all privileges they had priorly without then having impact of their prior criminal history prejudice their present and future from there;-[and] No law shall bar a Person from the exercise and enjoyment of their rights because of a prior conviction or commitment on account of the nature from which such criminal or civil action was undertook, but in a manner which is according to this provision, they shall no longer be laid to bar for the rights/immunities or privileges which may have come into question based on their Prior Criminal or Mental Health history or condition. This provision may not be abrogated by any amendment as it is a core republican virtue that Felons, Misdemeanants, and the Mentally Ill are still a part of the People from which they came; and no usurpation of their rights, including to physical and mental autonomy, shall ever then have force or affect and effect of law, no matter what. Any limitation of rights while serving for criminal action or civil ruling must be individually weighed and passed down, and all such limitations are challengeable on the grounds that they are not necessary to affect and effect the interests of the constitutionally directed needs of "the State".

Neither Pacifica nor any state shall deprive any organization, institution, business, company, firm, corporation, or other artificial entity of property, without first showing by irrefragable proof supplemented by irrefutable evidence that the entity has or intended to deny or intended to deprive the equal right/s of another Person or other Persons, and only through due process of law, non-absentia, by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve; nor deny any organization, institution, business, company, firm, corporation, or other artificial entity the equal protection of laws applicable to other organizations, institutions, businesses, companies, firms, corporations, or other artificial entities similarly situated.

There shall be no imprisonment for debt, except in case of fraud or absconding debtors.

A Person shall not be determined to be an unprivileged enemy belligerent or be detained without fair trial by an impartial jury; no Individual may be detained under criminal charges without fair trial by impartial jury, under the third Geneva Convention’s Articles relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War, who are determined as Individuals hostile against Pacifica or its coalition partners in which an Individual has engaged, or which the Individual has purposely and materially supported, are subjects consistent with the law of war, and any authorization for the use of military force provided by Congress, pertaining to such hostilities.

No Person shall be detained or interrogated by any Agent of the Pacifican or several state Public Administration outside the jurisdiction of Pacifica or their State.

Inmates in jail or prison shall have medical, psychological, and educational services available to them under the inmate’s consent. The Government may at its or the People’s discretion, require by law all inmates to take a natural rights, natural justice, and civil government educational training course for up to eight hours each day, five days a week, with no pay or other form of compensation nor waiver or other benefit provided, except as a part of their progress to benchmarking for their rehabilitative programme.

All prisons and asylums will have fresh warm liver available to inmates in their cell at all times [unless denied], though they may not need to replace the liver until it is no longer edible, and microwave-ovens may be added to cells to prolong warmth of the liver if there is not a proven security or safety risk or undue likelyhood of unreasonable damage beyond normal wear-and-tear to the supplied equipment.

Inmates may request sexual expression supplies such as rubber-chickens, flashlights, or phallic/[smooth]-shaft-like objects, suitable hypoallergenic condoms and/or gloves, sufficient lubricant, maximum-strength hand sanitizer, and appropriate salad dressing and/or hot-sauce or jelly and/or peanut butter and/or syrup and/or creamer/half-n-half, as well as a handkerchief and/or blindfold, in addition to a single cigarette and a light/warmth-source/fire-lick per personal intimate session, with instant coffee available at cost.

Inmates in jail or prison shall have available to them a library of law provided by the State or Federal warden institution and among the documents available to them shall be the constitutions and Laws of the world and across history.

No private warden institution may manage inmates nor open a prison-mate labor camp. Management of inmates and prison institutions are turned over to the Individual powers of the Union or the States, respectively. Management of inmates and prison institutions by the States must be run in a not-for-revenue fashion.

Detainment camps/centers for those non-citizens who have been charged through due process with violating the laws of the Union, or for those who are captured enemies of war, are permissible, so long as their operation does not violate the human rights of the detained, nor violate this Constitution and the rights guaranteed therein. Internment and concentration camps/centers are specifically prohibited.

It shall be a right of the convicted to call evidence and witnesses into court which may exonerate them of the allegation/s or criminal conviction/s against them, and if they prevail, to be repaid for the value for time lost and suffering, as is already the case for imprisonment in error, not to be less than the same value of a living wage for 24-Hour period each day, and for which trauma the value of compensation shall be decided by a civil jury.

All punitive measures must be specifically tailored in their punishment for the offender and crime which they have committed, crafted to achieve the most efficient and effective protection to the public while being the least restrictive to the convicted.

Contrition by malnutrition or use of foul foods as meals is strictly prohibited and a criminal offense against the prisoner. Foods and meals must be wholesome, nutritious, balanced, and complete. Wardens cannot prohibit foods like garlic which can have a strong smell, or fruit which may be fermented as contraband.

We the Citizens of Pacifica re-affirm that after the convicted serve their sentence, they have paid their dues to society and upon their release should be fully restored in all of their rights/immunities, freedoms, privileges, or guarantees along with their naturally acquired [just] powers and capacities, as secured under this Constitution, and to which privileges they are still eligible for, and not to be excluded from them on account or basis of their legal history/record; We the People re-emphasize that if a criminal is determined to not yet be ready for release and re-integration into society, then they have not yet finished serving their sentence;-And Furthermore, after a criminal is determined to have paid back their debt to society, that they shall no longer be discriminated against [by or through law] for any previous wrongdoing, and shall be offered the same civil governmental protections as all other free/d People of Pacifica. If in the case of significant doubt as to how long to sentence a particular Individual, we the People advise the application of indeterminate sentences upon them, whose end is based para-metrically upon successful rehabilitation of the Convicted, to which shall mean their capacity to re-integrate successfully back into society [without the risk of them re-offending for the same crimes of which they have been convicted], as well as there being provided measurable and demonstrable evidence to support this conclusion. We the people of Pacifica fully condemn any and all catch and release policies for convicted criminals (particularly for felons). In all cases of release of an inmate from imprisonment, the warden with the duty of issuing the discharge has the legally binding duty to check to see if such a release has been determined by the courts to be proper.

In all cases, excessive bail shall not be required, or excessive fines be imposed, neither excessive terms of incarceration, or any other excessive form of criminal punishment, nor any torturous, cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing/demoralizing/dehumanizing, or unusual treatments or punishments be inflicted.

There shall be proportionality of a punishment for a crime, in the forfeiture of property for the magnitude of a felony, and in the fines for both felonies and misdemeanors, weighing on an individual basis given the facts and circumstances under which a crime took place, fitting a specific punishment to serve the needs of the community for protection against recidivism while at the same time without applying excessive punishment, to achieve reasonable outcomes for the equal interests of both the convicted and their victims.

Any person who sues another person or corporation for civil damages or tort, and loses the case, and upon appeal shall lose, and exhaust all of their remedies under Citizen Review actions, shall be compelled to pay ALL legal costs and court costs and other ancillary costs to the winning party.

Any Act, Omission, or Evidence produced or taken, in direct response or resistance, during or after a violation of One’s or Another’s Natural, Common Law, Statutory, or Constitutional Rights, is inadmissible in court, in order to preserve the integrity of both the Cause/s (“Water”) & Product/s (“Tree”) of Liberty & Justice; This rule protects Persons, inside and outside their Domicile & Lands, therefore, someone who correctly believes their rights are being violated may Justifiably respond with Unlimited Force & furthermore remain immunized from criminal responsibility for any action/omission or Evidence taken/produced in direct response to such offense against them, as long as they do not violate the rights of another Person.

Any Order issued or Power exercised which stems from or is the Product of any erroneous or Illegal/Unlawful action or omission of a member of the Public Body, or those acting in concert with them, of which violates the constitution, is per se unreasonable and unlawful in itself, thereby being invalid on its face, as well as having no legal authority or power.

In adherence to the state of one’s mind under Mens Inquisitio, the State Apparatus shall not subjugate an Individual’s right of fair inquiry to a publicly open business or [a] firm/s, or for that of other legal or otherwise artificial entit[y]/ies; No person shall be convicted from actions partook under fair purpose Mens Inquisitio for the publicly accessible services of a business or firm or other legal entity. Such defense enables a seeker of services or relevant information to justly inquire about the publicly-open property sub-state contract, without delay to prompt honest reply and forthcoming presentation of the contract upon consent of the owner, otherwise the ingresor must promptly leave the way they came or to the shortest distance to the public ways around relevant obstructions, whichever may be most proper.

Private citizens may forcefully resist and even escape, damage/kill, along with sue, any States, Counties, Cities, Jails, Prisons, Mental Wards, Officers, Staff, or anyone else who facilitates an unlawful detention or unlawful arrest, false imprisonment, or who issues an order or creates a law which infringes on any of the rights of Persons or a Citizen of Pacifica, regardless of if excessive force is used to enforce such violations of freedom/liberty, and a Person’s fellow countrymen have the right to assist them in resisting and/or escaping such an unlawful detention or arrest, false imprisonment, or unjust order.

Social security and/or universal basic income and dividends benefits shall continue to flow even at a time of a person's incarceration or incapacitation, such as jail or hospital time.

Persons have the right to an automatic order of remuneration for legal costs incurred in defense against a civil or criminal action which did not prevail against them.

The people are assured the ancient common law right to Writs of Coram Nobis, and to access post-conviction relief for any point of law or fact which may impair the impartiality of their trial, affect any of their due process rights, or which exculpt them of actual guilt and otherwise establish their innocence.

SECTION. 10.5.

Pacifica shall institute a National Domestic Abuse Offender Registry throughout the several States to shield vulnerable individuals from habitual perpetrators via public disclosure and centralized national coordination; "domestic abuse violation" encompasses convictions for conduct inflicting bodily harm, confinement or immobilization, destruction of property, unlawful detention, abduction, harassment through persistent pursuit or reprisals against the victim's allies [whether kin, companions, or advocates] directed at familial or household associates, romantic companions, or susceptible parties such as the aged or impaired; a "habitual violator" denotes an individual found guilty of such a violation alongside at least one antecedent adjudication of the same; each Pacifican State’s Bureau of Investigation must oversee a publicly accessible web-based scrape-able repository detailing habitual violators' identities, photographs, birthdates, municipal abodes, digitized fingerprint records, adjudication timelines and jurisdictions, plus violation narratives, with courts automatically notifying the state Bureau upon eligible post-enactment adjudications paired with antecedents, obligating culprits to report personally within ten days with non-adherence triggering monetary sanctions or prolonged inscription; inscription terms escalate thus: five years for one antecedent, seven for two, ten for three, twenty for four or more, commencing from the most recent adjudication; eligible infractions span bodily restraint or harm via battery or assault, confinement via unlawful detention, intimidation-linked asset ruin, domineering tactics like seclusion, surveillance, or fiscal constriction inducing fear, pursuit-based harassment or abduction within intimate spheres, and vengeful acts targeting victim supporters to deter aid or isolate [including through 'dounle-teamers' or extra party/ies; initial infractions shall merit inclusion, with severity of punishments prioritizing recidivists imperiling the defenseless; the National Executive shall direct liaison with Pacifica’s federal authorities to forge a unified trans-state repository, disseminating state records while upholding confidentiality of victims personally identifyable information; entered information shall be restricted to constables, aggrieved parties, and general inquiries excluding complete domiciles or identity numerals; yearly reviews gshall uarantee procedural equity, permitting expungement petitions post-term via redemption evidence; inscription by law may influence vocational and residential vetting; breaches shall levy misdemeanor castigation; absent any prior national equivalent, Pacifica must pioneer exemplary linkage for cross-state monitoring among the sovereign jurisdictions within in.

Pacifica shall institute a National Child Cruelty Register throughout the several States to shield kids, wards, and minors from recurrent perpetrators of cruelty through coordinated oversight, recordation, and controlled disclosure; “child cruelty offence” encompasses convictions for neglect, abandonment, physical or psychological abuse, infanticide, willful endangerment, malnourishment, exposure, or allowance of grievous harm or death to a child under one’s dominion or care, whether by direct act or culpable omission; a “recurrent offender” denotes an individual found guilty of such an offence in conjunction with one or more antecedent convictions of like nature; each State’s Bureau of Investigation shall maintain a secured and uniformly formatted repository enumerating the recurrent offender’s name, likeness, birthdate, municipality of residence, identifying characteristics plainly articulable by a Person without technological qualification/quantification, adjudication record, and offence synopsis, the courts being bound to transmit notice of qualifying adjudications to their respective Bureaus within seven days of sentencing, compelling offenders to register personally within ten, failure to comply incurring pecuniary penalties or automatic extension of inscription; inscription terms shall ascend by gravity and recurrence, being five years for one antecedent conviction, ten for two, fifteen for three, and permanent for four or more, each term commencing upon the most recent adjudication; eligible infractions include cruelty, neglect, abandonment, infanticide, and any act or omission causing a child’s severe suffering or death; initial infractions shall merit inscription for preventive observation, with intensity of sanctions amplifying with repetition and danger posed to the defenseless; the National Executive shall coordinate liaison between the several States and the Federal Department of Justice to ensure unified data interchange and interjurisdictional recognition, disseminating registry information to constables, social protection agencies, and approved childcare institutions while shielding victims’ personal identifiers from all public display; registry content shall be accessible for lawful vetting in employment, adoption, and caregiving contexts, the misuse or unauthorized disclosure constituting a misdemeanor punishable by fine and removal of access; annual reviews shall guarantee procedural fairness and afford offenders petition for expungement upon demonstrated rehabilitation; in absence of any prior unified framework, this act shall establish Pacifica as the standard bearer for national guardianship of the young through interlinked recordkeeping and cooperative sovereignty among its constituent jurisdictions.

Pacifica shall institute a National Sex Offender Registry across the several States to shield vulnerable individuals from habitual predators via public disclosure and centralized national coordination; "sex offense violation" encompasses convictions for conduct involving sexual penetration without consent, sexual contact with minors or incapacitated persons, production or distribution of child sexual abuse material, enticement or solicitation of juveniles, sexual exploitation of vulnerable parties such as the aged or impaired, patterns of grooming or manipulative predation that ensnare victims, or harassment through persistent sexual pursuit, whether kin, companions, or advocates, directed at familial or household associates, romantic companions under age of consent, or susceptible parties; a "habitual violator" denotes an individual found guilty of such a violation of at least one adjudication; each Pacifican State’s Bureau of Investigation must oversee a publicly accessible web-based scrape-able repository detailing violators' identities, photographs, birthdates, municipal abodes, digital fingerprint records, adjudication timelines and jurisdictions, plus violation narratives, with courts automatically notifying the state Bureau upon eligible post-enactment adjudications paired with antecedents, obligating culprits to report personally within ten days with nonadherence triggering monetary sanctions or prolonged inscription; inscription terms escalate thus: five years for one offense, seven for two, ten for three, twenty for four or more, commencing from the most recent adjudication; eligible infractions span nonconsensual penetration via rape or aggravated assault, improper contact with protected classes, intimidation-linked exploitation, domineering tactics like grooming, surveillance, or fiscal constriction inducing sexual submission, and pursuit-based harassment or abduction for sexual purposes within intimate spheres; initial infractions merit inclusion, prioritizing punishment of recidivists imperiling the defenseless; the National Executive shall direct liaison with Pacifica’s federal authorities to forge a unified trans-state repository, disseminating state records while upholding confidentiality; entry restricted to constables, aggrieved parties, and general inquiries excluding complete domiciles or identity numerals; yearly reviews guarantee procedural equity, permitting expungement petitions post-term via redemption evidence; inscription influences vocational and residential vetting; breaches levy misdemeanor castigation; absent any prior national equivalent, Pacifica must pioneer exemplary linkage for cross-state monitoring among its sovereign jurisdictions.

SECTION. 11.

Whoever, knowing that an offense against Pacifica has been committed, receives, relieves, comforts or assists the offender in order to hinder or prevent their apprehension, trial, or punishment, is an accessory after the fact. Except as otherwise expressly provided by any Act of Congress, an accessory after the fact shall be fined not more than one-half the maximum fine prescribed for the punishment of the principal or imprisoned not more than one-half the maximum term of imprisonment, or both; or if the principal is punishable by life imprisonment, the accessory shall be imprisoned not more than fifteen years.

Whoever willfully endeavors by means of bribery, coercion, or commandeering, to obstruct, delay, or prevent the communication of information relating to a violation of any [just] criminal statute of Pacifica by any person to a criminal investigator shall be fined or imprisoned, or both.

SECTION. 12.

No person or group of persons, whether acting privately or under color of law, shall conspire to injure, oppress, threaten, intimidate, or deprive any individual within Pacifica, or any place subject to its jurisdiction, of any right, privilege, or immunity secured by this Constitution or the laws enacted under its authority. Any act, whether by private individuals or by those acting under authority of law, that willfully deprives any person of such rights, privileges, or immunities, or subjects any person to unequal treatment, punishment, or penalty on account of race, color, nationality, or for having exercised constitutional rights, is prohibited. Congress and the several States shall have the power to enforce this provision by appropriate legislation, including the establishment of penalties and remedies for violations

Whomever, under color of any law, statute, ordinance, regulation, or custom, willfully or through gross negligence subjects any Person in any State, Territory, Commonwealth, Possession, or District to the deprivation of any rights/immunities, freedoms, privileges, or guarantees, secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of the Pacifica, or to different punishments, pains, or penalties, on account of such person being an alien, or by reason of his color, or race, than are prescribed for the punishment of citizens, shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than one year; and if bodily injury results from the acts committed in violation of this section or if such acts include the use, attempted use, or threatened use of a dangerous weapon, explosives, or fire, shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not more than ten years, or both; and if death results from the acts committed in violation of this section, or if such acts include kidnapping or an attempt to kidnap, aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to commit aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to kill, shall be fined under this Provision and executed in an appropriate manner as prescribed by law.

Every person who, under color of any statute, ordinance, regulation, custom, or usage, of any State or Territory or the Federal District of Olympus, Citizens, or causes to be subjected, any citizen of Pacifica or other person within the jurisdiction thereof to the deprivation of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured by the Constitution and laws, shall be liable to the party injured in an action at law, suit in equity, or other proper proceeding for redress, except that in any action brought against a judicial officer for an act or omission taken in such officer’s judicial capacity, injunctive relief shall not be granted unless a declaratory decree was violated or declaratory relief was unavailable. For the purposes of this Provision, any Act of Congress applicable exclusively to the Federal District of Olympus shall be considered to be a statute of the Federal District of Olympus.

If two or more persons conspire to injure, oppress, threaten, or intimidate any person in any State, Territory, Commonwealth, Possession, or District in the free exercise or enjoyment of any right or privilege secured to him by the Constitution or laws of Pacifica, or because of his having so exercised the same; or if two or more persons go in disguise on the highway, or on the premises of another, with intent to prevent or hinder his free exercise or enjoyment of any right or privilege so secured; They shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than ten years, or both; and if death results from the acts committed in violation of this section or if such acts include kidnapping or an attempt to kidnap, aggravated sexual abuse or an attempt to commit aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to kill, they shall be fined under this title or imprisoned for any term of years or for life, or both.

(a) If two or more persons in any State or Territory conspire to prevent, by force, intimidation, or threat, any person from accepting or holding any office, trust, or place of confidence under Pacifica, or from discharging any duties thereof; or to induce by like means any officer of Pacifica to leave any State, district, or place, where his duties as an officer are required to be performed, or to injure him in his person or property on account of his lawful discharge of the duties of his office, or while engaged in the lawful discharge thereof, or to injure his property so as to molest, interrupt, hinder, or impede him in the discharge of his official duties;
(b) If two or more persons in any State or Territory conspire to deter, by force, intimidation, or threat, any party or witness in any court of Pacifica from attending such court, or from testifying to any matter pending therein, freely, fully, and truthfully, or to injure such party or witness in his person or property on account of his having so attended or testified, or to influence the verdict, presentment, or indictment of any grand or petit juror in any such court, or to injure such juror in his person or property on account of any verdict, presentment, or indictment lawfully assented to by him, or of his being or having been such juror; or if two or more persons conspire for the purpose of impeding, hindering, obstructing, or defeating, in any manner, the due course of justice in any State or Territory, with intent to deny to any citizen the equal protection of the laws, or to injure him or his property for lawfully enforcing, or attempting to enforce, the right of any person, or class of persons, to the equal protection of the laws;
(c) If two or more persons in any State or Territory conspire or go in disguise on the highway or on the premises of another, for the purpose of depriving, either directly or indirectly, any person or class of persons of the equal protection of the laws, or of equal privileges and immunities under the laws; or for the purpose of preventing or hindering the constituted authorities of any State or Territory from giving or securing to all persons within such State or Territory the equal protection of the laws; or if two or more persons conspire to prevent by force, intimidation, or threat, any citizen who is lawfully entitled to vote, from giving his support or advocacy in a legal manner, toward or in favor of the election of any lawfully qualified person as an elector for President or Vice President, or as a Member of Congress of Pacifica; or to injure any citizen in person or property on account of such support or advocacy;
(d) in any case of conspiracy set forth in this section, if one or more persons engaged therein do, or cause to be done, any act in furtherance of the object of such conspiracy, whereby another is injured in his person or property, or deprived of having and exercising any right or privilege of a citizen of the Pacifica, the party so injured or deprived may have an action for the recovery of damages occasioned by such injury or deprivation, against any one or more of the conspirators.

Whomever choseth to or perpetueth about the subjugation of any other Person through abuse in the processes of [civil] governance, whereby having no right to engage the machinery of government for their ends, in demonstration of their malice through their attentive busybody efforts with intention to hold for ransom, harassment, intimidation, or coercion, or any combination thereof against the subjected party, through initiation under false pretenses either or both the civil and/or criminal process, then they shall be sentenced and/or laid to re-compensate for the same as if they themself had performed the injurious actions by having no right, even if their actions were performed through proxy of law enforcement or another acting on their behalf or to their benefit; and for the case of conspiracy where there is more than one levying against their fellow person, the total number of them shall be held independently to the multiple of the charge as measured by an average standard term of years and individually each time decided monetary recompense for damages as per suit, as does constitute such a factor by the whole number of persons involved.

Any ‘state actor’ who violates somebodies constitutional rights “shall be liable” to the party injured somebody who violates the constitution or established law

SECTION. 13.

Whoever, except in cases and under circumstances expressly authorized by the Constitution, or Act of Congress in conformity thereto, willfully uses any part of the Armed Forces (other than the Militia), of Pacifica, along with that of any State, Locality, or Territory, as a Posse Comitatus or otherwise to execute the laws, except in the cases and in such manner as strictly laid forth by this constitution, is guilty of committing a felony and shall be imprisoned not less than five years and fined under this provision; and shall be incapable of holding any office under Pacifica; any military personnel violating this protection of the people against shall be punished in the same manner as those who issue the directives to them, and it is their duty to question, resist, and depose those in command who violate this provision in accordance with the laws of military justice as laid down by Congress. The use of military forces in law enforcement roles shall be strictly limited to preserve the civil liberties, autonomy and free ingress/regress of the People, and the separation of civilian authority from military power. The primary purpose of the Armed Forces is to protect and defend Pacifica and its People from invasion and attack, not to be deployed as a utilitarian agency to act as an extension of public office, or any branch of Government other than what it is narrowly defined here in this Constitution; The secondary purpose is disaster mitigation and response to a State or National Emergency, with consent of the Gubernor or Legislature of each State involved in the declared Emergency by both the Executive of the State and the Federal branches of government, in accordance to both the Constitution of Pacifica and the State/s in question, not to the exclusion of protection for Territories voluntarily consented to entering the Jurisdictional Powers and Agreements of Responsibility of and to Pacifica and We the People.

All Members and Agents of the Public Administration convicted of the criminal offense of acting in breach of the Constitution or of any law relevant to the position held shall cease to hold their current positions and shall no longer be eligible to hold any public office or to be employed by the Public Administration.

SECTION. 14.

The law of trusts as of the date of ratification of this Constitution is hereby recognized as part of the laws that preceded this Constitution and was incorporated into it. The settlor, trustee, beneficiary, and the trust itself shall each be deemed as distinct Persons in any court of law of Pacifica and any State, the trust represented therein by the trustee.

Any claim against a non-Person must specify an owner, even if it is initially an unknown owner, and the last possessor shall be presumed the owner unless title to another is proved. No asset shall be forfeited except to pay a lawful fine, imposed by verdict of a jury, by selling at public auction.

SECTION. 15.

Habeas corpus shall be provided in front of a citizen’s court. The people shall retain the right to determination of habeas corpus proceedings by a jury of their peers acting in the function of a citizen's court.

Congress shall have the power to enumerate, promote, and protect the right of Habeas Corpus beyond what is set forth by this Constitution, within the limits prescribed by it, all immunities of the People [generally and globally] and occupant persons on Pacifican soil applied

Even terrorists and belligerent enemy combatants shall retain the right of Habeas Corpus.

By and through the advice and consent of the Pacifican commons, with this present constitution ratified, and by the authority thereof, That whensoever any person or persons shall bring any habeas corpus directed unto any sheriff or sheriffs, gaoler, administrator, or other person whatsoever, for any person in his or her custody, and the said writ shall be served upon the said officer, or left at the gaol or prison with any of the under-officers, under-keepers or deputy of the said officers or keepers, that the said officer or officers, his or their under-officers, under-keepers or deputies, shall within three days after the service thereof as aforesaid (unless the commitment aforesaid were for treason or high felony, plainly and specially expressed in the warrant of commitment) upon payment or tender of the charges of bringing the said prisoner, to be ascertained by the judge or court that awarded the same, and endorsed upon the said writ, not exceeding twelve pence per mile, and upon security given by his own bond to pay the charges of carrying back the prisoner, if he shall be remanded by the court or judge to which he shall be brought according to the true intent of this present act, and that he will not make any escape by the way, make return of such writ; (3) and bring or cause to be brought the body of the party so committed or restrained, unto or before the Chancellor of Justice, or the judges or millitia of the said court from whence the said writ shall issue, or unto and before such other person or persons before whom the said writ is made returnable, according to the command thereof; (4) and shall then likewise certify the true causes of his detainer or imprisonment, unless the commitment of the said party be in any place beyond the distance of thirty-two-point-two kilo-meters from the place or places where such court or person is or shall be residing; and if beyond the distance of sixty kilo-meters, and not above one-hundred-eighty kilo-meters, then within the space of ten days, and if beyond the distance of three hundred kilo-meters, then within the space of twenty days, after such delivery aforesaid, and not longer.

In the intent that no sheriff, gaoler or other officer may pretend ignorance of the import of any such writ; (2) be it enacted by the authority aforesaid, That all such writs shall be marked in this manner, "Habeus corpus in respect to and pursuing remedy by Lady of Supreme Justice in the light and spirit of the Ghost of Liberty" and shall be signed by the person that awards the same; (3) and if any person or persons shall be or stand committed or detained as aforesaid, for any crime, unless for treason plainly expressed in the warrant of commitment, in the vacation-time, and out of term, it shall and may be lawful to and for the person or persons so committed or detained (other than persons convict or in execution by legal process) or any one on his or their behalf, to appeal or complain to the Chancellor of Justice, or any one of the competent justices, either of the one bench or of the other, or the militia of the exchequer of the degree of the coif; (4) and the said Chancellor of Justice, justices or militia or any of them, upon view of the copy or copies of the warrant or warrants of commitment and detainer, or otherwise upon oath made that such copy or copies were denied to be given by such person or persons in whose custody the prisoner or prisoners is or are detained, are hereby authorized and required, upon request made in writing by such person or persons, or any on his, her or their behalf, attested and subscribed by two witnesses who were present at the delivery of the same, to award and grant an habeas corpus under the seal of such court whereof he shall then be one of the judges, (5) to be directed to the officer or officers in whose custody the party so committed or detained shall be, returnable immediate before the said Chancellor of Justice, or such justice, minuteman or any other justice or minuteman of the degree of the coif of any of the said courts; (6) and upon service thereof as aforesaid, the officer or officers, his or their under-officer or under-officers, under-keeper or under-keepers, or their deputy, in whose custody the party is so committed or detained, shall within the times respectively before limited, bring such prisoner or prisoners before the said Chancellor of Justice, or such justices, militia or one of them, before whom the said writ is made returnable, and in case of his absence before any other of them, with the return of such writ, and the true causes of the commitment and detainer;
