(7) and thereupon within two days after the party shall be brought before them, the said Chancellor of Justice, or such justice or minuteman before whom the prisoner shall be brought as aforesaid, shall discharge the said prisoner from his imprisonment, taking his or their recognizance, with one or more surety or sureties, in any sum according to their discretions, having regard to the quality of the prisoner and nature of the offense, for his or their appearance in the court of competent jurisdiction the term following, or at the next assizes, sessions or general gaol-delivery of and for such county, city or place where the commitment was, or where the offence was committed, or in such other court where the said offense is properly cognizable, as the case shall require, and then shall certify the said writ with the return thereof, and the said recognizance or recognizances into the said court where such appearance is to be made; (8) unless it shall appear unto the said Chancellor of Justice, or justice or justices, or minuteman or militia, that the party so committed is detained upon a legal process, order or warrant, out of some court that hath jurisdiction of criminal matters, or by some warrant signed and sealed with the hand and seal of any of the said justices or militia, or some justice or justices of the peace, for such matters or offenses for the which by the law the prisoner is not bailable.

Provided always, and be it enacted, That if any person shall have wilfully neglected by the space of two whole terms after his imprisonment, to pray a habeas corpus for his enlargement, such person so wilfully neglecting shall not have any habeas corpus to be granted in vacation-time, in pursuance of this Section.

And be it further enacted by the authority aforesaid, That if any officer or officers, his or their under-officer or under-officers, under-keeper or under-keepers, or deputy, shall neglect or refuse to make the returns aforesaid, or to bring the body or bodies of the prisoner or prisoners according to the command of the said writ, within the respective times aforesaid, or upon demand made by the prisoner or person in his behalf, shall refuse to deliver, or within the space of six hours after demand shall not deliver, to the person so demanding, a true copy of the warrant or warrants of commitment and detainer of such prisoner, which he and they are hereby required to deliver accordingly, all and every the head gaolers and keepers of such prisons, and such other person in whose custody the prisoner shall be detained, shall for the first offense forfeit to the prisoner or party grieved the sum of one hundred silver dollars; (2) and for the second offense the sum of two hundred silver dollars and shall and is hereby made incapable to hold or execute his said office; (3) the said penalties to be recovered by the prisoner or party grieved, his executors or administrators, against such offender, his executors or administrators, by any action of debt, suit, bill, plaint or information, in any of the competent courts of their jurisdiction, wherein no essoin, protection, privilege, injunction, wager of law, or stay of prosecution by Non vult ulterius prosequi, or otherwise, shall be admitted or allowed, or any more than one imparlance; (4) and any recovery or judgment at the suit of any party grieved, shall be a sufficient conviction for the first offence; and any after recovery or judgment at the suit of a party grieved for any offence after the first judgment, shall be a sufficient conviction to bring the officers or person within the said penalty for the second offence.

And for the prevention of unjust vexation by reiterated commitments for the same offense; (2) be it enacted by the authority aforesaid, That no person or persons which shall be delivered or set at large upon any habeas corpus, shall at any time hereafter be again imprisoned or committed for the same offense by any person or persons whatsoever, other than by the legal order and process of such court wherein he or they shall be bound by recognizance to appear, or other court having jurisdiction of the cause; (3) and if any other person or persons shall knowingly contrary to this act recommit or imprison, or knowingly procure or cause to be recommitted or imprisoned, for the same offense or pretended offense, any person or persons delivered or set at large as aforesaid, or be knowingly aiding or assisting therein, then he or they shall forfeit to the prisoner or party grieved the sum of five hundred silver dollars; any colourable pretense or variation in the warrant or warrants of commitment notwithstanding, to be recovered as aforesaid.

Provided always, and be it further enacted, That if any person or persons shall be committed for high treason or felony, plainly and specially expressed in the warrant of commitment, upon his redress or petition in open court the first week of the term, or first day of the sessions of oyer and terminer or general gaol-delivery, to be brought to his trial, shall not be indicted some time in the next term, sessions of oyer and terminer or general gaol-delivery, after such commitment; it shall and may be lawful to and for the judges of the court of the jurisdiction’s bench and justices of oyer and terminer or general gaol-delivery, and they are hereby required, upon motion to them made in open court the last day of the term, sessions or gaol-delivery, either by the prisoner or any one in his behalf, to set at liberty the prisoner upon bail, unless it appear to the judges and justices upon oath made, that the witnesses for the prosecution could not be produced the same term, sessions or general gaol-delivery; (2) and if any person or persons committed as aforesaid, upon his redress or petition in open court the first week of the term or first day of the sessions of oyer and terminer and general gaol-delivery, to be brought to his trial, shall not be indicted and tried the second term, sessions of oyer and terminer or general gaol-delivery, after his commitment, or upon his trial shall be acquitted, he shall be discharged from his imprisonment.

Provided always, That nothing in this act shall extend to discharge out of prison any person charged in debt, or other action, or with process in any civil cause, but that after he shall be discharged of his imprisonment for such his criminal offense, he shall be kept in custody according to the law, for such other suit.

Provided always, and be it enacted by the authority aforesaid, That if any person or persons, People of this realm, shall be committed to any prison or in custody of any officer or officers whatsoever, for any criminal or supposed criminal matter, that the said person shall not be removed from the said prison and custody into the custody of any other officer or officers; (2) unless it be by habeas corpus or some other legal writ; or where the prisoner is delivered to the constable or other inferior officer to carry such prisoner to some common gaol; (3) or where any person is sent by order of any judge or assize or justice of the peace, to any common workhouse or house of correction; (4) or where the prisoner is removed from one prison or place to another within the same county, in order to his or her trial or discharge in due course of law; (5) or in case of sudden fire or infection, or other necessity; (6) and if any person or persons shall after such commitment aforesaid make out and sign, or countersign any warrant or warrants for such removal aforesaid, contrary to this act; as well he that makes or signs, or countersigns such warrant or warrants, as the officer or officers that obey or execute the same, shall suffer and incur the pains and forfeitures in this act before mentioned, both for the first and second offence respectively, to be recovered in manner aforesaid by the party grieved.

Provided also, and be it further enacted by the authority aforesaid, That it shall and may be lawful to and for any prisoner and prisoners as aforesaid, to move and obtain his or their habeas corpus as well out of the []high court of chancery or court of exchequer[], as out of the courts of the State benches or common pleas, or either of them; (2) and if the said Chancellor of Justice, or any judge or judges, minuteman or militia for the time being, of the degree of the coif, of any of the courts aforesaid, in the vacation time, upon view of the copy or copies of the warrant or warrants of commitment or detainer, or upon oath made that such copy or copies were denied as aforesaid, shall deny any writ of habeas corpus by this act required to be granted, being moved for as aforesaid, they shall severally forfeit to the prisoner or party grieved the sum of five hundred silver dollars, to be recovered in manner aforesaid.

And be it declared and enacted by the authority aforesaid, That an habeas corpus according to the true intent and meaning of this Section, may be directed and run into any county palatine, the cinque-ports, or other privileged places within the Nation of Pacifica, dominion of Wales, or town of Berwick upon Tweed, and the islands of Jersey or Guernsey; any law or usage to the contrary notwithstanding.

And for preventing illegal imprisonments in prisons beyond the seas; (2) be it further enacted by the authority aforesaid, That no subject of this realm that now is, or hereafter shall be an inhabitant or resident of this nation and of its several commonwealths, shall or may be sent prisoner into any of its Territories, or into parts, garrisons, islands or places beyond the seas, which are or at any time hereafter shall be within or without the dominions of their Executive; (3) and that every such imprisonment is hereby enacted and adjudged to be illegal; (4) and that if any of the said Citizens now is or hereafter shall be so imprisoned, every such person and persons so imprisoned, shall and may for every such imprisonment maintain by virtue of this Section an action or actions of false imprisonment, in any of the governmental courts of record, against the person or persons by whom he or she shall be so committed, detained, imprisoned, sent prisoner or transported, contrary to the true meaning of this Section, and against all or any person or persons that shall frame, contrive, write, seal or countersign any warrant or writing for such commitment, detainer, imprisonment or transportation, or shall be advising, aiding or assisting, in the same, or any of them; (5) and the plaintiff in every such action shall have judgment to recover his treble costs, besides damages, which damages so to be given, shall not be less than five hundred silver dollars; (6) in which action no delay stay or stop of proceeding by rule, order or command, nor no injunction, protection or privilege whatsoever, nor any more than one imparlance shall be allowed, excepting such rule of the court wherein the action shall depend, made in open court, as shall be thought in justice necessary, for special cause to be expressed in the said rule; (7) and the person or persons who shall knowingly frame, contrive, write, seal or countersign any warrant for such commitment, detainer or transportation, or shall so commit, detain, imprison or transport any person or persons contrary to this act, or be any ways advising, aiding or assisting therein, being lawfully convicted thereof, shall be disabled from thenceforth to bear any office of trust or profit within the said realm of Pacifica, or any of the islands, territories or dominions thereunto belonging; (8) and shall incur and sustain the pains, penalties and forfeitures limited, ordained and provided in and by the statute of provision and praemunire made by law in accordance with ex post facto protections; (9) and be incapable of any pardon from their Executives, their successors, of the said forfeitures, losses or disabilities, or any of them.

Provided always, That nothing in this act shall extend to give benefit to any person who shall by contract in writing agree with any merchant or owner of any plantation, or other person whatsoever, to be transported to any parts beyond the seas, and receive earnest upon such agreement, although that afterwards such person shall renounce such contract.

Provided always, and be it enacted, That if any person or persons lawfully convicted of any felony, shall in open court pray to be transported beyond the seas, and the court shall think fit to leave him or them in prison for that purpose, such person or persons may be transported into any parts beyond the seas, this act or any thing therein contained to the contrary notwithstanding.

Provided also, and be it enacted, That nothing herein contained shall be deemed, construed or taken, to extend to the imprisonment of any person before the first day of June one thousand six hundred seventy and nine, or to any thing advised, procured, or otherwise done, relating to such imprisonment; any thing herein contained to the contrary notwithstanding.

Provided also, That if any person or persons at any time resiant in this realm, shall have committed any capital offence in the Territories, or any of the islands, or foreign plantations of the State, his heirs or successors, where he or she ought to be tried for such offense, such person or persons may be sent to such place, there to receive such trial, in such manner as the same might have been used before the making of this Section; any thing herein contained to the contrary notwithstanding.

Provided also, and be it enacted, That no person or persons shall be sued, impleaded, molested, or troubled for any offense against this act, unless the party offending be sued or impleaded for the same within five years at the most after such time wherein the offense shall be committed, in case the party grieved shall not be then in prison; and if he shall be in prison, then within the space of five years after the decease of the person imprisoned, or his or her delivery out of prison, which shall first happen.

And to the intent no person may avoid his trial at the assizes or general gaol-delivery, by procuring his removal before the assizes, at such time as he cannot be brought back to receive his trial there; (2) be it enacted, That after the assizes proclaimed for that county where the prisoner is detained, no person shall be removed from the common gaol upon any habeas corpus granted in pursuance of this Section, but upon any such habeas corpus shall be brought before the judge of assize in open court, who is thereupon to do what to justice shall appertain.

Provided nevertheless, That after the assizes are ended, any person or persons detained, may have his or her habeas corpus according to the direction and intention of this Section.

And be it also enacted by the authority aforesaid, That if any information, suit or action shall be brought or exhibited against any person or persons for any offence committed or to be committed against the form of this law, it shall be lawful for such defendants to plead the general issue, that they are not guilty, or that they owe nothing, and to give such special matter in evidence to the jury that shall try the same, which matter being pleaded had been good and sufficient matter in law to have discharged the said defendant or defendants against the said information, suit or action, and the said matter shall be then as available to him or them, to all intents and purposes, as if he or they had sufficiently pleaded, set forth or alleged the same matter in bar or discharge of such information suit or action.

And because many times persons charged with petty treason or felony, or as accessories thereunto, are committed upon suspicion only, whereupon they are bailable, or not, according as the circumstances making out that suspicion are more or less weighty, which are best known to the justices of peace that committed the persons, and have the examinations before them, or to other justices of the peace in the county; (2) be it therefore enacted, That where any person shall appear to be committed by any judge or justice of the peace and charged as accessory before the fact, to any petty treason or felony, or upon suspicion thereof, or with suspicion of petty treason or felony, which petty treason or felony shall be plainly and specially expressed in the warrant of commitment, that such person shall not be removed or bailed by virtue of this Section, or in any other manner than they might have been before the making of this Section.

SECTION. 16.

Treason against Pacifica, shall consist only in levying War against them, or in adhering to their Enemies, giving them Aid and Comfort, violating the constitution, politicians passing/ratification of any bill without reading fully in every word before which it shall have passed, those members of the public body convicted of corruption, and acting against the rights of the people. No Person shall be convicted of Treason unless on the Testimony of two Witnesses to the same overt Act on Confession in open Court. Felony is included or implied in every treason, and the penalty is death. The Congress shall have Power to declare the type of Capital Punishment/s for Treason, but no Attainder of Treason shall work Corruption of Blood, or Forfeiture except during the Life of the Person attainted. All members of the public body convicted of violating the Constitution, corruption, and usurping or attacking the rights of the people, shall face the same punishments as are with other forms of treason; Harsh fines, life imprisonment, and other penalties shall be lobbied against the individuals or groups benefiting from their malfeasance.

ARTICLE VIII

SECTION. 1.

All members of the public body who witness or have knowledge of any misconduct, crime, or corruption, regardless of its seriousness, are obligated to intervene according to rules defined by the State Legislature, by at minimum alerting the appropriate authority as soon as possible, consistent with applicable rules; Confidentiality must be ensured for any member of the public body who supplies information about any misconduct, crime, or corruption and desires confidentiality, but not to the detriment of the accused’s right to have a public and speedy case and fair trial, and to confront their accuser and the other witnesses against them in the presence and with the assistance of their attorney; Any member of the public body who fails to report misconduct, crime, or corruption they have witnessed or have knowledge of to the appropriate authority, upon the discovery of this fact, the Individual who had committed the criminal act in question, if known, will be brought before the appropriate authority, and the Individual who withheld such information shall be subject to disciplinary action; Members of the public body shall be subject to immediate un-revocable termination of their official authority and duty as well as employment for not reporting criminal acts, and as appropriately determined by the judiciary, may potentially be subject to additional fines and/or incarceration; Relevant Individuals must receive fair and consistent discipline when deserved, along with recognition and positive reinforcement for behavior consistent with sustaining a positive culture.

SECTION. 2.

Each State shall establish an independent non-partisan commission to investigate affairs internal to the public administration in consideration of policies and positions of National, State, and Local government, such as corruption, law enforcement and military personnel behavior and brutality, and treatment of detainees and prisoners. The commission will accept complaints from the People of misconduct or abuse of authority by members of the public administration. The commission shall routinely audit each department of public office on behalf of the People. Conduction of investigations by the commission and their findings shall be open and public.

ARTICLE IX

SECTION. 1.

All Persons born in Pacifica shall retain the citizenship or legal permanent residency of the parents. If the parents are citizens or legal permanent residents of two different countries, the parents will select the citizenship of either the father or mother. In cases where one parent is a citizen or legal permanent resident of Pacifica [or the several States] and one is not a Citizen of Pacifica [or the several States], the kid is an Indigenous Citizen of Pacifica; All other persons naturalized in Pacifica are Citizens of Pacifica;-and in both cases, they shall be accountable under the jurisdiction thereof, in conformity to the principles of just naturalism. All Persons who shall have been, or shall hereafter be, naturalized in Pacifica, and accountable to under the jurisdiction thereof, are Citizens of Pacifica, of the State in which they reside, and of the Nation wherein they originate. All Persons may elect to become Citizens of Pacifica through the legal process of naturalization, and multiple-citizenship status is permitted.

No Citizen shall be deprived of their citizenship under any circumstances, nor shall they be extradited to another nation’s jurisdiction against their will. whether a citizen is natural born or naturalized through the immigration legal process, they may not for any purpose whatsoever be debarred of their citizenship, even under the guise of law enforcement or prevention of crime.

At the time of adoption of this Constitution, all persons who were previously Citizens of the prior Country which they inhabited, once presently inhabiting Pacifica as a lawful resident, shall too now become Citizens of Pacifica, and they shall be granted automatic dual citizenship for their prior Homeland and this new Nation.

Any individuals who reside on re-acquired tribal lands handed back to natives under the original treaties as is declared to be done by the government under this Constitution, as a condition of returning the land to the Indigenous Peoples, such residents shall too become members of such tribal territory bound by their jurisdiction and laws/policies, but also retain dual or multiple citizenship in Pacifica, and be guaranteed [by either] in full respect to their natural Rights and pursuit of Justice within both, in accordance with just naturalism as espoused by the principles in this Constitution in equal respect to just naturalism sports equivalent as espoused by tribal Custom or Law.

SECTION. 2.

The Persons within Pacifica shall consist of two primary classes, to wit: Adult Persons and Minor Persons. Adult Persons shall consist of all persons who shall have attained to the age of eighteen years and upward, or have become emancipated according to law in either the territories of Pacifica or of another jurisdiction (I.e. a foreign nation or other sovereign). Minor Persons shall consist of all Persons who shall not have attained the age of eighteen years, unless they are emancipated youth (according to the Pacifican custom of reciprocation in [negative] rights under international laws, for all Persons).

The Citizens of Pacifica shall consist of two primary classes, to wit: Adult citizens and Minor citizens. Adult Citizens shall consist of all Citizens who shall have attained to the age of eighteen years and upward, or have become emancipated according to law. Minor Citizens shall consist of all Citizens who shall not have attained the age of eighteen years, unless they are emancipated youth (according to the Pacifican principle of reciprocation in [negative] rights under interstate laws, for all Citizens).

SECTION. 3.

All Pacifican Citizens and nationals, as well as all non-citizens while they are on the national soil of Pacifica, except for duly certified foreign diplomats, are subject to this Constitution and constitutional laws as well as the laws under the territory or state in which they are located, and by serving as an active member of a jury, voting, or excercising public power, or receiving a public benefit or protection explicitly applied for or sought, shall be deemed as having taken an oath or affirmation to “Preserve, protect, promote, and defend, the sovereignty of Pacifica’s People, and their Constitution, against all enemies, foreign or domestic, to the best of their ability”. The grounds for this requirement are based upon the concept for which you must give in order that you intend to receive, and that all power implicitly retains duty.

ARTICLE X

This Mutual Friendship and Assistance Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into by and between:
The Sovereign Nation of Pacifica and the Free People thereof, a self-governing political entity ("Pacifica"),
and,
PARTY B: All Native American Indigenous Peoples and Nations, collectively and individually, each recognized as a sovereign indigenous nation ("the Indigenous Nations"),
Collectively referred to as "the Parties".

WHEREAS, Pacifica recognizes all Indigenous Nations as sovereign entities with inherent rights to self-governance, territorial integrity, and independence from external authority;
WHEREAS, the Indigenous Nations possess original sovereignty over their traditional lands and territories, which sovereignty predates and exists independently of any treaty relationship with Pacifica;
WHEREAS, the Parties desire to establish a framework for mutual friendship, defense, peaceful coexistence, and cooperative relations, including free and open commerce between sovereign nations;
WHEREAS, the Parties acknowledge the historical precedent of the original 1621 Peace Treaty between the Plymouth Colony and the Wampanoag Nation;
WHEREAS, the Parties recognize the principles of the Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States (1933) as applicable to all sovereign entities under international law;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:

Section. 0.

Citizens who are considered Tribal Natives are entitled to rights of Tribal and Territorial Sovereignty, Treaty Rights, Reserved Rights Doctrine, and a Trust Relationship wherein the National government of Pacifica has a duty to protect the tribes and represent their interests in interstate and international ordeals or issues (I.e., concerns), provided the courts have necessary legislative and executive authorities to effect that duty, and consent of the tribes involved.

Treaties with Native Tribes shall be honored, either with the original land which had been taken through conquest or appropriation from them being returned to them, land of equivalent value deeded to them, or money equal in current value to the land taken paid to them. Conveyance or payment shall be to a trust for each tribe controlled by that group. Administrative supervision of tribes shall be terminated, and not be revived.

All Nationally recognized Pacifican Native Tribes are forever sovereign, defined by their treaty or other legal relationship to Pacifica, with rights to decide their own government and laws, and to enforce those laws on all residents and visitors within their territory.

All Pacifican Native Tribes have permanent and absolute rights to their current reservation lands, forever. All State lands, or lands reacquired by Pacifican Native Tribes, that are within these tribes’ historically recognized boundaries, or protected by treaty, will be part of their reservations. All sacred sites of Nationally recognized Pacifican Native tribes shall be returned immediately, or protected by State partnership if requested by tribes.

Section. 1.

Subsection 1.1 — Prohibition of Hostile Acts
Neither Party, nor any agent, member, citizen, or affiliate acting on behalf of either Party, shall commit, authorize, or permit any act of violence, aggression, or harm against the persons, property, or territorial integrity of the other Party.

Subsection 1.2 — Affirmative Duty to Prevent Harm
Each Party shall exercise due diligence to prevent members under its jurisdiction from causing harm to the other Party and shall take reasonable measures to maintain peaceful relations and friendship.

Subsection 1.3 — Recognition of Indigenous Sovereignty
Pacifica expressly recognizes that:
(a) Each Indigenous Nation possesses inherent sovereignty over its traditional lands and territories
(b) Such sovereignty is not derived from, granted by, or dependent upon this Agreement or any action of Pacifica
(c) The Indigenous Nations retain full authority over their internal affairs, governance, and territorial jurisdiction without interference from Pacifica
(d) This Agreement creates no power in Pacifica to impede upon, diminish, or regulate the sovereign authority of any Indigenous Nation within its indigenous sovereign territory

Section. 2.

Subsection 2.1 — Primary Jurisdiction Based on Territorial Sovereignty
(a) When an offense is committed within the indigenous sovereign territory of an Indigenous Nation, that Indigenous Nation shall retain exclusive primary jurisdiction for investigation and prosecution.
(b) When an offense is committed within the territorial jurisdiction of Pacifica, Pacifica shall retain exclusive primary jurisdiction for investigation and prosecution.
(c) When an offense involves members of both Parties or occurs in areas of shared use, the Parties shall confer to determine appropriate jurisdiction based on principles of fairness, territorial sovereignty, and the interests of justice.

Subsection 2.2 — Extradition Upon Request
Either Party may request extradition of an offender to the territory of the requesting Party for prosecution under the following conditions:
(a) The requesting Party shall submit a formal written extradition request to the competent authorities of the other Party, detailing:
The identity of the accused
The specific offense(s) charged
Supporting evidence establishing probable cause
The applicable laws under which prosecution is sought
(b) The requested Party shall review the extradition request in accordance with its own legal procedures and may grant or deny extradition at its sole discretion as an expression of its sovereign authority.
(c) Extradition shall be granted only for offenses that constitute crimes under the laws of both Parties (principle of dual criminality).
(d) The requesting Party shall guarantee that the extradited individual shall receive due process, fair trial, and humane treatment consistent with recognized standards of justice.

Subsection 2.3 — Courts of Pacifica
All references to judicial proceedings, prosecutions, or legal actions within Pacifica shall be conducted before the competent courts of Pacifica having proper jurisdiction over the matter, in accordance with Pacifica's laws and constitutional procedures.

Subsection 2.4 — Alternative: Prosecution in Place of Extradition
If extradition is denied, the requested Party agrees to prosecute the offender under its own laws for conduct substantially similar to the offense charged by the requesting Party, as an exercise of its own sovereign judicial authority.

Subsection 2.5 — Restitution and Remedies
The Party with jurisdiction over an offender shall ensure that:
(a) Victims of the offense receive appropriate restitution or compensation
(b) Stolen or damaged property is restored to its rightful owners
(c) Remedies are enforced through available legal mechanisms

Section. 3.

Subsection 3.1 — Collective Defense Obligation
The Parties recognize that an armed attack or act of unjust aggression against either Party shall be considered a threat to the peace and security of both Parties.

Subsection 3.2 — Mutual Aid Commitment
Each Party pledges to:
(a) Provide military, logistical, or other assistance to the other Party when requested
(b) Act to meet common dangers in accordance with its own constitutional or governance processes
(c) Maintain and develop its individual and collective capacity to resist armed attack
(d) Come to the aid of the other Party in times of natural disaster, humanitarian crisis, or other emergencies upon request

Subsection 3.3 — Armed Forces and Equipment
(a) General Rule: When visiting the territory of the other Party, members of either Party shall leave their weapons, firearms, bows, arrows, or other offensive instruments at designated locations or in the custody of appropriate authorities.
(b) Exception for Mutual Defense and Assistance Operations: Notwithstanding subsection (a), weapons and defensive equipment may be brought into the territory of the other Party when:
(i) Prior written consent has been obtained from the host Party's authorized representative
(ii) The purpose is for joint defense operations, training exercises, emergency response, or mutual assistance to threats against either Party
(iii) The specific types, quantities, and bearers of weapons are identified in the consent authorization
(iv) The visiting Party agrees to comply with any conditions or restrictions imposed by the host Party regarding the use, storage, or deployment of such weapons
(c) Emergency Exception: In cases of imminent threat where prior consent cannot reasonably be obtained, weapons may be brought into territory with immediate notification to the host Party's authorities, followed by formal ratification of the emergency authorization within 48 hours.
(d) Indigenous Sovereign Territory: When Indigenous Nations exercise their sovereign authority to permit armed members or defense forces within their indigenous sovereign territory, such action requires no consent from Pacifica and shall not be impeded by Pacifica, as it is an expression of inherent Indigenous sovereignty.

Section. 4.

Subsection 4.1 — Duty to Inform Confederates
Each Party shall notify its allied nations, confederates, and affiliated entities of the terms of this Agreement to ensure that:
(a) Such allied nations do not commit hostile acts against the other Party
(b) Allied nations may, by mutual agreement, be included in the protections and obligations of this Agreement

Subsection 4.2 — Indigenous Nations' External Relations
Each Indigenous Nation retains the sovereign right to:
(a) Establish relations with other Indigenous Nations
(b) Enter into agreements with other sovereign entities
(c) Maintain its own confederacies and alliances independent of Pacifica

Subsection 4.3 — Third-Party Relations
Neither Party shall enter into any agreement with a third party that would obligate it to act against the interests or security of the other Party.

Section. 5.

Subsection 5.1 — Inherent Sovereignty
Pacifica recognizes and affirms that:
(a) Each Indigenous Nation possesses inherent, original sovereignty over its traditional lands, territories, and waters
(b) Such sovereignty is not derived from any treaty, statute, or action of Pacifica
(c) Indigenous sovereign territory includes all lands traditionally occupied, used, or claimed by each Indigenous Nation, whether or not such lands are currently under the physical control of that Nation
(d) This Agreement does not create, grant, or confer sovereignty upon any Indigenous Nation; it merely recognizes sovereignty that already exists independently

Subsection 5.2 — Non-Interference
Pacifica shall not:
(a) Impede upon the sovereign authority of any Indigenous Nation within its indigenous sovereign territory
(b) Assert jurisdiction over internal matters of Indigenous Nations
(c) Require Indigenous Nations to seek permission from Pacifica for actions within their own indigenous sovereign territory
(d) Use this Agreement or any provision herein as a basis for regulating, limiting, or controlling Indigenous Nations' exercise of their inherent sovereignty

Subsection 5.3 — Territorial Integrity
The boundaries of indigenous sovereign territory shall be determined by each Indigenous Nation according to its own laws, traditions, and historical claims, without interference from Pacifica.

Subsection 5.4 — Montevideo Convention Statehood Criteria
Pacifica recognizes that each Indigenous Nation, as a sovereign entity under international law, possesses the qualifications set forth in Article 1 of the Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States (1933):
(a) Permanent Population: Each Indigenous Nation has a permanent population, which may include both resident and nomadic members, with intention to establish permanent residency within the Nation and to be recognized as its inhabitants
(b) Defined Territory: Each Indigenous Nation has a defined territory, which includes traditional lands, territories, and waters, whether or not borders are contested, provided the territory has sufficient consistency
(c) Government: Each Indigenous Nation has a government that exercises effective authority over its territory and population, without requirement of any special type of government structure
(d) Capacity to Enter into Relations with Other States: Each Indigenous Nation has the capacity to enter into relations with other sovereign entities, including Pacifica and other Indigenous Nations, as an expression of its independent sovereignty

Subsection 5.5 — Political Existence Independent of Recognition
In accordance with Article 3 of the Montevideo Convention:
(a) The political existence of each Indigenous Nation is independent of recognition by Pacifica or any other sovereign entity
(b) Even before recognition, each Indigenous Nation has the right to defend its integrity and independence, to provide for its conservation and prosperity, and consequently to organize itself as it sees fit, to legislate upon its interests, administer its services, and to define the jurisdiction and competence of its courts
(c) The exercise of these rights has no other limitation than the exercise of the rights of other sovereign entities according to international law

Subsection 5.6 — Juridical Equality of Sovereign Entities
In accordance with Article 4 of the Montevideo Convention:
(a) All Indigenous Nations are juridically equal to Pacifica, enjoy the same rights, and have equal capacity in their exercise
(b) The rights of each Indigenous Nation do not depend upon the power which it possesses to assure the exercise of those rights, but upon the simple fact of its existence as a person under international law
(c) Pacifica and all Indigenous Nations are juridically equal, regardless of differences in population, territory, or other characteristics

Subsection 5.7 — Fundamental Rights Not Susceptible to Impairment
In accordance with Article 5 of the Montevideo Convention:
The fundamental rights of Indigenous Nations are not susceptible of being affected in any manner whatsoever by Pacifica or any other entity

Subsection 5.8 — Recognition Unconditional and Irrevocable
In accordance with Article 6 of the Montevideo Convention:
(a) Pacifica's recognition of each Indigenous Nation signifies that Pacifica accepts the personality of that Nation with all the rights and duties determined by international law
(b) Such recognition is unconditional and irrevocable
(c) Recognition does not create sovereignty but acknowledges sovereignty that already exists

Subsection 5.9 — Equal Application of Montevideo Rights to Pacifica
Pacifica acknowledges that:
(a) All rights recognized in this Section apply equally to Pacifica as a sovereign entity under international law
(b) Pacifica possesses the same qualifications under Article 1 of the Montevideo Convention (permanent population, defined territory, government, and capacity to enter into relations with other states)
(c) Pacifica's political existence is likewise independent of recognition by Indigenous Nations or other sovereign entities
(d) Pacifica enjoys juridical equality with all Indigenous Nations, with the same rights and equal capacity in their exercise
(e) The fundamental rights of Pacifica are not susceptible of being affected in any manner whatsoever
(f) The rights and obligations set forth in the Montevideo Convention apply reciprocally to both Pacifica and all Indigenous Nations as equal sovereign entities under international law

Subsection 5.10 — Jurisdiction Over Inhabitants
In accordance with Article 8 of the Montevideo Convention:
(a) The jurisdiction of each Indigenous Nation within the limits of its national territory applies to all inhabitants
(b) Nationals and foreigners are under the same protection of the law and the national authorities of the Indigenous Nation
(c) Foreigners may not claim rights other or more extensive than those of nationals within indigenous sovereign territory
(d) The same principles apply within Pacifica's jurisdiction over its inhabitants

Section 06: INTERNATIONAL COMMERCE AND TRADE

Subsection 6.1 — Preservation of Commerce Rights
Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to:
(a) Reduce, diminish, or impair the rights of international commerce between the Indigenous Nations and Pacifica
(b) Restrict the free exchange of goods, services, or resources between the Parties conducted in accordance with the laws of either jurisdiction
(c) Create any barrier to trade that did not previously exist under applicable international trade principles
Subsection 6.2 — Exchange of Defensive Implements
The Parties expressly recognize that:
(a) Weapons, firearms, defensive implements, and related materials may be exchanged between the Parties through lawful international trade
(b) Such exchanges shall be conducted in accordance with the laws and regulations of the exporting Party and the importing Party as applicable to rules of international trade
(c) Each Party retains sovereign authority to regulate imports and exports within its own jurisdiction, provided such regulations are applied in a non-discriminatory manner and do not unreasonably impede commerce between the Parties
(d) Indigenous Nations retain the right to acquire, possess, and trade defensive implements within their indigenous sovereign territory without interference from Pacifica
Subsection 6.3 — Applicable Trade Laws
Commerce between the Parties shall be governed by:
(a) The laws of Pacifica as applicable to international trade with sovereign nations, for transactions occurring within or originating from Pacifica's jurisdiction
(b) The laws of each Indigenous Nation as applicable to international trade, for transactions occurring within or originating from that Nation's indigenous sovereign territory
(c) Principles of international trade law recognizing the sovereign equality of trading partners
Subsection 6.4 — No Diminishment of Pre-Existing Rights
The Parties affirm that:
(a) This Agreement does not reduce any pre-existing rights of commerce or trade between Indigenous Nations and Pacifica
(b) Indigenous Nations retain all rights to engage in commerce with Pacifica and with other sovereign entities as they have historically exercised
(c) Nothing herein shall be interpreted to require Indigenous Nations to obtain permission from Pacifica to engage in international trade
Subsection 6.5 — Trade Disputes
Any disputes arising from commercial transactions between the Parties shall be resolved:
(a) Through good faith negotiation between the Parties
(b) In accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction governing the transaction
(c) Through mutually agreed arbitration or mediation, if both Parties consent

Section 07: DISPUTE RESOLUTION
Subsection 7.1 — Good Faith Negotiation
Any dispute arising from the interpretation or application of this Agreement shall first be addressed through good faith negotiations between authorized representatives of both Parties.
Subsection 7.2 — Respect for Sovereign Decision-Making
In any dispute resolution process:
(a) Each Indigenous Nation retains the right to determine its own position and actions according to its sovereign will
(b) No Indigenous Nation shall be compelled to accept a resolution that it determines violates its sovereignty or interests
(c) Pacifica recognizes that Indigenous Nations may withdraw from dispute resolution processes at their discretion as an exercise of sovereign authority
Subsection 7.3 — Mediation
If negotiations fail to resolve the dispute within 30 days, the Parties may agree to submit the matter to a mutually acceptable mediator.
Subsection 7.4 — Arbitration
If mediation fails, the Parties may agree to binding arbitration, with each Party selecting one arbitrator and both Parties jointly selecting a third arbitrator to chair the tribunal, provided that no Indigenous Nation shall be required to submit to arbitration against its will.

Section 08: AMENDMENTS AND MODIFICATIONS
Subsection 8.1 — Amendment Process
This Agreement may be amended or modified only by written instrument signed by authorized representatives of Pacifica and the affected Indigenous Nation(s).
Subsection 8.2 — Individual and Collective Application
(a) This Agreement applies collectively to all Indigenous Nations that choose to be bound by its terms
(b) Each Indigenous Nation may, through its own sovereign decision-making process, determine whether to adopt this Agreement
(c) Individual Indigenous Nations may, by mutual agreement with Pacifica, add individualized provisions addressing specific matters relevant to that Nation
Subsection 8.3 — No Impediment to Sovereignty
No amendment or modification of this Agreement shall be interpreted as granting Pacifica authority to impede upon the inherent sovereignty of any Indigenous Nation.

Section 09: DURATION AND TERMINATION
Subsection 9.1 — Term
This Agreement shall remain in force indefinitely, unless terminated in accordance with this Section.
Subsection 9.2 — Termination by Pacifica
Pacifica may terminate this Agreement with respect to itself by providing one (1) year written notice to the Indigenous Nations.
Subsection 9.3 — Termination by Indigenous Nations
(a) Any Indigenous Nation may terminate this Agreement with respect to itself at any time, by written notice to Pacifica
(b) Such termination is an exercise of inherent sovereign authority and requires no justification or cause
(c) Termination by one Indigenous Nation shall not affect the Agreement's continued application to other Indigenous Nations
Subsection 9.4 — Effect of Termination
Termination shall not affect:
(a) Ongoing extradition proceedings initiated prior to termination
(b) Obligations arising from acts committed during the term of this Agreement
(c) Any rights or remedies accrued prior to termination
(d) The continued recognition of Indigenous sovereignty, which exists independently of this Agreement
(e) Pre-existing rights of international commerce between the Parties, which exist independently of this Agreement

Section 10: FINAL PROVISIONS
Subsection 10.1 — Recognition of Sovereignty
Pacifica expressly recognizes and affirms:
(a) The inherent, original, and independent sovereignty of all Indigenous Nations
(b) The territorial integrity of indigenous sovereign territory
(c) The right of each Indigenous Nation to self-governance free from external interference
(d) That this Agreement creates no power, authority, or jurisdiction in Pacifica over Indigenous Nations or their indigenous sovereign territory
Subsection 10.2 — Good Faith Performance
The Parties agree to perform all obligations under this Agreement in good faith and in accordance with the principles of mutual respect, friendship, and cooperation.
Subsection 10.3 — Governing Principles
This Agreement shall be interpreted in accordance with:
The inherent sovereign rights of all Parties
Principles of international law applicable to agreements between sovereign entities, including the Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States (1933)
The historical spirit of peaceful coexistence and mutual friendship embodied in the original 1621 Treaty
The principle that Indigenous sovereignty predates and exists independently of this Agreement
Subsection 10.4 — No Diminishment of Rights
Nothing in this Agreement shall be interpreted to:
(a) Diminish, limit, or impair the inherent sovereignty of any Indigenous Nation
(b) Grant Pacifica any authority over Indigenous Nations or indigenous sovereign territory
(c) Create any obligation for Indigenous Nations to seek permission from Pacifica for actions within their own sovereign territory
(d) Impede upon the full and free exercise of Indigenous sovereignty
(e) Reduce rights of international commerce that existed prior to this Agreement
Subsection 10.5 — Execution
This Agreement shall be executed in duplicate, with one copy retained by Pacifica and one copy made available to each Indigenous Nation that chooses to be bound by its terms. The Agreement shall take effect upon signature by authorized representatives of Pacifica and each participating Indigenous Nation.
Subsection 10.6 — Open Accession
Any Indigenous Nation that has not initially agreed to this Article may accede to it at any time through written instrument executed by its authorized representatives, without requiring approval or consent from Pacifica.

ARTICLE XI

SECTION. 1.

Full Faith, Credit, and Respect shall be given in each State to the public Acts, Records, and Judicial Proceedings, every other State, and the Congress may by general Laws prescribe the Manner in which such Acts, Records, and Proceedings, shall be proved, and the Effect thereof, or in the event that congress fail to provide such, then such decision shall be left thereupon the Several States in three-fifths accordance or greater; Full Faith, Credit, and Respect shall be given in each State to the private Contracts, Health Professional Statement/s, Recommendations, and Prescriptions, in addition to the reciprocation of property rights [to and from] every other State, and the Congress may by general Laws prescribe the Manner in which such Contracts, Health Professional Statement/s, Recommendations, and Prescriptions, along with Conveyance or Relocation shall be proved if necessary and suitable/proper, and the Effect thereof, or once again, in the event that congress fail to provide such, such decision shall be left thereupon the Several States in three-fifths accordance or greater.

Each State shall be free and independent, treated as sovereign entities subject only to the Constitution of Pacifica and of their State, as well as the will of their People bound by Just Authority doctrine. The maintenance of their free institutions and the perpetuity of the Union depends upon the preservation of the right of Local self-government, unimpaired to all the States, and self-governance of the People, unimpaired as individuals.

Each State in the Union shall respectively retain every power, jurisdiction, and right, which is not by this Constitution delegated to the Congress of Pacifica or to the departments of the National government.

The Federal union, upon the terms and for the purposes specified in its compact with the several States, shall be conducive to the Life and Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-Security and Self-Defense, Privacy, Property, and Pursuit of Happiness for the members in their compact and the Citizens thereof; The several States composing Pacifica are not united on the principle of unlimited submission to their general government; but that, by compact, under the style and title of a Constitution for Pacifica, and of amendments thereto, they constitute a general government for special purposes, delegated to that government certain definite powers, reserving, each state to itself, the residuary mass of right to their own self-government; and that whensoever the general government assumes un-delegated powers, its acts are un-authoritative, void, and of no force; The government created by this compact, is not made the exclusive or final judge of the extent of the powers delegated to itself, since that would make its discretion, and not the Constitution, the measure of its powers; but that, as in all other cases of compact among powers having no common judge, each party has an equal right to judge for itself, as well of infractions as of the mode and measure of redress; Those who administer the general government [at any level or branch] shall not be permitted to transgress the limits fixed by this compact; Nullification, through judgment by the sovereignties of the several States, or by We the People, of all un-authorized acts done under colour of the instrument of government, shall be the rightful remedy; The commonwealth of Pacifica does declare, that acts, laws, and actions, which are in their opinion, palpable violations of the constitution, may be nullified by the sovereignties of the States; Each State is unequivocally attached to the Union, and to that compact, agreeable to its obvious and real intention, will be among the last to seek its dissolution; Although the commonwealth is a party to the Federal compact and will follow to the laws of the Union, it does at the same time declare, that it will not now, nor ever hereafter, cease to oppose in a constitutional manner, every attempt from what quarter soever offered, to violate the compact of the Union.

Each State shall exercise exclusive Legislative jurisdiction in all Cases whatsoever, over their territory within their own borders, and to exercise like Authority over all Places within their jurisdiction;

SECTION. 2.

The powers, duties, and responsibilities of the Legislative, Executive, and Judicial branches shall be prescribed by the constitution of their State.

SECTION. 3.

Each State shall assign through the legislature Districts, and within them, Counties, which may be further divided into Municipalities, to hold Local, State, and Federal votes and/or elections. At each level, they shall function as a republic with popular constitutionally-bound democratic powers of the People's sovereign will. Each District will be multi-member. The legislature of each State is prohibited from gerrymandering Districts.

Within all the territories of Pacifica, including each State, each piece of privately owned property is its own sub-state, and shall retain its own sovereignty, freedom, and independence, and every power, jurisdiction, and right of such a free State. this shall not impair their obligation to obey the general laws of state and Pacifica in accordance with rule of justice and right, in addition to the principles of Just Naturalism.

SECTION. 4.

By each State entering into Union as Pacifica, they pledge to mutually adhere towards their People a baseline set of responsibilities for their execution, and wield such necessary powers which are outlined in this Section and in other places throughout this Constitution. They shall have the duty to at all times in which they are able, execute the foregoing powers, on behalf of the Citizens of Pacifica. This list is not exhaustive, and is meant to cover the baseline functions in which the common People of Pacifica decide are reasonable and necessary, not to impair just powers of the States extending beyond written here in scope or subject; Any additional responsibilities, powers, and limitations should be decided by each State’s People and integrated together with these into their Individual constitutions:

Each State shall have exclusive power to regulate industry and commerce that takes place exclusively within the jurisdiction of their State;

Each state shall establish an Office for Consumer Rights and Transparency, vested with authority to protect, enforce, and advance the rights of consumers within the several Counties of their State, under the direction and supervision of the Legislature. The purpose of this office is to safeguard the public against fraudulent, misleading, exploitative, deceptive, or harmful commercial practices; to ensure that all products and services offered in their State are represented truthfully; and without producing injury to rights in Persons, Animals, and the Environment, and to uphold the principle that consumers are entitled to full, accurate, and accessible information in the marketplace, to make informed choices and enable their right of economic vote. The mission of the office is to: Promote consumer sovereignty by guaranteeing truthful representation of goods and services; Deter and remediate deceptive and harmful or destructive business practices through enforcement, education, and corrective action; Ensure transparency and fair play in commerce as a cornerstone of fairness, accountability, and trust between buyers and sellers, as well as promoting common good and mutual gain, and preventing predatory business practices like price fixing and price gouging;-and Empower individuals and communities through education on their rights and accessible remedies when harms occur. The official motto of this office shall be: “Truth in Commerce, Freedom in Choice.” The motto reflects the core principle that only when consumers are provided with clear, honest, and complete information can they make free and sovereign choices in the marketplace. Deceptive restrictions, concealment of information, or manipulation of representations are recognized as forms of coercion incompatible with the liberty of the individual, and any injury to rights is unjust;

Each State shall have no power to lay and collect taxes on incomes, regardless of whatever source derived, except as explicitly permitted by this constitution, and for only the purpose/s stated;

Each State shall establish a Department of Revenue, charged with administering the profits of the State’s Department of Goods and Services. Every county, district, and municipality/town/city shall retain the same powers as the State to establish a Department of Revenue and administer revenues from Local Departments of Goods and Services at each level;

Each State shall establish a Department of Finance, to serve as the fiscal policy advisory and to promote long term economic sustainability and responsible resource allocation;

Each State shall establish their respective Publicly-owned State banks, and all State and Local money shall be deposited therein. The State banks will loan and invest its funds exclusively within their State, and shall prioritize sustainable development and enhancing the welfare of all State residents. The State banks shall accept business and personal deposit accounts. All records of the State banks shall be open and public. The right of localities to establish Public banks and financial services is guaranteed, though those institutions shall be regulated by the legislation of Congress and their State. The right of Citizens to establish private banks and financial services is guaranteed, though those institutions shall be regulated by the legislation of Congress and each State. State-chartered banks shall be eligible to receive and loan out federal monies, provided that all such loans are repaid in full with interest, the rate of which shall not exceed a maximum set by law. State banks entrusted with federal funds may issue  national currency such as money, representative notes, or bills of credit, solely as evidence of such loans, provided these instruments are fully backed by the value of the loans and are redeemable in lawful currencies and monies of Pacifica. Congress shall have the power to regulate the maximum permissible interest rate on such loans, ensuring it promotes the general welfare and prevents the concentration of financial power. All privileges and responsibilities herein granted to State banks shall be subject to oversight by Congress, but no law shall be passed granting monopoly or exclusive rights to any single institution or group, in keeping with the principle that government shall not favor the wealthy or powerful over the interests of the people;

Each State shall establish a Department of Goods and Services, and shall have Power to establish facilities, as well as procure resources and labor for the manufacturing and retailing of goods or services desired by the public, to pay for State expenditures that would had otherwise been funded on collected taxes, which Public Sector businesses shall be operated autonomously in like manner to that of a citizen-owned co-op and worker’s council [bicameral stakeholder system] where the people’s co-op house is the representative branch, and the worker council is the senatorial power, in a profit-for-the-public-good venture; but it shall not have the power to conscript the resources or labor of any person; nor shall it use tax dollars to establish or maintain itself, meaning that the ‘Public sector’ businesses established must be operated on their own revenues at their own expense, with any profits not re-invested into them placed into the general fund of their State; The States are encouraged to accept donations from the People, designated by the People, for the purpose of funding the Department of Goods and Services; ‘Public sector’ business shall be subject to the same laws and regulations as Private business, and neither shall hold an exclusive monopoly to operate within Pacifica. The People shall be free to petition through Initiative or Referendum to engage/produce, query, or cease any Operation, action, Product, manufacture, method, or other mode of execution in the Department of Goods and Services as so alike shall the Legislature if in conformity to the will of the People’s Just Authority;

In each State, total outlays for any fiscal year shall not exceed total receipts for that fiscal year. Prior to each fiscal year, the Budget Officer shall transmit to the State Legislature a proposed budget for the State Government for that fiscal year in which total outlays do not exceed total receipts; A Bill to increase revenue shall not become law unless citizens approve this Bill in a referendum;

The Legislature and Gubernor/s of each state shall assemble at least once each year to balance the budget and manage the finances of their State;

[]
In order to secure the technological resilience, economic competitiveness, and continuity of self-government of the People, the several States, each within its own jurisdiction and by their mutual cooperation, may establish and maintain computing infrastructure as a public trust for their Citizens, and may join one with another, by compact, into a Federated Compute Infrastructure, organized upon interoperable, publicly documented, and open-source systems, including open hypervisor, container, orchestration, distributed-storage, and virtual-private-networking software such as, or equivalent to, KVM, Kubernetes, Ceph, WireGuard, IPsec/IKEv2, and open software-defined-networking controllers, no part of which may be enclosed by proprietary restriction, and each part of which shall remain auditable by the People of the several States through their respective representatives and through such independent oversight as the States, or Congress by their consent, shall establish, by means of an append-only and independently verifiable record of resource transactions, capacity contributions, utilization, and network-connection metadata; and any person, enterprise, cooperative, institution, or government within a participating State, meeting technical and security standards published by that State or by interstate compact, may contribute to the Infrastructure any computing capacity whatsoever, general-purpose processors, memory, persistent and distributed storage, graphics and artificial-intelligence accelerators, application-specific and field-programmable hardware, proof-of-work mining hardware, edge and embedded devices, and the networking, network-interface, and hardware-security equipment necessary to secure and interconnect the same, and may draw such capacity from the Infrastructure, in whatsoever form it is offered, whether as virtual machine, virtual private server, container, bare-metal allocation, distributed cluster for training, inference, high-performance, or mining workloads, or serverless function, through open and voluntary exchange, no owner of hardware being divested of title by virtue of participation, nor any person or State compelled to participate or to remain within any compact against their will; and every such person, enterprise, cooperative, and institution shall be free to sell or lease access to its own computing resources and to its own virtual private networking, encrypted tunneling, and zero-trust access services upon the exchange at prices of its own choosing, negotiated freely with purchasers, that the People and their private and cooperative associations may deal one with another as a market among themselves and not merely as suppliers to the States; and a participating State, or an authority established by compact among participating States, may offer computing or networking capacity for sale within the exchange upon the same terms available to private participants, at prices no lower than fair market value as independently determined under standards coordinated by Congress, so that the presence of any State government in the exchange shall be that of a competitor upon equal terms and never that of a destroyer of private enterprise; and Congress shall have power to coordinate among the several States and any compacts they form, to establish uniform technical, interoperability, and security standards, including minimum standards for encryption protocols, key lengths, authentication methods, and certificate issuance, which standards shall themselves remain open and shall not vest control of authentication in any single entity, for the exchange of computing capacity through this system across State lines and with foreign nations, to facilitate settlement of such exchanges, and to encourage, but not compel, the participation of every State, provided that Congress may itself own, administer, or operate computing infrastructure under this system paradigm while a participating State requests its facilitation, given it has an environmentally responsible method of implementation and maintenance, such as using ocean-floor-based water-cooled data centers powered partially by wave-energy harvesters and ocean-based geothermal; and each participating State shall maintain, or secure through compact, sovereign computing capacity equal to not less than 8.333333333333 per centum (~8.333%) of the total computing capacity privately available through this system within its jurisdiction, and there shall be permanently reserved, from the whole of the computing capacity available within each participating State with regard to ownership, not less than 5.555555555555 per centum (~5.555%) thereof from the public capacity for the free or subsidized use of its People, allocated under proportional and transparent rules established by that State or by compact, both such reservations to be enforced at the point of scheduling and not merely by subsequent accounting; and exchanges of computing capacity under this Provision, whether within a State or across State lines, may be settled in Pacifican money, Treasury legal tender representative notes, constitutional bills of credit, or such other constitutional monetary instruments as Congress or the several States may by law authorize, no exchange being denied settlement solely for its choice among such legal instruments; and no agency of any government, State or federal, shall inspect, retain, or condition access to the data, workloads, or network communications of any person using infrastructure established under this Provision absent a warrant or order issued according to law, all such communications being secured end-to-end by tenant-controlled encryption such that infrastructure operators and governments alike may observe only connection metadata, timestamps, endpoints, and data volumes, and never payload content, this limitation not to be suspended or narrowed except as this Constitution otherwise provides for the suspension of like protections; and all revenue derived from the sale of computing or networking capacity by a participating State, whether within Pacifica or to foreign nations, shall be treated as public infrastructure receipts of that State, held in a segregated and publicly reported account, and applied exclusively to the expansion, security, and universal accessibility of its Infrastructure, including the hardening and redundancy of its virtual private networking and zero-trust access systems, and to no other purpose, except as that State's law may otherwise for cause direct, any compact formed under this Provision being free to provide for the equitable sharing of revenue among its members; and the several States, and Congress within the coordinating power herein granted, shall have power to enforce this Provision by appropriate legislation, including the establishment of technical standards, marketplace rules, procurement procedures for hardware security modules and other security-critical equipment, decentralized or multiply-rooted systems of certificate authority so that no single entity may control authentication across the Infrastructure, and independent bodies for oversight, pricing, and dispute resolution, provided that no legislation of Congress under this Provision shall diminish the primacy of the States in establishing and administering their own infrastructure and network-security policy, nor the openness, auditability, or non-displacing character of the Infrastructure as guaranteed herein.
[]

Each State shall establish a Department of State Treasury. Publicly-owned Local Banks of a given State may elect to serve as partial-extensions of the State treasury [with the consent of the Legislature and approval of the Gubernor/s], in that they may hold deposits of State government money and legal tender, distribute its money and legal tender for it as the State Legislature shall decide, and freely exchange the legal tender for lawful money with all parties operating in a lawful manner with them [including the People of their State and with the Pacifica of Sovereign Persons], and vice versa, as well as fungibly in-between notes or moneys, with a one-to-one ratio of interchangeability with eachother, in the case of State dollars, in accordance with this Constitution and the laws in the legislature of Congress and of their State;

Each State shall establish a Department of Industry and Commerce, concerned with promoting economic growth. Among its tasks are gathering economic and demographic data for business and government decision-making, and helping to set industrial standards. This organization’s main purpose is to create jobs, promote economic growth, encourage sustainable development and improve standards of living for all State residents. The mission of the department is to “promote job creation and improved living standards for all State residents by creating an infrastructure that promotes economic growth, technological competitiveness, and sustainable development, and to foster, promote, and develop the National and State commerce.”;

Each State shall establish a Department of Statistics, to serve as the central statistical authority on primary data collection in their State, by conducting entirely voluntary and informedly consented to, censuses and community surveys on different sectors of their State’s economy, such as population, housing, agriculture, fisheries, and business. It shall collect, compile, analyze, and publish statistical information on economic, social, demographic, political affairs, and general affairs of the People in their State;

Each State shall establish a Department of Public Works and Internal Improvements, tasked with producing construction and infrastructure projects, such as highways, dams, ports, and intrastate-networks, financed by public funds and constructed by the government for the benefit or use of the [general] public;

Each State shall establish a Department of Transportation, which will establish and manage public resources of roads, waterways, aero-space facilities, and outer-space launch-pads and interplanetary, interstellar, and intergalactic, but not inter-dimentional, travel/transit systems. It shall be under the authority of the People to grant or limit the use of such [vehicular/craft and traversal/teleportation] technologies or regulations implemented by the government for public purpose, and no government agent deploy such technology except as needed to properly execute the laws of their State and of the Union. Each State shall provide under this Department, intra-state bus and high-speed rail services to connect disparate cities on the intra-state highways and within the bounds of their State upon the Federal inter-state highways and railways, while providing adequate cargo storage space for personal property, running potable water, housing and equipment standard electricity and interfaces (such as 120EvoltAC 50Hz and 5Evolt/9Evolt/12Evolt USB fast-charge adaptive or power-delivery smart charger without data-lines aside from charger negotiation, and isolated powerline to prevent USB-jacking), internet and GPS beacon over Single-Wire, Radiant, Bluelink, and WiFi/Wireless Network, ventilation, and environmental regulation such as air conditioning and heaters as well as air filtration and window-defogging, and additionally, lavatories for all passengers and staff, as well as a host kitchenette and meals provided as premium services. The right of the People to travel the public ways of roads, waterways, aerospace, and the [terranullius] way of outer-space shall not be obstructed, nor retarded, or rescinded, neither any provision interactive to this one be obscured in such a way as to impact the ability of a free Person coming and going as they decide in their own private manner, though the Jurisdiction to capture fleeing criminals may be ascertained by the Rules of the Air, Sea, and Space, and Terranulius, as well as to Maritime [Interstate] Law Enforcement measures and acts which may be passed by Congress within Due Process of Law. The right of People to establish Private transportation resources and services is guaranteed;

Each State shall see to it that sufficient funding is provided necessary to establish and maintain adequate and cost-effective public transportation within each municipality, and promote timely transportation that is broadly accessible to the People within the towns and cities they may occupy or visit. The State may subsidize public transportation to reduce the cost for riders beyond the standard at-cost rate;

Municipal governments in each State shall establish, fund, and continuously maintain a Free Bicycle Loan Program that offers low-income residents access to bicycles for temporary personal transportation without rental charge. Each municipality shall either directly administer the program or contract with public or private entities to do so. They shall ensure that bicycles are reasonably available throughout the jurisdiction for purposes including, but not limited to: commuting to work or school, running errands, attending medical or social appointments, and engaging in physical activity that promotes personal wellness and public health. Participation in the program may be conditioned only on the provision of a security interest, refundable deposit, guarantor, or comparable form of assurance that is narrowly tailored to protect public property from loss, theft, or damage; Any such condition shall be reasonable in amount, nondiscriminatory in application, transparent in its terms, and promptly released or refunded when the bicycle is returned in accordance with program rules. Municipalities shall further maintain the bicycles in safe operating condition through periodic inspection, repair, and replacement. They shall provide or make available basic safety information regarding lawful and safe bicycle operation on public ways. Municipalities shall prioritize access for persons who lack a private motor vehicle or who reside in neighborhoods underserved by other transportation options. They shall administer the program in a manner that advances the goals of reducing dependence on private automobiles, lowering traffic congestion and associated emissions, enhancing connectivity to public transit systems, fostering active lifestyles, and supporting broader environmental sustainability objectives. Municipalities may finance the Free Bicycle Loan Program from general revenues, transportation-specific fees, dedicated environmental or mobility funds, voluntary contributions, or other lawful sources, provided that no budgetary decision shall wholly extinguish the program or render it merely illusory. The legislature may enact implementing legislation setting baseline standards for safety, accessibility, maintenance, and geographic coverage, granting municipalities technical assistance, or encouraging inter-municipal cooperation; However, no such legislation shall diminish the core obligation created by this Provision to provide a genuine, functional, and substantially equivalent free bicycle loan program to low-income individuals which is grounded in the principles of mobility, equal access, and responsible stewardship of public resources.

Each State shall establish a Communications and Public Access Network Commission, which will establish and manage public resources of [intra-state] government networks, and lease contracts, upon request after review, and to lease their access to the network to industrial and commercial entities, at a [uniform] rate equal to their share of the construction, operation, and maintenance costs entailed in providing them service, as shall be determined and they may be directed by the Legislature, and at the discretion of the Legislature may be charged an additional uniform amount not exceeding 16.666bar% of the base cost, with such leases granted for the conduction of regular business activities (not those activities which are subletting access, or selling services based on core dependency, to the Public network, e-commerce excepted);

Each State shall provide for free and open access to the general Public (in a non-commercial and non-industrial capacity) for all public cellular and wireless or single-wire networks which can connect to the internet that are deployed by the public body that are available from a public place which are not for Emergency or State security purpose. They shall also deploy a telephony database administered for the benefit of the people to get free cellular calling including short messaging services and multimedia messages, internet accessibility, and access to the serval Network in times of emergency;
