ARTICLE XIII

That the true Purpose of government is to secure the People and their Rights from assault and infringement, there shall be conveined, within two years from the ratification of this Constitution, to be a declaration or bill of rights asserting, and securing from encroachment, the essential and unalienable rights of the People in some such manner as follows from the will of them (the People).

SECTION. 0.

All external action starts with the individual self. There is always a requirement of the self to choose to initiate any action. Without a physically tangible form of initiation by the Individual, they cannot interfere with others. People can only ever possibly be coerced/extorted by others, their minds cannot be manually over-ridden.

Every person shall have the right to be free from extortion, defined as any demand for property, money, or services under threat of unlawful harm, coercion, or abuse of official power, whether by private individuals or government authorities. No law, regulation, or official act shall permit or enable the obtaining of property, money, or services by means of threats, intimidation, or abuse of authority, including but not limited to actions "under color of official right". Any person subjected to extortion, whether by private parties or public officials, shall have standing to seek immediate judicial relief and restitution, and all such acts shall be prosecuted as felonies. This right shall not be construed to prohibit lawful negotiation or voluntary exchange, provided no threat of illegal action or misuse of official power is involved.

There are certain natural rights, of which men, when they form a social compact, cannot deprive or divest their posterity; among which are the enjoyment of life and liberty, with the means of acquiring, possessing and protecting property, and pursuing and obtaining happiness and safety, as well as to health and [a]religious dignity and worship [or the lack thereof]. That government ought to be instituted for the common benefit, protection, and security of the people; and that the doctrine of non-resistance against arbitrary power and oppression is absurd, slavish, and destructive of the good and happiness of mankind.

All Persons are universally endowed un-assaultable un-serverable fundamental inherent un-alienable in-separable in-violate essential omnipresent rights which exist in and at all locations of space and time in any reality, and within all frontiers of any simulations and/or consciousness, for all people, no matter their type or kind, and cannot be negotiated to compromise, transferred, waived, surrendered, suspended, revoked, denied, or otherwise assailed, for any reason whatsoever, except for limited causes and purposes whereupon lawful conviction of a crime by a jury of 12 supervised by a judge, under due process of the law of the land or a lawfully prescribed punishment and/or jury vetted court order, specifying limited terms and conditions, for upon which such restrictions may be placed under a ‘compelling and justified public purpose’ in protecting the rights of another, in conformity to this constitution and also in conformity to the constitution of their State as relevant; No individual shall have their liberty restricted except upon clear and compelling public purpose justified underneath the limitation of power in government and in accordance to all the rights of Persons, and of the People of Pacifica, and of each State.

All natural rights come from the universe, are inherent to the Autonomy/Independence in self-organizing beings as well as to the Creativity of Persons, and in their true state of nature, are equal in all and the same everywhere; Their synthesis in law derives from self-evident principles, NOT from speculative principles, nor from facts; a natural right has no logical necessity, rather, it rests directly or indirectly upon the evidence of experience, and from abstract reason. The purpose of enumerating rights is to formally produce a framework to recognize and protect the People’s, their guest/s'[s], and visitor/s'[s] essential individual characteristic needs for freedom necessary to their primary and all other level functions, namely, for promoting the legal defense of their life, liberty, and property, from any source of usurpation, oppression, and tyranny, whether from the public or private “natural criminal” elements, being those individuals or aggregations of them acting unlawfully or in error, and thereby constituting a “natural injustice”.

There are no rights but those that exist for all people, as Individuals. All rights are based on the truth of self-ownership. No third party can take away an individual’s rights, and no government permission is needed to have and use these rights. The only time rights may sometimes be taken away are in individual cases if required to stop the violator from violating the equal rights of others. Therefore: Rights are those things where the individual is justified in using Force to defend: Life and Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security [and freedom to secure others] and Self-defense [and freedom to defend others], Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness. Individuals do not need to demonstrate to Government agents or officers/officials that some special need exists in order to exercise a naturally, constitutionally, Common Law, contractually, or legislatively conferred right. No permission is necessary to need to use rights, period. there might be narrow exceptions carved out in law for incompetent youth to require direction by their parents and those restrictions based within the proscribed age ranges for the ability to consent to sexual activities and to engage in the use of [controlled] psychoactive substances, as according to a constitution

That the powers of government may be re-assumed by the people, whensoever it shall become necessary to their happiness: That the rights of the States respectively to nominate and appoint all State officers, and every other power, jurisdiction, and right, which is not by the said Constitution clearly delegated to the Congress of Pacifica, or to the departments of government thereof, remain to the people of the several States, or their respective State governments, to whom they may have granted the same; and that those clauses in the said Constitution, which declare that Congress shall not have or exercise certain powers, do not imply, that Congress is entitled to any powers not given by the said Constitution; but such clauses are to be construed, either as exceptions to certain specified powers, or as inserted merely for greater caution.

That elections of representatives in the Legislature ought to be free and frequent — and all men having sufficient evidence of permanent common interest with and attachment to the community, ought to have the right of suffrage: And no aid, charge, tax, or fee, can be set, rated or levied upon the people, without their own consent, or that of their representatives, so elected; nor can they be bound by any law, to which they have not in like manner, assented for the public good.

Each individual person has the right to maintain and control his or her own LIFE, FREEDOM, and Personal PROPERTY.

FORCE is only sometimes justified, and in such instance, is used in order to defend someone’s Life, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security [and freedom to secure others] and Self-defense [and freedom to defend others], Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness; Since GOVERNMENTS naturally grow over time, this Constitution forbids that growth, so that the least amount of FORCE needed is used (to defend Life, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security [and freedom to secure others] and Self-defense [and freedom to defend others], Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness) and the greatest amount of FREEDOM is preserved; All people are permitted to arm themselves with whatever weapons they believe is needed to defend themselves and others, with the exception of nuclear, radiological, chemical, biological, massively destructive, or any other “unjust weapon/s”. Private PROPERTY owners are permitted to further restrict weapons within their boundaries for the safety of themselves, their PROPERTY, or any other rights, THOUGH BY DOING SO, THEY ARE OBLIGATED TO GUARANTEE [the] Safety of Persons within against all injury they might had been able to avoid by having the means to defend themselves or others; All PROPERTY owners have the right to expel anyone on their PROPERTY, or deny access to their PROPERTY, for any reason they desire, except to militia or governmental law enforcement under presentment of a valid warrant presented to the ingress pole or marker for at least twenty-four hours, where Mail is to be delivered and an officer of law, EMT/paramedic, or fireman is free to go up to in order to request access to the property or issue a notice, unless they have prior explicit consent for the Public Safety Officers of those types to enter their home in exigency, which must be clearly marked. Individuals may disagree with the reason the PROPERTY owner gives or may think the reason is invalid, but this does not justify violating another Person’s PROPERTY.

Neither the GOVERNMENT of Pacifica nor any organization has any rights except for those rights which exist for each individual person; The GOVERNMENT may not use FORCE, except the minimum needed to stop the unjust use of FORCE, MURDER, RAPE, KIDNAPPING, or THEFT (as defined in this Constitution).

Consent must be recorded in a way that it can be proven to the world that consent was indeed given. If individuals are accused of using FORCE, they shall be presumed innocent until proven guilty, but consent is assumed not to have been given unless it can be proven. If individuals are shown to have used FORCE, they must prove their self-security [or freedom of securing others] or self-defense [or freedom of defense of others] justification or else be in violation of the limitation on FORCE, though the State is burdened with the discharge of Evidence to the contrary of a self-security/self-defense claim.

Consent cannot be given to certain subject areas until after a certain age, and are provided here, other than are as elsewise provided by this Constitution:
LIFE: You can give consent regarding your LIFE as an adult class citizen (agree to assisted suicide, et cetera). You can defend your LIFE at any age.
FREEDOM: You can give consent to give up your FREEDOM/LIBERTY by using addictive substances, or trade your own labor for a fixed term or renewable number of them, in exchange for products or services (indentured servitude or debt), et cetera… as an adult class citizen, on condition that an end-date is specified in the contract. (Overcoming addictions acquired will be an individual responsibility.)
PROPERTY: You can give consent regarding PROPERTY (minus your own body) at age 10 (your Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s can provide the consent until that age), including the right to real estate and personal property, but the individuals ability to control, sell or mortgage that property is limited until they reach the age of majority, allowing minors to benefit from property while shielding them from the risks of premature disposition, in accordance with law laid down by the legislature within conformity to this constitution. You can provide un-restricted (I.e. not limited by law) consent regarding your body as an adult class citizen.
Consent can be legally granted to another (like “power of attorney”) if the person wishes, after that person is old enough to legally give that consent themself. Granted consent may be revoked by the Grantor at any time, which process may be defined by law.

In all things, consent is required to be documented in a way that would hold up as evidence in court if needed.

GOVERNMENT shall not have any rights to privacy. GOVERNMENT must provide timely public visibility into all actions it performs; Individuals may choose to implement privacy, but not at the cost of another individual’s rights to his or her own LIFE/Heath, FREEDOM/Liberty/Autonomy/Independence, Self- or Another’s- Security, Self- or Another’s- Defense, or PROPERTY. Privacy is best achieved by the people having control over their own PROPERTY.

There will be no EXTRADITION from Pacifica. The GOVERNMENTS of foreign nations which seek individuals, currently in Pacifica, who broke those foreign nation’s laws, may choose to arrest them in their respective nations, but they should not come to Pacifica seeking to arrest those people in Pacifica unless they themselves desire to be arrested, neither should they expect Pacifica to EXTRADITE said individuals.

Representatives of foreign nations are welcome to visit the territories of Pacifica, with consent from the federal district or State which they wish to be present, as long as they abide by the laws of the respective jurisdictions of Pacifica [including sub-States] and do not threaten another individual’s LIFE, FREEDOM, or PROPERTY. No individual, including the representatives of other nations, in Pacifica are given special rights that are not also equally available to all individuals within the jurisdiction of Pacifica, or of the State in question. Representatives of other nations will be required to abide by laws in accordance with this Constitution of Pacifica, just like everyone else.

Any use of FORCE or GOVERNMENT action not justified in this Constitution is forbidden and is in violation of individual rights; Any laws/regulations/executive-orders/et_cetera passed in Pacifica that are in conflict with this Constitution or otherwise repugnant to it are considered null, void, and invalid, and shall not be recognized by Pacifica’s courts, security forces (police, army, et cetera), or residents.

It is the greatest civic duty of the People for them to preserve and protect the equal rights of others [whom are non-aggressors], even in the case of perhaps disagreeable, though nonetheless just conduct, of an Individual through the exercise of their rights. All people have the freedom from retaliation for exercising any of their rights, guarantees, or privileges. Both public and private actors/parties owe an obligation to any other entity they may interact or transact with to uphold the mutual natural and constitutional rights in the other or others, animals, and nature.

The freedoms and rights guaranteed to the People by this Constitution shall be maintained by the constant endeavor of the People.

No one shall be excluded from a Public place on account of exercising their rights, including them carrying arms, protest, disability including mental illness, or exercising their religion peaceably.

SECTION. 0.5.

The rights protected by this Constitution shall be the highest authority of law throughout Pacifica, and all governmental functions & actions or laws produced therewith, as well as all contractors with the government, and those cooperating with either, therefore shall be subordinate to them. This government shall at all times strictly adhere and be held accountable to uphold “Just Naturalism”, meaning Natural Rights, Natural Justice, and the Independence/Autonomy of Persons, Animals, and Nature (I.e. the "Environment").

The rights protected by the Constitution of Pacifica are the rights of natural Persons and do not extend to for-profit corporations, limited liability companies, or other artificial entities established for business purposes or to promote business interests under the laws of any State, Pacifica, or any foreign State. People, Peoples, Person, Persons, Individual, or Individuals as used in this Constitution does not include corporations, limited liability companies, or other artificial entities established by the laws of any State, Pacifica, or any foreign State, and such commercial entities established under law are subject to such regulation as the People, through their elected State and Federal representatives in the legislative process, deem reasonable and are otherwise consistent with the powers of government under this Constitution, and do not limit the freedom of speech or the press.

All Persons are born equally free and independent and have certain natural, essential, inherent, absolute, self-regulating, and unalienable rights and powers stemming from therewith, among which may be reckoned the right of enjoying and defending their lives and liberties; of acquiring, possessing, and protecting property; and of seeking and obtaining their safety, health, and happiness; in all just ways. In enjoying these rights, all Persons recognize corresponding responsibilities. All persons are entitled to the full and unrestrained use of all their natural and acquired powers and capacities; but such use by the individual, or by aggregations of individuals, shall never extend to infringement upon, or abridgment of, the same use in other persons. Rights are neither collective nor additive in character, and no group can possess rights in excess of those belonging to its individual members. In accordance to Just Authority doctrine, rights cannot be removed or reduced, even through popular will by initiative or referendum.

Every generation is equal in rights to generations which preceded it, including to self-determination and self-governance, by the same rule that every individual is born equal in rights with his contemporary; Whether or not Individuals and Governments will heed to these rights and conduct themselves within the limitation in their actions drawn up around them by the rights of others does not invalidate that rights are inherent in Personhood and Nature itself.

Universal unalienable natural rights to life, liberty, property, self-ownership, and pursuit of justice and happiness inhere in every individual from birth, vesting moral primacy in the rights-holder as the sole legitimate decider over their exercise, absent aggression toward others. Sagacity and capacity naturally evolve and improve on an individual basis, a gradual process no mere law can define or enforce without inherent fault or arbitrariness or exception in fact+virtue. No external authority, paternalistic or otherwise, may justly override this sovereignty through subjective assessments; instead, parents provide the initial best determination of readiness, while courts intervene upon petition by the individual [subjected] (child or youth below age of majority) for restoration of exercise, injunction permissive in favour towards rights, or a finding of emancipatory competence and stability. This principle demands tolerance for harm-free expressions of liberty, ensuring civil order rests on voluntary consent and contextual judgment rather than rule by supposed superiors.

The People of Pacifica have the sole and exclusive right of governing themselves, as a free nation, composed of sovereign and independent States; and to alter and abolish their Constitutions and form of government whenever they may deem it necessary to their Safety in Life and Protection of their Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Security and Defense against aggressors violating their or another’s Rights, Privacy, protecting the just procurement and defense of Property, and Happiness, provided, such change be not repugnant to the core [constitutionally restrained] Republican and anti-feudal neo-libertarian values of the Constitution of Pacifica [as first ratified and as may be amended]; There is no requisite that their constitutions be Socially Democratic as envisioned by the original Constitution of Pacifica, but their composition should always protect the rights and interests of the People as Individuals through a ‘Constitutional Republic’, rather than conform to “the whims of a majority”, as found in a ‘Pure Democracy’, as there is no greater minority than the Individual.

The community has the right, under this Constitution, to organize and maintain government, by which every Individual shall be protected in the exercise of personal rights, and prevented from interfering with those of others; But by organizing government the people shall surrender no rights.

The essence of fundamental rights are inviolable.

Fundamental rights must be upheld throughout the legal system. Whoever acts on behalf of the state is bound by fundamental rights and is under a duty to contribute to their implementation. Fundamental rights may not be negotiated away, regardless of frontier, circumstance, or other reason.

The People shall not be prevented from enjoying any of the fundamental human rights. These fundamental human rights guaranteed to the People by this Constitution shall be conferred upon the People of this and future generations as eternal and inviolate rights.

At all times, the natural rights of the People as Individuals shall trump any aspect of function in or execution of government, at either the National or State level.

The authorities shall ensure that [fundamental] rights, where appropriate, apply to interactions and relationships among private persons; To the extent that one enters contracts through with which one transfers away some aspect of their dominion of [such] rights, they at all times retain the option of rightful exit out of such a contract that restores those rights immediately, though they may be subject to restitution for damages or repayment for received goods or services rendered by such contract which were not reciprocated by its terms, subject to judicial review and discretion insofar as the reasonableness of the contract and its penalty for severance. In general, contracts cannot mute unalienable rights, and only in narrow cases justified by the fair reciprocation of interests may contracts temporarily bar one from exercise in the interest of mutual benefit, until the point in time which the contract may be severed. Assent or consent alone are not justifications for a contract to cause deprivation of rights, and the justification for any deprivation must be plainly written out in the terms of the contract including the reasoning and rationale behind such restriction, as well as delineating in simple terms the benefits and limitations placed upon all party/ies subject to its terms, including by clearly naming the interests that benefit from such reduction and the ways they benefit from them.

The [fundamental] rights enshrined in this Constitution shall not be prohibited, restricted, compromised, abridged, or overridden in pursuance of a/n organization’s, institution’s, business’, company’s, firm’s, corporation’s, or other artificial entities’ inclination/s. At all times, the natural rights of the People as Individuals shall trump any aspect of function in or execution of any privately or publicly operated institution, within the jurisdiction of Pacifica, or within any facility, fort, or installation under its direction.

All of the People shall be respected by the government, under law, as Individuals. Everyone possesses the natural right to Life, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security [and freedom to secure others] and Self-defense [and freedom to defend others], Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness, and nobody under any circumstance shall be circumvented from one’s rights. The natural rights to Life, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security and Self-defense, Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness, shall, to the extent that it does not [demonstrably and directly] interfere with the People’s, their guest[s]’s, and Visitor[s]’s, welfare, then shall be the supreme consideration in legislation and in other governmental affairs, and for which rights at no point at time shall be de-based or discarded as pertinent in the issues of law which may arise under this Constitution or any legislation or ruling of common law made in accordance therewith.

Human life shall be secured by law from violation/assault. The dignity of the human being is sacrosanct. Every Person’s moral and physical integrity shall be inviolable.

The ultimate human dignity to determine the time, place, and manner of one’s death and disposal shall not be denied or abridged by Pacifica or by any Territory, District, County, other Locality, or State. All People are ensured a right to a decent cremation, burial, or composting (by mixing with soil or integrating into a bio-urn), and to choose the location of such [spreading of] ashes, burial, or compost, as will be carried out by their Family, Legal Guardian/s, Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s, or designated Friend/s, unless there is no living Family, Legal Guardian, Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s, or Designated Friend/s, then such cremation, burial, or composting (by mixing cremated remains with soil or integrating into a bio-urn) will be paid for and completed through the State in which they were born or which they were originally Naturalized within, as according to the deceased Citizen’s last testament and will for final disposition.

All People are equal before the law, in accordance to this constitution. They have equal public rights and duties. There can be no discrimination between them in that regard. The highest Duty of all Autonomous Entities is to obey the Universal obligation to “live honestly, to hurt no one, to give to every one his due” towards every other.

Everyone in Pacifica shall enjoy equal rights and freedoms, regardless of age, sex, sexual orientation, body type, color, race, ancestry, nationality or place of origin, language, relationship status such as being with a romantic partner as well as in a marriage or part of a family, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, political or ideological beliefs, intelligence, education, capability or disability, medical history, previous condition of servitude, property, economic situation, social origin, social circumstances, social condition/status or other characteristics, personal background, immutable traits, or other condition, as is defined by this constitution.

No one shall be privileged, favored, prejudiced, deprived of any right, or exempted from any duty, on the basis of age, sex, sexual orientation, body type, color, race, ancestry, nationality or place of origin, language, relationship status such as being with a romantic partner as well as in a marriage or part of a family, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, political or ideological beliefs, intelligence, education, capability or disability, medical history, previous condition of servitude, property, economic situation, social origin, social circumstances, social condition/status or other characteristics, personal background, immutable traits, or other condition, as may be defined by this constitution.

No law shall be passed granting to any citizen or class of citizens privileges or immunities, which, upon the same terms, shall not equally belong to all citizens.

Neither Pacifica nor any State, Territory, or any other Jurisdiction under their dominion, shall make or enforce any law which shall abridge any of the Rights, Privileges, or Immunities of the Citizens of Pacifica or of any State therein, as defined by this constitution; nor shall Pacifica or any State disable the exercise or deprive any Person of Life and health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security [and freedom of securing others] and Self-defense [and freedom to defend others], Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness, without the defendant having first been being irrefragably proven through supplementation of irrefutable evidence to have deprived or intended to deprive the equal right/s of another Person, and only through due process of law, non-absentia, by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve; nor deny to any Person within its jurisdiction, or within any facility, fort, or installation under its direction, the equal protection of the laws.

Equality of rights under the law [made in accordance with this constitution] shall not be denied or abridged by Pacifica or by any State, Territory, or other Jurisdiction under their dominion, on account of age, sex, sexual orientation, body type, color, race, ancestry, nationality or place of origin, language, relationship status such as being with a romantic partner as well as in a marriage or part of a family, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, political or ideological beliefs, intelligence, education, capability or disability, medical history, previous condition of servitude, property, economic situation, social origin, social circumstances, social condition/status or other characteristics, personal background, immutable traits, or other condition. Congress and each State shall have the power to enforce this provision by appropriate legislation.

This Constitution explicitly rejects Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion ("DEI") and its principles as well as Marxist origins, which mandate group-based quotas, preferences, and engineered outcomes to enforce proportional representation regardless of individual merit, as fundamentally contrary to a fair and open civil society grounded in the rule of law and just naturalism. DEI undermines the rule of law by prioritizing collective identities over impartial justice, violating equal protection through discriminatory remedies that favor some groups at others' expense; just naturalism, rooted in the inherent dignity and unequal capacities of free individuals, justifies liberty for a Free People by affirming that natural hierarchies emerge from voluntary effort and competence, not coercive leveling, thereby fostering true prosperity through personal responsibility and innovation rather than resentment and stagnation. Governmental bodies, public services, employment, education, and contracts shall enforce strictly classless, color-blind, as well as sex/gender-unbiased content-neutral policies that eliminate systemic obstacles via meritocratic standards applied equally to all, unleashing the full potential of Pacifica's people.

A person's rights/immunities, freedoms, privileges, or guarantees do not end when they exercise a privilege or receive a governmentally disbursed benefit. No Good, Service, or Benefit, or Privilege derived from the Government shall be require or otherwise seek to sacrifice the Right/s, Immunit[y]/ies, Guarantee/s, or Privilege/s of any Individual.

The claim and exercise of a constitutional right cannot be converted into a crime. No law shall obstruct or penalize the free exercise of rights, privileges, and guarantees protected/provided through/under this Constitution.

The vote of the majority shall never take away the rights of the individual, as listed above, below, and enumerated throughout this Constitution.

Those edicts, frequently cited as ‘laws’, ‘orders’, ‘regulations’, or ‘licenses’, which generally or specially/specifically prohibit any categor[y]/ies of right/s or its/their free exercise and the naturally just effects thereof, are un-constitutional on their face and remain forever invalid, thereby, they shall be instantly rendered null and void in the moment in which they are incited.

Individuals shall not have their rights restricted unless they have been convicted of a criminal act, so far as is necessary for the protection of others [whom are non-aggressors] and to practically affect their sentence of incarceration, nor their lawfully derived property seized (whether [a]spiritual/[a]religious or not), except so far as it is necessary to make restitution to their victim/s and/or to pay the costs of their capture, trial, and housing, or, if it was procured through, or is the gains from, criminal activity or enterprise, but only in the case that they are convicted of a crime through due process of law, by unanimous verdict of a jury of twelve in a court of law of proper jurisdiction. Limitations or restrictions on the exercise of any of a Person’s rights can only be lawfully enacted and enforced if the Individual is currently [lawfully] incarcerated, on parole or probation, or is subject to a court order restricting specific rights or their modalities for the meaningful protection of others [whom are non-aggressors] for which are in of immediate need of such protection from an active and real/[true] threat against their person, property, or other rights.

We the people reserve the right to be secure within every freedom, the whole of the truth as far as transparency into the operation fo the Public Instrument, and assurance that true justice shall be secured and delivered to the People by their Government, and in equal respect by the Private sector in their own manner as self-organization and volition may allow.

SECTION. 1.

All People have a natural right to Life. Part of the natural right to Life is the natural right to Self-security and Self-defense as well as to voluntarily secure or defend or aid in the security or defense of others [whom are non-aggressors] against the initiation of force, including any violation of rights. The right of Life includes the right to procreate, and to treat and resist one’s own illnesses and to [potentially] have another Person voluntarily assist in treating one’s illnesses, as well as the right to end one’s life such as euthanasia [as an adult or terminally ill minor] (this also covers suicide) or to re-initiate one’s life such as resurrection (also covers porting of consciousness/awareness into a non-activated {non-agent; developed under comatose neural-supression} clone or other lawfully-derived surrogate).

All People have a natural right to Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence. Every Person is free to do that which they will, provided that they infringe not the equal freedom of any other Person. All people have the right to self-determination and Autonomy/Independence.

All people have a natural right to the pursuit of privacy.

All People have a natural right to the pursuit of Happiness. Ideally, anybody can pursue the path they choose to embark upon, to their own peril, and to change the path they embark upon, to their own peril. This also covers not suffering or being inflicted any excessive nor torturous, cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing, or unusual form of criminal punishment or treatment. Pursuit of happiness shall include the freedom to make for yourself with your efforts, what you love, for yourself, particularly that which reflects a quality of one’s self or what they hope to become; The right to pursuit of happiness includes the right to define what one peruses as their happiness and to define pursuit of happiness for one self. Pursuit of happiness shall include a person’s own personal definition of full independence.

The right of dissent, as well as freedom from governance (liberty), shall [additionally] entail the allowance of a Person to denounce citizenship of any jurisdiction, including that of Pacifica or the several States, without sacrificing their Natural Rights or being denied the rule of Natural Justice, throughout Pacifica or by any entity under its direction; In all cases, Pacifica and the several States shall adhere to a perpetual guarantee of [mutual] non-aggression.

Immigration laws, enforcement powers, and related authorities of foreign states or supranational entities shall have no jurisdiction, authority, or applicability within the territory of Pacifica, nor against any Pacifican Sovereign Person recognized as a Citizen of Pacifica. No agent or instrumentality, internal or external to Pacifica, may undertake any detention, deportation, investigation, or other enforcement action premised on foreign immigration law against a Pacifican Citizen. The rights of Pacifican Citizens are guaranteed, and may not be infringed by any institution or law purporting immigration authority over Pacifican persons or territory. All governmental entities within Pacifica must actively resist, block, and remedy any attempt to subject Citizens of Pacifica to foreign immigration jurisdiction or action, through civil, criminal, and constitutional mechanisms overseen by Pacifican courts. Violations of this provision constitute grounds for judicial relief, reparations, and penalties, enforceable by the Courts of Pacifica by judicial review.

The right of asylum shall be guaranteed to foreigners and Stateless Persons who are the object, or are under grave threat of persecution as a result of their activities in favor of democracy and republicanism, social and national liberation, peace among Peoples, individualism, and freedom or rights of the human Person. Refugees may not be deported or extradited to a state in which they will be persecuted. Refugees who plan on immigrating to Pacifica are obligated under law to Remain within the boundary of the country they are entering into Pacifica from, until they are vetted and passed for entry temporarily while they await permanent Citizenship in some other country or are entered into a Lottery for Naturalization and Citizenship to Pacifica;

No person may be deported to a state in which they face the threat of torture, or any other form of cruel or inhumane treatment or punishment.

That religion, or the duty which we owe to our very own Creation and that of the Universe around Us, and the manner of discharging it, can be directed only by reason and conviction, not by force or violence; and therefore all people have an equal, natural and unalienable right to the free exercise of religion, according to the dictates of conscience, and that no particular religious sect or society ought to be favored or established, by law, in preference to others. Congress, the several States, any locality, and all other levels of government, shall make no law, respecting an establishment of any [a]spirituality/[a]religion or superstition, sect, or society, neither establishing any particular denomination of religion in preference to another, nor prohibiting the free exercise thereof, neither shall any national or state religion or church be constructed and/or maintained; or abridging, restricting, prohibiting, or otherwise infringing upon the freedom of speech, the press, or of conscience, association, and choice, no matter its perceived offensiveness, value, or the lack thereof; or the right of the People peaceably to assemble and consult for their common good, to instruct their representatives, protest, and to petition the government for a timely and effective redress of grievances. The rights of electoral participation and political association are fundamental; Political choices and competition are primary interests of the citizenry.

Every person has the right to choose freely their [a]spirituality/[a]religion or their philosophical convictions, and to profess them alone or in community with others. Every person has the right to join or to belong to a [a]spiritual/[a]religious community, and to follow [a]spiritual/[a]religious teachings. No law shall prohibit praying in a Public place, nor provide sanction for the same performance on Private property, in so far as it does not violate the rights of the Property’s owner.

A well educated mass, being necessary to the good spiritual health and intellect of a free world and several Churches, the right of Natural Persons, and Spiritual People, to discover, keep, reject, share, and profess a diversity of religious and spiritual opinions, articles, and information sources, along with experiences, shall not be interfered with. The freedom of Spiritual and Religious beliefs, and their exercise, shall not be obstructed or impaired, insofar as it does not violate anothers rights, by the virtue of Liberty, and by Justice in such case, only shall be denied to the degree which is necessary to secure another’s rights, differences in faith aside.

The right to not practice [a]spirituality/[a]religion or hold [a]spiritual/[a]religious beliefs, freedom from [a]religion/[a]spirituality on one's own Private Property or that which is under their lawful control or subject to such authority, and to promote and/or propagate [a]theism, shall also be upheld.

No Person shall be compelled to take part in any [a]spiritual/[a]religious act. No person may be forced to join or belong to a [a]spiritual/[a]religious community, to participate in a [a]spiritual/[a]religious act, celebration, rite, ritual, practice, or to follow [a]spiritual/[a]religious teachings.

The right to [a]spiritual/[a]religious belief and [a]spiritual/[a]religious practice shall not be denied or abridged, except in the case of violation of any right/s, and only through due process of law, under a unanimous verdict by a jury of twelve, in a court of proper jurisdiction. At the same time, [a]spirituality/[a]religion and [a]spiritual/[a]religious practice may not be used to carry out exploitation and to accumulate private capital, in violation of the law, or to engage in violation of the law in some other way; nor may [a]spiritual/[a]religious Persons, groups, or institutions be granted rights or privileges which do not apply to the People in this Republic in general.

For [a]spiritual/[a]religious beliefs to be protected by law, they do not have to be tied to any [recognized]/[official] faith’s doctrine, so long as they are sincerely held. The government may not burden a person’s exercise of [a]spirituality/[a]religion unless it can prove that relieving the burden would seriously impair an important governmental interest, and that no other means may be made available to achieve those ends. Any law targeting a particular [a]spirituality/[a]religion is per se un-constitutional.

The separation of [a]spirituality/[a]religion as well as superstition, and of ‘the State’, shall be applied, upheld, and enforced; [a]spiritual/[a]religious gatherings, organizations and institutions, or connected affiliates are not allowed to be involved in political activity, including: Participating in/for, or intervening in/against (including the publishing or distributing of statements), a political campaign on behalf of [or in opposition to] any candidate for public office, and endorsing or opposing and advocating or protesting legislation; No governmental body, member, or representative of the government, may advocate, promote, or propagate [a]spirituality/[a]religiosity, through their public office, nor on the other hand suppress or restrict [a]spiritual/[a]religious belief and practice, except in accordance with provisions here and elsewhere in this Constitution, and laws made and enforced in conformity with this Constitution; No functions of the State or of the law may be performed in the name of [a]spiritual/[a]religious or by persons or institutions invoking [a]spiritual/[a]religious authority, including but not limited to [a]spiritual/[a]religious instruction, prayer, hyms, or other s[a]spiritual/[a]religious exercise on public property or within public institutions such as a public school, courtroom, correctional facility, or government agency or department, but this shall not prohibit nor restrict the very same from Private Persons operating in their own Personal Capacity; [a]Spiritualities/[a]Religions shall not be taught in Public/Governmental Schools except from a social, philosophical, and historical perspective, and are not to be delivered or conveyed as fact, but State Institutions are by no means barred from carrying Religious and Spiritual Texts, such as in School, Prison, and City, State, or Federal Libraries, Bookstores or Subscription services operating under the Department of Goods and Services within it’s Jurisdiction, and on Public Broadcasting services, nor shall they prejudice against Private Actors professing beliefs in any of the same which may be furnished in one of these several and other modes, such as commentaries on tape, podcasts, news articles, journalist shows, and documentaries; This provision shall be upheld, so far as it does not interfere or disparage the right of an Individual Person to do the same in an un-official or un-affiliated capacity.

No money raised by Public Donation, nor by the Department of Goods and Services in Congress or any State for the support of public schools, or derived from any public fund therefore, nor any public lands devoted thereto, shall ever be under the control of any [a]spiritual/[a]religious group or sect, nor shall any money so raised or lands so devoted be divided between [a]spiritual/[a]religious groups, sects, or denominations, but this shall not prohibit or restrict the establishment of non-denominational churches for common worship in Jails, Prisons, Psychiatric Institutions, Hospitals, Military Bases, and in the Capitol District of their State or the Federal power.

No [a]spiritual or [a]religious organization or institution shall receive any privileges from Congress, the States, or any Territory, nor within any Facility/Fort/Installation under the direction of them, nor exercise any political authority.

All people shall be secure in the Natural right, to worship [a] deity/ies according to the dictates of their own consciences.

No law shall in any case whatever control the free exercise, and enjoyment of religious opinions, or interfere with the rights of conscience.

No person shall be rendered incompetent as a witness, or juror in consequence of his opinions on matters of religion;  nor be questioned in any Court of Justice touching his religious belief to affect the weight of his testimony.

No law shall abridge the freedom of feeling, thought, conscience, and will/choice or their peaceful expression or dissemination, as in speech, press and other media, artistic depiction, or [a]spiritual/[a]religious practice; nor shall any law promote or hinder any sex, color or race, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, artistic culture, scientific research, or specific community, except as is in line with the principles set forth by this constitution. The freedom to use any language is guaranteed, including those which are informal, or those which are un-recognized by others which includes “the State”.

Media organizations must declare upfront their sponsorship relationships to businesses.

The equal rights in freedom of feeling, belief, thought, conscience, will/choice, expression, and speech shall not be violated. Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and belief without interference, and everyone shall have the right to freedom of formulation and communication. This right includes freedom to seek, receive, gather, and impart information and ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers, either orally, in writing, in print, in the form of art, construction, or through any other medium of one’s choice. Every person has the right freely to form, express, and impart their opinions. Free Expression is an index of the mind, and this Right is primal to the Independence of Persons. No thought, belief, opinion, or idea is ever a crime unto itself. Nobody may be subject to discrimination on behalf of the public body by account of their political ideology, except as neccessary to secure the requirements of this constitution that Members of the Public Body not espouse a belief system which undermines the separation and limitation of powers within Government.

No content‑neutral or viewpoint‑neutral prohibitions on expression or [in other words any form of] communication shall be permitted, even in pursuit of a compelling state interest, except where the expression itself constitutes an actual violation of rights or a demonstrable, imminent threat to violate rights.

The right to speech includes the right of Private Persons to abstain from speaking and to remain silent, so long as one decides, as well as to not be coerced, compelled, compulsed, or otherwise forced into speaking or remaining silent. It also includes the right to listen and for one to be heard [by consenting individuals], so far as it is within one’s right to speak or otherwise communicate; It is only just that the right to listen or read, and the right to be heard or read, both remain consensual, and be treated as one-in-the-same.

Along with the right to speak freely, is the equally poised right of the People to remain silent, and to abstain from engaging in compelled, coerced, compulsed, or otherwise extorted speech, whether in regards towards interactions with public or private entities.

Every person shall have the right to be wrong, to hold and express mistaken opinions, and even to tell falsehoods, without fear of government punishment, except as provided herein. No law shall abridge the freedom of speech, including the right to express opinions or make statements that may be untrue, except where a person intentionally and knowingly communicates false information to another, with the purpose of deceiving, and such deception is the direct and proximate cause of injury or death to a person, animal, sentient artificial being, damage to property, or destruction of the environment. Acts of intentional, harmful deception as described in this provision may be prosecuted in accordance with rules and procedures of due process, consistent with the customs of perjury, false statements, and obstruction of justice as recognized in American law. However, no person shall be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against themselves, nor deprived of the right to remain silent. This provision shall not be construed to restrict the right to honest error, satire, parody, or the expression of opinion, nor to criminalize mere mistakes or differences in interpretation, belief, or recollection.

[?]No Person shall [rightfully] demand nor be denied the truth, and any Private Person may deny them an answer to any question or inquiry, such as but not limited to their [potential] choices of: Remaining silent, pleading the right to not self-incriminate, or denying furtherance of the conversation or topic/subject-matter; Without regard to the status of their culpability or ‘guilt in fact’ surrounding any action, including unlawful/criminal conduct; Public officials are non-exempted, and cannot deny to answer another the truth upon their inquiry or questioning, while the member of the public body is exercising their official duties in the course of their public service, unless it pertains to their rights as a Criminal defendant or their Private life. This provision shall not impair or impact the artistic performance of an individual or group, nor that of comparative analysis or commentary, and it shall not preclude publishing fictional materials or proposing hypothetical situations if they are denoted as such.[?] Congress shall establish standards for adjudicating deliberate misinformation by Public officials.
[]

No person shall knowingly provide false information or advice, or intentionally mislead another, where such information or advice is acted upon and directly results in physical injury or death to any individual. A violation of this provision, when committed with knowledge or reckless disregard for the truth, shall constitute a felony offense, subject to both criminal penalties and civil liability for damages to each injured party, including any survivors present at the time of their death. Any person who, without intent but through negligence or reckless disregard for factual accuracy, provides false information or advice that is acted upon and results in physical injury or death, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and liable for civil reparations to each injured party. In all cases, the injury or death must be proven by clear, objective, and measurable evidence, with a direct causal link to the false information or advice provided. Criminal conviction under this provision requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt; civil liability requires proof by a preponderance of the evidence. All charges and civil claims under this provision shall be adjudicated by a citizen’s court, composed of randomly selected peers, with no governmental agency involvement beyond the provision of data or evidence. Any data or experimental evidence provided by a government entity must meet high scientific standards: double-blind controls, statistically significant sample sizes, and repeatability, with all raw data made available for independent verification. No person shall be prosecuted or held liable under this Provision for good faith efforts to assist, rescue, or advise another in an emergency, provided their actions are reasonable under the circumstances and not grossly negligent. This provision shall not restrict the free exchange of ideas, opinions, or scientific debate, nor penalize individuals for expressing sincerely held beliefs, except where statements are presented as fact and directly cause proven harm as described above. Each injured party shall have an independent right to bring charges and seek reparations. All enforcement of this amendment shall be consistent with the mutual non-aggression principle: no person’s liberty or property shall be reduced except as a direct response to proven, initiated harm. No law or regulation enacted under this amendment shall establish any governmental body or agency with authority to determine “truth” or censor speech beyond the scope of proven, direct harm as outlined herein.

The right to question and/or challenge, criticize and/or chastise, not respect and/or disrespect, as well as loathe and/or hate, shall not be denied or abridged by Pacifica, nor permitted to be denied or abridged by any other through the laws of Pacifica.

The right of each individual to generate and project sound through natural, mechanical, or electronic amplification in spaces held open to public discourse shall be deemed an inviolable extension of free expression, constrained only where the government can demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence that such amplified sound constitutes an objective and direct threat to public safety, peace, or the physical integrity of persons or essential systems. Any law or administrative regulation purporting to govern amplified sound must be narrowly and demonstrably tailored to mitigate only those specific harms universally recognized and objectively measurable: namely, the emission of sound levels known to inflict permanent hearing loss or material injury; sustained interference with emergency or infrastructural operations essential to both individual and collective safety; or deliberate, targeted disruption of lawful assembly or ordinary domestic quiet during commonly accepted hours of rest. No ordinance shall condition the permissibility of sound upon the content, viewpoint, intensity, emotional register, or popularity of the expression, nor shall irritation, offensiveness, or personal discomfort of listeners constitute disorder or nuisance. The threshold at which sound may be deemed lawfully excessive shall correspond to demonstrable physical injury or structural risk, evaluated in context with ambient conditions, locality, and hour, with the evidentiary burden borne entirely by the enforcing authority. Amplified sound whose generating apparatus operates at thirty-five watts root-mean-square [per second] (35P RMS/s), or whose acoustic power output does not exceed eighty-four decibels at one meter (84dB@1m), or is plainly audible no more than thirty meters (30m) beyond the source, whichever is greater, and which is not audible inside of a dwelling which is not the source of the sound during the common sleeping hours, shall constitute rightful noise in all circumstances and enjoy full protection under this Provision, immune from any punitive or discriminatory regulation except upon proof of clear and present harm to life, health, or property. Individuals possess the enduring liberty to defend their person, habitation, or bodily autonomy from actual injury caused by abusive or dangerously excessive sound, but such recourse shall never abridge the natural right of others to lawful expression. The government shall bear the affirmative duty to prove any alleged nuisance or disorder through irrefutable evidence of real and proximate harm, and no enforcement action may rest upon conjecture, aesthetic aversion, or collective discomfort. The peaceful amplification of voice, art, or idea within ordinary waking hours shall never be deemed unconstitutional noise unless the aggrieved claimant meets the highest evidentiary threshold of irrefragable proof of tangible damage. Those finding themselves discomforted by rightful and lawful sound amplification retain at all times the reciprocal liberty to exercise locomotion, to relocate themselves and/or their possessions, or to insulate their property from sound intrusion.

The People possess the freedom to inquire into any subject with which one has the lawful authority to obtain the results, such as may be permitted by another who has the right to such information, and as according to the proprietor in cases of personal information, and the People possess the right to research and discovery, including scientific and inventive freedom.

The rights to freedom of [a]spirituality/[a]religion, conscience, thought, opinion, and speech, as is with other forms of liberty, are in themselves not right/s to censor or otherwise infringe on the freedom of [a]spirituality/[a]religion, conscience, thought, opinion, and speech, or any other libert[y]/ies, of another.

No Authority ought, in any case whatever, to control or interfere with the rights of conscience and thought, and no preference shall be given in law. But it shall be the duty of the legislature to pass such laws as may be necessary to protect equally every denomination of opinion and thought in the peaceable enjoyment and just defense of its own modes of public display of such conscience and ideas.

Freedom of consciousness, including the freedom from mind altering substances one does not consent to, can never be rightfully suspended, even in cases of punishing convicted natural criminals. The People have the right to be free from Mind Control, and any other form of mental coercion or intimidation, and manipulation of a person’s consciousness, regardless of its purpose for deployment, including punishing crime, except as may be permitted under the rules and laws governing the theory of consent; Mind control and mental manipulation are the highest possible crimes (higher than murder), since they are the fountain from which springs forth all misunderstandings and insanity, and of with which entices people to do terrible things because they were drawn to the wrong conclusions by some external force which directly interfered with their free and independent thinking. Without sanctity of the domicile of one’s mind, there can be no free choice, and no person who has been found to be directly afflicted by mind control shall be held liable for their actions, but rather their handlers/manipulators/controllers shall be held accountable, and be brought to Justice by life in prison; Un-consented mind control is not ever justifiable, for any purpose whatsoever, and as with all other forms of consent, any willingful submission to it may be revoked at any time.

We the People reserve the right to freedom of thought including to expand our consciousness with or without technology or drugs to enhance our human and spiritual experience/s, where appropriate.

Pacifica and the several States shall promote the development of privacy-preserving technologies, such as decentralized AI and encrypted communication systems, to protect individual autonomy and freedom.

Freedom of the press, radio, television, internet, and all other forms of dissemination of features and information by means of public and private communications is guaranteed. Censorship, distortion, or suppression by the government of naturally lawful information and communications is prohibited. The protection of a journalist’s or reporter’s sources shall be guaranteed by law. This provision shall not preclude the enforcement of protective pornography laws which protect minors.

No level of government or public employee in Pacifica, nor any contracted through them, shall require, mandate, or enforce the implementation, embedding, transmission, or recognition of any content rating control systems, codes, or associated technologies in software, hardware, broadcasts, streams, local files, or any media distribution method. This protects the People's right to unrestricted access and use of purchased media without state-imposed content controls or censorship mechanisms.

SECTION. 1.5.

The Right to Be Free from Disturbance

Subsection 1. Fundamental Principle

Every person possesses an inherent, self-evident, and self-regulating right to exist, rest, move, gather, decide, and live without unjustified disturbance. This right arises from the natural autonomy of the person and shall not be granted, revoked, conditioned, or withdrawn by any authority.

All interpretations of this Section shall preserve the primacy of individual liberty, including the freedom to think, behave, associate, refuse, or exist in ways others may not understand, approve of, or prefer.

Subsection 2. Definition of Disturbance

“Disturbance” means any intentional or negligent act that results in substantial, undue, or coercive disruption of a person’s physical presence, mental state, habitation, or lawful activity, including conditions that produce severe or intense stress, fear, disorientation, deprivation, or forced movement.

Ordinary, incidental, or socially expected stress arising from everyday interactions, disagreement, or lawful activity shall not, by itself, constitute disturbance under this Section.

No act shall be considered disturbance solely because a person’s behavior is unusual, nonconforming, self-directed, or reflective of disability, illness, belief, or personal choice.

Disturbance includes, but is not limited to:
(a) Forced displacement from a place of rest or shelter without provision of safe and adequate alternatives;
(b) Harassment, intimidation, escalation, or repeated unwanted engagement that results in substantial disruption or severe stress;
(c) Seizure, destruction, or destabilization of personal belongings essential to survival, regulation, or dignity;
(d) Intentional use of sound, light, chemical agents, environmental manipulation, or physical presence to significantly disrupt rest, sleep, orientation, or peace;
(e) Logging, surrveillance, or monitoring that materially interferes with free association, expression, exercise of rights, or psychological stability absent individualized cause;
(f) Coercive, confusing, or destabilizing interventions against individuals experiencing mental, physical, cognitive, or economic vulnerability without due process and least-restrictive alternatives;
(g) Conduct that would reasonably be understood to provoke, inflame, or escalate a person experiencing mental or behavioral distress into a state of severe dysregulation.

Subsection 3. Disturbance as Abuse

Any disturbance that exploits, overrides, or interferes with a person’s inherent capacity for self-regulation, particularly through the imposition of severe or destabilizing stress, shall constitute an abuse of the person.

Abuse includes, but is not limited to:
(a) Knowingly or recklessly escalating a person in mental or emotional distress into a heightened or crisis state;
(b) Imposing demands, commands, or compliance conditions that are unreasonable, unattainable, or disproportionate to a person’s physical, cognitive, or situational capacity, including impossible or self-contradictory demands placed upon the disabled, elderly, or impaired;
(c) Substituting external control for a person’s own decision-making absent lawful justification under Subsection 5;
(d) Using authority, presence, or environmental pressure to induce panic, confusion, submission, or breakdown;
(e) Penalizing a person for manifestations of disability, illness, trauma, poverty, or self-directed behavior;
(f) Creating or maintaining conditions that foreseeably lead to severe disorientation, regression, or loss of self-regulation.
No claim of administrative convenience, social preference, perceived normalcy, or generalized order shall justify such abuse.

Subsection 4. Protected Status of Persons

All persons are equally protected under this Section, with heightened protection afforded to individuals whose condition increases susceptibility to coercion, escalation, or severe disturbance, including but not limited to:
(a) Children and families;
(b) Elderly persons;
(c) Persons with disabilities or medical conditions;
(d) Persons experiencing mental or behavioral health conditions;
(e) Persons without stable housing;
(f) Lawfully present non-citizens, including refugees and asylum seekers.

Heightened protection shall not diminish autonomy, but shall reinforce the presumption that such individuals are entitled to greater freedom from severe or coercive interference.

Subsection 5. Presumption of Liberty and Lawful Basis for Interference

All persons shall be presumed competent in their own self-regulation and shall have the right to remain undisturbed in their chosen place and manner of living.

No government actor shall disturb a person unless the person is engaged in conduct that constitutes:
(a) An imminent and specific threat of physical harm to another person; or
(b) A clear and articulable violation of the rights of another person; or
(c) An otherwise unlawful act established by valid law consistent with this Constitution.

Status, condition, poverty, disability, mental state, appearance, or nonconformity shall not constitute a lawful basis for disturbance.

Any interference must further satisfy all of the following:
(d) It serves a compelling and immediate purpose directly tied to the unlawful conduct;
(e) It is narrowly tailored to stop or prevent that conduct;
(f) It uses the least intrusive means available;
(g) It is limited in duration and scope;
(h) It preserves, to the greatest extent possible, the person’s autonomy, property, and dignity;
(i) It does not rely on demands or expectations that exceed the person’s reasonable capacity to understand or comply;
(j) It does not introduce, exploit, or amplify severe or unnecessary stress beyond what is strictly required to address the unlawful conduct.
Subsection 6. Habitat and Continuity Protections
(a) Any place where a person regularly rests, shelters, or maintains personal effects shall be treated as a protected human habitat.
(b) Disturbance of such habitat is prohibited unless justified under Subsection 5 and accompanied by meaningful, safe, and adequate alternatives that preserve continuity, autonomy, and dignity.
(c) Destruction, confiscation, or displacement of personal property essential for survival, identity, regulation, or well-being is prohibited without consent, due process, and prompt restitution.

Subsection 7. Temporal and Condition-Based Protections

Recognizing the necessity of rest, recovery, and self-regulation, heightened protections against disturbance shall apply:
(a) During periods of sleep or rest;
(b) During illness, recovery, disability, or cognitive variation;
(c) During caregiving or family cohesion activities;
(d) During extreme environmental conditions;
(e) During periods of acute psychological distress or altered mental state.

Subsection 8. Freedom from Harassment, Targeting, and Escalation

No person shall be subject to repeated, targeted, or cumulative disturbance in a manner that results in substantial disruption or predictably produces severe stress, destabilization, or escalation.

Patterns of conduct that cumulatively interfere with a person’s ability to remain regulated and autonomous shall be deemed a violation unless each act is independently justified under Subsection 5.

Subsection 9. Duty of Care and Non-Escalation

All public authorities have an affirmative duty to respect and preserve the self-regulating autonomy of persons while minimizing severe or unnecessary disturbance.

This includes:
(a) Designing public spaces and systems to accommodate presence, rest, and difference without coercion;
(b) Providing supportive, voluntary, and non-coercive services in lieu of enforcement where vulnerability is present;
(c) Prioritizing consent-based and person-directed engagement;
(d) Avoiding commands, deadlines, or compliance structures that are unrealistic, contradictory, or unattainable for the person’s condition;
(e) Training personnel to recognize and avoid escalation dynamics, including interactions with individuals experiencing mental distress, disability, age-related impairment, or trauma;
(f) Refraining from tactics intended or likely to provoke, destabilize, or induce compliance through stress or confusion.

Subsection 10. Private Right of Action and Remedies

Any person subjected to unlawful disturbance may seek immediate and effective relief, including:
(a) Injunctive protection against further disturbance;
(b) Restoration of property, habitat, or prior condition;
(c) Compensation for material, dignitary, and psychological harm resulting from substantial or severe disruption;
(d) Structural, institutional, or policy remedies necessary to prevent recurrence.

Subsection 11. Construction

This Section shall be interpreted liberally to expand freedom, minimize coercion, and uphold the inherent, self-regulating nature of individual liberty. Where ambiguity exists, interpretation shall favor autonomy, require a clear showing of unlawful conduct, and prohibit disturbance based on status, condition, or nonconformity.

Subsection 12. Non-Derogation

No law, policy, or practice shall diminish, reinterpret, or evade the protections of this Section. Any conflicting authority is void to the extent of the conflict.

Subsection 13. Limitation to Lawful Enforcement

Intervention is justified only to prevent or stop unlawful conduct as defined in Subsection 5. The preservation of public safety, order, or welfare shall not be interpreted to permit disturbance based solely on suspicion, general risk, or perceived disorder.

Actions that impose or amplify severe distress, destabilization, or coercion beyond what is strictly required to address unlawful conduct shall be presumed invalid.

Subsection 14. Standard of Review

Any act of disturbance by a government actor shall be subject to the highest level of judicial scrutiny. The burden shall rest entirely on the actor to demonstrate, with clear and convincing evidence, that all conditions of Subsection 5 were satisfied and that no less intrusive alternative was available.

Failure to meet this burden shall render the disturbance unlawful per se.
