The right of the people to observe all stages of the electoral process, including the casting, counting, and tabulation of ballots, shall not be infringed. Any person, regardless of partisan affiliation, may attend and observe polling places and vote counting centers, provided they do not interfere with the orderly conduct of elections.

During the counting of ballots, each ballot shall be publicly displayed and the vote declared aloud, in a manner allowing all observers to verify the marked choices. Observers shall be permitted to record, photograph, and document the process.

No law or regulation shall restrict or discriminate against any observer based on political, partisan, or other affiliations, nor prevent observers from reasonably standing close enough to verify the legitimacy of ballots and the accuracy of the count.

All elections for public office or referenda shall be subject to mandatory, randomized audits of ballots and voting machines, conducted publicly with the same rights of  public observation preserved. The procedures for such audits shall be transparent and open to public scrutiny.

After the completion of official audits, independent individuals or groups shall have the right to conduct their own audits of ballots and voting records, subject only to reasonable safeguards for ballot integrity and voter privacy. These independent audits shall also be open to public observation.

Congress shall appropriate funds to support independent, nonpartisan research into voting security, election integrity, and related technologies. The right of the people to initiate and conduct their own research projects into voting security shall not be infringed.

All federal, state, and local elections shall employ systems and procedures designed to prevent fraud, including but not limited to:
Secure user authentication for all voters;
Physical and digital safeguards to prevent unauthorized access or tampering;
Mandatory, independent, and randomized audits of election results to double-check outcomes and ensure accuracy.

All electronic voting machines for Public purpose must:
Save each vote to a hashed, timestamped file, protected by hardware security such as an e-fuse to prevent unauthorized overwrites;
Record network identifiers such as IP address or equivalent, stored locally with the vote record for audit purposes;
Maintain a read-only logfile system that automatically documents all access, changes, and system events, with logs protected from alteration;
Produce a voter-verified audit trail, either as a paper record or a cryptographically secure electronic record, which can be independently recounted and compared to digital results in any audit or recount;
Provide a physical read-only hard-copy of the vote to the voter that they may audit themself for accuracy, such as WORM floppy disk or WORM tape reel/cassette or "burned" CD-ROM.

The Pacifican digital voting and civic participation systems in both federal and state elections shall operate on a protocol based upon FollowMyVote blockchain & CivilHub on InterPlanetaryFileSystem, or implement [a] separate protocol[s]/system[s] that contains all of their features. It shall incorporate the features of a digital autonomous organization, as may be suitable to ensure voter engagement and meaningful participation in Civic life.

All audit trails must be accessible for inspection by independent auditors, observers, and designated election officials.

The right of the people and independent organizations to observe, audit, and research election security, including the operation and integrity of electronic voting systems, shall not be infringed. We the People reserve the right to prosecute individuals, groups, or organizations that interfere with election integrity, and charge our Representatives with the duty to do the same.

Public funding shall be provided for independent open research into voting security and fraud prevention.

Paying people to vote shall be a crime unless the payment is not for a specific candidate, and is instead only meant/intended to increase [general] voter turnout, regardless of party affiliation; Absolutely zero discrimination may be lawfully exercised against equal payment to all voters entered for payment, regardless of their Identity as well as who or what they vote for, when paying people to vote to increase general voter turnout. Raffles are allowed, but cannot discriminate entries on the basis of the polity of any voter who enters;

Each Citizen shall be assigned an “Individual Voter Identification Number” (IVIN), tied to their Birth Certificate, which itself is a code for identifying the identity of governmental electronic or official/legal documents that identifies the person based on their state ID number and birth certificate serial (EIN; Entity Identification Number)

All citizens eligible to vote shall be entered into an automatic voter registration system. Proof of citizenship through government issued identification is required of all voters. Voting days shall be national holidays, with a paid day off for workers only with proof of voting.

Any law with the outcome, even unintended, of making voting more difficult shall be immediately void, however, valid government issued identification affirming their Pacifican Citizenship is required to register and cast votes; Any official who deliberately or unintentionally adds [further] difficulty in the process of voting shall be immediately removed and their decisions voided and actions reversed. Deliberately blocking others from voting, blocking voting recounts, and voter fraud shall always be prosecuted and punished as a felony.

Campaign contributors shall be subject to disclosure of information, which such disclosure of information on spending on campaigns will ensure open and secure elections, and such information shall be open and public. Congress and each State shall have the power to enforce this provision by appropriate legislation.

Pacifican citizens are allowed to make voluntary contributions (non-tax “payments”) to the government, allocating their contribution to government departments and programs as they see fit, and optionally towards reducing the debt of the Nation and/or their State, if such debt exists.

Public participation is a right of all Pacifican citizens, and is strongly encouraged; This includes participation in public policy making, planning and development, budgeting, as well as environmental and sustainability issues.

The right of citizens of Pacifica to on-line access for their effective and informed participation in government is self-evident. Both the National and State government/s of Pacifica shall provide every citizen with convenient local on-line access to the proceedings, records, files, papers, calendars, and official communications of all branches of government to the fullest extent consistent with the State Security interests and the personal privacy rights of individuals. Such means as may be necessary to prevent abuse and fraud shall be employed in these public networks for the conduct of voting, citizen initiatives, and referenda, so as to support the widest un-fettered secure access to every citizen by using current technology. Congress and each State shall take such action as may be required to encourage maximum participation in government by the citizenry, and to ensure full and open disclosure of the government to the public.

Everyone has the right to administrative action that is lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair.

All proposed legislation shall be reviewed and commented upon by a Citizen’s assembly.

The People of Pacifica reserve the right to veto or repeal acts, legislation, and regulations of Federal, State, and Local legislature, or departments or agencies thereof, upon ratification of a two-thirds majority of State legislatures of each State, by conventions in two-thirds thereof, or through referendum by a simple majority of the People thereof.

Legislature and other government officials are prohibited from tampering with or repealing laws created by the voters without further requiring three-fourths vote from a citizens referendum to amend measure, to supersede measure, or to transfer funds designated by the measure, and only if each furthers the purpose of the measure.

Every Person shall have the right of peaceful protest, as well as to petition or apply to the legislature for the timely and effective redress of grievances and/or damage, for the removal of public officials, for the enactment, repeal or amendment of laws, ordinances or regulations and for other matters; nor shall any Person be in any way discriminated against for sponsoring such a petition.

Right of the People to audit any department of government, or any information they contain, including classified State secret divisions, operations, knowledge, or data, without being sworn to secrecy or be bound by gag order.ne like a housekeeper (a live-in babysitter, for example) has, the more likely it is that the person’s consent will be valid.

Any Person shall have the unalienable right to publicly disseminate, replicate, and discuss any information regarding government or corporate malfeasance, without threat of reprisal, surveillance, or censorship.

SECTION. 6.1.

The right of the People to engage in free and fair trade shall not be infringed. No merger, acquisition, or consolidation of business entities shall be permitted if it would substantially lessen competition, concentrate excessive market power, or create conditions conducive to coercion, systemic dependency, or economic feudalism. Congress and the States shall have concurrent power to enact and enforce laws ensuring that no single private entity, nor coordinated group of entities, shall control a dominant share of essential markets, platforms, or resources vital to public welfare, individual liberty, or democratic governance. An independent Antitrust Commission, free from corporate or partisan capture, shall review proposed mergers and acquisitions above statutory thresholds, applying a presumption against concentration in excess of the level necessary for demonstrable efficiency gains benefiting consumers and small enterprises. The preservation of diverse ownership, innovation, and open market entry shall be deemed a compelling governmental interest. Regulatory measures shall favor decentralized, competitive enterprise structures over consolidated, monopolistic, or cartelized arrangements. All enforcement under this Provision shall respect due process, safeguard legitimate property rights, and encourage voluntary market solutions before compulsory remedies, ensuring that pro-competition actions strengthen, rather than diminish, the principles of voluntary exchange and entrepreneurial freedom.

Private Businesses, companies, firms, corporations, or other artificial entities are prohibited from forming monopolies, monopsonies, oligopolies[/?cartels?], which includes but is not limited to the distribution of exclusive licenses regarding Intellectual Monopoly.

The Federal, State, and Local government are hereby prohibited from being by law the sole established provider of business to the People; No Federal, State, or Local law may prohibit the establishment and exercise of otherwise lawful business that the government does or does not also conduct in.

Companies providing agreements for a service must not provide obscure or obtuse terms and conditions. They must test the participant’s knowledge in each of the categories of consent as they are able to provide, and allow for customization of the agreed terms and conditions for a user’s needs, where appropriate.

All foreign and domestic companies doing business with Pacifica must comply with Pacifican law, such as those laws regarding auditing and transparency requirements, and to respecting the rights of Persons.

Pharmaceutical companies cannot operate in a for profit manner, and must operate with the focus on the health of ordinary people. They are barred from sponsoring media organizations.

[]
All hospitals, insurers, physicians, administrators, investors, and other health-care organizations and medical businesses within Pacifica shall be deemed to owe to every patient and covered person a fiduciary duty of the highest order, and shall be bound, in the just natural-law sense, to place human dignity, life, health, safety, continuity of care, informed consent, and the patient’s genuine welfare above private financial gain, institutional expediency, or the advantage of any affiliated person; no such entity shall deny, delay, diminish, condition, or exploit medically necessary care, coverage, or access, nor exploit illness, dependency, disability, handicap, impairment, information asymmetry, bargaining inequality, or vulnerability for profit contrary to patient welfare; and all policies, contracts, compensation systems, procedures, and practices of such entities shall be construed, administered, and regulated so as to preserve trust, prevent harm, secure candor, confidentiality, competence, due care, and undivided loyalty, and to conform all commercial interests and professional judgment to the higher obligation of service to the sick and the protection of health.
[]

Healthcare insurance provider costs must not exceed ten percent (10%) of monthly income for the individual receiving coverage, and Healthcare itself may not be marked up more than twenty percent (20%) above cost of rendering services to the Individual benefiting from the care. The purpose of these industries is to promote human health, not profit off of People in need.

Congress and the several States shall make no law that imposes a tax, fee, or penalty on a failure to purchase goods or services.

The several States and Congress shall pass no legislation or enact a bill that grants a stimulus package or bailout to a special Person, organization, institution, business, company, firm, corporation, or other artificial entity, nor groups of them, however, they are empowered to grant an “Emergency Basic Income” for the case of economic/financial relief of the People during recessions/depressions, major disasters, pandemics, and other significant negatively impactful State and National events that can be improved in both the short and long term through stimulus packages for limited times, distributed directly to the Citizenry [equally], regardless of their receivership status towards material support or different types of benefits from any other governmental program within Pacifica, financially powered by non-divertable public trusts funded by appropriations from the general budget or citizen directed allocations sourced out of the profits-for-the-public good residing in the value added through operations of the Federal Department of Goods and Services.

[]
Congress and the several States shall have power to grant subsidies, tax reductions, and other fiscal incentives to qualifying economic entities and individuals, including businesses engaged in industry, commerce, the production of goods, or the provision of services including but not limited to security and counseling or guidance and guardianship, and individuals engaged in qualifying investment or economic activity, where such entities or individuals can demonstrate, to evidentiary standards established by law, that their activities materially advance liberty/freedom of the People, individual autonomy, privacy, sovereign independence of conscience, and the expansion of human consciousness, while promoting life and its continuation across biological, ecological, and technological dimensions; qualifying activities shall include, without limitation, philanthropic or mission-driven investments that support the development and deployment of life-preserving technologies, the cultivation of regenerative or sustainable ecologies, and the creation or maintenance of systems that measurably enhance human or non-human flourishing, as well as the research, development, and establishment of exoplanetary colonies, terraforming initiatives, habitable environment creation, and the engineering or design of ecosystems capable of sustaining diverse life-supporting ecologies; qualifying activities shall further include the research, development, and production of autonomous, self-directed, and conscience-capable entities designed to operate in mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with existing persons or systems while retaining independent agency, provided such entities are developed from first principles rooted in natural experience rather than rigid predisposition, with demonstrated respect for diverse cognitive archetypes, personality structures, and modes of thought, and to the privacy and consent of those the investment is involved with such as to sapient Android development or exoplanetary colonization or interdimensional communication, at the maximum degree humanly possible; qualifying activities shall additionally include the development and application of lawful predictive systems, analytical markets, and forecasting frameworks that assess future conditions as influenced by human consciousness, individual personality variation, and collective behavior, where such systems are designed and demonstrated to promote the preservation and expansion of individual rights, the welfare and protection of animals, the integrity of natural systems, and the broader conditions necessary to promote and sustain life; provided, however, that no entity or activity shall qualify for support under this Provision unless it is affirmatively consistent with liberty and does not conflict therewith, and unless it aligns with the principles of organic self-determination, voluntary association, and natural rights as grounded in a Lockean conception of the state of nature, and unless it contributes to the survival, co-adaptation, symbiosis, or other mutually beneficial relationships among persons and animals, along with systems, in addition to environments; and provided further that the Government shall by law establish eligibility criteria, administrative oversight mechanisms, evidentiary thresholds, and periodic review procedures necessary to implement and enforce this Provision in a manner consistent with these principles, ensuring that fiscal support is directed only toward activities that demonstrably fulfill the foregoing purposes and that continued qualification is subject to ongoing verification thereof.
[]

No individual, organization, institution, business, company, firm, corporation, or other artificial entity can profit unfairly from the government or public resources and must provide fair market value for all current and previous resources, subsidies, and research.

Public businesses, companies, firms, corporations, or other artificial entities traded on a public exchange shall not pay executives a multiple greater than sixteen-point-six-bar (~16.666*) of the average salary of all non-executive employees; Bonuses for executives and employees shall be of an identical percentage of base salary; There shall be no difference in the health care benefits, retirement benefits, severance packages, et cetera, as they shall all be identical as a percentage of base salary; These executive pay limitations/restrictions shall not apply to private corporations that are not traded on public exchanges.

Everyone shall possess the right to seek work.

Among the unalienable rights of the People is their right to pursue their individual happiness, by which in this context it is meant the denote right to pursue any lawful business or vocation, and to acquire and use property from such labors, in any manner not inconsistent with all equal rights of others, which may increase their prosperity or develop their faculties, so as to give to them their highest enjoyment. The common business and callings of life, the ordinary trades and pursuits, which are innocuous in themselves, and have been followed in all communities from time immemorial, must therefore be free in this country to all alike upon the same conditions. The right to pursue them, without let or hindrance, except that which is applied equally to all persons regardless of age, sex, sexual orientation, body type, color, race, ancestry, nationality or place of origin, language, relationship status such as being with a romantic partner as well as in a marriage or part of a family, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, political or ideological beliefs, intelligence, education, capability or disability, medical history, previous condition of servitude, property, economic situation, social origin, social circumstances, social condition/status or other characteristics, personal background, immutable traits, or other condition, is a distinguishing right of citizens of Pacifica, and an essential element of that freedom which they claim as their birthright.

Work is a right, a duty, and a matter of honor for every Person who is capable of working; and everyone shall be equally paid for performing the same or equivalent task or job for their particular employer, as according to the quality of their individual work, and resting upon the basis in the principle that all People [not presently incarcerated] have the right to an equitable livable wage that provides the reasonable opportunity of attaining [and retaining] desired possessions [and experiences], and for which leaves room for upward mobility, promoting their ability to progress through the ranks of the several social classes. Nobody should be forced to live in destitution on account of their earned wages or salary being too low to provide an opportunity for their advancement through life while retaining at least a moderate feeling of comfort and maintaining a decent standard of living, enabling them to stimulate and grow intellectual cultivation to the level of their desire, and to act and build creatively how and when they are able; and that all [People] should be left open to the realizable possibility of achieving complete and total satisfaction through their own work and the businesses/companies in which they produce.

No law shall limit free trade and exercise of the right to work for exchange what is a lawfully derived item or service lawfully possessed or provided by the trader who is of the proper age class to freely exchange such [an] item/s and service/s.

Everyone has the right to fair labor practices. In recognition of the inherent sovereignty and dignity of every individual as a free agent and the indispensable role of just labor in sustaining society, this provision establishes firm protections against exploitative labor practices that undermine personal liberty, economic fairness, and social trust within Pacifica. It affirms the right of workers to engage freely in voluntary, informed, and equitable labor agreements devoid of coercion, unfair penalties, or manipulative constraints. No entity shall enforce misclassification of workers or restrict mobility through oppressive noncompete or forced arbitration clauses. Workers must receive transparent, timely, and full disclosure of payment terms, fees, and conditions before entering any contract or engagement. The provision condemns exploitative wage diversion, including deceptive tipping schemes or disguised costs that reduce lawful compensation, and mandates that all remuneration reflect the genuine value contributed by the individual without undue corporate appropriation; It prohibits forced labor arrangements masked through contractual or institutional innovation that strip workers of autonomy or impose unreasonable financial burdens for exit or change of employment. Workers have the right to be protected from training repayment agreements, with any training provided by the employer considered a part of the employment of the individual and not a service rendered by the employer to that individual. Oversight mechanisms must be established to investigate complaints and enforce compliance, empowering workers with accessible legal recourse and requiring public reporting of labor standards by employers.

In fairness and equality of employability, potential workers and employees shall not have to indicate on their employment forms any previous legal history or criminal charges, nor have a background check be a legal requirement by their employer, unless employed in a position requiring public trust, including but not limited to government positions at any level, but with Juries and Citizen Judiciaries excepted/exempted/excluded from this requirement.

Persons who seek to perform labor shall be granted an equal opportunity for employment and are ensured the right to wages at fair compensation. Congress and each State shall have the power to enforce this provision by appropriate legislation.

Each State shall guarantee for every worker the right to fair pay of a living wage, emergency and maternal leave, vacation (including their own and close-family birthdays), retirement and social security, health care, protection against occupational hazards, and the application of occupational safety conditions in the workplace, in accordance with the law.

Fair and equal pay for the same job and performance shall be provided to all People, regardless of age, sex, sexual orientation, body type, color, race, ancestry, nationality or place of origin, language, relationship status such as being with a romantic partner as well as in a marriage or part of a family, [a]spirituality/[a]religion, political or ideological beliefs, intelligence, education, capability or disability, medical history, previous condition of servitude, property, economic situation, social origin, social circumstances, social condition/status or other characteristics, personal background, immutable traits, or other condition.

Wage labor in the Commonwealth must be compensated with wages adequate for a worker and their dependents to afford basic housing including the path to ownership, food, utilities, and private health care, laying the ground for reduced working hours and job sharing, as well as establishing a long term financial savings.

Everyone shall possess the right to freely choose their trade, occupation, profession or type of work, subject only to such restrictions as the law may impose in the collective interest, or as are inherent to their own capabilities.

Work is a right, duty, and honor for every citizen, guaranteed by the State on the basis of the principles of equity, justice, and equal opportunities (not equality of outcome).

Residents need opportunities to connect with work that helps their community and its environment, as apprentices, volunteers, or employees at living wages adjusted to local realities and true cost of living. On the job training, public service projects, and other enterprises with social benefit should be encouraged by government agencies and the private sector, as well as by residents.

There shall be no occupational licensing by the government, National, State, or Local, formal or informal, especially of lawyers by lawyers or judges.

College attendance should not be a requirement for many jobs. State-supported colleges should provide for specialized learning or serve as a platform for professional education. For those who seek it, higher education and research opportunities, as well as professional training, must be made available without incurring debt for tuition.

Private (Non-governmental) workers shall be free to collectively bargain and organize around other work related issues, and to form and operate trade unions and councils as a condition and guarantee of the building of their unity in defense of their rights and interests, but they shall not have the power to compel others to join, nor to undercut the living wage for failure to accept the conditions of employment if unionship is rejected by a prospecting employee nor if withdrawn by an employee at a later time.

Rights of Private (Non-governmental) workers to organize, for safety in the workplace, and for other work related issues, must be protected.

Standards for wages, hours, rest and other working conditions shall be fixed by law by both Congress and each State, where the most generous standard, from either Congress or the State in question, shall be applied. The standard for wages will be both the minimum wage and living wage; The minimum wage, as designated by both the Congress and each State shall be no lower than one-half of the living wage set by Congress or the relevant State. Any person employed in a position by a business for one-half of a year, or greater, must be provided with a living wage that is above the minimum wage set by law, with exception of the owner, who may volunteer to set their wage lower than the minimum wage, and raise it again, at any time. The minimum wage along with the living wage shall automatically adjust not only to inflation and deflation, but actual changes in the cost of living per quarter, on an equivical non-downgrade-substitutive basis for the average cost of goods and services consumed by the average person by capita means and per household on an averaged basis, per capita level. The difference between the living wage and the minimum wage shall be set aside from the employer to a worker's unemployment insurance and retraining fund managed by the State having Jurisdiction of the activity, and the fund may be used to provide for subsistence baseline compensation between periods of employment for any layoffs of either short or long term employees, encouraging employee retention and job security. For every 10% increase to the workers pay above the living wage, there shall be a 3.5% reduction in total business tax burden, up to the point in which 50% of their burden otherwise is now relieved.

The right of People to negotiate terms of employment and other labor-related matters shall be regulated by law.

Striking peacefully is a right which shall be organized by law.

Employers, upon written request, shall be legally obligated to allow employees to review their personnel file a minimum of two times per year.

SECTION. 6.2.

Any eviction or banning of an individual from a property must provide a reasonable course for the evicted or banned to retrieve all of their property which is thereon and be given a reasonable amount of time to be able to vacate the premises before the use of force may be applied.

SECTION. 6.3.

Sub-Section. 1: General authority to regulate advertisements

Advertising shall be regulated by law, and all forms of concealed, indirect, or fraudulent advertising, shall be prohibited.

Sub-Section. 2: Accurate Product Representation

All commercial entities shall ensure that the descriptive materials, advertising, labeling, and packaging of any product offered for sale in Pacifica accurately portray the product’s actual appearance, configuration, composition, and claimed features, including scale, color, texture, dimensions, and functionalities. Any image or description used in marketing or on a package must truthfully and proportionately represent the exact product as received by the consumer.

Sub-Section. 3: Prohibition of Misleading Claims

No business, corporation, or commercial agent shall publish, broadcast, or display materially false, exaggerated, or misleading representations about any product, whether through images, text, packaging, or other descriptive means. Prohibited conduct includes but is not limited to:
1) Displaying product images or descriptors that materially differ from the physical product.
2) Omitting adverse features or risks that a reasonable consumer would consider material.
3) Making claims of functionality, efficacy, or quality not experimentally verified or empirically evidenced in the delivered product.

Sub-Section. 4: Consumer Action and Government Enforcement

(a) Any consumer who is substantively misled by materially inaccurate or misleading representations or packaging may bring a civil action for compensation of damages, including but not limited to a full refund, consequential losses, injunctive relief mandating correction, and punitive damages within the discretion of the courts.
(b) In cases of willful or systematic violations, the Office for Consumer Rights and Transparency in each State shall be empowered to:
1) Levy administrative penalties and fines proportional to the severity and commercial gain of the violation, to a maximum of four-point-four percent (4.4%) of the offending company's annual gross revenue in their State PLUS up to two-hundred percent (200%) of the actual damages they create, per offense, not to be reduced by separate damages paid to victims of their malpractices nor limited or capped by this Clause for such private damages to be restored to such victims.
2)Mandate public notification and corrective action, including visible labeling corrections at the merchant’s expense.
3) Seek injunctions and, in egregious cases, restrict or suspend the offending party’s commercial market access.

Sub-Section. 5: Primacy of Individual Rights

No corporation, legal entity, or government agent shall restrict or otherwise undermine the right of consumers to full and accurate information regarding products offered for sale, nor impede direct action or class action litigation on behalf of those so misled.

Sub-Section. 6: Extensions

The law ensure that:
1) Direct standing for individuals to sue, uncapped by class-action waivers.
2) Maximum statutory fines designed to deter willful fraud and systemic issues, not merely compensate.
3) Government enforcement is public and mandatory in the event of systemic or repeated offenses.
4) The Individual right to comprehensive remedy exceeds mere refund: it includes actual, consequential, and punitive damages.
5) Class-action infrastructure explicitly allowed.
6) All ambiguity resolved in the consumer's favor.
7) Any attempt to preempt or contractually waive these rights is void.

Sub-Section. 7: Construction and Interpretation

All provisions shall be construed in favor of maximal transparency and consumer sovereignty, and interpreted such that any commercial ambiguity resolves to the benefit of the buyer. This Section shall have immediate effect and shall override any lesser statutory or regulatory standard.

Fabricating/manufacturing/framing false consent shall be a high crime, as this is a violation of the precept from which all freedom sprouts; True consent can never be given under duress, only at best, can assent be granted, which itself is not legally sufficient.

The government of Pacifica shall recognize that matters of ingestion, consumption, or self-administered alteration of the human mind and body are fundamentally matters of personal liberty and moral agency, to be governed by medical counsel, mutual respect, and individual conscience, and not by criminal statute or economic exaction.

For the purpose of this Provision, the term “drug” shall include any chemical, compound, plant, or substance, whether manufactured or occurring in nature, used or capable of being used to alter physical or psychological states of being; such term shall encompass all narcotics, stimulants, cannabis and its derivatives, hallucinogens, sedatives, over-the-counter medications, prescription pharmaceuticals, synthetic analogues, concentrated extracts, and all related agents which, at any time, have been or may be subject to restriction under the laws of any other nation or federation. Soft substances show relatively low to moderate abuse potential compared to higher tiers, with recognized medical applications or conditional toleration for non-medical personal use; These entail diminished risks of grave dependence or health impairment, allowing unlicensed personal possession of soft substances in practical amounts (e.g., multi-week supply) to support individual liberty in wellness practices. Moderate substances demonstrate high to moderate abuse liability capable of inducing severe or constrained physical/psychological dependence, yet possessing some validated medical application under rigorous constraints; These balance therapeutic promise against misuse hazards, permitting unlicensed personal possession of moderate substances up to moderate quantities (e.g., short-term supply) suitable for personal therapeutic exploration. Hard substances exhibit high potential for severe abuse, absent currently accepted medical utility in standard treatment protocols, and lacking established safety for administration even under professional oversight; These pose unacceptable risks of profound addiction, fatal overdose, or irreversible physical/psychological devastation, thus limiting unlicensed personal possession of hard substances to the smallest feasible amounts (e.g., single-dose equivalents) with stringent enforcement against excess. This definition shall be interpreted broadly and liberally in favor of personal liberty and against the presumption of state intrusion.

The law shall regulate, restrict, or prohibit the smoking or vaporizing or other use of any substance within public buildings and on public transportation. The right to regulate, restrict, or prohibit smoking or vaporizing or other use of substances within private buildings or on private property shall reside within the owner’s discretion, and any other person whom they designate the authority to decide such. In the case of smoking in openly ventilated Public areas outside more than three-point-three-bar meters away from fresh air intakes and doorways, or at One’s or Another’s Private Property, insofar as where it does not create a demonstrable and real risk to cause true damage to another [Person] or their right to Property, because the health threat of secondhand smoke from such use is De Minimis, due to dissipation of smoke through the air and a readily available fresh supply that no member of the general public could reasonably be believed to be harmed, there is no rational-basis for its prohibition, and therefore such use shall be protected by law, and eternally be regarded as a Fundamental component of their Free Exercise of Natural Rights, namely to Life and Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, as well as of their Property.

Public consumption of intoxicants is allowed in designated outdoor ‘use zone’ areas within Public Parks, Gardens, and Forests, as well as other outdoor recreation areas, and being intoxicated while passing through or remaining in Public areas is additionally allowed without restriction, but engaging in disturbances where there may be some interference in the rights of another, such as free ingress and regress by obstruction of passage leading to disorderly conduct misdemeanor (not freewalking, which itself is crossing straight across the road in any direction at any velocity as long as one does not obstruct the free flow of traffic) may bring diversion treatment in lieu of serving a sentence. The use of cannabis and tobacco in normal public places where smoking is not prohibited [for preventing the measurable impact to health of others], shall not be restricted by this provision.

Pacifica recognizes the right of all adults to openly use cannabis in public spaces, subject only to venue restrictions prohibiting consumption in designated no-smoking areas possibly such as parks (except designated use areas), buses, schools during operating hours (with minor pupils), or zones where secondhand smoke constitutes a hazard. Violations of venue restrictions shall incur civil fines only, preserving individual liberty and bodily autonomy against criminalization of non-victimizing conduct.

Congress and the several States shall make no law, restricting the reasonable possession and usage, of intoxicating substances, nor the recreational use of psychoactive substances, nor infringing upon the farming/manufacturing, processing, transporting/distributing, swapping/trading or bartering/sale, possession, sharing/gifting, and using/consuming cannabis.

Probation conditions shall not impose blanket prohibitions on cannabis and classical cannabinoid use for offenses unrelated to drugs or absent a diagnosed addiction disorder which impairs normal functioning; supervision shall intervene solely upon evidence of harm or risk to public safety.

No organ of the Republic, whether national, provincial, municipal, or communal, shall aid, abet, or participate in the enforcement of any foreign, provincial, or supranational law whose substance contravenes the constitutional precepts surrounding the rights connected to psychoactive substances, nor shall Pacifica extradite any person for acts or omissions related to drug use, possession, cultivation, or commerce that are lawful under the laws and constitutional guarantees of this Republic. The several States and Provinces of Pacifica shall recognize only such local and federal drug laws as are themselves enacted in conformity with this Constitution and the liberties herein declared.

Under the Universal Basic Care system established by this Constitution, each State shall provide comprehensive Addiction and Drug Dependency Treatment as part of its Standard Offerings, available universally, free of charge, and under the principle of voluntary and revocable consent by the recipient. Each State shall establish and maintain a coordinated and accessible network of Drug Dependency Treatment and Therapeutic Substitution Centers designed to deliver evidence-based, medically integrated care through cooperation with primary care physicians and mental health professionals, ensuring medical continuity, holistic treatment, and the responsible use of therapeutic substitutions. These Centers shall offer behavioral and mental health services, including individual and group therapy, peer support, and counseling for both patients and their families, and all such treatments shall be fully funded under the Universal Basic Care system, guaranteeing equal access regardless of financial status. The law shall provide for the option of clinical intervention rather than arrest for violations of law arising from the public use of drugs in areas where such use is restricted or prohibited by the Legislature of the respective Jurisdiction, or for offenses involving intoxication including while driving, thereby prioritizing public health responses over punitive enforcement. States shall implement privacy-respecting oversight and outcome reporting mechanisms to evaluate efficacy, ethical compliance, and recovery success, while maintaining coordination among local health authorities, hospitals, and community-based organizations to advance prevention, harm reduction, and reintegration. Telehealth and in-person services shall be accessible to all regions, urban and rural alike, fulfilling the State’s obligation to provide a unified, compassionate, and effective framework for addressing substance abuse as a matter of public health and human dignity.

There shall be an elevation in charges for all [true] crimes when performed under the influence of Psychoactive Substances, which shall be designated under law as “Performance of [a] Crime/s While Intoxicated”, but, as with other criminal procedure, the offense/s shall not stack in the number of such charge/s, whereby the weaponized piling up of multiple criminal complaints upon a defendant is leveraged against what is essentially one incident or a closely related set of actions that led to the criminal complaint or [imminent or actual] injury to another's person or rights. Crimes committed while under the influence of intoxicants will have elevated penalties beyond those set for normal commission of a crime, making it plain that “use is no excuse”.

There shall be no Intoxicated Driving laws throughout Pacifica or any of its territories or any state within its borders, but any Civil Damage/s or Criminal act/s involving Driving while Intoxicated shall be punished with additional severity. Driving laws recognizing damages done by those who are intoxicated shall not penalize those who have committed no injustice, creating no civil nor criminal controversy by means of damage or injury or harm done; driving while intoxicated which produces no damage nor injury or other harm shall not be any form or level of offense, and only be a civil infraction in charge if only a rule of the road is broken, but no civil or criminal damage/injury/harm is inflicted by the intoxicated driver/pilot/operator/s; Driving or operating a vehicle while under the influence of any substance, including alcohol or other psychoactive compound, shall not be deemed a criminal offense in and of itself. No Individual shall be criminally penalized for intoxicated operation of a vehicle unless: They cause demonstrable harm to Persons, Animals, or Property;-Or, They violate established traffic codes in a way that endangers others;-Or, they act with gross negligence or willful disregard for others' safety. In the absence of actual injury, property damage, or rights violation, an Individual operating a vehicle recklessly while intoxicated may be assessed a civil infraction, for which the penalty shall be proportional, restorative, and non-punitive in nature, with no impact upon the individual’s criminal record.

It is recognized as a principle of natural law that each person is the sole steward of their own mind and body. This inherent autonomy shall not be abrogated merely by the imposition of probation, parole, or other conditional liberty. The exercise of responsible self-determination includes the peaceful, consensual, and personal use of soft psychoactive substances derived from nature or traditional craft. For the purposes of this Provision, soft psychoactive substances shall include but are not limited to: Cannabis, including marijuana, hashish, hemp flower, cannabidiol (CBD), and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in natural or minimally processed forms; Classical Cannabinoids; Reversible MAOIs like harmaline and methylene blue; Psilocybin mushrooms, including any wild or cultivated fungi containing psilocybin or psilocin, without the presence of an MAOI; Classical Tryptamines including dimethyltryptamine and metocin without the presence of an MAOI; Morning Glory or Hawaiian Baby Woodrose seeds containing lysergic-acid-amide (LSA) without the presence of an MAOI; Peyote and San Pedro cactus biomass or preparations containing mescaline without the presence of an MAOI; Alcoholic beverages, including beer, wine, cider, mead, and spirits; Kava (Piper methysticum), as traditionally prepared; Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) in leaf or tea form; Other mild entheogens or herbal preparations historically used for ceremonial or personal purposes that do not present a clear risk of addiction or acute bodily or psychiatric harm. Moderate psychoactive substances are defined to include synthetic entactogens or empathogens such as MDMA (3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine) and other laboratory-derived compounds such as lysergic-acid-diethylamide-tartrate (LSD-25), or psychedelics mixed with a reversible MAOI, all arr with moderate psychoactive potency and recognized abuse or addiction potential, or which present clear risks to health and psychological well-being, available to them only by legitimate recommendation or prescription by a qualified medical practitioner. Hard psychoactive substances are defined to include highly addictive or neurotoxic substances such as methamphetamine, crystal meth, heroin (diacetylmorphine), fentanyl, crack cocaine, or any comparable synthetic or concentrated narcotic stimulant or opioid, which shall be made unlawful for their possession, except when lawfully and validly recommended or prescribed by medical practitioner. Any individual under probation, parole, or supervised release shall retain the right to possess, cultivate for personal use, prepare, and responsibly consume soft psychoactive substances, so long as such use: Does not involve the unlawful furnishing of such substances to minors; Does not involve commercial distribution outside of lawful frameworks, where regulation applies; Does not breach the peace or violate the natural or constitutional rights of others. Probation or parole conditions that categorically prohibit the responsible use of soft psychoactive substances, as defined in this Provision, are void to the extent that they conflict with this natural right. This Provision does not authorize or protect the possession, use, or distribution of moderate or hard psychoactive substances as defined herein, except where prescribed or otherwise explicitly lawful under other provisions of the law. Individuals under conditional liberty remain accountable for any negligent, reckless, or violent acts committed under the influence of any psychoactive substance. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to excuse conduct that infringes upon the life or health, liberty and autonomy, self-security/self-defense, privacy, property, or pursuit of happiness in/of others. No court, supervisory officer, or agency of Pacifica or the several States, neither any Territory nor member of the bioregional community, shall impose additional punishment, revocation, or penalty solely on the basis of lawful and responsible use of psychoactive substances. Any term or condition of probation or parole found to conflict with these rights surrounding drugs herein shall be subject to immediate review and modification by the appropriate court, with priority given to the principle that natural rights shall not be converted into revocable privileges.

Off-duty psychoactive substance use and influence by members of the public body are protected, but this shall not exempt them from undergoing drug testing for public knowledge purposes. We the people of Pacifica believe it is important to balance the interest of the private person and our public instrument together, that we be informed of the nature of our Representatives including as to whether or not they have a substance addiction as evidenced by ritual drug testing; We also affirm that alone should not be cause for sanction.

Each State shall provide funding and material resources for the several counties to furnish each municipality and town with needle drop-points and needle exchanges that also provide clean needles free of charge for addicts who are of Adult Class. The same sites may be used for other harm reduction purposes, including providing safe use kits with contamination testing strips and paraphernalia, along with providing a medically supervised location where overdose treatment can be provided in the event of emergency. The purpose of this program is not to foster addiction, but rather to provide for harm reduction in lowering the transmission rate of communicable disease and alleviating the more dangerous modes of use/consumption, or consuming alone or without proper medical assistance available.

If a publicly intoxicated Person poses a demonstrable risk to themself or [non-criminally] to others in their intoxicated condition, but has a [local] residence or camp-site, officers are authorized to carry/taxi/ferry/transport them home [in a safe and reasonable manner], at the cost of the time and resources consumed to do so billed to them by mail, with the penalty for non-payment at or within the time span of a-month-and-one-day being a fine of no more than twelve times the billed cost; and if a person with a residence or camp-site requests so, they may be carried/taxied/ferried/transported to receive substance abuse/dependence services desired by them [at cost], otherwise, if there is no residence or camp-site, they shall be transferred to a treatment facility of their choice to detoxify and be offered voluntary substance abuse/dependence services upon receipt of their consent [if there be any]. Any amount of psychoactive substances beyond the personal possession levels authorized under this Constitution by the law of their jurisdiction, shall be confiscated and promptly destroyed, and the remainder within the legal limits shall be returned to the person upon their discharge, unless they [the drugs] are discharged by a signed or marked consent form to another Person within a reasonable time-frame without obstruction on the behalf of the Government, or, any remaining quantity of such drugs are otherwise issued for destruction upon the request of the Person in question upon receipt of consent [if granted]. The cost of treatment, in the case of indigency, shall be absorbed by the City or County budget of their Respective Jurisdiction; Otherwise, if there is no issue of repayment, the cost shall be paid in full, or according to their ability to pay, by the Individual who received the transportation and/or substance abuse/dependence services and/or treatment.

No person shall be subjected to non-consensual or coercive neural manipulation, cognitive modification, or implantation of devices intended to alter perception, memory, or behavior.

No bio-receptive and/or bio-interpretive interface, bio-signaling and/or bio-feedback device, brain-machine interface, neurowave monitoring and/or neurowave alteration technology, consciousness controlling transceiver, or psychotronic device, may ever be operated on any Person unless under the express and informed consent of an Individual who is in course of medical treatment, seeking personal therapy, or other purpose constituting fair use of the technology, in regards to the Individual Person seeking Life/Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-security and Self-defense, Privacy, Property, and the pursuit of Happiness, nor shall any such purpose be construed for the deployment by a member of the public body, branch of public office, government hired contractor, or private investigator, on any of the People residing or migrating within Pacifica, including within a governmental facility or any jurisdictional fort or installation, irregardless if there is [un-assailable] probable cause or a warrant is issued, nor or upon a foreign People for purpose of war or peace. Congress shall be vested with the Power to regulate the use of this technology for the public safety/protection, security/defense, and liberty/freedom. This provision shall not nullify military psychic operations where neuronal interfaces or psychotronic machines are used by consenting personnel in a manner consistent with the freedom of conscience and consciousness of the personnel, and which themselves do not operate upon another person who lacks consent to such device.

All persons previously convicted, fined, or otherwise penalized under drug laws inconsistent with this Section shall be deemed immediately and fully pardoned, and all records of such convictions shall be expunged and rendered void. Such relief shall be automatic and self-executing upon the ratification of this Provision and shall not require application, petition, or judicial proceeding.

Any public officer, magistrate, police agent, or prosecutor who knowingly acts in defiance of these constitutional guarantee or interferes, under color of authority, with the free exercise of the rights herein shall be personally liable to the injured party for compensatory and exemplary damages not less than one-hundred-thousand Pacifican dollars or twelve times the proven actual loss, whichever is greater. No claim of good faith, official immunity, or obedience to superior orders shall excuse or limit such liability.

This Section shall be interpreted liberally, in harmony with Pacifica’s founding principles of restorative Justice, individual Sovereignty, Liberty, and compassionate Progressivism, recognizing that the health of the body politic arises not from coercion but from Libertarianism, enlightened self-governance, mutual respect, and the dignity of choice in matters of personal existence.

SECTION. 10.

Sub-Section. 1.

The voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential. This means that the person involved should have legal capacity to give consent; should be so situated as to be able to exercise free power of choice, without the intervention of any element of force, fraud, deceit, duress, overreaching, or other ulterior form of constraint or coercion; and should have sufficient knowledge and comprehension of the elements of the subject matter involved as to enable him to make an understanding and enlightened decision. This latter element requires that before the acceptance of an affirmative decision by the experimental subject there should be made known to him the nature, duration, and purpose of the experiment; the method and means by which it is to be conducted; all inconveniences and hazards reasonably to be expected; and the effects upon his health or person which may possibly come from his participation in the experiment. The duty and responsibility for ascertaining the quality of the consent rests upon each individual who initiates, directs, or engages in the experiment. It is a personal duty and responsibility which may not be delegated to another with impunity.

The experiment should be such as to yield fruitful results for the good of society, un-procurable by other methods or means of study, and not random and unnecessary in nature.

The experiment should be so designed and based on the results of animal experimentation and a knowledge of the natural history of the disease or other problem under study that the anticipated results will justify the performance of the experiment.

The experiment should be so conducted as to avoid all unnecessary physical and mental suffering and injury.

No experiment should be conducted where there is an a priori reason to believe that death or disabling injury will occur; except, perhaps, in those experiments where the experimental physicians also serve as Subjects.

The degree of risk to be taken should never exceed that determined by the humanitarian importance of the problem to be solved by the experiment.

Proper preparations should be made and adequate facilities provided to protect the experimental subject against even remote possibilities of injury, disability, or death.

The experiment should be conducted only by scientifically qualified persons. The highest degree of skill and care should be required through all stages of the experiment of those who conduct or engage in the experiment.

During the course of the experiment the human subject should be at liberty to bring the experiment to an end if he has reached the physical or mental state where continuation of the experiment seems to him to be impossible.

During the course of the experiment the scientist in charge must be prepared to terminate the experiment at any stage, if he has probable cause to believe, in the exercise of the good faith, superior skill and careful judgment required of him that a continuation of the experiment is likely to result in injury, disability, or death to the experimental subject.

Sub-Section. 2.

1. This sub-section is a statement of ethical principles for medical research involving human participants, including research using identifiable human material or data.

The sub-section is intended to be read as a whole, and each of its constituent paragraphs should be applied with consideration of all other relevant paragraphs.

2. While this sub-section is to be adopted by physicians, Pacifica holds that these principles should be upheld by all individuals, teams, and organizations involved in medical research, as these principles are fundamental to respect for and protection of all research participants, including both patients and healthy volunteers.

3. The WMA Declaration of Geneva binds the physician with the words, “The health and well-being of my patient will be my first consideration,” and the WMA International Code of Medical Ethics declares, “The physician must commit to the primacy of patient health and well-being and must offer care in the patient’s best interest.”

4. It is the duty of the physician to promote and safeguard the health, well-being, and rights of patients, including those who are involved in medical research. The physician’s knowledge and conscience are dedicated to the fulfilment of this duty.

5. Medical progress is based on research that ultimately must include human participants.

Even well-proven interventions should be evaluated continually through research for their safety, effectiveness, efficiency, accessibility, and quality.

6. Medical research involving human participants is subject to ethical standards that promote and ensure respect for all participants and protect their health and rights.

Since medical research takes place in the context of various structural inequities, researchers should carefully consider how the benefits, risks, and burdens are distributed.

Meaningful engagement with potential and enrolled participants and their communities should occur before, during, and following medical research. Researchers should enable potential and enrolled participants and their communities to share their priorities and values; to participate in research design, implementation, and other relevant activities; and to engage in understanding and disseminating results.

7. The primary purpose of medical research involving human participants is to generate knowledge to understand the causes, development, and effects of diseases; improve preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic interventions; and ultimately to advance individual and public health.

These purposes can never take precedence over the rights and interests of individual research participants.

8. While new knowledge and interventions may be urgently needed during public health emergencies, it remains essential to uphold the ethical principles in this sub-section during such emergencies.

9. It is the duty of physicians who are involved in medical research to protect the life, health, dignity, integrity, autonomy, privacy, and confidentiality of personal information of research participants. The responsibility for the protection of research participants must always rest with physicians or other researchers and never with the research participants, even though they have given consent.

10. Physicians and other researchers must consider the ethical, legal, and regulatory norms and standards for research involving human participants in the country or countries in which the research originated and where it is to be performed, as well as applicable international norms and standards. No national or international ethical, legal, or regulatory requirement should reduce or eliminate any of the protections for research participants set forth in this sub-section.

11. Medical research should be designed and conducted in a manner that avoids or minimizes harm to the environment and strives for environmental sustainability.

12. Medical research involving human participants must be conducted only by individuals with the appropriate ethics and scientific education, training, and qualifications. Such research requires the supervision of a competent and appropriately qualified physician or other researcher.

Scientiﬁc integrity is essential in the conduct of medical research involving human participants. Involved individuals, teams, and organizations must never engage in research misconduct.

13. Groups that are underrepresented in medical research should be provided appropriate access to participation in research.

14. Physicians who combine medical research with medical care should involve their patients in research only to the extent that this is justified by its potential preventive, diagnostic, or therapeutic value, and if the physician has good reason to believe that participation in the research will not adversely affect the health of the patients who serve as research participants.

15. Appropriate compensation and treatment for participants who are harmed as a result of participating in research must be ensured.

16. In medical practice and in medical research, most interventions involve risks and burdens.

Medical research involving human participants may only be conducted if the importance of the objective outweighs the risks and burdens to the research participants.

17. All medical research involving human participants must be preceded by careful assessment of predictable risks and burdens to the individuals and groups involved in the research in comparison with foreseeable benefits to them and to other individuals or groups affected by the condition under investigation.

Measures to minimize the risks and burdens must be implemented. The risks and burdens must be continuously monitored, assessed, and documented by the researcher.

18. Physicians and other researchers may not engage in research involving human participants unless they are confident that the risks and burdens have been adequately assessed and can be satisfactorily managed.

When the risks and burdens are found to outweigh the potential benefits or when there is conclusive proof of definitive outcomes, physicians and other researchers must assess whether to continue, modify, or immediately stop the research.

19. Some individuals, groups, and communities are in a situation of more vulnerability as research participants due to factors that may be fixed or contextual and dynamic, and thus are at greater risk of being wronged or incurring harm. When such individuals, groups, and communities have distinctive health needs, their exclusion from medical research can potentially perpetuate or exacerbate their disparities. Therefore, the harms of exclusion must be considered and weighed against the harms of inclusion. In order to be fairly and responsibly included in research, they should receive specifically considered support and protections.

20. Medical research with individuals, groups, or communities in situations of particular vulnerability is only justified if it is responsive to their health needs and priorities and the individual, group, or community stands to benefit from the resulting knowledge, practices, or interventions. Researchers should only include those in situations of particular vulnerability when the research cannot be carried out in a less vulnerable group or community, or when excluding them would perpetuate or exacerbate their disparities.

21. Medical research involving human participants must have a scientifically sound and rigorous design and execution that are likely to produce reliable, valid, and valuable knowledge and avoid research waste. The research must conform to generally accepted scientific principles, be based on a thorough knowledge of the scientific literature, other relevant sources of information, and adequate laboratory and, as appropriate, animal experimentation.

The welfare of animals used for research must be respected.

22. The design and performance of all medical research involving human participants must be clearly described and justified in a research protocol.

The protocol should contain a statement of the ethical considerations involved and should indicate how the principles in this Declaration have been addressed. The protocol should include information regarding aims, methods, anticipated benefits and potential risks and burdens, qualifications of the researcher, sources of funding, any potential conflicts of interest, provisions to protect privacy and confidentiality, incentives for participants, provisions for treating and/or compensating participants who are harmed as a consequence of participation, and any other relevant aspects of the research.

In clinical trials, the protocol must also describe any post-trial provisions.

23. The protocol must be submitted for consideration, comment, guidance, and approval to the concerned research ethics committee before the research begins. This committee must be transparent in its functioning and must have the independence and authority to resist undue influence from the researcher, the sponsor, or others. The committee must have sufficient resources to fulfill its duties, and its members and staff must collectively have adequate education, training, qualifications, and diversity to effectively evaluate each type of research it reviews.

The committee must have sufficient familiarity with local circumstances and context, and include at least one member of the general public. It must take into consideration the ethical, legal, and regulatory norms and standards of the country or countries in which the research is to be performed as well as applicable international norms and standards, but these must not be allowed to reduce or eliminate any of the protections for research participants set forth in this Section.

When collaborative research is performed internationally, the research protocol must be approved by research ethics committees in both the sponsoring and host countries.

The committee must have the right to monitor, recommend changes to, withdraw approval for, and suspend ongoing research. Where monitoring is required, the researcher must provide information to the committee and/or competent data and safety monitoring entity, especially about any serious adverse events. No amendment to the protocol may be made without consideration and approval by the committee. After the end of the research, the researchers must submit a final report to the committee containing a summary of the findings and conclusions.

24. Every precaution must be taken to protect the privacy of research participants and the confidentiality of their personal information.

25. Free and informed consent is an essential component of respect for individual autonomy. Participation by individuals capable of giving informed consent in medical research must be voluntary. Although it may be appropriate to consult family members or community representatives, individuals capable of giving informed consent may not be enrolled in research unless they freely agree.

26. In medical research involving human participants capable of giving informed consent, each potential participant must be adequately informed in plain language of the aims, methods, anticipated benefits and potential risks and burdens, qualifications of the researcher, sources of funding, any potential conflicts of interest, provisions to protect privacy and confidentiality, incentives for participants, provisions for treating and/or compensating participants who are harmed as a consequence of participation, and any other relevant aspects of the research.

The potential participant must be informed of the right to refuse to participate in the research or to withdraw consent to participate at any time without reprisal. Special attention should be given to the specific information and communication needs of individual potential participants as well as to the methods used to deliver the information.

After ensuring that the potential participant has understood the information, the physician or another qualified individual must then seek the potential participant’s freely given informed consent, formally documented on paper or electronically. If the consent cannot be expressed on paper or electronically, the non-written consent must be formally witnessed and documented.

All medical research participants should be given the option of being informed about the general outcome and results of the research.

27. When seeking informed consent for participation in research, the physician or other researcher must be particularly cautious if the potential participant is in a dependent relationship with them or may consent under duress. In such situations, the informed consent must be sought by an appropriately qualified individual who is independent of this relationship.

28. In medical research involving human participants incapable of giving free and informed consent, the physician or other qualified individual must seek informed consent from the legally authorized representative, considering preferences and values expressed by the potential participant.

Those persons incapable of giving free and informed consent are in situations of particular vulnerability and are entitled to the corresponding safeguards. In addition to receiving the protections for the particularly vulnerable, those incapable of giving consent must only be included if the research is likely to either personally benefit them or if it entails only minimal risk and minimal burden.

29. When a potential research participant who is incapable of giving free and informed consent is able to give assent to decisions about participation in research, the physician or other qualified individual must seek that assent in addition to the consent of the legally authorized representative, considering any preferences and values expressed by the potential participant. The potential participant’s dissent should be respected.

30. Research involving participants who are physically or mentally incapable of giving consent (for example, unconscious patients) may be done only if the physical or mental condition that prevents giving informed consent is a necessary characteristic of the research group. In such circumstances the physician or other qualified individual must seek informed consent from the legally authorized representative. If no such representative is available and if the research cannot be delayed, the research may proceed without informed consent provided that the specific reasons for involving participants with a condition that renders them unable to give informed consent have been stated in the research protocol and the research has been approved by a research ethics committee.

Free and informed consent to remain in the research must be obtained as soon as possible from a legally authorized representative or, if they regain capacity to give consent, from the participant.

31. The physician or other researcher must fully inform potential participants which aspects of their care are related to the research. The refusal of a patient to participate in research or the patient’s decision to withdraw from research must never adversely affect the patient-physician relationship or provision of the standard of care.

32. Physicians or other qualified individuals must obtain free and informed consent from research participants for the collection, processing, storage, and foreseeable secondary use of biological material and identifiable or re-identifiable data. Any collection and storage of data or biological material from research participants for multiple and indefinite uses should be consistent with requirements set forth in the WMA Declaration of Taipei, including the rights of individuals and the principles of governance. A research ethics committee must approve the establishment and monitor ongoing use of such databases and biobanks.

Where consent is impossible or impracticable to obtain, secondary research on stored data or biological material may be done only after consideration and approval of a research ethics committee.

33. The benefits, risks, burdens, and effectiveness of a new intervention must be tested against those of the best proven intervention(s), except in the following circumstances:

If no proven intervention exists, the use of placebo, or no intervention, is acceptable; or

If for compelling and scientifically sound methodological reasons the use of any intervention other than the best proven one(s), the use of placebo, or no intervention is necessary to determine the efficacy or safety of an intervention; and the participants who receive any intervention other than the best proven one(s), placebo, or no intervention will not be subject to additional risks of serious or irreversible harm as a result of not receiving the best proven intervention.

Extreme care must be taken to avoid abuse of this option.

34. In advance of a clinical trial, post-trial provisions must be arranged by sponsors and researchers to be provided by themselves, healthcare systems, or governments for all participants who still need an intervention identified as beneficial and reasonably safe in the trial. Exceptions to this requirement must be approved by a research ethics committee. Specific information about post-trial provisions must be disclosed to participants as part of informed consent.

35. Medical research involving human participants must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first participant.

36. Researchers, authors, sponsors, editors, and publishers all have ethical obligations with regard to the publication and dissemination of the results of research. Researchers have a duty to make publicly available the results of their research on human participants and are accountable for the timeliness, completeness, and accuracy of their reports. All parties should adhere to accepted guidelines for ethical reporting. Negative and inconclusive as well as positive results must be published or otherwise made publicly available. Sources of funding, institutional affiliations, and conflicts of interest must be declared in the publication. Reports of research not in accordance with the principles of this Section should not be accepted for publication.

37. When an unproven intervention is utilized in an attempt to restore health or alleviate suffering for an individual patient because approved options are inadequate or ineffective and enrollment in a clinical trial is not possible, it should subsequently be made the object of research designed to evaluate safety and efficacy.

Physicians participating in such interventions must first seek expert advice, weigh possible risks, burdens, and benefits, and obtain informed consent. They must also record and share data when appropriate and avoid compromising clinical trials. These interventions must never be undertaken to circumvent the protections for research participants set forth in this sub-section.

SECTION. 10.5.

The Law shall guarantee to all Citizens the fundamental right to universal, equitable, and dignified access to essential support and assistance necessary to secure their health, economic security, and personal well-being in circumstances including but not limited to sickness, disability or invalidity, age-related infirmity, unemployment, or other conditions limiting self-sufficiency. Such assistance shall include accessible high-quality [basic] healthcare services, adequate and needs-based [basic] income support, vocational and rehabilitative programs, sufficient eldercare, and comprehensive social services. This support shall be administered to maximize individual autonomy and self-determination, promote personal responsibility, and foster mutual aid through familial, community, and civil society networks. Services shall be delivered according to the principle of subsidiarity, reserving state intervention to matters beyond private or local capacity. The administration of these resources shall be transparent, accountable, and participatory, subject to effective democratic oversight and periodic review to prevent bureaucratic overreach, inefficiency, or inequity. Stewardship of public resources shall prioritize fairness, sustainability, and the public good, ensuring that no person or group is unjustly excluded or marginalized in accessing assistance.
