In fulfilling these guarantees, the Law shall safeguard against dependency by integrating empowerment and capacity-building measures, promoting equitable economic inclusion, and respecting all civil liberties and human rights. Any limitation or condition placed on such assistance shall be clear, reasonable, and justifiable through natural law and democratic processes, subject to judicial review, and consistent with the overarching principles of social justice and individual dignity. Each State shall have the authority to enforce this Provision by appropriate legislation.

Each State shall furnish [Quality] Free Universal [basic] Health and Psychological Care, which is guaranteed for all sectors of the lawfully residing population to their Public health and psychological services [With Priority for all the Citizens of each State before any other Person], or upon their request, to [external]/Private resources equivalent to three-quarters of the [actual] value of Public care and services worth in health insurance vouchers; the States shall guarantee a rational and efficient nationwide coverage in terms of health care units and human resources; Coverage shall include, but not be limited to [except by law], necessary and preventative testing along with treatment and maintenance care doctor visits, ambulatory services, emergency care, surgery, hospitalization, maternity and newborn care, mental health and substance use disorder treatments, prescription drugs, sexual health tests and exams as well as treatments or cures for infections and diseases, preventive services, pediatric services, dental, vision, auditory health, along with physical and psychological therapy, in addition to all connected laboratory and testing services associated with public doctor recommendations and scheduled diagnostics, supervised and managed by functional  naturopathic practitioners [to the highest degree humanly possible], unless another form of doctor is desired by the patient and accessible to them through Public funding. The States shall construct, staff, and maintain [basic] functional naturopathic health and psychological care facilities throughout their State. Everyone is entitled to the same level of care from the universal basic care system. The right to establish private health and psychological care services is guaranteed.

A Person may choose to be forwarded to another caretaker of their choice if necessary for an alternative opinion or course of treatment. The Pacifican system of Health and Psychological care shall place an emphasis on holistic naturopathic care, and hybrid adjunct treatment with modern medicine, in addition to preventative along with complimentary, integrative, functional, and regenerative techniques.

Patients with a qualifying medical or psychological condition may be allowed access to any medical or psychological testing and/or treatment with the discretion of a Private (Non-governmental) Physician to recommend or prescribe it, or to treatments that may be available under the Public Option Universal Basic Care plan which may be prescribed by the Patient’s Public Physician; “Qualifying medical/psychological condition” means any condition for which medical, psychological, or therapeutic procedure or treatment would be beneficial, as determined by the patient’s physician, psychiatrist, or Therapist, whether Public or Private, and consensually upon acceptance and use by the patient as they so need and desire for testing, treatment, cure, and/or therapy.

Terminally ill patients have a right to try experimental treatments, including but not limited to drugs and biologics or genetic therapies and immunological agents with limited clinical trials that have not been proven safe and effective, upon signing a waiver of liability, after granting [the] [highest standard of] informed consent [available].

All Individuals shall possess the inherent and inviolable right to control their own bodies and to make autonomous decisions regarding all forms of medical, surgical, psychiatric, psychological, or therapeutic testing and treatment. This right includes the freedom to test and treat their own ailments, illnesses, and diseases by any lawful means, or to refuse and abstain from any such medical or psychological testing or treatment, as well as the freedom to pursue private options for care as personally desired or medically necessary, regardless of whether such services or coverage are offered by any public option or recognized institution. No Individual shall be denied or obstructed from such freedom on account of their mental state or legal status, including whether they are deemed cognitively deficient, insane, institutionalized, civilly committed, incarcerated, or have previously been convicted of crimes. All Individuals are free to enter into consensual agreements for medical treatment or operations as are medically necessary or personally desired, and likewise may assist in the medical aid of another, with that other’s express permission, for any lawful reward or for none. No Individual shall be subjected to any form of medical, surgical, psychiatric, or psychological treatment without their express and informed consent, except in exigent circumstances where the Individual is incapable of consenting and no lawful Grantor of consent can be identified, as shall be defined by law. In such cases, should life-saving experimental treatment become available, medical practitioners may apply to the Civil Court for permission to conduct such treatment upon good cause shown. The citizens of Pacifica shall further possess an inviolate right to refuse any medical, surgical, psychiatric, or therapeutic treatment recommended or prescribed by a physician or psychiatrist, and this right shall not be infringed by Pacifica, its Congress, any agency or instrumentality thereof, nor by the several States or their respective legislatures, agencies, or instrumentalities. Eligibility for public assistance, disability benefits, unemployment compensation, or any similar welfare program shall not be conditioned, reduced, denied, or terminated on account of noncompliance with any physician’s or psychiatrist’s recommendation, prescription, or prescribed regimen, except upon a judicial determination by clear and convincing evidence that imminent and substantial harm to the individual or others would result absent such treatment, after due process including notice, hearing, and independent counsel where incapacity is alleged. The Congress of Pacifica shall have power to enforce this Provision through appropriate legislation.

All Individuals have the right to abstain from being forced into medical or psychological housing, except as may be ordered by the court for the protection of the People from those found through and under law to be either or both, [violent], remedials and/or madmen, and any such lodging must be for a limited and defined period of time, where there shall be periodic reviews within the period specified and at its end to determine if such retention remains necessary and in the best interest of the community and entity in question, and shall at all times be subject to public presentation before a both a [competent] Consular Praetor and Jury, composed of the People, and most importantly, witnessed by the People, for the purposes of habeas Corpus proceedings in conformity to what is set forth here and elsewhere through and under the Constitution of Pacifica.

All individuals have the right to considerate, respectful, and nondiscriminatory medical and psychological care, to be informed of the names and roles of their care providers, and to receive information about their diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in terms they can understand. Patients have the right to receive as much information as needed to give informed consent or refuse any treatment or procedure, including information about risks, alternatives, and the identity of those providing care. No medical or psychological treatment, procedure, or research may be performed without voluntary, informed consent, except in real incapacity as provided by law. Patients have the right to privacy in all aspects of their care, including confidential treatment of all communications and records. No photographs, recordings, or videos may be taken of a patient without their explicit, informed consent. With the patient’s revocable consent, the closest relative or next of kin shall be notified of the patient’s medical or psychological situation. If the patient is unable to provide or revoke consent, notification shall follow the patient’s advance directive or, if none exists, the best interests of the patient as determined by law or court order. All medical and psychological care and research must comply with the principles of the Nuremberg Code and the Declaration of Helsinki, ensuring voluntary participation, protection from unnecessary harm, and the right to withdraw from any research or experimental treatment at any time. Patients shall have access to a clear process for submitting complaints regarding violations of their rights, with prompt review and appropriate remedies. All patient rights apply equally to any person legally authorized to make healthcare decisions on behalf of the patient.

Minors may give [fully informed] consent to contraceptive services (birth control), testing and treatment for HIV and other sexually transmitted diseases or infections (sexual health), abortion (in the case of rape or incest being the pregnancy’s cause), prenatal care and delivery services (for reduction in potential infant mortality), treatment for psychoactive substance abuse and/or addiction (for the public’s health), and outpatient psychological care [which does not involve the use of psychotropic drugs] (for the public’s wellbeing); Parental notification is not necessary for any of these cases, though still recommended for transparency purposes, as may be appropriately decided in either case for protecting the kid from the undue risk of demonstrable and irreparable harm or danger, as according to the Legislature of Congress and the several States, with the least permissive/lenient rule/s trumping the other/s within their relevant jurisdiction/s.

Youth have the right to donate and sell their blood at the age of sixteen and beyond without requiring the permission of a Parent, Legal Guardian, or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s. Those aged thirteen or older may consent to donate their blood with the permission of their Parent, Legal Guardian, or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s.

Consent of a minor’s Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s is generally required prior to the disclosure of health or psychological care information about the minor; In those circumstances when a minor legally authorized treatment without their Parent/[s]'[s], Legal Guardian/[s]'[s], or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s/[s]’s consent, then only the minor can consent to the release of the information.

No Minors or those who lack mental capacity shall be subjected to any form of treatment or procedure without either the express and informed consent of their Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s, or unless with their own consent where allowed by law, unless under exigent circumstances where neither the Parent/s or Legal Guardian/s nor the competent patient is capable of consenting; a Parent/[s]'[s] or Legal Guardian/[s]'[s], or Protective and Caregiving Custodian/s/[s]'[s] decision shall be capable of being overridden by an Order of the Civil Court, issued under the “consent of a jury” by an impartial authorized citizen’s consulate judge of proper jurisdiction, where it is proved to the satisfaction of the Civil Court through the Jury that the decision in question is not in the best interest of the patient and the treatment is essential for their life or designed to prevent them sustaining any serious permanent injury (minor-protection based provisions); no Minors or those who lack mental capacity shall be subjected to any permanent or [moderate-to-seriously] harmful treatment or procedure which is not medically necessary, even upon the consent of their Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s.

The People have the right to be free from electro-shock therapy or other unduly hazardous procedures, though they may volunteer to have them performed regardless, so far as there is no coercion, compulsion, or extortion in any other way by another for them to do so.

No person shall be required to undergo any medical or psychological certification, treatment, or procedure to engage with any public services or to use any of the public lands and areas, nor to come or go from Pacifica or any of its Territories or the several States, neither to receive a publicly conferred benefit, but this provision shall not preclude the requirement to show proof of need or disability to receive means-tested social-safetynet public funds, from the governmentally established program/s intended for off-setting incapacities from such.

An employer of a worker who is at risk of contracting an infectious disease in the course of employment, shall provide to the worker time off of work to receive preventive immunization, and if there are side effects that prevent the immediate return to work, to additionally provide extra time off for mounting a response to a received preventive immunization for infectious disease, if such preventive immunization is available, and is medically appropriate; Such preventive immunization shall be provided by the [free] Universal Basic Care program of their State, and being as it is free, at no cost to the worker or the employer; Neither a Worker nor Employer shall be required as a condition of work to be immunized under this Provision, and they shall not be subject to sanction for their refusal to receive such immunization.

An individual’s right to personal reproductive autonomy is central to the liberty and dignity of determining one’s own life course and shall not be denied, infringed, or compromised except upon demonstration of a compelling State interest advanced by the least restrictive means, and this foundational right extends equally to both parents, whose joint consent in matters of abortion, parental responsibility, genetic derivation, and the lawful disposition of fetal or embryonic material shall govern the exercise of such autonomy within the jurisdiction of Pacifica; therefore, during the first trimester, a mother and father, or inseminating donor in equal right, may mutually elect to terminate a pregnancy for any reason of conscience, provided that both agree to the termination for it to be lawful, and may further decide, through express and informed consent, whether to authorize the donation of the fetus’s biological material for public or private open scientific research and for lawful medical or biogenetic advancement, including stem cell development, organ generation, or the creation of lawful human clones, provided such practices are expressly permitted and regulated under the laws of Pacifica, subject to oversight and audit by the People through referenda convened to maintain transparency and ensure that all research is directed toward the treatment and understanding of disease, disability, infertility, degenerative conditions, or mortality; and all remnants of aborted fetuses or related biological matter so used shall be treated as medical material or waste and disposed of in a manner that safeguards the health of People, Animals, other life, and the Property of others; beyond the first trimester, the power to regulate the conditions and limitations under which pregnancy may be terminated, or under which genetic material may be donated or cloned, shall be reserved to the several States or Territories of Pacifica, subject to uniform national ethical standards ensuring respect for human dignity, scientific transparency, and parental autonomy; after the point of fetal viability, defined as the demonstrable capacity of the fetus to survive outside the womb, termination shall be permissible only where the mother’s life or physical health is under sincere, measurable, and demonstrable risk, and in such cases, the law shall safeguard both the mother’s autonomy and the emergent interests of the viable fetus; a fetus shall not be deemed vested with independent rights prior to viability, and until birth, any fertilized egg, embryo, or fetus shall constitute the mutual property of the mother and father, who shall jointly bear the exclusive decision-making rights and responsibilities concerning it; this provision shall not annul any laws placing liability upon parents who endanger or impair the development of an unborn child, nor shall it limit the lawful scientific, therapeutic, or reproductive use of genetic material as permitted under Pacifican law; once a fetus attains viability, it gains limited protection from abortion except under exigent circumstances defined by law, thus recognizing its transitional moral standing as the “interest to be born”; furthermore, where one parent denies to the other the option of abortion, the parent denying such procedure shall bear full financial, personal, and custodial liability for the child during gestation and after birth, and in cases of single parenthood, must sustain and raise the child independently unless lawful consent for shared support is obtained; nothing herein shall be construed so as to inhibit the exchange of gifts or benefits between parents and children, nor to interfere with the familial rights of visitation, cohabitation, or kinship association among close relatives as provided by law, the governing principle remaining that reproductive autonomy, scientific progress, and the welfare of both progenitor and progeny shall coexist in harmony with the public interest and the rule of law.

No Person may be cloned, nor genetically engineered (or both), unless the procedure has been found suitable through Public open scientific research, reviewed and audited by the People, through queries individually authorized for the research, regulation, audit, or review, and such specific research or regulation to take place [or be enacted], which shall be initiated through referendum, which referendum shall require a majority vote cast by the People for authorization, which may enable [on a generalized basis] individual[ized]/specific medical treatment for the remedy of disability, infertility, illness, disease, or death, [and] only through the express and informed consent granted of the pre-existing parties involved, un-obstructed by another. If an infraction of this provision occurs, cloned or genetically engineered [or both] victims are to be provided protection under this Constitution. This provision is to be upheld and maintained through the legislature of Congress and each State.

Industrial and Commercial biological hacking, implants, RNA and DNA computers, as well as genetic-therapies, shall be regulated by law to protect the People, Animals, and the Environment/Nature from harm and irreparable injury or death.

No Person shall be compelled, incentivized, or coerced to accept an implanted chip, nanodevice, bio-metric tag, neural link, or any other internal tracking technology for identification, industry or commerce, employment, medical monitoring, exercise of a Privilege or to receive a public benefit, or the exercise of any natural or constitutional right. Any forced implantation shall constitute aggravated assault punishable as a felony crime under Pacifican law.

A Person’s body, organs, and genetics are their own, and no medical treatment sought or issued, either through implantation, infusion, or through other means integrated into the Person’s physiology, when in the case of debt, may ever be repossessed on demand or through coercion nor under duress from them, whether by any creditor or contractual obligation, nor through any other means otherwise occur, though this provision shall not affect the regulated legal acquisition of cadavers, organs, or genetics through their consenting donor/s, nor shall it restrict their legal inheritance upon death [however it shall be entrusted] through will or other testamentary disposition.

In the sovereign People's Nation of Pacifica, every individual holds an inalienable right to body hacking as an extension of personal sovereignty and self-ownership, encompassing the freedom to integrate, retain, use, maintain, modify, or remove cybernetic enhancements, implants, or bio-technological augmentations within one's physiology, including wireless networking capabilities such as Wi-Fi, BlueLink, nG cellular, and mesh networks; citizens may voluntarily augment their bodies with devices like multi-protocol signal emulators for RFID/NFC, sub-GHz, and infrared alongside nerve/neural interfaces, GeneralPurposeInputOutput equivalents, and sovereign wireless modules, without requiring external approval, provided no injury is inflicted on the rights others, while enjoying absolute liberty to use, reprogram, extract, disable, or abstain from any augmentation at any time, thereby upholding organismic integrity as paramount and ensuring all functions remain strictly user-controlled with no mandatory logging, backdoors, or surveillance; this right is grounded in the core principles of openness, decentralization, hands-on access, and mistrust of authority, promoting merit-based innovation, playful exploration, and collective improvement through secure, self-reliant bio-experimentation that extends to personal-[purpose] wireless connectivity; enhancements must respect others' rights and public safety, prohibiting non-consensual interfacing, signal spoofing, or disruption of critical infrastructure including unauthorized device or network access; the state shall not mandate, restrict, or regulate personal augmentations beyond general harm prevention, and rights to personal health, ensuring decentralization from medical, corporate, or governmental gatekeeping; ultimately, this right affirms the body as a domain of free access, mirroring the ethical hacker imperative to tinker, share, and evolve without coercion. No person shall be made to submit any of their implants or bodily extensions to the government for search or seizure, not even under warrant. All direct integrations into the body are considered extensions of that body and therefore protected absolutely under the right to integrity and autonomy. This Provision also covers prohibitions on governmental Van Eck phreaking of implants or a Person's body, and that the government may not attempt to use side channel attacks to circumvent the privacy or security of any person including their implant/s or bodily extension/s, even those of bionic, electronic, or cybernetic category, neither shall they [the implant/augmentation/s] be modified, restricted, or disabled for any public or private purpose except upon explicit consent of the individual who possesses them as a part of themself.

In order to stave of cases of genetic fraud, repel misplaced parental confidences, and reduce pedigree errors, it shall be required by law for Citizenship process established within Pacifica, that when a birth certificate is filed under any State, Territory, Fort, Facility, or Installation of Pacifica, for completion at the moment a child is born, there must be offered reliable and accurate DNA paternity testing which shall require an independent third-party to witness the sample collection, and which shall be required to be completed if requested by the man presumed of fatherhood, after [mandatorily available] being offered to him [for his approval/consent], before a he can lawfully be lawfully listed as the genetic father of such child/ren. No paternity finding shall be considered final until a DNA test proves the identity of the biological father. Non-biological fathers are exempt from having to pay child support in any case whatsoever. Likewise, in the case of female-to-female genetically-engineered-hybrids, the inseminating genetic-donor shall be offered parental-affirmation testing in similar manner to that of traditional paternity testing.

Neither Pacifica nor the States or any Territory nor Locality shall administer a DNA database of [a] Person/s or their Animal/s, except as shall be immediately necessary for the execution of laws & administration of Justice, and any entries within such a collection which are no longer required, or themselves are deemed un-reasonable to keep, shall be purged by secure erasure method without any traces or remnants or fragments or samples left behind; Any such database ⁸ be secured, and be protected by cascaded-layered quantum-secure encryption which required at least two personnel cooperate to access each layer, and only for reasonable purposes, subject to detailed logging of all entry creation, access, and deletion, and at all times shall be subject to the Natural Power of Audit by the People, as is consistent with the privacy interests of the parties contained within.

No Person’s DNA, bodily tissue, or bio-signature shall be collected, stored, manipulated, patented, or commercialized by any entity without explicit, revocable consent, nor shall any forced genetic therapy or editing be imposed under any medical, commercial, or emergency decree. All People retain sole ownership of their biological essence, and their children’s DNA until reaching adult class [where such title/possession right automatically transfers to the progeny upon adulthood], their family lines, and any emergent biotechnologies derived therefrom.

A dead Person is considered organic medical waste and must be disposed of, or otherwise [responsibly] dealt with, in a manner which does not endanger or otherwise threaten the health or life of People, Animals, other life, or damage the Property of others. A body is exempt from disposal if the body is stored in an appropriate manner to be re-animated at a later time, or if it is to be transferred in whole or by any requisite part/s for receipt as a piece of property, at the prior request of the deceased as according to contract; A dead Person still retains the Right to ‘Privacy of Person’, and examinations of the brain and nervous system must not attempt to extract information about a Person’s consciousness or private information such as memories, and of their neural-terrain, except in the case of consciousness storage and/or transfer/implantation at the prior request/testament through consent of the deceased, which process requires absolute confidentiality of the Individual’s consciousness, memories, and neuro-mapping; A violation of this Provision is punishable by imprisonment in for not less than seven-and-a-half, but not exceeding twenty-five years, if the offender shows definitive signs of [true] rehabilitation, otherwise the sentence shall become indeterminate with maximum penalties amounting up to life in prison without the possibility of parole and destruction of their brain upon death with no lawful potential for re-animation.

All forms of human experimentation shall be regulated by Congress and the legislature of each State, where the least forgiving and/or permissive law shall rule within their jurisdiction.

Congress shall have the authority to regulate the advertising of prescription medicines and treatments to ensure that all information presented to the public is truthful, transparent, and easily understood. All advertisements for prescription medicines or treatments shall be required to:
(a) Clearly state both the chemical/s name/s and, if applicable, the brand name of the medicine, presented side-by-side or top-by-bottom with equal prominence;
(b) Include a statement advising viewers to “do your research, and ask your doctor for advice, if you feel comfortable with this treatment or medicine”;
(c) Disclose all known side effects in a manner that is clear, conspicuous, and understandable to an average person, such that a reasonable viewer with average intelligence and standard abilities can comprehend the information upon first viewing. Rapid speech, fleeting text, or other methods that obscure or minimize side effect information are expressly prohibited. Any regulation or enforcement action under this Provision shall respect the principles of free speech, individual autonomy, and informed consent, and shall not impose unnecessary burdens beyond what is required to protect the public from deception or harm.
This Provision shall not be construed to limit the right of individuals to seek, receive, or share information about medicines or treatments from any lawful source.

Manufacturers, sellers, engineers, and creators of vaccines and other medical products shall bear full civil and criminal liability for any harm, injury, or death caused by their products, regardless of government approval or public recommendation. No law, regulation, or executive order shall grant immunity or shield from liability any individual or entity involved in the design, creation, production, distribution, or sale of vaccines or other medical products. All individuals harmed by a vaccine or medical product shall have the right to seek redress and compensation directly from any responsible party in a court of law, with no requirement to exhaust administrative remedies or participate in government compensation programs as a prerequisite. This Provision shall not be construed to limit the right of individuals to make informed medical choices, nor to restrict access to truthful information about medical products and their risks.

Recognizing the inherent dignity, autonomy, and liberty of every individual, this Provision affirms and protects the civil rights, natural freedoms, and equal opportunities of persons with disabilities in Pacifica by prohibiting discrimination, guaranteeing accessibility, and ensuring respect for their choices and self-determination. A person shall be considered to have a disability if they have a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such an impairment, or are [honestly] regarded as having such an impairment. Major life activities include, but are not limited to: caring for oneself, learning, working, communicating, attaining/maintaining rationality/sanity or operating without severe delusions that unground the individual from reality, and participating fully in society. No person shall, on the basis of disability, be denied the full and equal enjoyment of any public or private place, employment opportunity, government service, transportation, education, housing, or telecommunications. Discrimination includes exclusion, segregation, denial of reasonable accommodations, or any adverse action that limits equality of opportunity. Public and private entities shall provide reasonable accommodations and modifications necessary to enable persons with disabilities to perform essential functions, access services, and participate in community life, unless doing so would impose an undue burden, defined as significant difficulty or expense fundamentally impairing essential operations or liberties. Accommodations shall respect the individual's preferences and dignity. All entities shall ensure effective communication with persons with disabilities through accessible formats, auxiliary aids, services, technologies, and personnel appropriate to their needs, including but not limited to braille, sign language, captioning, telecommunications relay services, and dual trained medical-psychiatric staff. Persons with disabilities shall have the right to prompt, fair, and transparent legal processes protecting their rights in all matters, including accommodations and institutionalization decisions. Their privacy, bodily autonomy, and personal data shall be safeguarded against unwarranted intrusion or coercion. Employers shall provide equal opportunity and reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities without discrimination. Medical examinations or inquiries related to disability shall be strictly limited to ensure protection of privacy and non-discrimination. Persons with disabilities shall have equal access to inclusive, quality education and necessary supports, respectful of their individual educational needs and aspirations. Persons with disabilities have the right to access healthcare and supportive services necessary to maintain health, independence, and participation in society, provided on a voluntary, informed-consent basis, respecting their autonomy, and to receive the irrevocable privilege to welfare benefits and public programmes, so long as the disability persists. No person shall be subject to retaliation, coercion, or adverse actions due to their exercise of disability rights or advocacy, including filing complaints or participating in investigations. Pacifica shall promote policies, technologies, and practices that enhance accessibility, inclusion, and self-determination for persons with disabilities, supporting their full participation and [capable] contributions to society.

Every person with a disability shall have the unalienable right to be accompanied by a service animal trained to perform tasks directly related to that disability. Service animals shall be permitted access to all places open to the public and private services, including transportation, housing, employment, education, and government facilities, without fees or restrictions except for the safety of others. No inquiry into the nature, severity, or existence of a person's disability shall be allowed. No documentation, certification, registration, license, or disclosure of disability shall be required as a precondition for service animal access. Service animals must be maintained under the handler's control by appropriate means. Where use of standard control devices conflicts with the handler's disability or the animal's task, alternative means of control shall be accepted. The right of disabled individuals [acting lawfully] to use service animals for assistance [for such purpose] shall take precedence over conflicting public or private interests, except where there is a clear, significant, and directly demonstrable threat to health or safety. Animals currently in training to become service animals shall enjoy all protections afforded to fully trained service animals. Emotional support, therapy, or companion animals shall not be considered service animals under this Provision, but maybe protected elsewhere in law. Handlers shall remain responsible for the conduct and welfare of their service animals.

No person with a disability [including but not limited to psychiatric disturbance] shall be involuntarily institutionalized or segregated in a public facility when community-based treatment and support services are appropriate and available, and the person does not object to such placement. Public entities shall provide sufficient necessary services and supports in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of persons with disabilities, ensuring full participation in community life, including but not limited to family, social, educational, education, employment, and cultural activities. Unjustified institutionalization or segregation of persons with disabilities constitutes discrimination and is prohibited. Community-based services shall be provided unless doing so would impose an undue burden, defined by a significant and unreasonable cost that fundamentally alters essential public services. Individuals shall have the right to prompt review and appeal of any institutionalization decisions affecting their rights under this Provision.

In the interest of justice, all conversion therapy that is not explicitly consented to by the recipient without coercion or manipulation, is hereby deemed unlawful, not merely illegal.

SECTION. 11.

Any Person owning or controlling real estate or other premises who voluntarily damages or destroys a drone, robot, or other device or vehicle/craft trespassing upon the real estate or premises, whether automated or not, being either on the land or within the airspace of the premises which is not otherwise regulated by the government as according to this Constitution, shall, together with any successors in interest, if any, NOT be civilly or criminally liable for causing the damage or destruction to the property of such Person or other entity.

No government agency or member of the public body may deploy drones, robotic, or surveillance device except under specific circumstances; the members of the public office or agency of government may not deploy drones, robots, or automated devices, except in the case of State rescuers in search and rescue missions, or as prescribed by law and approved by citizens in a referendum for a specific purpose or goal.

SECTION. 12.

People have a right to freely use the common electric, magnetic, and electromagnetic frequency spectrums, and to operate their equipment thereon, within the public or private domain, in accordance with the [mutual] non-aggression principle; This includes but is not limited to: Use, experimentation, or operation of oscilloscope, signal generator, radio scanner, spectrum analyzer, RF imager, transmitter, receiver, transceiver, transmission array, broadcasting or communication equipment, radio-telephone or radio-videophone, modem, computer, robot, particle accelerator, electro-laser or lamdaser, electrodynamic craft, astro-dynamic energy system, scientific experiment, or other related device; The Legislature has no power to deny to a Citizen the right to use the electric, magnetic, and electromagnetic spectrum/s in the Public or Private domain, and to operate their equipment in the ordinary course of their inclination or pleasure; No government agent or agency may deploy such technology except as needed to properly execute the laws of the Union in conformity to this Constitution, which trust shall be placed under the Authority of the People, who will grant or limit the use of such technology by the government.

The government is strictly prohibited in engaging in the design, development, creation, implementation, integration, use, or requirement of blackboxes, backdoors, and password protection or encryption skeleton keys, in publicly or privately held and/or operated hardware, equipment, devices, programming languages, micro-code, firmware, operating systems, drivers, and software. This shall not preclude the ability of the government to remotely administer its own systems for equitable purposes.

There is no right to have customers consuming your services, nor to have receivers tune your transmissions, but you as a Person have a right to provide such services and transmissions as an option available, without obstruction of your freedom to offer them, to others, except for as may be provided under this Constitution and by the laws made in conformity underneath it. This shall not prohibit laws being enacted and enforced which protect the People from decibel levels of artificially created or amplified noise which they find interruptive/disruptive to their ability to think, or which interferes/disrupts with their person-to-person verbal communication which happens within a physical-proximity of distance reasonable to expect that they may be heard, or that which causes damages to their person or any other rights. This fact of there not being a right to the unwilling co-participation in your rights or privileges with others extends to the correctly attained interpretation of its base/core principle/s, that there is no protection by law for a business against people speaking out to others in opposition against any particular business or alliance/group of them, nor to people deciding to refuse to transact for any reason; Neither is there any protection against outside sources of interference with one’s wireless transmissions, or to have People tune into your transmissions, though there is the right to openly and un-constrainedly produce such emissions for personal purpose, and the [potentially restricted] privilege for commerce. This shall not prohibit laws being enacted and enforced which protect the People from field strength and power levels of artificially created or amplified wireless transmissions which they find causes physical damages to their Person or another person, or which damages any other rights. The right to exercise one’s freedoms is not the power to require another participate in/with such exercise, or to cooperate with or alter their otherwise just behavior in order to meet conformity to the will or intention expressed through your exercise.

SECTION. 13.

The right to privacy shall consist in each citizen of Pacifica or the several States retaining ownership and possession of identifying information about themselves. The right to privacy should be understood as an extension of the right to property: we own identifying information about ourselves; having such information taken without our consent by the government or by private corporations is a form of theft. The right to privacy is a vital bulwark guarding citizens against concentrations of power in both the public and private sectors, and is a clear and reasonable implication of other existing enumerated rights in this Constitution.

An artificial entity must provide a legally binding declaration of their terms of use, information/data collection policy and its use, as well as privacy and security provisions, which documentation shall be incorporated and readily apparent at the first instance of interaction or use of their provided service, as well as be presented in a similar fashion every time it is changed/updated and implemented, and describe and provide an easily accessible mechanism to change privacy settings, to review the presented notice, and enforce opt-in consent to anything related to the product, program, service, or questionnaire/test in question, including declining to enable transmission of personal information/data from the second party of the artificial entity with any additional outside or third parties. All terms must be provided for download, and which shall include all formatting found within the document, and shall by law be required to contain zero tracking, phone home, or other malicious code.

All People have a natural right to privacy; All people have a right to keep their personal lives to themselves, and to keep secrets, which is related to their right to not self-incriminate. Every person has the right to privacy in relation to their communications, including but not limited to, mail, telecommunications, and electronic messaging.
All People have a natural right to privacy; All people have a right to keep their personal lives to themselves, and to keep secrets, which is related to their right to not self-incriminate. Every person has the right to privacy in relation to their communications, including but not limited to, mail, telecommunications, and electronic messaging.

The right to and freedom of Pseudonymity, as well as to that of Anonymity, shall not be restricted, denied, suspended, abridged, obstructed, infringed/impacted/impaired, or otherwise compromised upon, regardless of circumstance, except as may be prescribed [and as shall be limited] under this Constitution.

The right to Pseudonymity, Anonymity, and Privacy, unless it can be shown to directly and obviously harm others or affect State Security [in a specific instance, on a case by case basis], shall not be abridged in any way. Private Individuals shall not have their private lives divulged in any form without their consent unless they commit felonies, or failure to divulge such information can be shown to affect or harm others in a direct and obvious way.

Professional-client confidentiality and privilege shall be defined by law.

In protecting the right of privacy, anonymity in public, and [greater] liberty of the People, there shall be no neighborhood watch, as such can become Cause Stalking or Gang-stalking, furthermore, having such a neighborhood watch goes against the right to privacy, as well that no one can be accused without knowing the accusation and the accuser before him/her, while neighborhood watching implies a Person’s guilt before proving their innocence.

The People shall be secure against general and pervasive surveillance in private and public places, whether done by government or private actors, that has a chilling effect on their private and civic activities, without specific public court orders pursuant to acts of Congress for State Security, narrowly tailored to the scope of an ongoing investigation of [a] specific individual/s or an organization/institution, or the Legislatures of the several States for their own Security. As a part of the protection in the People’s right to be free from surveillance, mass surveillance, otherwise known as “bulk collection”, is strictly unconstitutional, and is an act of treasonous aggression against the Naturally Free and Sovereign Persons of Pacifica.

The right to build, use, or conceal personal anti-surveillance measures, signal jamming, encryption, or counter-monitoring technologies shall be unrestricted.

There shall exist and be recognized as inherent, unalienable, pre-political, and universally endowed a natural right of personal sovereignty over all sensing, scanning, fingerprinting, and tracking of persons, their property, their movements, their presence, their motions, their gestures, their activities, their behaviors, and their biometric and behavioral data, whether such sensing is effected by wireless or radio-frequency means including but not limited to beamforming feedback information, channel state information, radio fingerprinting, Wi‑Fi sensing, RADAR, or any analogous electromagnetic or photonic or electric or acoustic or sonar or lidar or optical or thermal or magnetic or inertial or multipath or reflection-based or time-of-flight or phase-based or amplitude-based or polarization-based or frequency-domain or time-domain or spatial-domain sensing modality, and whether such sensing is conducted by any governmental actor at any level, or by any industrial, commercial, private, nonprofit, or other non-governmental actor, and whether such sensing is conducted in public places or private places or on public or private property or across any boundary or through any barrier, and whether such sensing is active or passive or cooperative or non-cooperative or device-dependent or device-free or user-aware or user-unaware, and whether such sensing is framed as anonymized or aggregated or de-identified or statistical or experimental or research or security or public-safety or convenience or efficiency or commercial-innovation or any other purpose. Except as expressly and narrowly provided herein, in no event shall any such sensing be lawfully employed to infer, deduce, record, store, transmit, analyze, monetize, share, sell, license, aggregate, cross-reference, persist, retain, or otherwise exploit the presence, motion, gesture, activity, identity, location, trajectory, pattern, habit, preference, health state, emotional state, or behavioral profile of any person or property without that person’s explicit, opt-in, priority, informed, revocable, and freely given consent that is obtained prior to any such sensing and that may be revoked at any time by the data subject for any reason or for no reason, such revocation to take immediate effect and to bind all actors and all systems to cease sensing, cease processing, cease storing, and securely delete all data derived from or related to that person and to refrain from any further inference or tracking of that person. A narrowly tailored exception shall exist for constitutionally warranted matters of State security and actual military operations in time of declared war, including limited testing, calibration, and debugging of national defense sensing systems, provided that such activities are strictly necessary and proportionate to a legitimate defense objective, are conducted pursuant to publicly accountable legal authorization, are subject to independent oversight and audit, employ data minimization and technical safeguards to prevent unnecessary identification of persons, and prohibit the use, retention, transfer, or repurposing of any incidentally collected data concerning identifiable persons except where strictly required for an active and lawful military objective, in which case such data shall be subject to strict temporal limits, access controls, and mandatory deletion upon cessation of necessity. A further narrowly tailored exception shall exist for the private, personal use of sensing technologies by a natural person acting in a private capacity, solely on their own property or in the course of lawful activity in public, and only as incidental to the operation of an essential technological device or contrivance, including but not limited to cameras, vehicles, night-vision systems, forward-looking infrared systems, navigation systems, or personal and premises security devices, and solely for the narrow purposes of exercising the rights to liberty, property, self-security, self-defense, and the defense of others; provided that such use shall not be employed for commercial exploitation, systematic or mass surveillance, persistent tracking of non-consenting persons, or the creation, retention, or dissemination of biometric or behavioral profiles of non-consenting persons beyond what is strictly incidental and ephemeral to the immediate function of the device, and any non-incidental data so collected shall remain fully subject to the consent, ownership, and deletion requirements herein. Any consent that is bundled, coerced, conditioned, buried in terms, presented as a default, made unavoidable to access essential services, or otherwise obtained without clear, conspicuous, accessible, and understandable disclosure shall be null and void ab initio and without legal force or effect. All biometric and behavioral data and all derived signatures, embeddings, fingerprints, profiles, inferences, estimates, reconstructions, and models that are generated from or by means of any such sensing modality shall be the exclusive personal property and sovereign data of the individual person from whom such data arise, and no person, entity, corporation, association, government, or other actor shall claim ownership, title, license, preferential right, or any form of dominion over such data, and no person, entity, corporation, association, government, or other actor shall assert a right to use, retain, process, transfer, license, sell, monetize, or otherwise exploit such data without the individual’s explicit, opt-in, priority, informed, revocable consent, and any such data collected or inferred in violation of this Provision shall be deemed product of intrusion and shall be subject to mandatory secure deletion, audit, and restoration of the data subject’s full sovereignty over their data, and no doctrine of abandonment, implied consent, public exposure, reasonable expectation of non-existence of privacy in public, or any analogous legal fiction shall be construed to diminish or negate the natural right of personal ownership and control over one’s own biometric and behavioral data as herein endowed. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to permit the use of any such sensing modality for the presence, motion, gesture, activity, or positioning or tracking of persons or their property without explicit opt-in priority consent with reservation of revocation, except as narrowly provided for in the foregoing exceptions, and no statutory, regulatory, contractual, administrative, judicial, or policy authorization, nor any warrant, subpoena, exigency, national-security claim, emergency declaration, public-safety assertion, or any other guise or pretext shall operate to override or dilute the opt-in priority consent requirement and the data-ownership reservation herein set forth outside the strict bounds of those exceptions, and any law, rule, regulation, order, policy, or practice that purports to authorize or excuse non-consensual sensing, non-consensual inference, non-consensual storage, non-consensual processing, or non-consensual sharing or monetization of such data shall be void as repugnant to the natural rights herein declared. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to permit the expansion of the foregoing exceptions beyond their expressly stated scope, and the burden shall rest on any actor invoking such exception to demonstrate strict compliance with necessity, proportionality, minimization, and accountability requirements, with any ambiguity resolved in favor of the data subject. Any actor who violates this Provision shall be held accountable under civil, criminal, and equitable remedies that include but are not limited to actual damages, statutory damages per person per incident, punitive damages where malice, recklessness, or willful disregard is shown, injunctive and declaratory relief, attorneys’ fees and costs, and individual and class-wide relief, and any person shall have standing to enforce this Section on their own behalf and on behalf of others similarly situated, and any sovereign, qualified, or other immunity that would shield actors from liability for non-consensual sensing or non-consensual exploitation of biometric or behavioral data is hereby abrogated to the extent necessary to ensure full redress and deterrence.
This Provision shall be grounded in and interpreted according to naturalism, which is the political philosophy that recognizes absolute self-regulating unalienable inherent omnipresent universally endowed pre-political natural rights and all innovations of modalities which rest upon those basic rights, namely to life and health, liberty and autonomy and independence, social security and self-defense and the right to secure and defend others, privacy, property, and the pursuit of happiness, and any construction that would undermine or diminish those rights in favor of governmental convenience, industrial efficiency, commercial profit, technological novelty, or any other interest shall be rejected as contrary to the natural law foundation of this Provision, and the enumeration of specific sensing modalities herein shall not be construed to limit the application of this Provision to future or analogous technologies that achieve the same ends of presence, motion, gesture, activity, or positioning or tracking of persons or property, and the rights herein shall be construed broadly in favor of the data subject and narrowly against any actor seeking to intrude, and the Congress or any State's legislative body shall enact such implementing legislation as may be necessary and proper to effectuate the natural rights herein declared, including but not limited to standards for consent, revocation, notice, data minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, secure deletion, audit, transparency, algorithmic accountability, and independent oversight, and no rule of strict construction, no canon of deference to agencies, and no doctrine of implied authorization shall be used to circumvent the explicit opt-in priority consent and data-ownership requirements of this Provision, and the people retain the right to defend themselves and others against violations of this Provision by all lawful means, including the right to secure and maintain personal countermeasures that prevent unauthorized sensing, scanning, fingerprinting, or tracking, and the right to demand that all devices, systems, networks, and venues be designed and operated by default in a privacy-preserving, consent-first, data-minimizing, and deletion-enabled manner that respects the natural rights herein proclaimed.
