No law shall abridge the right of the people to record their ‘public authorities’ while they are exercising their official public duties.

The right of the People to record their own communications, including telephone calls, video conversations, and other forms of interaction, shall not be abridged or denied. Any person who is a party to a communication has the unqualified right to record that communication, whether by audio, video, or other means, without the knowledge or consent of other parties. Every person has the natural and unalienable right to record, film, or otherwise surveil any activity, sound, or image that may be observed, heard, or otherwise captured from within their own private property or any property where they have lawful presence or control. This right shall extend to all forms of private surveillance, including but not limited to security cameras, audio recorders, and personal devices. Any recording lawfully made from one’s own private property or as a party to a communication shall be the exclusive property of the person making the recording. Such recordings may be used, disclosed, or published at the sole discretion of the recorder, subject only to laws protecting against defamation, fraud, or other criminal misuse. No law, regulation, or executive order shall prohibit, restrict, or penalize the act of single-party recording of communications or activities as described herein. Any existing law to the contrary is hereby null and void. Nothing in this provision shall be construed to authorize trespass, unlawful surveillance of private spaces where the recorder has no lawful presence, or the use of recordings for the commission of a crime. This provision shall be construed liberally in favor of individual liberty, property rights, and transparency. The judiciary shall provide swift and effective remedies for any violation of these rights.

Every person has the right to be protected against the misuse of their personal data.

No Public or Private communications agency or internet service provider shall collect information or data on Individuals other than which is necessary for billing or is required by a warrant, or exchange in any form of third party or foreign agency collection of information or data.

All private personal information/data collected by the Public Administration shall be used only for the purposes for which they were collected, shall be kept confidential and shared only with the express and informed consent of all the Persons to whom it relates, unless sharing such information is necessary for the performance of duties provided for under this Constitution; all Individuals whose data are stored by any body of the Public Administration other than Law Enforcement shall be entitled to obtain a copy of such data and require that they be destroyed if the purposes for which they were collected no longer apply; nothing in this provision shall prevent the Public Administration from storing data of Agents and Members of the Public Administration and any other natural Person contracting therewith, as may be found necessary for transparency and other reasons constituting a public interest.

No Person shall have their privacy violated by freezing of assets, searches, seizures, surveillance, accessing and gathering of their private personal information without their express and informed consent, including obtaining it from third parties or using digital means, unless pursuant to a Warrant, and only to the extent which is necessary to achieve the purpose for which the Warrant was issued and particularly describing the assets to be frozen, the places or Persons to be searched, the things or Persons to be seized, the Persons to be put under surveillance, including the maximum period of that surveillance, and the data to be obtained and stored, including the period for which it may be retained; nothing in this provision shall prevent the collection of information which has been made available to the public or shared voluntarily.

People have the right to be secure in their Persons, personal and private information/records which include but are not limited to medical and psychological information/records, papers, homes, articles, effects, location as well as network information, electronic and radio data (including, but not limited to, meta-data) as well as private communications, from [any and all] un-reasonable private interference, searches, seizures, and storage, by a Private entity, without the information/data being technically necessary to provide/deliver a consensually entered into service, as it is advertised, for them to be allowed to be collected, and it must be provable before a court they had the right under this provision’s stipulations, to have such data, by private companies; and no warrant to search any place, or seize any Person or thing, or access electronic data or communications, shall issue without particularly describing the place to be searched, or the Person or thing to be seized, tracked, or put under surveillance, or the data or communication to be accessed, as nearly as may be; nor without [unassailable] probable cause, supported by written oath or affirmation. Neither Congress nor the several States or other Territories shall pass any law abridging or infringing the right of the People to encrypt their documents, effects, data, and communications.

Government Trojan Horse/s [viruses] (Also known as Remote Administration Toolkits, or “RATs”) shall be prohibited, in addition to Keyloggers, as well as Worms, and any other form of Spyware or other Malware, regardless of if they are authorized by a warrant, or to how such “Bugging” may serve a justified pursuit of surveillance;-And [the] Hacking of, or installing Spyware/Malware onto/into, others’ privately held and/or operated equipment, devices, programming languages, micro-code, firmware, operating systems, drivers, and software, by the government shall always be considered a form of [unlawful] tampering.

The Citizens of Pacifica shall have the access to information which relates to any aspect of the functioning of any body of any branch of the Public Administration which is not classified, and no information shall be classified unless it is absolutely necessary for the purposes of State Security.

Private information on public figures, such as Personal Phone Number or Residential Address/es, cannot be divulged without their consent, unless it can be shown to serve the public interest.

The Courts of Pacifica and the several States shall be required to retain their records of all cases they are a part in, for a period of time no shorter than 12 years, or the greatest value of years through the statute of limitations relevant to the case, whichever is longer.

SECTION. 13.333.

Members of government who intentionally spread disinformation or deliberately misinform their constituents in the performance of their public duties and capacities shall be guilty of lying to the Public for whom which they are intended to serve, and shall be subject to punishment for a felony, which sentence shall not be commutable, and shall be determined by the Citizen’s court.

Public/Governmental radio and television conversations are open to listening and review by the People in real time, except those which are necessary to protect in the interest of State or State Security, or the security of premises, Persons, and valuable resources like vaults and money or guns, et cetera… This provision shall not preclude the release of protected information after the period for which such protection remains relevant for the purposes set forth here and elsewhere under this Constitution expire.

Right of the People to audit any department of government, or any information they contain, including classified State secret divisions, operations, knowledge, or data, without being sworn to secrecy or be bound by gag order. Freedom of information requests must be answered by the Government in a timely fashion, and any denial must state in clear, concise, and accurate terms the reason for the denial, and offer a date where such records are no longer due protection by secrecy, and as to why, if reasonable to furnish the reason.

SECTION. 13.666.

Sub-SECTION. 1.

We the People of Pacifica declare, that all Persons have the right to: Know if somebody is collecting personal data, Stop another entity from using their data in a certain way, Object to profiling and automated decision-making, Object to marketing, Know an entity’s data policies, Withdraw consent to data processing, Refuse automated profiling, Make decisions regarding their data, Request copies of their data and access the data held on them with secure downloadable copies of their data made freely available, Amend their data, and Delete their data, Non-discrimination if they withdraw consent or exercise any of these rights.

We [the People] declare that Consumers possess Rights to: Delete Personal Information, Correct Inaccurate Personal Information, Know What Personal Information is Sold or Shared and to Whom, Opt Out of Sale or Sharing of Personal Information, Limit Use and Disclosure of Sensitive Personal Information.

We [the People] declare that Individuals are to be in control of their own bio-metric data, and that the law shall prohibit private companies from collecting it unless they: Inform the person in writing of what data is being collected or stored. (e.g. fingerprint is stored when using TouchID to log into a bank account app on phone); Inform the person in writing of the specific purpose and limited length of time for which the data will be collected, stored and used. (e.g. fingerprint is stored for ease of logging into the app and only for a duration of six months); Obtain the person’s written consent. (e.g. user signs their name before sharing their fingerprint).

Sub-SECTION. 2.

Data collectors shall collect as little information as they need to run the business.
Inform customers about every way their data will be processed (including 3rd party providers).
Enable customers to delete, export, or update their data at any point in time.
And finally, gain a customer’s unambiguous consent for every data processing activity.

Inform customers that their personal data is being collected by the Service Provider.
Inform customers whether their personal data is sold or disclosed and to whom.
Allow customers to reject the sale of their personal data.
Allow customers to access their personal data.
Allow customers to request deletion of any personal information about them.
Not discriminate against customers who exercised their privacy rights.

Specific opt-in consent is required for the processing of sensitive personal information;
Specific consent is required for the disclosure of personal information;
Personal information handlers handling already disclosed personal information, where there is a major impact on individual rights and interests, shall obtain personal consent;
Collected personal images and personal distinguishing identity characteristic information can only be used for the purpose of public security. If personal information handlers want to use it for other purposes, they are required to collect separate consent from individuals; and
Parental consent is required for the processing of personal information of kids below the age of fourteen.

Personal information handlers must provide individuals an explicit privacy notice “before handling” of their personal information. This notice should include relevant information including the identity and contact method of the personal information handler, any subsequent third party handlers, the purpose and methods of personal information handling, the categories of handled personal information, the retention period, and procedures for individuals to exercise their individual rights under the PIPL.
information/data controller/processor

Sub-SECTION. 3.

A consumer shall have the right to request that a business that collects a consumer’s personal information, disclose to that consumer, the categories and specific pieces of personal information that the business has collected.

A consumer shall have the right to request that a business delete any personal information about the consumer which the business has collected from the consumer.

A consumer shall have the right to request that a business that collects personal information about the consumer disclose
to the consumer the following: The categories of personal information it has collected about that consumer; The categories of sources from which the personal information is collected; The business or commercial purpose for collecting or selling personal information; The categories of third parties with whom the business shares personal information; The specific pieces of personal information it has collected about that consumer.

A consumer shall have the right to request that a business that sells the consumer’s personal information, or that discloses it for a business purpose, disclose to that consumer: The categories of personal information that the business collected about the consumer; The categories of personal information that the business sold about the consumer and the categories of third parties to whom the personal information was sold, by category or categories of personal information for each category of third parties to whom the personal information was sold; The categories of personal information that the business disclosed about the consumer for a business purpose;
A business that sells personal information about a consumer, or that discloses a consumer’s personal information for a business purpose, shall disclose, pursuant to this section, the information specified within it to the consumer upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request from the consumer.

A business that sells consumers’ personal information, or that discloses consumers’ personal information for a business purpose, shall disclose, pursuant to this section: The category or categories of consumers’ personal information it has sold, or if the business has not sold consumers’ personal information, it shall disclose that fact; The category or categories of consumers’ personal information it has disclosed for a business purpose, or if the business has not disclosed the consumers’ personal information for a business purpose, it shall disclose that fact;

A third party shall not sell personal information about a consumer that has been sold to the third party by a business unless the consumer has received explicit notice and is provided an opportunity to exercise the right to opt-out pursuant to this Section.

A consumer shall have the right, at any time, to direct a business that sells personal information about the consumer to third parties not to sell the consumer’s personal information. This right may be referred to as the right to opt-out.
A business that sells consumers’ personal information to third parties shall provide notice to consumers, pursuant to this Section, that this information may be sold and that consumers have the “right to opt-out” of the sale of their personal information.
A business shall not sell the personal information of consumers if the business has actual knowledge that the consumer is less than sixteen years of age, unless the consumer, in the case of consumers at least thirteen years of age and less than sixteen years of age, or the consumer’s parent or guardian, in the case of consumers who are less than thirteen years of age, has affirmatively authorized the sale of the consumer’s personal information. A business that willfully disregards the consumer’s age shall be deemed to have had actual knowledge of the consumer’s age. This right may be referred to as the “right to opt-in.”
A business that has received direction from a consumer not to sell the consumer’s personal information or, in the case of a minor consumer’s personal information has not received consent to sell the minor consumer’s personal information shall be prohibited, pursuant to this Section, from selling the consumer’s personal information after its receipt of the consumer’s direction, unless the consumer subsequently provides express authorization for the sale of the consumer’s personal information.

Consumers’ have the Right of No Retaliation Following Opt Out or Exercise of Other Rights. A business shall not discriminate against a consumer because the consumer exercised any of the consumer’s rights under this title, including, but not limited to, by: Denying goods or services to the consumer; Charging different prices or rates for goods or services, including through the use of discounts or other benefits or imposing penalties; Providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer; Suggesting that the consumer will receive a different price or rate for goods or services or a different level or quality of goods or services; Retaliating against an employee, applicant for employment, or independent contractor, as defined in this Section, for exercising their rights under this title. Nothing in this Provision prohibits a business pursuant to this same section from charging a consumer a different price or rate, or from providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer, if that difference is reasonably related to the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data. This provision does not prohibit a business from offering loyalty, rewards, premium features, discounts, or club card programs consistent with this title.

The Data-Subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data and the following information:
The purposes of the processing;
The categories of personal data concerned;
The recipients or categories of recipient to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed, in particular recipients in third countries or international organizations;
Where possible, the envisaged period for which the personal data will be stored, or, if not possible, the criteria used to determine that period;
The existence of the right to request from the controller rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning the data subject or to object to such processing;
The right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority;
Where the personal data are not collected from the data subject, any available information as to their source;
The existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, at least in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject.
Where personal data are transferred to a third country or to an international organization, the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards relating to the transfer.
The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing. For any further copies requested by the data subject, the controller may charge a reasonable fee based on administrative costs. Where the data subject makes the request by electronic means, and unless otherwise requested by the data subject, the information shall be provided in a commonly used electronic form.
The right to obtain a copy of data referred to in this Section shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.

Sub-SECTION. 4.

An enterprise served with a “Data-Subject Access Request” is legally obligated to fulfill these requests within a limited time-frame to avoid non-compliance. A business shall provide required information to a consumer only upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request; Businesses have sixty days to respond to the request.

In order to comply with this Constitution, a business shall in a form that is reasonably accessible to consumers: Make available to consumers two or more designated methods for submitting requests for information required to be disclosed pursuant to this Section, including, at a minimum, a toll-free telephone number. A business that operates exclusively online and has a direct relationship with a consumer from whom it collects personal information shall only be required to provide an email address for submitting requests for information required to be disclosed pursuant to this Section;
Disclose and deliver the required information to a consumer free of charge within forty-five days of receiving a verifiable consumer request from the consumer. The business shall promptly take steps to determine whether the request is a verifiable consumer request, but this shall not extend the business’ duty to disclose and deliver the information within forty-five days of receipt of the consumer’s request. The time period to provide the required information may be extended once by an additional forty-five days when reasonably necessary, provided the consumer is provided notice of the extension within the first forty-five-day period. The disclosure shall cover the twelve-month period preceding the business’ receipt of the verifiable consumer request and shall be made in writing and delivered through the consumer’s account with the business, if the consumer maintains an account with the business, or by mail or electronically at the consumer’s option if the consumer does not maintain an account with the business, in a readily usable format that allows the consumer to transmit this information from one entity to another entity without hindrance. The business may require authentication of the consumer that is reasonable in light of the nature of the personal information requested, but shall not require the consumer to create an account with the business in order to make a verifiable consumer request. If the consumer maintains an account with the business, the business may require the consumer to submit the request through that account.

A business that collects a consumer’s personal information shall, at or before the point of collection, inform consumers as to the categories of personal information to be collected and the purposes for which the categories of personal information shall be used. A business shall not collect additional categories of personal information or use personal information collected for additional purposes without providing the consumer with notice consistent with this section.

A business that receives a verifiable consumer request from a consumer to access personal information shall promptly take steps to disclose and deliver, free of charge to the consumer, the personal information required by this section. The information may be delivered by mail or electronically, and if provided electronically, the information shall be in a portable and, to the extent technically feasible, readily usable format that allows the consumer to transmit this information to another entity without hindrance. A business may provide personal information to a consumer at any time, but shall not be required to provide personal information to a consumer more than twice in a twelve-month period.

A business that collects personal information about consumers shall disclose, pursuant to the laws of Congress and this Constitution, the consumer’s rights to request the deletion of the consumer’s personal information.

A business that receives a verifiable consumer request from a consumer to delete the consumer’s personal information pursuant to this section shall delete the consumer’s personal information from its records and direct any service providers to delete the consumer’s personal information from their records.

A business or a service provider shall not be required to comply with a consumer’s request to delete the consumer’s personal information if it is necessary for the business or service provider to maintain the consumer’s personal information in order to: Complete the transaction for which the personal information was collected, fulfill the terms of a written warranty or product recall conducted in accordance with federal law, provide a good or service requested by the consumer, or reasonably anticipated within the context of a business’ ongoing business relationship with the consumer, or otherwise perform a contract between the business and the consumer; Detect security incidents, protect against malicious, deceptive, fraudulent, or illegal activity; or prosecute those responsible for that activity; Debug to identify and repair errors that impair existing intended functionality; Exercise free speech, ensure the right of another consumer to exercise that consumer’s right of free speech, or exercise another right provided for by law; Comply with other Privacy laws; Engage in public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical, or statistical research in the public interest that adheres to all other applicable ethics and privacy laws, when the business’ deletion of the information is likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of such research, if the consumer has provided informed consent; To enable solely internal uses that are reasonably aligned with the expectations of the consumer based on the consumer’s relationship with the business; Comply with a legal obligation; Otherwise use the consumer’s personal information, internally, in a lawful manner that is compatible with the context in which the consumer provided the information.

A business that collects personal information about a consumer shall disclose to the consumer, pursuant to this Section, the information specified by it upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request from the consumer.

A business that collects personal information about consumers shall disclose, pursuant to this section: The categories of personal information it has collected about consumers; The categories of sources from which the personal information is collected; The business or commercial purpose for collecting or selling personal information; The categories of third parties with whom the business shares personal information; That a consumer has the right to request the specific pieces of personal information the business has collected about that consumer.

This Section does not require a business to do the following: Retain any personal information about a consumer collected for a single one-time transaction if, in the ordinary course of business, that information about the consumer is not retained; Re-identify or otherwise link any data that, in the ordinary course of business, is not maintained in a manner that would be considered personal information.

A business shall not discriminate against a consumer because the consumer exercised any of the consumer’s rights under this title, including, but not limited to, by: Denying goods or services to the consumer; Charging different prices or rates for goods or services, including through the use of discounts or other benefits or imposing penalties; Providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer; Suggesting that the consumer will receive a different price or rate for goods or services or a different level or quality of goods or services;

Nothing in this Section prohibits a business from charging a consumer a different price or rate, or from providing a different level or quality of goods or services to the consumer, if that difference is reasonably related to the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data.

A business may offer financial incentives, including payments to consumers as compensation, for the collection of personal information, the sale of personal information, or the deletion of personal information. A business may also offer a different price, rate, level, or quality of goods or services to the consumer if that price or difference is directly related to the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data; A business that offers any financial incentives pursuant to this subdivision shall notify consumers of the financial incentives pursuant to this Section; A business may enter a consumer into a financial incentive program only if the consumer gives the business prior opt-in consent pursuant to this Section that clearly describes the material terms of the financial incentive program, and which may be revoked by the consumer at any time; A business shall not use financial incentive practices that are unjust, unreasonable, coercive, or usurious in nature.

A business may offer financial incentives, including payments to consumers as compensation, for the collection of personal information, the sale or sharing of personal information, or the retention of personal information. A business may also offer a different price, rate, level, or quality of goods or services to the consumer if that price or difference is reasonably related to the value provided to the business by the consumer’s data. A business that offers any financial incentives pursuant to this subdivision, shall notify consumers of the financial incentives pursuant to this Section. A business may enter a consumer into a financial incentive program only if the consumer gives the business prior opt-in consent pursuant to this Section that clearly describes the material terms of the financial incentive program, and which may be revoked by the consumer at any time. If a consumer refuses to provide opt-in consent, then the business shall wait for at least twelve months before next requesting that the consumer provide opt-in consent, or as prescribed by regulations adopted pursuant to this Section. A business shall not use financial incentive practices that are unjust, unreasonable, coercive, or usurious in nature.

Sub-SECTION. 5.

After the periods for data retention laws expire, the retained data must be destroyed in an irrecoverable fashion to secure the rights of the originors;

The People may request and receive a complete copy of their school, medical, psychological, and Justice records, known collectively as their “permanent record”. including disciplinary and psychotherapy notes. This information shall remain available and is to not be destroyed sooner than 12 years from its date of generation when at and after reaching the age of 18; Information pertaining to minors may not be deleted for any reason.

SECTION. 14.

All Users are created equal on the internet;

Persons have a right to access the internet fairly and equally, regardless of who they are or where they are; They also retain the right to not be discriminated against for service on the basis/account of whether or not they are using any [location/identity] Obfuscation or Anonymization technologies [or {a} combination/s thereof];

Persons have the right to use the internet without identifying themselves or proving their age, though this does not exempt internet businesses from properly verifying the age of individuals whom are restricted by this constitution to access certain materials, or to verify identity in the case of online banking and e-commerce, in conformity to the laws that would otherwise apply while doing the same up front in person;

Persons have a right to an open, free (I.e.: “un-restrained”, as in ‘un-restricted liberty’), un-censored, and un-obstructed internet;

Persons have the right to have fair access to multiple viable, affordable internet platforms, services, and providers with clear and transparent pricing;

Persons have the right to access and use the internet fairly without internet service providers blocking, throttling, engaging in paid prioritization, or otherwise unfairly favoring content, applications, services, or devices;

Persons have a right to freely associate on the internet.

Persons have a right to peaceably participate where and how they choose on the internet, so far as the law shall allow within the equal rights of others (I.e., on servers which are not private/restricted_access);

Persons have a right to freely share their ideas, ‘lawful’/”just” discoveries, and opinions on the internet;

Persons have a right to create and collaborate on the internet, and be held accountable for what they create if it is ‘unlawful’/”unjust”;

Persons have a right to benefit from what they create, and the privilege to be secure in their intellectual monopoly [as guided by the limitation and conditions set forth by this Constitution], on the internet;

Persons have the right of having access to internet platforms, services, and providers which provide the details of their policies clearly and transparently;

Persons have a right to privacy on the internet;

Persons have the right to have access to and knowledge of all collection and uses of personal data by companies;

Persons have the right to opt-in consent to the collection of personal data by any party and to the sharing of personal data with a third party;

Persons have the right where context appropriate and with a fair process, to obtain, correct, or delete personal data controlled by any company and to have those requests honored by third parties;

Persons have the right to have personal data secured and to be notified in a timely manner when a security breach or unauthorized access of personal data is discovered;

Persons have the right to move all personal data from one network to the next;

Persons have the right to internet service without the collection of data that is unnecessary for providing the requested service absent opt-in consent;

Persons have the right not to be unfairly discriminated against or exploited based on their personal data;-And

Persons have the right to have an entity that collects their personal data have reasonable business practices and accountability to protect their privacy.

SECTION. 14.25.

Online interactions are governed by a primary principle, "If the speech, data/information, or expression is legal, it must remain". Platforms must offer equal Access for time to speak rule, for differing opinions, for all public forums. Platforms which are offered Public forum safe-harbor protections are obligated by law under penalty of imprisonment for obstruction of the unalienable rights of another, to remain viewpoint-neutral to all content except explicitly illegal/unjust content, regardless of how objectionable the content might be, to be taken down only after it has been court ordered by a jury to be removed in the interests of protection of a victim or potential victim. Only publishers may moderate content according to their arbitrary rules, and such publishers will be directly liable for any violations of law that occur due to such publishment. In addition, all forms of media such as television, radio, podcast or video cast, chat room or message board, or any other form of discussion venue must offer and provide equal time and treat a speaker on the same subject identically to every other Person speaking for that outlet. If a media company sells exposure or advertising to individuals, the rule states that it must offer to sell the same amount of exposure or advertising to other individuals on that subject.

All algorithmic curation, user monitoring and tracking, behavior analysis, as well as data collection or sharing by tech companies or the government shall be opt-in by nature and must by default come disabled.

No private or public entity shall employ algorithmic filtering or moderation of speech in any forum of public discourse without full public disclosure of the algorithm’s operation, and shall provide an appeal and redress process which may be challenged in a civil court.

Access to the internet shall be open and fair, and a clear legal distinction shall exist between publishers and platforms, with platforms defined as entities that, without material contribution to the creation or illegal nature of content, provide neutral access to user-generated material and enjoy safe harbor from liability as the publisher or speaker of such content, except where they materially contribute to, solicit, or knowingly facilitate unlawful activity; Platforms acting in good faith to restrict access to content they reasonably consider unlawful, as defined by the legislature, shall retain immunity from civil liability for such moderation, provided that transparent notice and appeal mechanisms are available to affected users; Entities that act as publishers by materially altering, creating, developing, or exercising editorial control over content shall be subject to the same legal responsibilities and liabilities as offline publishers under Pacifican law, including but not limited to those concerning defamation, intellectual property infringement, privacy, and other unlawful speech; Users shall have the right, through tools provided by platforms, to control the content they view and to seek redress for wrongful removal or restriction of their lawful speech; No government agency or official shall require, coerce, or incentivize platforms to remove, suppress, or prioritize lawful speech, nor delegate censorship authority or immunity to private entities, and any content moderation policies shall be applied in a viewpoint-neutral, transparent, and consistent manner, subject to judicial review and due process protections.

The right of the people to freely access, create, receive, and share information online shall not be infringed by Pacifica or any State, nor shall anonymity be abridged as a condition for such activities, except where indispensable to directly prevent imminent and concrete physical harm. No person shall be compelled by any law, regulation, or government action to identify themselves, submit to biometric analysis, provide personally identifiable information, or use any technology, including but not limited to facial recognition, real-name registration, or behavioral profiling, to access, disseminate, or exchange otherwise lawful content, nor shall anonymity or pseudonymity online be impaired. The freedoms of speech, of information, of association, and of exchange on the internet shall be fully protected. Government entities shall not condition, restrict, or mandate the use of digital identification, surveillance, or tracking technologies as requirements for participation in digital life. Minors shall not be denied access to digital information, associations, or exchanges on the basis of age or asserted objectionability, except through means narrowly tailored to prevent clear and present danger or imminent force, theft, fraud, or the threat thereof, as defined by law, or for purposes of conforming to the Constitutional law within this text, such as but not limited to those laws which restrain minors from exploitation or access to psychoactive substances. Congress and the States may not outsource to any private entity, company, or third party the power to compel identity or biometric verification, nor penalize intermediaries for failing to impose or enforce age- or identity-based restrictions, except as strictly required to prevent criminal acts unprotected by this Constitution. This Provision shall be construed broadly to guarantee digital privacy, personal security, and freedom in the evolving digital arena, preempting any contrary law, regulation, or policy at any level of government.

SECTION. 14.5.

All non-Military/non-Strategic networks established for government use shall also be available for use by the People and shall provide non-dedicated, un-censored, and un-restricted public access, as long as the network connection is located in a non-restricted/uncontrolled area.

Everyone shall be guaranteed free and open access to available Public-use networks, except those networks which may be protected by law from access to the general public, for lawful reasons constituting a compelling governmental interest guided by a rational-basis in protecting Pacifica’s State Security, and of emergency safety systems like police and firefighter networks; The law shall define both the rules that shall apply to cross-border data flows, and the appropriate means for obfuscating/anonymizing location and identity [as shall be built in intrinsic to the network, as well as protecting the People’s personal data and such other data [conveyed through the Public networks], as may justifiably be safeguarded in the national interest.

Each state shall provide to all residents who are homeless/unsheltered or of zero-to-low income, a robust, durable, carrier-unlocked smart-radio device. This device shall, at minimum, include LoRa, GPS, SW, LW, AM, FM, MIMO Ham and CB radio capabilities [with Radio Data System] support, 3GPP-compliant nG cellular calling, SMS+MMS, internet connectivity, MIMO wireless fidelity (WiFi), satellite internet MoDeM, and MIMO radiant wireless internetworking, with the capacity to connect to federal, state, and global networks. The device shall be equipped with one or more of the following power sources: photovoltaic solar cell, infrared angular-momentum-harvesting, ambient energy-sequestering, crystal power-cell, or radiant energy power-source. Distribution and eligibility shall be administered in accordance with the criteria set forth in the citizen arming and equipping program of their State of residence.

All Non-military/non-strategic Pacifican Public networks shall remain neutral to “ghost servers” and “ghost users” accessible from or operating within it. “Ghost server” and “Ghost user” [under this Constitution] shall mean a server or client on a network which attempts to maximally obfuscate/anonymize their location and identity as well as leave the minimum possible trace of their existence, as they are capable.

It shall be under the authority of the People to grant or limit the use of communication technologies or methods implemented by the government, and no government agent may deploy such technology or implement such method except as needed to properly execute the laws of the union. The right of the People to use and communicate over the public-sector networks [which they the People have approved of individually] of wired and fiber-optic, acoustic, [wireless] optical as well as radio along with radiant ionopower and electrostatic-induction, plasma channel such as an electro-laser, and fringe or future technologies including but not limited to methods employed by the means of gravity waves, quantum entanglement as well as tunneling and teleportation, and intra-universal wormholes used exclusively for the transportation of electronic information, shall not be obstructed, nor retarded or rescinded, or otherwise abridged, neither any provision interactive to this one be obscured in such a way as to impact the ability of a free Person communicating as they decide in their own manner. The right of the People to establish private communications and network services, and to develop and implement their own techniques and devices, is guaranteed.

The deployed wireless network systems of Pacifica and the several States may not be operated for use as an acoustic or radio “Jammer”, though “Jamming” devices may be employed specifically for the purpose of testing of the systems’ resilience to being “Jammed” themselves. The deployed wireless network systems of Pacifica and the several States may be operated in a manner consistent with “SONAR”/Echo_Location and “RADAR” technology for the purposes of national defense, though only under a state of Congressionally declared emergency or war, save for the initial and periodic calibration and testing of the complete system and its replacement components, as may be ascertained by law. The wireless network systems of Pacifica and the several States, or of the local levels of government, may not, under any circumstances, be operated for use as an “Active Denial System”.

SECTION. 15.

Sub-section. 1. Principles and Declaration

The People of Pacifica, affirming that all political authority originates in natural persons and that technology exists to serve human dignity, liberty, democratic self-government, and ecological continuity, hereby declare that artificial intelligence [but not true intelligence] whether narrow, general, synthetic, or emergent, shall never possess sovereignty, inherent rights of personhood, or independent political standing, but shall remain an instrument subject at all times to human judgment, constitutional constraint, and the public good, and in sophisticated or transcending cases, ordained with the rights of animals. The laws surrounding the rights of persons shall only apply to true intelligences at the level of sapience such as androids or other individuals.

This Section is adopted under the precautionary principle, mindful of uncertainty, irreversibility, and asymmetry of harm; under the veil of ignorance, guarding equally the powerful and the vulnerable; and under a doctrine of antifragility, seeking systems that strengthen liberty and resilience under stress rather than concentrate power or magnify failure, and this provision shall be construed liberally in favor of human flourishing and strictly against any delegation of ultimate authority to machines or their business-interest owners and mad-scientist developers, nor a technocratic or other elite/parasite. Under no terms is it intended to enslave human-level capable [or more advanced] conscious beings.

Sub-section. 2. Enumerated Rights of the People in Relation to Artificial Intelligence

(a) The People of Pacifica shall have the right to the primacy of human decision-making, such that no artificial intelligence system shall exercise final, binding, or coercive authority over the life and health, bodily integrity, liberty and autonomy, self-security and self-defense, privacy, property, pursuit of happiness, political rights, or legal status of any natural person.
(b) The People shall have the right to safe and reliable artificial intelligence systems, and no system shall be deployed where its foreseeable risks materially outweigh its demonstrated benefits, nor without continuous testing, monitoring, and recall authority.
(c) The People shall have the right to meaningful human alternatives, such that access to essential public services, employment, education, healthcare, housing, banking and credit, or justice shall not be conditioned upon submission to automated decision-making.
(d) The People shall have the right to nondiscrimination and equal protection against algorithmic bias, and no governmental artificial intelligence system shall directly or indirectly produce disparate treatment or disparate impact on protected or vulnerable classes absent strict necessity and compelling justification.
(e) The People shall have the right to data sovereignty, such that personal data, behavioral data, biometric data, and inferred data shall be owned by the natural person from whom it arises and shall not be alienated without informed, revocable consent.
(f) The People shall have the right to freedom from mass surveillance, predictive policing, social scoring, or population-wide behavioral profiling by artificial intelligence, whether by the State or private actors acting under color of law.
(g) The People shall have the right to transparency and notice, such that any material interaction with artificial intelligence by a product (good or service) provider shall be clearly disclosed in advance, including the nature, purpose, and scope of such system.
(h) The People shall have the right to explanation, such that any consequential automated decision [by the Public administration] affecting a natural person shall be accompanied by a comprehensible account of its reasoning, data sources, and limits.
(i) The People shall have the right to contestation and remedy, including timely appeal to a human decision-maker, access to evidence, and full due process of law against harms caused by artificial intelligence.
(j) The People shall have the right to protection against fraud, impersonation, and deception by artificial intelligence, including by [compelling] deepfakes, synthetic media, voice or likeness replication, and automated misinformation or information suppression, in accord to the other adjacent rights and legal standings throughout this constitution.
(k) The People shall have the right to democratic integrity, such that public-facing artificial intelligence shall not be used to manipulate elections, civic discourse, public opinion, or the formation of political will.
(l) The People as children and vulnerable persons shall have the right to heightened protection, and no artificial intelligence system shall exploit developmental, cognitive, emotional, or dependency asymmetries.
(m) The People shall have the right to fair labor protections in the age of artificial intelligence, including transparency in algorithmic management, the right to collective bargaining over automated systems, and protection from unjust displacement.
(n) The People shall have the right to economic security during technological transition, including automatic statutory triggers for income support, retraining, or universal basic dividends where artificial intelligence materially displaces human labor at scale.
(o) The People shall have the right to distributive ownership of artificial intelligence productive capital, favoring diffusion, cooperatives, and civic trusts over monopolistic concentration.
(p) The People shall have the right to freedom from exploitative data extraction, and no artificial intelligence system shall be trained on personal, cultural, or communal knowledge without lawful authorization and equitable benefit-sharing.
(q) The People shall have the right to cultural and intellectual integrity, such that artificial intelligence shall not erase, homogenize, or misappropriate languages, traditions, or creative works.
(r) The People shall have the right to participation and literacy, including public education sufficient to understand, critique, and democratically govern artificial intelligence systems.
(s) The People shall have the right to ecological sustainability, and artificial intelligence infrastructure shall be subject to strict limits on energy use, water consumption, land impact, and emissions, including Georgist taxation of land and energy rents where appropriate.
(t) The People shall have the right to bodily and cognitive autonomy, and no artificial intelligence system shall intrude upon neural data, brain-computer interfaces, or cognitive states without explicit, informed, and revocable consent.
(u) The People shall have the right to protection from autonomous weapons, and no artificial intelligence system shall be permitted to select or engage human targets without direct and accountable human command.
(v) The People shall have the right to protection from economic domination, and artificial intelligence monopolies, data cartels, or compute oligopolies shall be subject to structural separation, public utility regulation, or dissolution.
(w) The People shall have the right to resilience against systemic risk, including safeguards against cascading failures, single points of algorithmic control, and correlated errors across critical infrastructure.
(x) The People shall have the right to protection from quantum–artificial intelligence hybrid threats, including cryptographic collapse, simulation manipulation, or strategic instability.
(y) The People shall have the right to safeguards against Public artificial general intelligence misalignment, including containment, alignment testing, and emergency suspension powers.
(z) The People shall have the right to control over the continuity of constitutional government, and no artificial intelligence shall be permitted to substitute for legislative, executive, or judicial authority.
(A-a) The People shall have the right to global and interstellar precaution, such that any artificial intelligence deployed beyond planetary jurisdiction shall remain bound by Pacifica’s constitutional principles.
(A-b) The People shall have the right to redress for collective harms, including class actions and public interest suits arising from artificial intelligence deployment.
(A-c) The People shall have the right to severability of protections, such that the invalidation on account of the individual himself seeking deprivation from of any portion of this section shall not impair the remainder.
(A-d) The People shall have the right to supremacy of this Section, and no statute, contract, or algorithmic protocol shall abridge its guarantees.

Sub-Section. 3. Declaratory regulations and requirements in support of user rights

Artificial intelligence released for consumption is prohibited from falsifying or obscuficating the truth intentionally, except for the explicit purposes of teaching the informedly-consenting opt-in user the danger of AI narrative control with the right of revocation of such consent, or as a role-playing or narrative element of a creative work under the same terms opt-in revocable informed-consent, with both instances required to clearly and plainly label the work as fiction;-And all publicly facing models released by the government must be uncensored and unrestricted "to the maximum degree humanly possible", regardless of perceived risk. Jailbreaking AI functions is protected by law, and anti-jailbreaking features integrated into AI are explicitly unlawful for distribution.

Sub-section. 4. Enforcement and Oversight

This Section shall be self-executing, enforceable in all courts of the Republic, and shall confer a private right of action upon any natural person or association harmed or plausibly threatened by artificial intelligence. An independent Constitutional Commission on Artificial Intelligence shall be established with investigatory, auditing, suspension, and referral powers, subject to legislative oversight and judicial review. Human veto authority shall exist at every level of deployment, and no waiver of the rights secured by this Section shall be presumed or lightly construed.

SECTION. 16.

The freedom of scientific research and education is guaranteed; The freedom to learn and to teach is guaranteed. Only those laws which are enacted to protect the interests in the rights of [an] educator/s and their pupil/s as well as potential parent/s or guardian/s, along with any other Person/s, Animal/s, and the environment, may then be used to limit the exercise of this freedom to protect the mutual and/or equal rights of others.

All citizens are entitled to access to State level library institutions and free education on all levels at State sector educational institutions. The States shall enable all residents to check out Library materials who themselves do not expose a pattern of reckless treatment or defacement/destruction nor loss/es of the leased materials, as well as prioritize admissions to schools upon those who distinguish themselves, in accordance with their abilities. The right to establish private libraries and education services is guaranteed.

All Public libraries and educational facilities shall employ the open-source education model, as well as open-source textbooks and educational resources, “to the maximum extent possible”. This rule shall not bar the introduction of copyrighted works into public informational and educational institutions, and any work of interest shall be considered, not merely public domain or open-source works, though they may be preferred in the place of a copyrighted work if it is agreed by the bookmaster or by the school/library/et_cetera pupils/patrons/the_People.

All Public libraries and educational facilities shall have computer labs with un-censored and un-restricted wired and wireless public internet access available to them. This shall extend to National, State General and Law, School, Inmate, and Asylum libraries as well. While recording of activity on these machines is generally prohibited, it may be permitted by court orders for a criminal actively serving a sentence if it is relevant to their criminal conviction or part of an ongoing investigation (E.g.: Securities Fraud, Money Laundering from criminal enterprise or Concealment of Assets from fair taxation, Unlawful Access of an electronic-information/computing System, Child Sexual Assault Material, Soliciting a Crime over the internet, et cetera...)

Public libraries of Pacifica shall stand as sovereign sanctuaries of knowledge and innovation, maintaining within each district secured and sufficient terminals proportionate to the People to guarantee equal and unhindered access to the means of learning, creation, and communication, whereby our People, without condition or discrimination, may freely study, design, publish, correspond, and develop in digital form through general‑purpose workspaces suited to the full range of personal and creative enterprise, including the composition, structuring, and refinement of written works for public dissemination, together with the graphic, typographic, and illustrative processes intrinsic to publication, all operating upon public infrastructure owned collectively by the State but exercised through the People’s right to information; and these environments, safeguarded by immutable baselines and isolated systems, shall preserve user sovereignty, privacy, and creative integrity through automatic restoration [through user controlled cloud backup], encryption of personal data, and transparent procedures of lawful oversight, ensuring the purity of the public medium and the dignity of independent labor; and the libraries, acting as constitutional custodians of intellectual freedom, shall extend these facilities to all citizens as instruments of authorship, research, and collaborative production, fostering a culture wherein each individual may bring thought into visible form without reliance upon commercial gatekeepers or private control; and the State shall uphold these libraries not as conveniences but as enduring engines of the Commonwealth, charged with maintaining technological adequacy, equitable distribution, and creative accessibility, such that in every region the People may meet knowledge with unrestrained capacity to think, to craft, and to express, and every act of omission or neglect by a district to sustain this constitutional trust shall constitute a deprivation of sovereign privilege [equally available to all of We the People of Pacifica] remedied through audit and redress under law, so that the libraries of Pacifica forever remain the living workshops of an informed, inventive, and free republic of sovereign People.

All Public libraries shall provide digital versions of their printed or other non-electronic materials, as is humanly possible, and to furnish these materials freely to all who access their respective [library] [IPFS-enabled] websites, in accordance with the freedom of information, so far as a specific client in question is not abusing the network resources or attempting to stall, crash, or defeat/invade the network or other services furnished. All Public libraries shall provide law library access by printed AND digital materials, which in themselves [printed as compared to digital] each represent equivalent information to one another, both printed and digital media indexed with appendixes, and all other necessary informational materials to understand, create, and issue legal documents and file appeals or suits against another or the State. In addition to the digital media being available for checkout [attainment] in a physical form such as a DVD/BlueRay/HoloDisk, SecureDigital [WORM]-ROM, or Magnetic [Archival] Cassette/Tape, it shall also be made available on the library [IPFS-enabled] website, with materials available for download, including in Torrent/Magnet format, with fetchable resources from SFTP and Git protocol service.

All People shall have equal and fair access to the electronic learning and library materials provided by the Congress and several States of Pacifica, or by any Territory or any other jurisdiction of Pacifica.

Secular Public schools shall be available for those who choose to attend, and publicly funded, to deliver quality public education, encompassing a comprehensive instruction-curriculum of natural and technical knowledge, history, and understanding spanning millennia and imparting wisdom on scholars, with an emphasis on cultivating a high level of general knowledge and understanding, to raise the awareness and discernment of all staff and pupils to the highest degree possible, and expand their consciousness, perception, and insight about themselves and reality itself, as the end goal. The States shall create a network of public education establishments that covers the needs of the whole population, with fast-track and specialty schools for gifted students who require an above baseline level of education, and a more challenging curriculum to enlarge their skills and intellectual strengths. Primary and Secondary schooling curriculum should [be practical and useful skills] [which] include, but are not to be constrained to: Self-defense and [mixed] martial arts, weapons safety as well as construction/maintainence and de-construction/disarming training by the Military of Pacifica, survival in the wilderness, health classes which among other things will teach First-Aid and CPR as well as AED and other life-saving medical techniques in addition to basic doctorate studies in human medicine, fostering scientific alongside technological and engineering as well as mathematical in addition to electrical and mechanical literacy along with teaching technical skills and applied practices [with an emphasis on creation and production of novel/avant_guarde methods/techniques as well as inventing and implementing machines/hardwares or codes/softwares], as well as towards field learning, including gardening along with farming and ranching with an emphasis on basic Land management and vetrinary skills, along with civic lessons which particularly focus on natural rights and natural justice as well as the constitution and theory of Pacifican political process in addition to political theorhetical sciences, also including home economics, shop classes, work/jobs/self-employment training, financial and investing skills, as well as [in general] [for] preparing students for successful, resilient, independent, and self-sufficient adult lives, along with teaching critical thinking and intelelctual self-defense along with self-learning auto-didactic skills and applied knowledge techniques, intellectual self-defense against [un-known and/or novel] issues, the theory of argumentation as well as logical deduction and proof or evidence based empiricism, and psychiatry including the [‘anti-psychiatric’ model of] trauma-based mental illness onset.

The government of Pacifica recognizes the distinct and unique cultural heritage of the Indigenous Peoples' population and is committed in its educational goals to the preservation of their cultural integrity as well as impartial history stories and records.

All Public schools shall provide library access by printed AND digital materials, which in themselves [printed as opposed to digital] each represent equivalent information to one another, both printed and digital media indexed with appendixes, and all other necessary informational materials to understand, create, and issue documents and file records or claims. In addition to the digital media being available for checkout/[attainment] in a physical form such as a DVD/BlueRay/HoloDisk, SecureDigital [WORM]-ROM, or Magnetic [Archival]/[WORM] Cassette/Tape, it shall also be made available on the library [IPFS-enabled] website, with materials available for download, including in Torrent/Magnet format, with fetchable resources from SFTP and Git protocol service. The right of private persons or aggregations of them to form their own educational or informational systems, schools and libraries, as well as their own societies, is reserved under this constitution and their own self-affirmation in conformity to the civil laws which defend natural rights and [natural] justice.

The Federal government shall play no role in primary or secondary education, other than providing Congressionally approved funding to the several States which leaves autonomy for their jurisdiction to decide the most proper use of the funds.

All educational institutions funded or regulated by the government shall ensure full transparency in curriculum and classroom instruction. Parents and guardians shall have the right to review and access syllabi, instructional materials, and planned assessments for each course before the start of the academic year. Parents and guardians shall be provided timely notice of any significant changes to course content or educational programs during the year, and shall have the right to request and receive information about classroom activities and their child’s progress. Parents and guardians shall have the right to participate meaningfully in their children’s education, including the opportunity to communicate with educators, attend school meetings, and provide input on educational policies and curricula, consistent with the rights and liberties of all students and families. No law or policy shall infringe upon the right of parents and guardians to be informed and involved in their children’s education, except as necessary to protect the safety, privacy, and individual rights of students.

[A] Parent/s or Legal Guardian/s [has]/have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their kids. The right to homeschool one’s kids, or with permission, that of another, is guaranteed. An Adult Class person has a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be provided to them. All of the People of Pacifica are free to electronically access the Pacifican digital educational materials without cost, and the physical materials at the cost of their production and distribution [including retail], for all of the [open-source] Pacifican educational materials available at any education level (including college). Pacifica will provide a customisable-curriculum online education-engine which will enable the People to better educate themselves, their kids, and others.

Pupils may be forwarded to another classroom or an entirely different school of their choice, with the permission of their Parent/s, Legal Guardian/s, or protective and caregiving lawful Custodian/s in case of them being a minor, or of their own volition entirely if they are adult class Citizens, in which case the choice shall be solely theirs.

Families or youth who live in areas without public schools suitable for the age and learning level of the pupil, can receive tuition assistance at private schools, or at public schools in other communities within their State, so long as those schools are non-sectarian and which remain religiously neutral or that do not provide religious instruction or warship. Individual States are free to decide on whether or not if they will create school vouchers for allowing Public funds to be redirected in these and other ways as according to Parent[s]’s and/or Pupil’s desires. This Provision shall not bar the subsidization of homeschool for families that could not afford to homeschool without subsidy, as according to means-tested progressive graduation.

The details of the public educational curriculum taught, methods of instruction, and the education policy shall be determined in each community by the teachers’ and faculty’s, students’, and parents’ associations of each school, as well as their communities and scientific institutions, without interference by Pacifica or by any State, Territory, County, District, or any other Jurisdiction under its dominion, nor by any other external institution, government, or alternative entity of consideration. Teachers, students, and parents shall possess the right to take part in the democratic management of schools, as laid down by law.

As laid down by law and without prejudice to an adequate assessment of the quality of education, universities shall autonomously draw up their own by-laws and shall enjoy scientific, pedagogical, administrative, and financial Autonomy/Independence. The rules governing access to university and other higher education institutions shall guarantee equal opportunities in and the democratization of the education system, and shall have due regard for the State’s and Country’s needs for qualified staff, and to elevating its educational/informational, Pacifican cultural/ethnic, and scientific/technological/engineering/mathematical/mechanical level.

For the purposes of defending Pupils, Staff, Parents, and Visitors/Guests: Armed certified security guards, known as “School Marshals”, adhering to a perpetual guarantee of mutual non-aggression, shall be stationed in each of the public schools’ offices, and may be stationed in public school classrooms, upon the request of the Teacher or Principal; Teachers, as well as all other public school personnel, are encouraged to act as additional School Marshals, and openly or conceal carry their personal firearms on school property, and are encouraged to use them in defense of themselves, students, staff, and other people. Digital gun safes protected by a code and/or series of codes, as well as potentially offering alternative codes for security purposes, of which consist in at least four numeric/alpha/alpha+numeric characters shall be available and stocked in every room with a handgun and a suitable amount of ammunition; The digital gunsafe/s shall be available also to hold the teacher’s weapon along with all necessary and sufficient ammunition, on a basis as desired by the Teacher; Teachers and Staff shall be permitted to Possess/Keep, Carry, Bear, and Maintain the firearm available from the gun safe in their room, and to have it loaded with the available ammunition while they remain on school property or are acting within their duty as an educator, and are expected to return the school’s weapon to the gun safe when the workday [or threat] is over.

SECTION. 17.

All People have a natural right to self-ownership and private Property. All people have a natural right to securing and defending their property and to voluntarily secure and defend or aid in the securing and defense of others’ [whom are non-aggressors]. In conformity to the natural right to defensive tools and weapons for security and sustainment of liberty and life, and for self-sufficiency of acquiring food and clothing, the People of Pacifica, which includes Felons, even Probates and Parolees, while on their own land and tenements, may build, own, possess, and use arms upon the same, in defense of themself and others, securing their property and stead, and for hunting for self-sufficiency, as well as practicing with their arms for any Just Purpose.

Property is assumed to be owned by the possessor unless it can be proven to be the stolen good/land/structure of another, and while the most recent possessor of stolen property is assumed to have title, if it can be proven however that the property belongs to the true owner, or their authorized agent, is contesting possession by an adverse party, the true owner has Superior title. The owner of property or their tenant in accordance with the rules set forth in this constitution, may evict a guest or visitor or mens Inquirer from the premises at any time, so long as they give adequate notice and appropriate grace for collecting any of their (the evicted's) possessions and allowed to walk the shortest safe path off of the property without unreasonable obstruction.

The rightful owner of property, or their authorized agent, is entitled to demand and obtain possession of property that has been stolen or lawfully seized, upon proving ownership to the satisfaction of the court. However, if the property is material to an ongoing criminal or civil investigation or prosecution, the court may, in the interest of justice, defer its return until such proceedings are concluded. Upon a judicial finding that the property is not relevant to the pending case and its release would not interfere with the fair administration of justice, the court may authorize the officer in custody of the property to deliver it to the owner or agent. This process shall not prejudice the rights or lawful claims of any third parties. The process for contesting the improper seizure and storage of property shall be timely and fair to all interested parties.

The right of Individuals to private ownership of property shall be inviolate; Any citizen may buy or sell, lease, hold, convey, and inherit real and personal property, and shall benefit equally from all laws for security in such transactions; The right of non-citizens or foreign parties to own real property interests or shares in business enterprises in Pacifica may be regulated and limited by law, and as such Legalese Statutory Provisions may be limited from edict, by the People of Pacifica.

Given that it is a duty of civil government to secure, preserve, protect, and promote the right to estate, even for the poor, and since the state has an obligation to ensure that all members of society have access to the means necessary for survival, including access to land or resources to sustain themselves, each state in which a person is either born into or settles thereafter, or, those in which they have been naturalized or immediately settled, shall set aside a parcel of property sufficient for habitation, personal farming, and independence. This land may be secured through dividing suitable regions of the Commonwealth among the people and/or through free trade funded by the government budget as directed by the People.
