Pacifica's principles [which underlie civil society] shall forbid economic practices that appropriate consumer wealth without fair value creation or reciprocal benefit. Wealth capture is legitimate only when rewarding innovation or genuine provision of new value. Extractive rent-seeking or monopolistic exploitation leveraging regulatory capture or market dominance is subject to corrective measures, as laid forth by this Constitution, and as furthermore prescribed by the Legislature.

Pricing models must distinguish between rental or service-based access and outright ownership. Businesses shall not impose ongoing time-based fees, subscriptions, or charges that extract wealth from consumers based on usage of products they own. Value capturing is permissible where ongoing new value is provided, but continued charges for mere use of owned property constitute exploitative extraction. All costs, fees, surcharges, penalties, or material contract terms related to purchases must be disclosed clearly and prior to contract acceptance. Hidden, junk, or otherwise obscure fees that mislead consumers or bind them financially beyond reasonable expectations are prohibited. Businesses shall not engage in predatory pricing practices intended to eliminate competition and subsequently exploit a captive market.

Contractual terms creating unreasonable customer lock-in, such as excessive cancellation fees or non-transparent bundling, are forbidden, protecting consumer freedom to choose without undue economic coercion.

The right of Individuals and businesses to “un-lock” or re-program electronic devices of which they own, including but not limited to market products, shall be guaranteed; Any Person or business may “un-lock” or re-program their owned electronic devices, or with permission, that of another Person or Business. People who create methods to unlock or re-program their devices may freely and openly share their methodologies/techniques as well as modifications and/or homebrew.

The right of the people to manufacture, sell, buy,  own, modify, and use general-purpose computing devices, operating systems, software, hardware, and tools, without government-mandated embedded controls, attestation mechanisms, liability-shifting safety features, or restrictions based on imputed knowledge of potential misuse, shall not be usurped. Neither the openness nor closed nature of source code, firmware, or designs shall affect this protection, and no law shall regulate such devices/implements for hypothetical harms by compelling alterations  or integrations that presume criminal intent or enable indirect censorship of expression, association, or code execution.

Individuals and Businesses/Companies are prohibited from building in soft-bricking functions in their commercial products that make functional hardware, equipment, devices, programming languages, micro-code, firmware, operating systems, drivers, and software useless to the property purchaser/owner. Devices with planned obsolescence, including designed [timed] failure rate, programmed-in performance inhibiting triggers or timed switches, task destabilization and interruption, or other forms of sabotage or intentional disorder or meditated stoppage, except as a specific desired design feature such as a deadman switch, self-sanitize, or self-destruct, are unlawful to be sold in commerce.

All Commercial Neuronal Apparatus Hardware, Software/Programs/Applications, Firmwares/EEPROM-images, and Operating Systems, as well as Neurally interfacing Scripts, Algorithms, Automatons, and Artificial Intelligence, must be made freely available as open-source to the purchasers of such devices and related products. This provision shall also apply to Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality systems on the commercial market, as they are considered cybertronic extensions of the body/vessel of a Person, and must be reviewable by them to ensure safety, security, and user liberty, as well as enable community review, audit, and explanation, to enable furtherance of the Individual right to informed consent.

Property owners throughout Pacifica hold an unalienable general right to energy independence and freedom of market choice in utilities. This encompasses absolute sovereignty over on-site energy generation, storage, distribution, and consumption, free from licenses, permits, fees, mandates, zoning restriction, or interference, other than minimal, provable safety standards that demonstrably prevent harm to others' equal rights. No public utility, such as those under the Department of Goods and Services or Private provider may compel grid connection, deny zero-export interconnections, impose non-consensual purchases, or enforce monopolies; all contracts must remain strictly voluntary, revocable at will, and self-executingly null and void upon violation of core Pacifican constitutional principles. Pacifica’s governments at every level shall affirmatively secure this right through policies promoting microgrids, competitive markets, and technological pluralism (including solar, wind, and nuclear or quantum, in accordance to Just Naturalism), while prohibiting any usurpation thereof, subject to immediate citizen resistance, civil liability, and judicial nullification, with an emphasis on bio-regional autonomy, open-source innovation, resilient self-sufficient communities, and non-aggression/self-determination principles.

No law/s other than as provided by this Constitution, shall regulate the use of private property; anything found in proximity under one’s land, or growing naturally on it, extending downwards to the center of the planet, and upwards to 166.666 meters above the highest land feature, shall belong to the owner; nor shall any law restrict the use of one’s land or natural resources found thereon, unless such use would pollute the air, ground, or water beyond the boundaries of one’s property, or compromise the structural integrity of property outside one’s own. The limitations on pollution found here do not extend to pollution from natural activities occurring on the property, including but not limited to burning bio-mass or bio-fuel for personal warmth and cooking as well as transportation, animal and bio-decomposer off-gassing from personally producable quantities of the animals or organic materials, and naturally dispersed pollen or seeds from any non-genetically-engineered plants grown, as needed for a self and their companions, if there be any, as well as for any invited guests, on a given private property.

Except as may be prescribed otherwise by this Constitution, emanations beyond property lines which are themselves beyond the natural [“background”] levels considering a given circumstance (such as weather, season, or time of day) for their type (such as noise, light, or gasses), which shall become a nuisance which is proven through irrefragable proof supplemented by irrefutable evidence by the affected party or their proxy that it impacts the free exercise of their rights through the impartation of real damages stemming directly from the emanation, such as damages to persons or property, being as those emanations are infractions against the rights [of others], they are hereafter declared to be unlawful, and shall be punishable as a civil infraction and through remuneration for any and all losses incurred due to the emanation; and furthermore, upon repeat offenses against the same victim or property, the offender shall be subject to court order of which whose violation shall be punishable as a misdemeanor; upon the case in which an emanation beyond the boundaries of an individual’s or group’s property results in damages beyond one-hundred ‘Pacifican dollars’, or which shall result in the damage or loss of animal or human [physical] health or life, the violation shall be punishable as a felony; the sentencing severity of either these cases shall be left to the discretion of the court [as it may be laid down by law].

Further elaborating upon the restriction on government to regulate the use of private property, there shall be no regulation of Individually held Privately owned money, including but not limited to incomes derived from any lawful source, monetary resources, gifts, or any other form of capital, up to the point in which it does not conflict with Lockean precepts of property or preeminence in the priority for employment towards citizens over foreignerd. In the interest of Justice and securing legitimate property rights, whereas a Person has a right to all they can employ upon in their own labour, so that they have no temptation to acquire for themself more than they can make use of, and this leaving no room for controversy about their right to title, nor for lawful encroachment upon such right of others, it must also be said, that it is useless, as well as dishonest, vile, repugnant, disgusting, covetous, gormandish, unethical, exploitive, and improprietary, to carve too much out of common resources, as well as to take or acquire more than one needs for securing and maintaining their life and livelihood and that of their close kin, the law shall ensure that Individuals and Artificial Entities do not accumulate so much property that there is not enough resources for others, or that others are deprived of viable means to sustain themselves; Such caps on wealths shall begin at 12* (twelve times) the national mean income, where there shall be a total and a complete limit of yearly wealth at 108* (one-hundred-and-eight times) at the mode of national income (top cap); and a maximum combined stowed wealth and/or financialized wealth in investment accounts which can be no more than 9* (nine times) the base value of 37.6991* (thirty-seven-point-six-nine-nine-one times) the mean national income (top cap); with a progressive ‘greed penalty’ rate at a twelve divisors for both of them, between twelve-point-five percent (12.5%), up to fifty percent (50%) for the maximum cap limit, and eighty percent (80%) upon all excess wealth thereafter, upon the value exceeding the maximum caps, on all wealth, whether income, investment dividends/annuities, or stowed; All investments into small or family-owned businesses shall receive a 50% reduction in their total stowed wealth tax on the actual investments held as well as dividends or annuities derived therefrom;-And all investment into local community establishments shall be fully exempt from wealth tax, including annuities derived or dividends thereof, with a two year (2 annum) residency requirement for the investor in the jurisdiction which the investment is taking place for this exemption to apply. Any landowner who acquires a plot of land or number of them, whether through inheritance or purchase, must be limited to what their person and co-habitating members can actively employ their labor on to productively use without waste; This means land sufficient for self-sufficient farming or habitation without waste or spoilage, roughly equal to the amount needed for subsistence and support of [a] household/labor; “Reasonable use” means enough land so a person can sustain themselves and pursue a livelihood but no more than necessary to do so well; Simply owning or hoarding land beyond what one can use violates the proviso; Because of this, they shall pay an "excessive land" penalty on parcels exceeding twice the baseline size (appraised on an individualized basis), not to exceed seven-point-two percent (3.6%) per annum for parcels up to eight times the necessary and sufficient amount of land for sustenance and shelter and up to twenty-five percent (12.5%) on all land thereafter, upon the assessed value of the parcel/s, improvements excepted, held in excess of their individual or familial need, and taking one's own profession into account as needed to attain a good way of life above poverty and below the greed-penalty rate for wealth, as ascertained by law; An exception shall be made to the land-hoarding penalty for privately owned wildlife reserves that engage exclusively in baseline subsistence activities and maintenance, such as camping along with hunting for survival and foraging for food along with gathering water or firewood, as well as protecting the land, rather than any form of commercial enterprise; In the event that ownership of such a wildlife preserve is transferred, all profits derived from the transaction shall be subject to taxation at a rate up to one hundred percent (100%), as determined by the legislature of the respective State in which the reserve resides. The money collected from this mechanism shall be placed into a secure non-diverable trust fund, for the purposes of dispersing National Wealth Dividends to Citizens [except those of high income], both as Social Security account deposits for all Pacificans, and direct payments for zero-to-low income individuals who are Citizens of Pacifica, to be partitioned and dispersed as provided by law, by the legislature or People of each State independently. The purpose of this Provision is to ensure that there is not waste and to make sure there is enough left in as good of a condition for others to acquire in a like manner, as well as that there be common means in attaining sufficiency for life and preservation, in order that all can fairly participate with economic opportunities and provide for their own needs; The attainment and use of property must not worsen the situation of others by depriving them of access to sufficient resources for their own subsistence and use, including through exclusion by ratio of wealth and scarce resources or land; No law shall impair lawful attainment and use of property, income, or wealth, except to prevent circumstances in which the accumulation or use of property would materially worsen the condition of the poor and others with respect to their opportunity to sustain themselves, or to preserve the equal rights of all Persons in relation to common resources. This Provision shall rely on self-reporting, with confiscation as a consequence for falsification [or withholding] if found during an audit; self reporting is only necessary if one is at or above/beyond the lowest cap for each type of wealth. The holders of abundance must uphold institutions that secure property for all, including by supporting the government in securing the right to property even for those with little or none, as property exists to support life and freedom, not dominance and decadence. Each State to have the power to enforce this Provision by appropriate legislation.

The Federal Government shall establish and maintain a comprehensive system for the equitable governance of technological and economic transformation, imposing a progressive Automation Impact Charge upon enterprises deriving substantial financial value from automation technologies, including robotics, artificial intelligence, and other forms of machine labor that supplant or diminish the need for human labor, while exempting enterprises owned and operated entirely by their owners and small locally-owned/family-operated businesses and small worker-council guilds as defined by Congress. This charge shall be proportionate to the degree of labor displacement and value added by automation, and shall not exceed fourty percent (40%) of the net gains generated thereby, with such revenue deposited into a "Worker Benefit and Transition Fund" held in trust for the people and rendered non‑divertible for any private or governmental purpose outside those herein specified; Revenues from this fund shall be used exclusively to finance unemployment insurance, wage replacement, retraining and education programs, worker retirement public benefits (of the actual workers displaced); this shall serve as a social mechanism that upholds the right of every worker to economic security and personal dignity in the face of rapid technological change. Simultaneously, every Citizen [except those of high income] shall receive a Universal Basic Dividend (UBD) as a perpetual property right representing their equal share in the collective technological, ecological, and productive inheritance of the nation, derived from natural resource royalties and automation levies not exceeding six‑and‑two‑thirds percent (~6.666%) of total profits for each. There shall also for the purposes of the dividend be a business tax which shall not exceed thirty‑three‑and‑one‑third percent (~33.333%) of total profits, and the combined total burden of all automation and business related charges and profit‑based taxes levied under this Provision for the purposes of the dividend shall not exceed fourty percent (40%) of all value added and profits derived therefrom, so as to balance public equity with economic vitality. Business tax brackets, automation thresholds, and compliance standards shall be established by law, adjusted to economic conditions and inflation/deflation, subject to anti‑avoidance and transparency requirements to prevent concentration of wealth or evasion of civic/social duty/responsibility. The Universal Basic Dividend shall be unconditional in receipt, protected from seizure, garnishment, or conversion into a mechanism of dependency or control, and freely distributed in a manner ensuring equity, privacy, and efficiency while preserving material independence as the foundation of intellectual and spiritual liberty and the pursuit of Happiness. The purpose of this unified structure is to equitably distribute the gains from automation and collective enterprise while preserving individual prosperity and free market dynamism, thus ensuring that technological progress and economic growth serves humanity without subjugating it. Small/local/community enterprises shall remain exempt, and medium size or non-local or non-community business only lightly burdened (except for interstate or international businesses run by an individual and up to seven additional non-family employees or single family including the owner [extended] to immediate family, which count as small business for the purposes of this Provision), with big/large business/enterprise without local/community nature/virtue assessed at a higher rate under progressive brackets, to encourage entrepreneurship, innovation, and individual initiative; Businesses and guilds that are both family and/or employee owned in addition to operated by either or both may receive a reduction in their business tax up to thirty-five percent (35%) of such burden, with cooperatives (CO-OPs) provided to an additional fifteen percent (15%) off on top of the prior relief, as a flat discount (added together, up to fifty percent {50%} less taxation than businesses without such virtues) across business tax brackets. The Federal Government shall further revise fiscal and industrial incentives to eliminate any subsidies or advantages that unduly favor automation over employment or that contribute to wealth concentration incompatible with a free, open, and participatory market and civil society at large. Through this universal dividend, the economic rights of all Citizens shall be secured as an extension of their natural liberty, recognizing ownership should be widespread, not concentrated, harmonizing technological advancement and economic growth with human welfare and a moral economy for a freer society.

The Nation of Pacifica affirms that the economic benefits of its civil society shall primarily accrue to its citizens, and declares a compelling national interest in preserving domestic employment opportunities and preventing the displacement of Pacifican workers by foreign labor. To advance this interest, the several States may impose a tax upon income earned by foreign persons whose labor directly or indirectly displaces, substitutes for, or precludes the employment of a citizen of Pacifica. Such taxation may include a tax not exceeding twenty-five percent (25%) on income earned by foreign persons physically present and performing labor within the jurisdiction of Pacifica, and a tax not exceeding thirty-five percent (35%) on income earned by foreign persons performing labor outside the jurisdiction of Pacifica where such labor benefits a business, entity, or economic activity operating outside Pacifica. This provision shall apply to any labor or service performed for the benefit of individuals, businesses or corporations, and entities subject to the jurisdiction of Pacifica, including its several States and territories, where such labor is not performed by a Citizen of Pacifica. Each State shall have the authority to administer, collect, and enforce such taxes within its jurisdiction, consistent with this Constitution and the will of its people, while Congress shall retain authority to enact uniform standards defining displacement, regulating enforcement mechanisms, preventing evasion, and ensuring that this provision is applied in a manner consistent with due process and equal protection under the law; The purpose of such taxes is to restitute for displacement of Citizens from the workforce or from loss of housing and economic opportunity for poor Citizens. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to prohibit lawful immigration, punish permanent naturalization and citizenship while being foreign-born, or to deny fundamental legal protections to foreign persons; however, economic preference for Citizens shall remain a paramount principle of national policy. The guiding principle of this Provision is that those who sustain and belong to the civil society of Pacifica shall be its primary beneficiaries, and that no external labor shall unjustly advantage non-members at the expense of Citizens. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to impose a tax on a person who was at any point in time a natural born Citizen of Pacifica, or has through the legal processes set forth by Congress become naturalized to the nation of Pacifica as a citizen, even if they have dissolved their association to it.

Every sovereign Person’s unalienable right to self-ownership, through their own labor, free exchange, or private enterprise, extends absolutely to appropriating from the common Earth, resources, and Pacifica’s natural heritage such productive property as they individually determine secures their dignity, autonomy, self-security, self-defense, privacy, property, and freedom from wage servitude or dependency, provided they leave enough and as good for every other sovereign person and confine personal holdings to their chosen family- or craft-scale needs under subsidiarity. Medium and large-scale businesses remain fully permissible under this Constitution and legislation enacted in conformity therewith, through voluntary association, partnership, or progressively tiered redistributive mechanisms that preserve individual dominion while preventing enclosure of commons or oligarchic excess; any property redistributed through such mechanisms shall be eternally owned outright by the individual sovereign person who lawfully possesses after acquisition from redistribution of it as their private domain, never reverting to state ownership, public lease, or temporary access devoid of true title, explicitly rejecting not only communist abolition of private property and socialist nationalization of business into state control, but also disparity in common meaningful private acquisition and ownership or exchange of Property. Any excess beyond twelve-times-pi-equals-approx-thirty-seven-point-six-nine-nine times ({3*4*pi=~37.699}*) the amount constituting individual [real] property possession baseline, (wildlife preserves and [financially] non-profit religious grounds exempted) shall be deemed social spoilage within congruence to the Lockean Proviso of property rights (See: 2nd Treatise of [civil] Government), and may revert via personal initiatives, voluntary local guilds, or referenda directly into the public commons for future private acquisition and ownership by recipient sovereign persons, thereby anchoring free individual production to distributist equity, non-aggression, and universal law, barring all coercion, taxation, or centralized power not explicitly authorized by this Constitution from impairing any sovereign person’s absolute, perpetual dominion to own, trade, scale ethically, and prosper as master of their own life within independent communities.

Abandoned property shall be decommissioned after three months at a place of rental/lease, more than six months in a public place such as a bike rack or state locker, or in excess of six months in the lost and found (after turnover from the rentor/leasor and/or public place), where it shall then be free for claiming by the owner of the area where the property remains; The priority in property right belongs to the most recent possessor after purchase or transfer without force, theft, fraud, or the threat thereof, as according the the directions to decommission abandoned property.

In elaboration to the restriction on government to regulate private property, there shall be no zoning laws or dedicated use requirements for, nor permits or licensing to construct or maintain, a structure or facility, on privately owned/held land.

For fairness and to promote the equality of access to housing, potential tenants and active tenants shall by law not be required to indicate on their housing forms any legal history or criminal charges, nor have a background check be a legal requirement by their landlord, though landlords are free to discriminate applicants upon their choice/volition to inquire about the same legal/criminal nature at their own expense of time and money to do the same.

No landlord-tenant contract shall require the tenant sacrifice any of their rights, natural or otherwise, at the whim or meditated demand of their landlord, and only in cases of violation of the landlord’s natural rights, such as destruction of their property or sub-letting without consent, shall a tenant then be ordered to pay restitution/remittance, ordered to repair damages, or be required by law to leave the premises due to breach of contract. The tenant shall at all times have a minimum of thirty (30) days to vacate the premises from the date of termination of their rental agreement, and if they have been an occupant of the dwelling for more than one year, they shall have sixty (60) days to vacate the premises, but they shall owe in full the entire amount of rent through that period of time, and proportionally for the amount of any month they stay past the end of the previous month, which is during the grace period of their temporary continued residency.

It is a pre-political right and liberty of the people to create, assemble, construct, as well as establish, maintain, or propagate, along with exercise all the effects, of the following, so long as their performance does not defraud others, cause injury to another, cause damage to another’s property, or otherwise exert aggression/[[un-just_]force/offensive_violence upon another or their property, or the threat thereof, which include but are not limited to: Documents of identification [excluding however official governmental documents of identification], information/records, scrips and/or Private currency, papers, communications, articles, structures as well as shelters/housings, pathways and/or roads, gardens, ponds and/or lakes and/or creeks and/or rivers, fisheries, waveforms, matter, elements, molecules/chemicals also including artificial atoms and artificial molecules, crystals, viruses, bio-organisms [including xeno-biologies], stem cells, archaea, bacteria, eukarya, fungi, plants including but not limited to food crops and lumber, animals, wagons and/or carriages, vehicles/crafts, Arms, scientific experiments, technological devices, machines, networks, electronics, electronic data, computers, algorithms, automatons and autonomic hardware, robotics, and mecha-organisms.

Every citizen shall have the right to operate as their own financial institution, including the issuance of loans, acceptance of credit, and management of personal financial instruments, subject only to voluntary contracts and the non-initiation of force or fraud. Citizens shall be entitled to a unique financial institution minting code, compatible with the prevailing STAR system and a separate Pacifica-specific system, enabling secure and interoperable financial transactions within and beyond the region. No law shall restrict the free association, formation, or operation of such decentralized, citizen-owned financial institutions, provided they adhere to principles of voluntary exchange and transparency. The government shall not interfere in the voluntary financial arrangements or private trust structures of individuals, except in cases involving proven fraud, coercion, or violation of the rights of others. All powers not expressly granted to the government regarding personal financial sovereignty and trust arrangements are reserved to the people.

The right of the People to anonymity in their personal, financial, communicative, and associative dealings shall not be abrogated. No law shall compel disclosure of private transactions or identities absent probable cause supported by oath or affirmation, nor shall the use of anonymous instruments of exchange, including physical currency or cryptographic mediums, be denied.

Every individual has the right to direct the transfer of their estate, property, and effects to heirs or inheritors of their choosing, as expressed in a valid will or testament, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and individual liberty. The testator’s will shall take priority in determining the disposition of their estate. Only those matters not addressed by the will may be decided by a court, and solely under due process of law and as prescribed by the legislature of the jurisdiction securing the right of estate. No law or governmental action shall infringe upon or override the right of individuals to secure, enjoy, and transfer their property, except as necessary to protect the equal rights of others or to prevent fraud or coercion. This provision shall be interpreted in the spirit of the principle that the preservation and transfer of property is a fundamental natural right, and that government exists primarily to protect such rights. There shall be no tax on the transfer of property nor upon inheritances.

Each citizen shall have the right to establish a separate, privately-managed, publicly-protected trust known as the “Death Certificate Insurance Checking Account,” linked to their birth certificate entry, maintained in the records of their state of birth. This account shall be secured by two sources: contributions from the parents or guardians until the age of majority, and thereafter by the citizen themselves as the secured party. The government shall provide a separate, state-backed insurance security upon birth, guaranteeing a sum equivalent to sixteen-thousand (16kilo) silverbacks, accessible only upon the issuance of a valid death certificate. Access to this insurance shall require a unique Account Identification Number (AIN), distinct from any social security or general identification number. Disbursement of funds through death certificate insurance shall be detailed in the final testament of the individual for whom the certificate was issued for, or by arbitration in a Court of competent and proper Jurisdiction in the case that no final testament is given on such topic, and be the property of the receiver/s.

Congress and the several States are reserved the power to create anti-trust laws in order to protect the competitive nature of markets and the rights/wellbeing of consumers.

Local living wage should be managed through states, and the federal living wage be a mean average from each and all State’s highest costs of living combined by addition and divided by the number of States whose values were added, and adding twelve-point-five percent (12.5%) up to twenty-two-point-two-bar percent (~22.2...%) on top of the baseline cost of living for quality of life savings and spending.

SECTION 17.25

The development, deployment, and use of emergent technologies, defined as technologies whose full societal, ethical, and safety implications are not yet comprehensively understood, shall be governed by a framework ensuring freedom of innovation while safeguarding individual rights, public safety, and civil society. No law, regulation, or administrative action may unduly restrict technological innovation or scientific research, but all emergent technologies must undergo transparent and periodic ethical and safety assessments before and during their deployment. Such assessments shall include, at minimum: a) Independent safety evaluations by qualified experts to identify potential risks to health, environment, public security, and civil liberties; b) Open public forums and comment periods to allow affected communities and stakeholders to deliberate on the technology’s uses, consequences, and ethical concerns; c) Ongoing monitoring and review processes to adapt regulation responsively as technology and its impacts evolve; d) Mechanisms to prevent misuse or abuse of technologies that could infringe individual autonomy, privacy, or democratic governance. The legislature of Congress shall establish an independent Technology Ethics Commission, with members appointed for staggered terms, drawn from diverse fields including but not limited to ethics, science, law, civil rights, and community representation. This commission shall oversee the implementation of the framework, ensuring adherence to constitutional liberties and public accountability. The rights to free speech, privacy, property, and liberty shall be preserved in all governance of emergent technologies, and no regulation shall enable censorship or intrusive surveillance beyond what is strictly necessary to prevent imminent, demonstrable harm. This power shall not be construed to hinder technological progress or the lawful commercial exploitation of new technologies but to prevent the creation or enforcement of dystopian regimes or conditions through technological means

All Persons, in their Private capacity, retain the right to use and pay for digital and physical services anonymously.

Congress and the several States shall have the authority to regulate devices sold within Pacifica to reduce e-waste and promote consumer alongside owner rights, such as but not restrained to requiring a universal power connector that is industry standard for common categories of device or mandating for example phone/tablet and laptop/handheld plus smart-glasses batteries be readily removable and replaceable by the user, for all [relevant] devices available on the open market.

SECTION. 17.5.

No person experiencing homelessness or unsheltered shall be criminalized, penalized, or forcibly removed from public spaces solely on the basis of their housing status, presence in encampments, or lack of permanent shelter, or for engaging in essential life activities due to their circumstances.

No law shall criminalize homelessness or being unsheltered, nor create a penalty for sleeping or camping in a public place on public property which does not obstruct a right of way or emergency personnel, but the law may require individuals to move after camping no less than two-weeks. Each "providence" or county shall set aside multiple accessible areas designated for long term homeless camping in excess of two-weeks, with basic amenities like: running water (including potable water for drinking, which may be filtered or purified) either from a gravity-fed tank, a pump attached to a water line or well, or connection to the town/city mains, or combination thereof; electricity, which may be from the mains or generated on site, or a combination thereof; bathrooms suitable to handicap access; storage lockers with handicap access and basic security features like [redundant] closed-circuit surveillance for claim/crime resolution/solving. Also, each county/"providence" shall create emergency programmes to house the homeless and unsheltered, for those times of the year where one could die of exposure to the cold, heat, and air pollution. Permanent housing projects including rent-to-own pathways will be made available to the homeless and unsheltered on a triaged basis, prioritizing first the elderly, then the disabled as well as those with moderate or severe medical or psychiatric illness or disease, in addition to domestic violence victims, following with families with children, and finally the remainder of the general population.

The People retain the right to be in any public place (such as but not limited to: planting strips, sidewalks, parks, public buildings, and transportation) so long as not posing a clear and present security risk or threat to safety safety nor obstructing the free passage of others, as with disorderly conduct, and they are otherwise acting lawfully and are legally present.

The People retain the right to rest, sit, sleep, or shelter oneself in a non-obstructive manner in public spaces, without harassment or discrimination based on housing status.

The People have the right to open access of long-term camping in designated areas, with basic amenities, along with access to transportation and food+water in near proximity, in as disability accommodating of manner as humanly possible, particularly as it protects the homeless and vulnerable.

The People retain the right to be free from searches, detention, or harassment by law enforcement based solely on housing status.

The People retain the right to privacy and protection of personal property, even in public spaces, to the extent that it does not infringe on others’ rights or public order.

The People retain the right to equal access to public services, such as emergency medical care, voting, library, bus service, post office box, employment opportunities, banking, and citizen arming plus equipping benefits, without discrimination due to homelessness or lack of shelter.

The People retain the right to give and receive charity (such as but not limited to: food, shelter, and aid) in public spaces, provided it does not violate other laws or obstruct public use.

The People retain the right to occupy one’s own legally parked vehicle or another’s with permission, as a temporary shelter.

The People retain the right to be free from criminal penalties for life-sustaining activities (such as but not limited to: sleeping, eating, and resting) in public, when no adequate alternatives exist and so long as these activities are non-obstructive and non-threatening.

No person shall be denied the right to rest, sleep, or shelter peacefully in public spaces, including but not limited to parks, planting strips, sidewalks, commons, and other lands held in the public trust, so long as no other person’s rights are infringed thereby. It shall not be a civil or criminal offense to camp, sleep, erect temporary shelters, or maintain one's personal belongings in any public area, provided that such actions do not obstruct essential access ways, interfere with the use of critical infrastructure, or pose an immediate and proven danger to health and safety. The mere status of being unhoused, lacking permanent shelter, or appearing disheveled shall not constitute probable cause for detention, search, removal, citation, or harassment by any agent or authority. No State nor local or collective ordinance shall prohibit survival behavior by the indigent, including but not limited to resting, sleeping, or gathering under non-violent, non-destructive conditions, unless viable, freely accessible, and non-coercive alternatives are concretely provided. All persons retain the right to respectfully, and in accordance to the needs of the environment to occupy and homestead unreserved public domain land for survival purposes in any time of housing insecurity, economic crisis, or social displacement, without fear of removal, penalization, or enforced relocation. Shelter is not a crime. No authority, municipal or otherwise, shall confiscate, destroy, or discard personal property found in public unless it poses a direct threat to others or is abandoned by clear and consensual forfeiture. Indigent persons shall not be dispossessed of their meager possessions under color of law. The dignity, privacy, and liberty of every person shall be respected regardless of housing status. The right to exist peacefully in shared public spaces is inherent and shall not be abridged or otherwise reduced.

We the People of Pacifica find and declare that the preservation of Life and Health, Liberty/Freedom and Autonomy/Independence, Self-Security and Self-Defense, Privacy, Property, and the Pursuit of Happiness requires the recognition and protection of diverse forms of habitation, including mobile and vehicular domiciles, and that no Person shall be deprived of dignity, shelter, safety, or practical access to civilization merely because they lack ownership, leasehold, or occupancy of a conventional fixed dwelling; therefore, in accordance with the principles of Natural Rights, Just Naturalism, individual sovereignty, compassion toward the human condition, and the duty of government to serve the People rather than burden them, every Person lawfully present within Pacifica shall possess the fundamental right to reside, travel, rest, sleep, prepare food, maintain sanitation, receive guests, store possessions, and otherwise conduct the ordinary activities of domestic life within a vehicular domicile. For the purposes of this Constitution, a vehicular domicile shall include any lawful mobile dwelling or habitation unit, whether self-propelled, towable, transportable, floating, flying, or otherwise mobile, including but not limited to vans, camper vans, truck-and-camper combinations, motorhomes, recreational vehicles, travel trailers, fifth-wheel trailers, sleeper trailers, utility trailers converted for habitation, boats, watercraft, aircraft, spacecraft occupied by their operators, bicycle or motorcycle habitation systems, and all substantially similar forms of mobile shelter. The protections of this Provision shall extend equally to any attachment, module, camper, habitation pod, accessibility enclosure, utility enclosure, storage enclosure, trailer, or other residential component attached to, detached from, towing, being towed by, supporting, or supported by a vehicular domicile, and such integrated residential systems shall be treated as a single protected dwelling for all constitutional purposes. No Person shall be prohibited from occupying a vehicular domicile upon public streets, parking areas, rights-of-way, waterways, transportation corridors, rest areas, or other public places where no operational limitation on parking or occupancy has been established through a neutral and reasonable process directed solely toward the safety and convenience of the public and not toward the exclusion, displacement, punishment, or stigmatization of nomadic or unhoused Persons. Any regulation affecting mobile habitation shall be narrowly tailored to serve a compelling public interest, shall employ the least restrictive means available, shall remain content-neutral and class-neutral, and shall be subject to constitutional review, with all doubts resolved in favor of liberty, habitation, and peaceful occupancy. The government shall not enact or enforce blanket prohibitions against sleeping, resting, residing, or living within vehicular domiciles, nor shall it criminalize the mere condition of homelessness, nomadism, poverty, disability, unconventional living arrangements, or the absence of access to conventional housing. Reasonable accommodations shall be provided to Persons with disabilities, including but not limited to those experiencing physical impairment, mobility limitations, chronic illness, mental illness, neurodivergence, sensory disabilities, or age-related limitations, and such accommodations may include extended occupancy periods, proximity to medical services, proximity to transportation and essential resources, accessibility modifications, and protection from arbitrary displacement. The government shall recognize that many Persons rely upon mobile habitation to maintain autonomy, family unity, safety, employment, medical treatment, education, community participation, and freedom of movement, and that such habitation frequently reduces burdens upon conventional housing systems while preserving personal independence and self-sufficiency. No law, regulation, policy, ordinance, administrative action, or welfare program shall discriminate against a Person because they reside within a vehicular domicile, and no vehicular domicile used as a primary residence shall be treated less favorably than a conventional dwelling for purposes of legal recognition, occupancy rights, emergency assistance, self-defense, privacy, public benefits, or equal protection of the laws. A vehicular domicile shall constitute a dwelling and habitation for all purposes relating to defense of self, defense of others, defense of habitation, burglary, trespass, privacy, domestic relations, emergency response, and constitutional protections. Any social welfare, disability support, public assistance, retirement, or income-support program established by Pacifica shall exclude a primary vehicular domicile and its ordinary residential components from asset calculations, resource limitations, or eligibility determinations. The People further recognize that throughout much of the world there exists a recurring tendency for governments and institutions to restrict, discourage, or criminalize nomadic habitation despite its historical, cultural, economic, and practical importance, and therefore the rights secured by this Provision shall be interpreted liberally in favor of mobile habitation, freedom of movement, self-determination, and emancipation from homelessness, ensuring that future generations retain the ability to pursue shelter, security, dignity, independence, and prosperity through lawful nomadic living with minimal resources and maximum freedom consistent with the equal rights of all Persons.

The People retain the right to due process and reasonable notice before removal or clearing of actually existing encampments [, not anticipatory notices where there are no present camps], with respect for personal property and dignity.

The People have the right to be free from the passage of legislation or ordinances that prohibit sitting/laying, sleeping, panhandling, sharing food, enjoyment of entertainment, non-violent/non-aggressive/non-criminal/[just] communication, or religious practice in public spaces. No legislation or code shall outlaw loitering, vagrancy, sitting or lying on the planting strip or sidewalk [without actually obstructing free passage by others], begging, urinating [modestly and considerately], bathing, changing clothes, grooming, and eating in public, or squatting [respectfully], as well as other behaviors that disproportionately affect homeless and unsheltered people. The government of the several States shall address the root causes of homelessness and housing insecurity, in addition to provide services to assist them, not treat them as second-class citizens and criminalize their very existence [however contrived]. Allegedly neutral prohibitions on essential human activities including respect for biological reality as well as needs are unconstitutional, no matter time, place, or manner, when there is no suitable alternative available, nor shall the availability of an option preclude the right to object to it for any reason, so long as the free exercise does not place an undue burden on the privileges or rights retained by others or otherwise violate reciprocity of immunities amoung all, including freedom from interference by private actors in rights/immunities and the enjoyment of [justly] bestowed privileges.

In order to ensure that the homeless do not need to defecate in public or urinate in public, as well as that they may access potable water and places for the disabled or the elderly to rest temporarily, each state shall ensure that the several municipalities provide for access to 24/7/365 public bathrooms and adequate benches next to (potentially graphene-nanocellulose [patterned electrode array or electro‑osmotic actuator] [self-purging/auto-cleaning]/[reversible] reverse-osmosis filtering) water fountains, no less frequently than every 400 meters within the downtown locus, and no less than every 800 meters elsewise, within any town or city of more than 2000 people, and no less than one of each for all towns and cities regardless of population size. As part of redress for grievances, this provision has been entered in order to ensure that the public spaces serve the needs of both of the homeless and the disabled and the elderly and the greater public at large, and answer that basic town/city infrastructure can provide for the needs of many without punishing the few who are at the lowest of the economic rungs and may have no other place to do natural business and take care of essential needs. These locations may also provide GFCI outlet AC power with residual current breaker boxes and single-wire transmission magnetic clasp connections along with wireless fidelity internet and powerline-networking along the single-wire, in addition to any amenities that the local municipality has decided are necessary for their purposes to serve the needs of their People. Each municipality shall also be required by each state to possess at least one sufficient rest stop location for nomadic caravan travelers or overnight vehicle/craft camping, and sufficient parking to meet the needs of the whole community as well as transients or travelers. Access to all of these facilities shall not discriminate between housing status or social economic rank and other differentiating factors which would deprive another of equal protection of the law and fair access to privileges bestowed by the social compact.

As a means to prevent homelessness or lack of shelter and social insecurity of our people through displacement of housing by foreign Nationals, each State shall have the power to tax real property, including land, houses, and housing rent, when the profit from such property is derived from a foreign individual who is not naturalized to the nation of Pacifica and arises from a mutually agreed‑to and consented exchange, such as a lease, rental, or sale of residential or land‑based real estate, and each State shall fix the rate, base, and administrative procedures within an upper limit of one-point-five percent (1.5%) of the value of the transaction or the net income attributable to the transaction, as determined by the State, so that the tax remains targeted, predictable, and bounded at the level of real‑property‑related income. All revenues collected under this provision shall be dedicated exclusively to low‑income and affordable housing programs that benefit poor Citizens of Pacifica, and a meaningful portion of these revenues may be used to provide in‑facility services such as mental health professionals for crisis intervention, food services, and other free services directed to the poor, thereby ensuring that the taxation of foreign‑derived real‑property profits is directly tied to the material well‑being of citizens and to the protection of citizens from displacement by non‑naturalized foreigners. These free services may include, but are not limited to, Internet access and digital‑inclusion support such as devices, training, and connectivity programs; free toiletries and hygiene items such as toothbrushes, toothpaste, soap, shampoo, deodorant, toilet paper, sanitary products, diapers, dish soap, cleaning supplies, and paper towels; and on‑site laundry and shower facilities located within or adjacent to affordable housing developments, all of which help preserve dignity, health, and basic human standards of living for citizens of Pacifica. Additional services may encompass basic medical and first‑aid supplies, periodic health‑screening clinics, after‑school or youth enrichment programs, tutoring, literacy classes, and community‑space programs such as childcare drop‑in centers, community kitchens, and mutual‑aid hubs, which together strengthen social cohesion and reduce isolation among low‑income citizens who rely on rent‑controlled or affordable housing. States may also use portions of the revenue for legal aid and counseling services related to housing, benefits, and other civic‑support matters that protect vulnerable citizens from wrongful eviction or contractual exploitation, as well as transportation assistance or subsidized transit passes that enable residents to access employment, education, healthcare, and essential services beyond their immediate neighborhood, all of which reinforce the intent of this policy by bolstering the security and stability of citizens. Each State may establish performance standards, reporting requirements, and fairness metrics to ensure that the services supported by this tax are equitably distributed, accessible to the most vulnerable citizens, and regularly monitored for effectiveness and accountability, with explicit safeguards that the tax applies only to land, houses, and housing rent, and that benefits are prioritized for citizens of Pacifica and not for non‑naturalized foreigners. This provision shall not shield foreign property owners from paying greed penalty taxes for holding excess land as according to the powers bestowed in this constitution for civil society preservation. This framework ensures that foreign‑derived real‑property‑related profits are not only taxed but are systematically reinvested into the social infrastructure of Pacifica, particularly in the form of housing, health, education, and dignity‑preserving supports that protect citizens from displacement and economic marginalization while preserving the focus on land and housing as the core objects of the tax power.

Pacifica affirms the right of every individual to safe, stable, and adequate housing, which is accessible without undue burden or complexity, and provides a realistic path to private property ownership where humanly possible. Housing and shelter are recognized as fundamental rights of every person within the jurisdiction of Pacifica. Safe, decent, and affordable housing is essential to health, well-being, and dignity. A "Housing First" approach, prioritizing immediate access to permanent housing without immediate preconditions such as sobriety, treatment compliance, or employment of the disabled or insane, shall be the foundation of federal, state, and local homelessness policy within Pacifica. Each constituent jurisdiction within Pacifica shall provide immediate, non-discriminatory access to emergency shelter for all persons in need, meeting at baseline the following standards: Safe and habitable healthy shelter protected from weather elements; Adequate sanitary facilities, including restrooms and showers; Provision of basic necessities such as clean bedding, meals, and climate protection; Availability of supportive onsite services including case management, mental health and substance use treatment, housing navigation, and referral services. Emergency shelters shall be low-barrier to entry, decentralized across Pacifica to meet local needs, and designed to serve diverse populations including individuals, families, veterans, seniors, and persons with disabilities. Each constituent jurisdiction shall establish and maintain programs that provide pathways from emergency shelter to: Transitional housing with supportive services such as life skills training, job placement, behavioral health treatment, and addiction recovery; Permanent supportive housing units prioritized for those with chronic homelessness or housing insecurity, disabilities, mental health needs, and veterans. Housing First principles shall guide all permanent housing programs, removing unnecessary barriers to entry while ensuring wraparound services are voluntarily available to residents. Programs shall include access to rental assistance and subsidies ensuring affordability, with residents paying no more than thirty percent (30%) of income in rent where feasible. Each State within Pacifica shall have the duty to ensure adequate funding to provide shelters and housing, in addition to supportive services, for homeless/unsheltered individuals in every county within its jurisdiction, sufficient to meet demand and uphold the guarantee to rent-to-own housing provided herein. States and local jurisdictions shall coordinate with Indigenous nations, non-profits, cooperatives, and private housing providers to expand affordable rent-to-own and supportive subsidized housing stock. Pacifica shall maintain a coordinated homelessness response system that includes: A centralized twenty-four/seven/year-round (24/7/365.25) helpline and online access portal; Integration of housing, health, behavioral, and social services; Equitable distribution of programs and facilities to prevent geographic service gaps. Local and regional decision-making shall include representation from affected communities. Services shall prioritize: Families with minor children; Seniors; Veterans; Persons with disabilities or behavioral health needs; Survivors of domestic violence and other vulnerable populations. The Congress of Pacifica shall have the power to enforce this Provision through appropriate legislation, including funding allocations and oversight mechanisms to ensure compliance by states. Congress shall provide sustained funding support to states, provinces, and localities to help fulfill their obligations, and may establish penalties or corrective actions for noncompliance. Lawful residents denied rights under this Provision may seek judicial relief. Courts shall have authority to compel immediate compliance and order remedies consistent with the guarantees herein. All programs under this Provision shall be administered for citizens without discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin for lawful immigrants, social status, lack of income, or housing status.

[]
The Commonwealth of the several States of Pacifica and the Territories throughout shall have the constitutional power to establish, administer, fund, regulate, and enforce a Primary-Residence Access Program for the benefit of eligible individuals, and to create all offices, funds, procedures, records, forms, and subordinate mechanisms necessary to carry that program into effect. The purpose of this power is to ensure broad accessibility to productive property and practical ownership opportunity for all citizens, so that the Commonwealth fosters a widely held order of small proprietors, household stewards, and independent families rather than a system in which land, shelter, and the means of residence are concentrated in the hands of a few. The program shall provide a practical path for eligible individuals to obtain and maintain an inexpensive parcel of land or primary-residence site, together with essential support for making the property habitable, useful, and secure as an actual home, and eligibility shall extend only to those individuals whose annual income is at or below the national mean per-capita income, who are first-time homeowners, and for whom progressive priority and assistance shall be directed first to those of least means and with the lowest access prices reserved for those with the least ability to pay. The burden of application and qualification shall rest with the applicant, provided that the Commonwealth shall maintain a central office or equivalent administrative service to assist applicants in understanding, preparing, submitting, and maintaining their applications and related requirements, and any eligible applicant may designate a lawful proxy, advocate, agent, guardian, conservator, or supported-decision-making representative to act on the applicant’s behalf where such designation is lawful and consistent with the applicant’s dignity, autonomy, and best interests. This program shall not be limited to conventional houses or to any alleged homestead-development scheme, but shall include the acquisition of vacant land, the acquisition of existing land with a dwelling already upon it, and the financing or subsidizing of new construction, repairs, rehabilitation, and all necessary site and dwelling improvements, including roads, driveways, access works, water supply, wells, towers, cisterns, sanitation, septic systems, energy generation and storage, fuel tanks, gates, fences, bridges, drainage, and like infrastructure necessary to render the residence usable. It shall also include trailers, campers, modular dwellings, and other mobile or towable structures when they are used as the applicant’s actual primary residence, and it may apply to mixed-use parcels, rural lands, and farmland when the intended and lawful purpose is to establish a real home upon the land. The land acquisition price shall be set on a sliding scale, with the maximum allowable price for any eligible applicant capped at the applicant’s annual income at or below the national mean per-capita income divided by 365.25, and with the poorest eligible applicants paying as little as one dollar or such other nominal amount as the Legislature may set; and the Commonwealth may subsidize a substantial share of qualifying housing costs, including up to thirty percent or such other amount as may be required to make the dwelling actually usable, whether the need is for a new residence or for improvements, maintenance, or rehabilitation of an existing house already on the land. No applicant shall be denied eligibility merely because the residence is off-grid, self-supplied, or not connected to public utilities, and the Commonwealth may finance or subsidize essential housing costs without requiring ongoing housing payments as a condition of residence, though reasonable financing arrangements may be offered where needed. The Primary-Residence Access Program shall cooperate with the State Banks of the several States, with the Federal Bank of the federal district, and with such banking institutions as are distributed throughout the Territories as may presently exist, and such banks shall be authorized and encouraged to provide financing for any remainder of costs not covered by the program, including the unpaid balance of the seventy percent remainder of a residence development subsidy or any equivalent balance arising from land acquisition, construction, or improvement. All property acquired or assisted under this program shall be held and maintained under conditions that preserve the occupant’s autonomy, encourage personal stewardship, support the diffusion of ownership among the many rather than concentration among the few, and permit voluntary transfer, consolidation, or shared ownership only by free choice and not by legal compulsion. The Legislature shall have power to enact all laws needful and proper to implement this section, including detailed rules for eligibility, verification, subsidy administration, occupancy requirements, bank coordination, anti-fraud safeguards, recapture or resale restrictions, and any other matter not here expressly set forth, provided that all such laws shall be made in conformity with this Constitution and may not diminish the rights, guarantees, and purposes established herein.
[]

Every city or region above a six-thousand-five-hundred people (>6500 populus) shall operate, fund, or regulate at least one sanitary and utilified public [at-cost or free] hostel with 4 to 16 rooms [or more] that guarantees 24 hours a day, 7 days a week access to homeless/unsheltered people, regardless of weather, season, or time of year, with no night‑time curfew or seasonal closure for the portions reserved for them; within this hostel, homeless/unsheltered individuals (with or without documentation) must be given priority over tourists for available beds, receiving a small room with electric and bathroom, a key or key‑card to their space, and a lockable locker for belongings under a bed‑and‑key model that applies at all times, while also bearing the responsibility to leave their bedspace and shared areas clean and sanitary upon vacating or transferring out, properly disposing of trash and returning shared items, with non‑compliance addressed through supportive measures such as temporary cleaning duties and written warnings rather than immediate eviction, and each State government shall ensure adequate funding, along with cleaning supplies and laundry machines, staff training, and annual monitoring so that any persistent failure to provide uninterrupted 24/7 access and proper bed‑and‑key conditions for homeless and unsheltered people may result in changes of operator or withdrawal of State-provided funding. The hostels should operate as transitional housing for the homeless and unsheltered, so that they have a number of weeks to months they are permitted to stay before being requested to leave, at the discretion of the municipality rule prescriptions. the hostels should also provide access for basic needs, such as low-cost or free meals (breakfast + one main meal), showers, laundry, wireless internet, public computers for maps in addition to email and other digital needs, landline phone, and mail service, along with first‑aid, and as available to provide offers for light paid work (E.g.: cleaning, kitchen, reception) during their stay.

To secure the safety, dignity, and liberty of persons experiencing homelessness and housing insecurity, each State and its political subdivisions shall establish and maintain accessible public campsites within their jurisdictions, located in proximity to major population centers and areas of greatest need. These campsites shall be voluntary and consent-based, never coercive, and shall exist as a lawful option for habitation when an individual chooses them freely. No person shall be compelled to reside in such camps, nor shall their lawful right to remain elsewhere be diminished by the existence of the campsites. Residents of these campsites shall be granted occupancy permissions of no less than one month and no more than three months at a time, with extensions permitted under conditions of exigency, including but not limited to the unavailability of shelter beds or affordable and subsidized housing. Each campsite shall be equipped with essential amenities, including laundry facilities, outdoor kitchens, safe bathrooms, clean drinking water, electricity, telephone and internet access, food provisions, secure mailboxes, trash and sanitation service, showers, storage lockers, and shaded or weather-protected day-use shelters. To promote self-reliance and community health, such campsites shall further provide access to public food forests, community gardens, and reliable transportation via bus or train. These sites shall be managed in a manner that respects individual autonomy, fosters personal security, and recognizes the inherent liberty of all persons to direct their own lives. The purpose of this amendment is not to restrict freedom but to affirmatively guarantee that those who seek refuge will find lawful, humane, and dignified accommodations provided in common trust for the people.

Hostile architecture and designs which are intended to increase the difficulty of life for the homeless and unsheltered, or which obstruct the enjoyment of public utilities and/or works on account of homelessness or lack of shelter, shall be unlawful for deployment or implementation by the public body. The use of gates and fences to close off public areas in order to reduce homeless encampments or foot traffic is prohibited except for high security areas that require defense from passersby. The use of sirens or light generating equipment in order to increase the difficulty of sleeping for the homeless and unsheltered during the common resting hours shall also be barred from use by the government.

SECTION. 17.666

No common carrier, including any operator of carriage, ferry, stagecoach, or public conveyance by land, water, or air, shall refuse to transport any passenger to their intended destination upon tender of reasonable fare, provided that the passenger causes no disturbance, violates no rights of other passengers or the carrier, and complies with necessary safety regulations. Carriers shall be liable for safe delivery absent force majeure, public enemies, inherent defects, or the passenger's own gross misconduct. This provision enshrines the ancient common carrier doctrine as a fundamental right of public access to transit.

[]
This Constitution hereby affirms that all persons, especially vulnerable individuals such as youth in crisis, victims of crime/violence, those experiencing homelessness and housing insecurity, mental health emergencies, extreme weather, medical distress, or exploitation, shall enjoy an absolute irrevocable privilege to confidential, immediate, and cost-free transportation via any common carrier or public transit, including buses, trains, ferries, rideshares, taxis, airlines, and private shuttles operating publicly, to designated safe havens, preempting contrary laws and mandating maximal aid without inquiry into status, ability to pay, or documentation, with state legislatures empowered to prescribe individual conditions for implementation; this Provision hereby establishes a nationwide Safe Haven Transit Network requiring vehicles, stations, stops, apps, and facilities to display universal signage (e.g., "Safe Haven Here"), train personnel in de-escalation and recognition signals (verbal "Safe Haven," symbols, texts to centralized emergency-service lines), and provide 24/7 priority service modeled on national crisis programs, with pet accompaniment, language access, and non-police handoffs; complimentary transport shall include, but not be limited to, delivery to heat/cold exposure shelters, 24/7 homeless/unsheltered service centers, domestic violence/sexual assault/trafficking shelters, urgent care/hospitals/emergency medical transport, psychiatric crisis centers/mobile teams/inpatient stabilization/substance use facilities, police stations/alternative response units/youth runaway services, and any refuge under the broadest interpretation of relevant laws, including food banks, legal aid, and cultural/faith-based sanctuaries, prohibiting refusals and requiring coordination with crisis hotlines or local agencies for trauma-informed transfers; private and public carriers receive full tax write-offs at up to 200% of verifiable costs (fuel, maintenance, lost revenue, training), certified annually by the Treasury, plus grants for expansion (apps, electric vehicles, rural routes), and absolute civil/criminal immunity for good-faith actions in accordance with law, with the Legislature of Congress and each State funding signage, tech, and oversight for equity among Indigenous, rural, disabled, and migrant needs; an autonomous Safe Haven Commission with competent appointees [with oversight from the Legislature] shall enforce via legitimate fines, audits, and citizen suits, issuing annual reports and submitting amendments for approval by the Legislature, allowing State/Provincial enhancements, effective upon three-fourths State/Provincial ratification to entrench compassionate mobility as core to Pacifican Guarantees in daily life.
