No person shall cause, suffer, allow or permit or fail to take reasonable steps to abate or terminate the discharge from any source whatsoever of air contaminants or other material which shall cause injury, detriment, nuisance, or annoyance of the public or which endanger the comfort, repose, health or safety of the public or which cause or have a tendency to cause injury or damage to business or property; No person shall cause, suffer, allow or permit or fail to take reasonable steps to abate or terminate the discharge from any source whatsoever air contaminants or water or steam or a combination of such which cause, or combine with natural elements to cause, the reduction of visibility across any road or thoroughfare to such an extent as to cause a hazard; The intentional injection, release, or dispersion, by any means, of chemicals, chemical compounds, substances, or apparatus within the borders of Pacifica, any State, or any Territory, into the atmosphere with the express purpose of affecting temperature, weather, or the intensity of the sunlight, is strictly prohibited. Nothing in any other section of this constitution relating to regulation of emission or pollutants shall in any manner be construed as authorizing or legalizing the creating or maintenance of a nuisance as described in this regulation or as may otherwise be deemed by law to be a nuisance. Congress and the several States shall have the power to uphold this Provision.

Each State shall apply preventive and restrictive measures on activities that might lead to the extinction of species, the destruction of ecosystems, and the permanent alteration of natural cycles. The introduction of organisms, along with organic and inorganic material, that might definitively alter the Nation’s genetic assets, is forbidden.

Persons, Communities, Peoples, and Nations shall be respected in their right to benefit from the environment and the natural wealth enabling them to enjoy the good way of living. Environmental services shall not be subject to appropriation; their production, delivery, use and development shall be regulated by the States.

Persons, Communities, Peoples, Nations, and international Communities are bearers of rights and shall enjoy the rights protected for them in the Federal and respective State Constitution/s as well as in international instruments. Nature shall be the subject of those rights that the Constitutions which both the Federal and Several States recognize for it. The Rights of Nature shall be balanced in interest with the Rights of Persons, so that both are given [as nearly as may be] an equal stake in the courts with regard to their continued existence and Autonomy/Independence, as well as, independence/freedom from all forms of aggression and exploitation against either of them.

All legislative, economic, and environmental decisions shall be subject to an Intergenerational Equity Review assessing their projected impact upon the seventh generation hence. This Federation of States as Pacifica shall maintain transparent, publicly auditable algorithms to calculate long-term ecological and social sustainability scores for all major policies, ensuring that present liberty does not become future bondage through debt, degradation, or depletion. Each generation is the steward, not the owner, of the Earth it inhabits, and owes to its descendants the right to live free from the consequences of unrestrained exploitation. The People of Pacifica shall treat the unborn as silent shareholders in the commonwealth of nature and time.

Everyone shall possess the right to a healthy and ecologically balanced human living environment and the duty to defend it. Future Generations possess the right to inherit an un-damaged environment and a sustainable commons, with any developments upon protected land being minimal and only as necessary for environmental stewardship and the reasonable public-use of such Land by the People.

Geo-engineering, including but not limited to solar radiation management, cloud seeding, and precipitation causing or enhancing chemical aerosols and suspensions or immersions, is prohibited throughout Pacifica, and anybody operating within or affecting it’s borders, and no partnership of inter-national comradery shall be established with those Nations or States partaking in, providing for, or directing the same.

No Individual shall be subject to Carbon Footprint Tracking within the Jurisdiction of Pacifica, its forts/installations/et_cetera, its territories, or any of its composing States or subdivisions thereof. No individual shall be required to submit to limitations of their rights under any carbon quotas.

Wildlife throughout Pacifica and the several States shall, to the greatest extent practicable, utilize principles of sound scientific management in making decisions regarding the taking of fish and game, taking into equal account the personal experience and opinions of real wildlife conservationists such as, but not solely, trappers and hunters that preserve the balance of ecology based on the Cycles of Life between predator and prey. Local commissions may take testimony from department personnel, independent experts, and others, and review scientific literature and data, among other sources, in support of its duty to use principles of sound scientific management. The Local commission of each jurisdiction shall issue orders regarding the taking of fish and game following a public meeting and an opportunity for public input.

Wherever occurring in their natural state, fish, wildlife, and waters are reserved to the People for common use. The privately owned lands and their resources belong to the property owner and are not subject to requisition or appropriation, except as according to this State’s constitution and the Federal pact.

[]
No state, county, municipality, special district, or other political subdivision, nor alternate branch of government federal or elsewise neither any power therein, shall impose, assess, or collect any tax, fee, or charge, directly or indirectly, based on the presence, incidence, intensity, duration, or surface-area exposure of naturally occurring elements, defined herein as precipitation (including rain, snow, and hail), sunlight, and wind (collectively referred to as, “natural elements”), upon any parcel of Private or Public property, such prohibited impositions including but not limited to any formula, proxy, or assessment mechanism, such as land area, roof area, or modeled environmental exposure, designed to approximate or substitute for such natural incidence, and applying without regard to whether the property owner, lawful occupant, or authorized operator collects, stores, diverts, converts, shares, or otherwise makes productive use of such natural elements through systems including but not limited to rainwater harvesting, solar energy generation, hydroelectric generation, or wind energy generation (collectively, “harvesting systems”), which uses are expressly recognized as lawful exercises of dominion over one’s property and extend to personal, commercial, and community applications, the latter defined as voluntary, consent-based arrangements in which multiple participants knowingly agree to share in the benefits of such systems under terms set by the owner or operator, in conformity with the other parts of this constitution and laws made in accordance therewith; this prohibition arises from the principle that taxation must attach to defined human activity, exchange, or the provision of public services, rather than to passive exposure to phenomena that no person creates, controls, or exclusively possesses, that the assignment of taxable value to such exposure is inherently speculative and administratively arbitrary, that conditioning liability on the mere receipt of ambient natural forces and the effects thereof severs any rational nexus between taxation and governmental service, that imposing such charges would penalize productive, conservation-oriented uses of property while duplicating or distorting existing property tax frameworks, and that the freedom to capture, use, and share naturally occurring resources incident to land ownership, subject only to neutral, narrowly tailored health, safety, environmental, and non-pretextual land-use regulations, constitutes a fundamental attribute of property rights that shall not be burdened, diminished, or indirectly encumbered through fiscal measures masquerading as regulation or cost recovery, except as how such regulations may be permitted by this constitution in order to protect People, Animals, and the Environment/Nature from real and demonstrable damage.
[]

Every enterprise engaged in extraction, manufacturing, agriculture, energy generation, or material transformation shall be constitutionally bound to maintain a regenerative and symbiotic ecological footprint no less than equal to the totality of its environmental impact, measured and verified through decentralized ecological accounting. The principle of Self-Regeneration shall hold that economic activity is only legitimate when it preserves or enriches the bioregional integrity of Pacifica and its living systems. Entities that fail to uphold ecological parity shall face automatic contract suspension, loss of market participation, or transfer of their assets into public ecological trusts.

There shall be established in the sovereign Nation of Pacifica a split "Harmony Pull Authority", both at the National and State level to be vested with the power to commit federal and state public resources for the procurement of innovations achieving verified outcomes of human-centered stewardship, biologic harmony, and equitable flourishing, disbursed solely upon independent certification of such ends. The federal Harmony Pull Authority shall consist of a National Sovereign Fund, administered by a rotating Council of Citizen-Stewards appointed by joint resolution of Congress and confirmed by the several bioregional Assemblies of each State. The Council shall issue advance purchase commitments aligned with national precepts of distributist diffusion, libertarian safeguards, and reciprocity of societal benefits, subject to annual referenda and sunset provisions. Each State of Pacifica shall maintain a Bioregional Harmony Pull Network, organized under Legislature oversight, comprising pools drawn from state revenues and municipal consortia. State Authorities shall pledge procurements tied to regionally defined metrics of resilience and reciprocity, scaling public commitments while preserving local sovereignty, with powers exercised through elected Assemblies accountable to the People. All powers herein granted shall reinforce separation of authority: the Legislative Branch shall define outcome metrics and levies; the Executive Branch shall administer funds and verifications through independent Auditors; the Judicial Branch shall adjudicate disputes, enforce equity mandates, and void dystopian overreach. No branch shall encroach upon the others, nor upon the reserved rights of the People and Bioregions. Reinforcing mechanisms shall include mandatory diffusion of ownership in rewarded ventures, environmental safety nets funded by unclaimed commitments, as well as to the right of citizen initiative and referendum. Metrics of societal well-being, environmental preservation and biodiversity, in addition to autonomy, shall govern success, with automatic reallocation to grassroots empowerment upon failure, securing the perpetual harmony of Pacifica with the world at large.

The several States shall each provide for a Green Transition & Innovation Fund, existing solely as a non‑coercive, enabling instrument to foster open, market‑driven innovation in energy production, energy sources, energy efficiency, and pollution‑reducing technologies, and it may never be used to compel individuals or firms to abandon petrol chemicals or fossil‑fuel energy sources, or to mandate any particular form of energy adoption or rejection; the fund’s purpose is to accelerate the development of holistic systems that are designed from inception to retirement to avoid generating noxious waste products, so that whenever energy technologies are advanced, their materials, operations, and end‑of‑life pathways are structured to minimize or eliminate toxic, persistent, or bioaccumulative byproducts rather than merely shifting pollution across space, time, or social groups; any project of the State's Department of Goods and Services receiving support from the fund must demonstrate transparent, end‑to‑end material flows and disposal strategies that either render residual outputs harmless, rapidly degradable, or fully recoverable within safe reuse or regeneration cycles, and no technology whose lifecycle knowingly produces significant hazardous residues may be subsidized under this Provision; Citizens retain the social contractual right to petition for new projects that align with these principles and to petition for the review or termination of projects that fail to meet agreed‑upon progress and environmental criteria, ensuring that the fund remains accountable not only to official management but to the people whose environment and health it is meant to protect; the States shall encourage the development of open‑source, do‑it‑yourself‑friendly designs that individuals can build or adapt in their homes, garages, or local laboratories; through this framework, Pacifica affirms that the transition away from petrol chemicals and fossil‑fuel dependence, where it occurs, must emerge as a rational, voluntary choice driven by the attractiveness, reliability, and cleanliness of alternative options rather than by state compulsion, and that the Green Transition & Innovation Fund is constitutionally bound to serve that persuasion‑based transformation without undermining individual freedom, energy sovereignty, or ecological integrity.

Carbon monoxide is hereby declared a noxious poison and a direct injury to the rights of persons, animals, and the environment/nature to life, health, and clean air; accordingly, its emission beyond one’s property or into shared air may be taxed, regulated, and remediated as a harm. There shall be placed by each State, and by the Federal Legislature within their jurisdiction, an individualized carbon monoxide harm tax upon all vehicles, engines, and industrial or commercial activities that emit carbon monoxide into air external to the engine or it's assembly, or out into the environment/nature, measured by actual or reasonably estimated output attributable to engine type, size, usage, and fuel consumption along with efficiency, along with consideration of any sequestering design of the engine while in actual operation, as may be established by law. This tax shall not apply to carbon dioxide as such, nor to establish carbon credits, greenhouse-gas quotas, or any scheme founded upon indirect climate accounting rather than direct [toxic] injury or the true risk/threat thereof. The Legislature may provide reductions, rebates, or exemptions, with opportunity for public comment by 'the People' and initiative or referendum over-ride by the same.

The use of all roads, ways and waterways necessary to promote the transportation of the raw products of mine or farm or forest or water for beneficial use or drainage is necessary to the development and welfare of the state/s and is declared a public use.

Every person has the right of public access or freedom to roam, which is the People’s right to access certain public land (they are required to stay off of private property) for recreation and exercise, including but not limited to resting, sitting, walking/hiking, cycling, animal riding, boating, and camping in nature, so long as they “Don’t disturb – Don’t destroy – Leave no trace”. People are allowed to access any public park or forest; They are within reasonable limits allowed to collect flowers as well as edible mushrooms and plants or their products, graze their own animals so long as they leave resources available for all other visiting persons and their livestock as well as maintain and preserve the sustainment of natural stocks of wildlife, and within reasonable limits allowed to catch fish and hunt or trap wildlife for food, they may put up a tent and camp for a limited period of time as necessary to accommodate other visitors, collection of tinder and brush is acceptable and campfires are allowed within reasonable limits as long as they are in a safe area and not left un-attended (they must be fully extinguished before leaving them), swimming and boating in streams and rivers as well as ponds and lakes is allowed, and they may access any beach open to the ocean or any waterway connecting to a public right-of-way and 3.5 meters (3.5m) in from the surge-level high-water mark of such waterway, with reasonable extentions under the principle of 'Common Law passage' that allow navigation around [natural] obstacles or [present] dangers so long as the least invasive ingress into a Private property boundary occurs that allows safe land-based navigation and travel alongside the publicly-accessible waterway, within the limits set by Law to protect the equal interests of the adjacent Private property-owners [if any].

The public parks, greenways, commons, and all lands reserved for recreation, rest, and renewal, shall be declared perpetual and irrevocable holdings of the People, administered in trust by every level of government within Pacifica as living estates of universal/shared/basic dignity rather than as instruments of exclusion or privilege. These spaces shall serve equally [to the maximum extent humanly possible] the housed and unhoused, the resident and the sojourner, the young, the aged, the disabled, and all conditions between, ensuring that the right to peaceable occupation, repose, and recreation within such public grounds shall not be abridged except by lawful cause narrowly defined to protect the safety and equal enjoyment of all, without abridging or otherwise reducing the rights of Individuals. No person shall be deprived of free access to the air, water, shade, resting features like benches and tables, or shelter naturally or humanly provided within these public domains, as well as electric and internet access, which stand as visible proofs of the social compact by which the community sustains its own humanity. Their management shall respect both individual freedom and collective harmony, guided by civic stewardship that emphasizes cooperation, regenerative ecology, and public beneficence, so that the grounds of leisure become a common grounds of belonging. Within these community spaces, every person, regardless of circumstance or means, shall find the affirmation of liberty, peace, and subsistence as inherent attributes of Citizenship and Personhood under the constitutional order of Pacifica.

Each state shall set forth and set aside and devote for use by homeless/unsheltered individuals certain public lands deemed reasonable for on foot and transit access, in each of their several Counties, and within each County in Towns or Cities with a population at or above two-hundred-thirty Persons. Each homeless camping parcel set aside for public use shall have electricity, potable water, bathrooms, kitchenettes, along with cellular calling and general internet access as well as other network systems approved by the People of their jurisdiction. Then as directed further by their People, additional amenities may be added such as storage lockers and washing rooms for doing laundry, along with any other needful improvement that the State or Counties see necessary to provide for the homeless/unsheltered community in their Jurisdiction, as directed by the People.

Each State shall set forth to set aside and devote for the use of public lands to consist of State forests, which forests are considered part of the national heritage and regional commonwealth, where the State Bureau of Land Management shall provide for the allocation of resources from the public forests for proper campsites and facilities for water craft as well as shooting/firing ranges.

Each State shall set forth to set aside and devote lands to cultivate and maintain statewide self-sustaining bio-diverse food forests, which land shall be devoted as State parks, where People may [mutually] share in the bounty of the land; State funds and resources shall be set aside for the establishment of County and Local organic bio-diverse community gardens, primarily for the purpose of providing for the People of the counties and localities within each State who show need for nutritional assistance.

Each State shall keep a sanctuary for endangered fungi, plant, and animal species found in their State, and the sanctuary will be open to the public and generate revenues to further protect and restore endangered species and their habitats. The sanctuaries will breed such life in captivity and from time to time release and integrate endangered life back into the environment.

Each State shall each establish a Green Initiative Commission to provide green incentives for green engineering and solar or radiant design, alternative energy and bio-fuel, and carbon neutral or carbon capturing projects; The States shall provide for the partial funding of those projects for Persons and families of zero to low income.

The Green Initiative Commission of each State shall contribute to the Local communities of such State by energy infrastructure involvement, including but not limited to solar and radiant energy, wind, biomass, battery and capacitor technology, and ion power, as well as geothermal facilities, in addition to energy harvesting and zero-point power-extraction; They shall fund research and development in support of the State industry, commerce, and business related to clean energy and green engineering as well as regenerative infrastructure, which shall not be limited to research and product innovation, development, and collaborative commercialization efforts between public and private entities; They shall provide oversight in the development of sites and facilities Statewide for and in support of industry, commerce, distribution, and research and development related to clean energy and green engineering in addition to regenerative infrastructure.

[]
We the People of Pacifica, as individuals in solidarity with the truth and righteousness, declare that all rights arise from the natural order, which exists independent of human will and activity which is knowable by reason, and that in the state of nature the earth, its lands, waters, air, and living systems existed as an integrated and self-sustaining whole, within which humanity emerged as a participant and beneficiary, not as a sovereign apart; from this it follows that no person possesses a rightful claim to destroy, exhaust, or corrupt the natural systems upon which all life depends, and that each stands under a duty of mutual preservation, such that the exercise of liberty must remain consistent with the continued integrity of that order. Civil society and government are therefore instituted not to override or replace natural law, but to secure more effectively the preexisting rights derived from it, and any authority exercised contrary to that end is without just foundation. Accordingly, the earth and its systems are a common inheritance held in trust for present and future generations, and their use shall be governed by the principles of stewardship, renewal, and restraint, such that they are not impaired beyond their capacity to sustain life and regenerate. In accordance with the common law and its enduring maxims, including sic utere tuo ut alienum non laedas, meaning that one must use one’s own so as not to harm another, together with the doctrines of public trust and nuisance, the inherent authority of government to secure health, safety, liberty, and well being, and the principles of precaution and intergenerational equity, it is established that the welfare of the people is the supreme law because all legitimate rights, institutions, and powers derive their justification from their role in preserving the conditions necessary for life, liberty, and human flourishing; and because such welfare is inseparable from the condition of the natural environment and the well-being of other living beings, whose existence forms an essential part of the same natural order upon which human life depends. Therefore, the rights to life and health, liberty, autonomy, sovereignty, and independence, self-security and defense of self and others consistent with natural law, privacy, and the pursuit of happiness are affirmed as primary, inherent, and binding, and shall take precedence over all derivative claims. Property, though a natural right, arises only through the just application of labor to resources not previously appropriated or rightfully held, and exists as a conditional extension of these primary rights; it is therefore inherently limited by the requirement that its use neither causes harm, nor creates unreasonable risk of harm, nor deprives others of the equal enjoyment of their rights or of access to the basic conditions necessary for life. Accordingly, neither property nor contract, nor any form of commerce or organized enterprise, shall be construed to justify conduct that degrades, monopolizes, excludes, or artificially restricts access to such essential conditions, nor to permit the subordination of natural rights to claims of economic gain, technological progress, or convenience. The State, as fiduciary of the People and guardian of the common inheritance, shall possess the authority and duty to prevent, restrain, and remedy violations of these principles through just and proportionate laws, while preserving the primary role of the People in stewardship and ensuring that power is not exercised in a manner that displaces or undermines their rights. Where property, capital, or agreements conflict with the primary rights herein secured, such claims shall yield, and no individual or collective entity shall evade these limitations through legal or structural artifices; the People shall retain the right to seek redress, and the courts shall provide effective remedies to prevent and correct harm. Any act or condition that poisons, degrades, or materially impairs persons, animals, or the environment, or that disrupts their natural development or life cycles, is contrary to natural law and constitutes an offense against the universal rights inherent in all beings, which endure independently of human enactment. Nothing herein shall prohibit productive activities necessary for human sustenance, including agriculture, resource extraction, and related pursuits, provided they are conducted in a manner consistent with stewardship, renewal, and the equal rights of others. This Provision shall not be interpreted to impair the natural right to acquire, hold, use, and defend property justly obtained through labor, nor the legitimacy of property created for the sustenance of oneself, one’s family, or one’s community; however, no accumulation or exercise of property, whether individual or collective, shall supersede or extinguish the primary rights herein established, and all property remains bounded by the enduring obligation to preserve the conditions necessary for life, liberty, and justice for present and future persons under this constitutional order.
[]

Enterprises operating within the Commonwealth of Pacifica that engage in the extraction, processing, or commercial distribution of petrochemical substances shall be obligated to render an ecological contribution equal to or less than thirty-five percent of the net value derived from such activities, as shall be set by Congress, or the People operating through its power. This contribution shall not constitute a punitive measure but a restorative instrument, ensuring that prosperity drawn from the industrial use of fossil resources directly sustains the ecological renewal of the region. Of all amounts collected, two-thirds or more shall be apportioned to the constituent states of Pacifica proportional to their population for environmental restoration, endangered species protection, wildlife coexistance programs and improvements/enhancements to public administration and infrastructure, sustainable energy transition, and the stewardship of local and regional parklands, as directed by their People; no more than one-third shall accrue to the federal treasury of Pacifica for the coordination and funding of interjurisdictional restoration programs and towards national parks, as directed by the People of Pacifica. Collection and distribution shall be transparent, publicly audited, and executed pursuant to statutes enacted in harmony with this Constitution, ensuring fairness and stability in assessment. The rate established herein shall reflect both the consent of the governed and the recognition that while petrochemical dependency cannot presently be abolished, its yield must become an instrument for the preservation and recovery of Pacifica’s living environment. By this provision, the people of Pacifica affirm the moral duty to transform industrial and commercial consequence into ecological restoration and promotion of the people's natural Rights in all modalities within the equal boundary balanced by the individual ambit of oneself over their own life, as well as safeguard the freedom and quality of life sustained by nature’s enduring balance.

To safeguard Pacifica’s natural resources, promote public health, and protect the common environment for present and future generations, the manufacture, sale, and distribution of single-use food containers made from expanded polystyrene foam (commonly known as Styrofoam) shall be prohibited, except as provided herein. Consistent with Pacifica’s tradition of local autonomy, voluntary stewardship, and decentralized governance, municipalities and communities retain the authority to implement stricter standards or additional bans on single-use food containers as they see fit, provided such measures do not infringe upon fundamental liberties or property rights. This prohibition shall not apply to reusable food containers, nor to packaging necessary for medical, emergency, or humanitarian purposes where no practical alternative exists, and for limited purposes related to the structural or operational integrity of technology such as energy or computer systems which are intended to be used long-term. Small businesses may apply for limited, time-bound waivers if compliance would cause undue hardship and no reasonable alternatives are available. All waivers must be publicly disclosed and subject to periodic review. Government agencies shall prioritize education, technical assistance, and voluntary incentive programs to support individuals, businesses, and communities in transitioning to sustainable alternatives, rather than relying on punitive enforcement. In keeping with Pacifica’s commitment to local solutions and non-regulatory stewardship, enforcement shall emphasize collaboration and remediation over punishment. Regulatory intervention shall be a last resort, reserved for egregious or repeated violations. Any citizen or business affected by this provision retains the right to challenge its application or enforcement in a court of law, ensuring due process and protection of individual rights.

No business entity within the jurisdiction of Pacifica, nor within any State, Territory, or the Federal District or Capitol thereof, shall import, manufacture, refine, process, stockpile, trade, supply, distribute, offer for sale, or sell any plastic or polymer product or material that is petrol-based or non-degradable, as defined by law; provided, however, that all plastic or polymer products procured, commissioned, or otherwise utilized in commerce shall be limited exclusively to oxo-degradable or biodegradable plastics or polymers, and any pro-degradant additive employed therein shall be subject to prior approval by the Legislature, which shall by statute prescribe and direct the Environmental Protection Agency of each State and of the Federal District or Capitol to evaluate, certify, regulate, and enforce such standards in such manner as may be provided by law. All plastics and polymers not expressly scheduled or classified by Congress or by the respective State legislature shall be deemed permissible only if they constitute compostable, biodegradable bioplastics or biopolymers produced without the addition of pigments, fillers, extenders, plasticizers, or other modifying agents, and any such pigment, filler, extender, plasticizer, or additive, if used, shall be individually scheduled, classified, and regulated in accordance with uniform or jurisdiction-specific rules established by Congress and by each State for their respective jurisdictions. All plastic or polymer products, materials, and packaging offered for commercial distribution shall bear clear, legible, and standardized labeling indicating the precise type and classification of plastic or polymer utilized, including whether such material is recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, or otherwise degradable under specified environmental conditions; and all recycled scheduled plastic or polymer products sold or distributed in commerce shall be conspicuously marked “Recycled plastic/polymer,” and where such recycled material was not previously authorized for food-contact use, has not been demonstrably maintained free from biological, chemical, or particulate contamination throughout the recycling process, or has not been subjected to validated testing sufficient to establish its purity and safety for reuse in food-contact applications, such products shall additionally and prominently bear the designation “unsafe for contact with food.” Congress and each State shall have the authority to regulate, restrict, condition, or prohibit the commercial uses, applications, and disposal of plastics, polymers, and their derivatives and by-products, including but not limited to their use in materials and products that come into direct or indirect contact with potable water, food or food preparation surfaces, pharmaceutical composition, packaging, and delivery systems, toiletries and cosmetic products, children’s toys and childcare articles, household chemicals and analogous consumer goods, materials exposed to solvents or reactive substances, and goods and materials utilized in gardening, agriculture, and horticulture, including but not limited to packaging, containers, sheeting, cloths, coverings, netting, tubing, and enclosures; and Congress and each State shall enact and enforce such implementing legislation, rules, and standards through their respective Environmental Protection Agencies or equivalent bodies. The prohibitions herein established shall not apply to plastics or polymers demonstrably necessary for structural applications, arms and munitions, or for educational, research, experimental, scientific, or medical equipment and devices, nor shall such prohibitions apply to petrol-based or non-degradable plastic or polymer components integral to imported consumer electronics or to such educational, research, scientific, or medical equipment, where the application of such prohibition would materially and substantially impair the availability, functionality, safety, or advancement of tools, instruments, or technologies relied upon by consumers, researchers, experimenters, scientists, medical professionals, or educators, or would confer a disproportionate advantage upon specialized or restricted industries. Every retail establishment or commercial entity providing plastic or polymer carryout bags or similar items to customers shall maintain, in a location readily accessible and clearly visible to customers, designated receptacles for the return of clean and dry plastic or polymer bags for the purpose of recycling or proper disposal in accordance with law; and all manufacturers, producers, or importers of single-use plastic or polymer items shall, prior to introducing such items into commerce within any State, Territory, or the Federal District or Capitol, register with the appropriate Environmental Protection Agency or regulatory authority of the relevant jurisdiction and shall remit an initial registration fee and a recurring annual renewal fee in such amounts as shall be determined by the legislature of the State and/or by Congress, which may also prescribe reporting, auditing, and compliance requirements. Congress and each State shall have concurrent power to enforce, implement, and give full effect to this provision through appropriate legislation, regulation, inspection, and penalties, including civil and criminal enforcement mechanisms as may be necessary and proper.

Individuals at all times retain the right to ‘ecologically conscious’ and ‘non-external impact’ Mining of one’s own property, and a privilege to prospect and stake mining claims on tracts of public land designated for the purpose of Public prospecting, and to homestead such claims into lawful land title property possession for private persons who produce over consecutive runs/seasons upon the same plot.

The lands, waters, air, and native species of Pacifica possess inherent legal rights to exist, regenerate, and evolve naturally. The People, acting through appropriate means, may defend these rights in any court of law as guardians of the biome, ensuring that no corporate, private, or public actor may degrade them in violation of these rights.

Individuals, animals, and the environment [including but not limited to wildlife such as plants and fungi and microbiome] have the right to clean natural water sources free from pollution from activities produced by humankind. This also requires that industry and personal private activities do not pollute tributaries, the ocean, or water tables, rainwater, and other natural sources of dihydrogen monoxide.

Congress shall within the scope of their enumerated powers to regulate Commerce, and each State in general, possess the power and authority to regulate the collection, transit and Individuals transporting, management and processing facilities, as well as import and export of re-cycling and waste, particularly those objects which qualify as poisonous, toxic, or hazardous materials. Congress and each State shall set forth such rules and regulations as are to be enforced through the Environmental Protection Agency of each State. Congress and each State shall have concurrent power to enforce this provision by appropriate legislation.

Organisms created through genetic engineering, including but not limited to cisgenics, intragenics, transgenics, synthgenics, or any other form of artificial gene modification or synthetic gene creation, shall be subject to mandatory quarantine under regulations established by Congress; such quarantine shall be maintained by the entity responsible for the organism’s development. No such genetically engineered organism may be released into the natural environment, including any ecological system of Earth or beyond, unless authorized pursuant to Congressional regulation. As a condition of such authorization, the organism must demonstrate complete reproductive isolation (speciation) from its originating or base organism(s), as well as from other species, such that it is incapable of engaging in sexual reproduction with its originating or base organism(s), incapable of interfering with or facilitating pollination or fertilization involving its originating or base organism(s), and incapable of disrupting or participating in the sexual reproduction of other organisms.

All Smart City projects must undergo regular independent environmental and social impact reviews conducted by Citizen tribunals with the power to halt operations if proven to degrade the health, privacy, or local ecology of the region or neighboring non-smart communities.

SECTION. 1.5.

Mistreatment of animals is prohibited. The state and its citizens must guarantee the protection, proper treatment, conservation, and care of all animals, as specified by law, being a fundamental constitutional principle.

The federal government shall have the authority and duty to enact and enforce comprehensive animal welfare laws, ensuring consistent protection for all animals, including companion animals, farmed animals, wildlife, and laboratory animals.

The government shall regularly review and update animal welfare standards in light of scientific and ethical advancements, with the aim of continual improvement in the treatment and status of animals.

Animal welfare standards and protections must be regularly reviewed and updated in light of new scientific knowledge and ethical considerations, with the goal of continual improvement.

Animal welfare legislation must recognize and accommodate the natural behaviors, needs, and characteristics of each species, including the right to express natural behaviors and live free from unnecessary confinement or suffering.

The law shall provide mechanisms for the protection of animals’ interests, including legal standing for advocates to challenge cruelty, neglect, or violations of animal welfare laws in court.

Protections shall extend to all animals, including but not limited to companion animals, farmed animals, wildlife, and laboratory/research animals, and animals used in entertainment regardless of their use or status, Special consideration shall be given to the natural behaviors and needs of each species.

Animals have the right to express their natural behaviors. Laws and regulations must ensure that animals are provided with sufficient space, enrichment, and opportunities to move freely, socialize, and engage in species-typical activities.

The breeding, use, and slaughter of animals for human purposes, as well as the use of wildlife in entertainment or profit-making shows, shall be regulated to prevent cruelty and ensure welfare standards that respect animals’ nature and dignity. The government shall actively promote and subsidize natural alternatives to the use of animals in research, food production, and entertainment, wherever possible, to reduce suffering and instrumentalization.

The state shall ensure the conservation of wild animal populations and habitats, and shall take measures to prevent illegal trade, trafficking, and exploitation of wildlife.

Wildlife shall possess an inherent and constitutionally protected right to be free from harassment, molestation, undue disturbance, reckless pursuit, unlawful capture, torment, and habitat disruption, and this right shall be construed liberally to preserve ecological integrity and peaceful existence; provided, however, that nothing in this provision shall be construed to prohibit the lawful and regulated taking of wildlife by humans for self-sufficiency, sustenance, customary or ritualistic use, or commerce, where such taking is authorized by law, conducted by humane and least-intrusive means, and subject to such limitations as are necessary to preserve public safety, conservation, and the continued existence of wildlife populations

Measures to control animal populations or address public health risks must be humane, scientifically justified, and minimize suffering.

The breeding, use, and slaughter of animals for food, research, product testing, or entertainment shall be regulated to prevent cruelty and to ensure welfare standards that respect the dignity and intrinsic value of animals.

The use of animals in scientific research or experimentation is lawful in Pacifica only under the following conditions:
A) The research is rational, necessary, and has a scientifically sound basis as determined by an independent review panel of qualified ethicists, scientists, and citizen observers;
b) The anticipated benefit of the research is substantially likely to produce new, useful, and verifiable knowledge relevant to human or animal health, ecological understanding, or safety;
c) The research cannot be effectively conducted using alternative non-sentient methods, including simulations, cell cultures, organoids, or artificial intelligence models.

All animal testing must conform to Minimal Harm Principles:
a) Pain, fear, or distress must be minimized using anesthesia, sedation, '[]enrichment[]', or alternative housing and handling.
b) Tests that produce suffering without clear predictive or translational value are considered unconstitutional.
c) Repetitive or duplicative tests which do not add substantial knowledge or resolve prior ambiguity shall be banned.
d) Psychological torment, deliberate starvation, mutilation, and extreme isolation are strictly prohibited.

Non-human animals shall only be entitled to those natural rights which they are capable of respecting/reciprocating, to which they may demand such mutual respect/reciprocation of them in others, including People, and they shall equally retain the right to defend their natural rights as is likewise the case in legal “Persons”; They may communicate the desire for enfranchisement in whatever form they determine to be sufficient, and upon questioning of their motivation to be recognized in the courts, they shall be either granted or denied recognition, based upon testing them to verify whether their decision to request such legal recognition was reached autonomously, or otherwise, without compulsion or coercion, or other form of direct manipulation. At all times they shall be reserved the right to not suffer any inhumane treatment, including but not limited to not have any excessive, torturous, nor cruel, degrading/demoralizing/dehumanizing, or unusual treatments or punishments be inflicted.

All sentient non-human animals possess the fundamental right to live free from unnecessary suffering, torment, or abuse. The Government of Pacifica, its institutions, and private entities operating within Pacifica shall be bound to treat animals in a humane, ethical, and compassionate manner, particularly in circumstances of captivity, research, or medical experimentation. Cruel practices, including those that cause unnecessary pain, suffering, or distress to animals, are strictly forbidden. This includes inhumane confinement, neglect, and exploitative shows or spectacles.

Research on any endangered or threatened species, or those recognized as highly intelligent, socially complex, or self-aware, such as, not limited to, Primates, Cetaceans (e.g., dolphins, whales), Elephants, Corvids and Cephalopods, shall be disallowed unless there exists a clear and present medical or ecological justification, and an inability to achieve results through lower-sentience species or non-animal models.

Animals used in research must:
1) Be housed in enriched and species-appropriate environments
2) Be provided adequate food, water, comfort, and social contact when possible
3) Be euthanized humanely and only when scientifically necessary
4) Be retired to sanctuaries or rehomed when continued use is not justified and life remains viable

The state shall actively protect wildlife populations and their habitats, combat illegal trade, and ensure the survival and well-being of native species.

Humane education, including respect for animal welfare and the intrinsic value of nonhuman life, emphasizing respect, empathy, and responsibility toward animals, shall be a mandatory component of educational curricula at all levels

The government shall promote and support alternatives to the use of animals in research, food production, and entertainment, prioritizing the reduction of animal suffering wherever possible.

The use of pesticides, herbicides, and other agrochemicals shall be strictly regulated and minimized to prevent harm to beneficial and essential insect populations, including bees, dragonflies, and other pollinators. Integrated pest management and organic alternatives shall be prioritized, and the precautionary principle applied where scientific uncertainty exists regarding harm to insects.

The government shall fund and promote research into the effects of cellular signals, electromagnetic radiation, and high-voltage discharges on insect and other animal navigation and health. Where evidence of harm exists, mitigation measures and restrictions on such emissions in critical insect habitats shall be enacted to protect vulnerable species.

Strict safeguards shall be imposed to prevent oil, hydraulic fluid, and chemical spills on roads, wetlands, and other habitats essential for insect breeding and nesting, especially for species such as dragonflies. Immediate containment and ecological restoration are mandated in the event of contamination, with priority given to restoring native vegetation and hydrology.

Critical habitats for at-risk and beneficial insects-including wetlands, wildflower meadows, and nesting areas-shall be identified, protected, and restored. Livestock and vehicular traffic shall be excluded from sensitive habitats, and invasive species shall be controlled to support native insect populations.

All beneficial and ecologically essential insects, including but not limited to bees, dragonflies, butterflies, and beetles, shall be eligible for legal protection as endangered or threatened species, as appropriate. The government shall establish and enforce recovery plans for at-risk insect populations, modeled after successful conservation agreements for certain species.

The government shall conduct regular monitoring of animal populations, including insects, and the impacts of chemical, electromagnetic, and environmental threats. Data and findings shall be made publicly available to inform conservation actions and policy decisions.

Public education campaigns shall promote awareness of the importance of insects to ecosystems and agriculture, and encourage citizen participation in pollinator-friendly practices, habitat restoration, and reporting of threats or declines.

The government shall support scientific research and technological innovation aimed at reducing threats to insects and other lifeforms, improving habitat restoration, and developing alternatives to harmful agricultural and industrial practices.

Section. 2.

The right of Persons, and all other entities of due consideration, to cultivate their own food, medicine, structural materials, and all other needful items/resources, is an essential human-or-otherwise right.

Farmers’/Ranchers’ rights include but are not limited to: Enabling Farmers/Ranchers to seek, maintain, and develop crop and livestock genetic resources as they have done since the dawn of agriculture and animal rearing; Enabling Farmers/Ranchers to continue being custodians of plant and animal genetic resources, and their rights to save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed/propagating ranch saved non-human-animal-eggs/genetic material; It also includes the right to self-sufficient farming/ranching practices; Farmers and/or Ranchers retain the right to defend their crops and other productive outputs of their plantation, including but not limited to magic mushrooms and cannabis, or any other form of non-human or otherwise non-sapient life, such as but not only fish, frogs, snakes, alligators, chickens, geese, rabbits, pigs, sheep, goats, bovines, buffalo, elk, and moose; These rights apply to both Personal and Commercial/Market Farmers/Ranchers.

Food sovereignty rights include, but are not limited to: The rights of peoples, communities and countries to define their own agricultural labour, fishing, food, and land policies which are ecologically, socially, economically and culturally appropriate to their unique circumstances; [The] true right to food and to produce food, which means that all people have the right to fair access of safe, nutritious, and culturally appropriate food, and to food producing resources, as well as the ability to sustain themselves along with their societies; This right also entails the freedom to prepare and use your own food as you see fit, and with permission, that of others; It is not the right to be fed whatever you want, however, it is right to use any lawfully acquired foodstuffs in accordance with one's own will, which also includes respect in exercise to serve as a cook for others.

[]
The People of Pacifica possess inherent, unalienable, absolute, self-regulating natural rights to food sovereignty and self-preservation rooted in the fundamental interest of Justice, and these rights necessarily include the freedom to hunt, fish, and trap animals for food and fiber and for pest reduction or management (which is ecological pest stewardship defined as the lawful removal or control of animals that threaten crops, livestock, stored food, public health, or safety, conducted in a manner consistent with humane standards and the laws made in accordance with this constitution, and as relevant, the constitution of the State where one resides as well), and to raise, harbor, and humanely slaughter livestock and poultry, including the performance of customary animal husbandry practices essential to herd health and welfare, the operation of commercial poultry enterprises and smallholdings, the conduct of rodeos and related culturalagrarian events (which are cultural sustenance performances and are defined as public demonstrations of husbandry skill and animal handling that reinforce community food systems), and the ethical use of animals in certain biomedical and agricultural research when such use is necessary to secure public health and food security, and these liberties are not granted by the State but are antecedent to it, arising from the natural condition of human survival in the ecological order wherein hunting and trapping are indispensable in the wild state and farming is indispensable in the technological state, and accordingly no Federal, State, local, or territorial law shall criminalize, unduly burden, or discriminatorily regulate these practices, for the people's right to life and self-preservation is the supreme determinant of lawful authority and economic sectors engaged in food production are protected only insofar as they serve individuals, who remain the primary bearers of these rights (the principle of individual primacy being that the economic instrumentality of agriculture is subordinate to the person's claim to sustenance and survival), and Congress alongside the several States shall have the affirmative duty to enforce this provision through due process according to the rules of law throughout Pacifica, including the issuance of protective injunctions against criminalization, the explicit recognition of: the right to hunt for subsistence and population management; the right to fish for subsistence and commercial harvest, the right to trap for food and fiber and for ecological pest stewardship; the right to raise livestock and poultry for food and fiber; the right to humanely slaughter animals for food; the right to perform customary animal husbandry practices including castration, dehorning, branding, and health treatments when necessary for animal welfare; the right to operate commercial poultry enterprises and smallholdings; the right to conduct rodeos and cultural sustenance performances;-and the right to engage in necessary animal research for public health and agricultural advancement. The recognition of food sovereignty is a justiciable cornerstone of self-preservation, and there must be established procedural safeguards that prevent the state from converting naturally lawful sustenance activities into crimes. The People further retain the power to self-regulate these practices through customary norms and community standards whenever such norms do not infringe upon the equal rights of others, thereby creating a self-regulating agroliberty regime (a term coined to denote a system in which the community's own husbandry and harvest norms coexist with constitutional due process to prevent arbitrary criminalization), and no interpretation of this provision shall elevate industry over the individual, nor permit the economic sector to claim immunity from reasonable safety and welfare laws that do not eliminate the core right to sustain life, and all lawful practices of hunting, fishing, trapping for food and fiber and for ecological pest stewardship, livestock slaughter, husbandry, commercial poultry operations, rodeos, and necessary animal research are hereby affirmed and declared immune from criminalization under the law of Pacifica, as expressions of the people's natural right to life, self-preservation, and food sovereignty, and this provision is not intended to criminalize the humane treatment of animals nor to prohibit reasonable care and welfare standards, but it likewise does not circumvent the interests of animals against abuse or cruelty, so that there must be reasonable treatment of the animals involved, meaning that all practices covered herein shall be conducted with humane restraint and without gratuitous suffering, and any regulation that enforces reasonable humane treatment shall remain valid so long as it does not eliminate the core right to sustain life and essential industry along with commerce through these practices.
[]

[]
No law, rule, regulation, subsidy, procurement program, licensing scheme, taxation device, or administrative condition shall interfere with the domestic production, processing, distribution, storage, marketing, sale, barter, exchange, or lawful private consumption of crops, livestock, animal products, seeds, breeding stock, feed, milk, honey, fungi, and all derivative goods produced within Pacifica, because the first duty of government relevant to food sovereignty rights is to protect the people’s own capacity to feed themselves rather than to manage them as dependents of external supply; nor shall any public authority favor imported, externally sourced, or foreign-controlled agricultural goods over internally or nationally sourced goods of the same class, because preferential treatment of outside supply weakens local resilience, transfers bargaining power away from the people, and creates avoidable dependence contrary to civil public stewardship and non-interference with the ordinary lives and productive labor of persons. The government may act only to secure the People against objectively demonstrable threats such as fraud, unsafe adulteration, concealment of origin, predatory monopoly, coercive market manipulation, or actual contamination, and any such action must be narrowly tailored, evidence-based, and proportionate to the least restrictive means compatible with public safety, because power in a free republic exists to protect rights, not to micromanage peaceful exchange or commandeer the food economy. Farmers, ranchers, growers, herders, fishers, and food producers shall retain the natural and civil liberty to save, use, exchange, and sell seeds, propagating material, offspring, breeding stock, and harvested output, to engage in self-directed husbandry and cultivation, to maintain customary practices of production, preservation, and distribution, and to dispose of their lawful products without forced surrender, compelled channeling, or discriminatory burden, because productive independence is the practical foundation of food security and property in the fruits of labor. Government shall be a steward and protector of the agricultural commons by preserving land access, water integrity, pollinator health, soil fertility, local processing capacity, transparent labeling, fair competition, open information, emergency resilience, and access to courts for redress, because food sovereignty fails when the people are denied the means of production even if formal legal rights remain on paper. No public procurement, public feeding program, emergency distribution system, or state-supported market arrangement shall exclude domestic agricultural products in favor of foreign alternatives where local goods are available on reasonable terms, because public funds and public institutions exist to strengthen the people’s own productive base, not to displace it. All protections historically used to defend domestic garlic, and by fair extension all food crops and animal products, against predatory import practices, false origin claims, and unfair dumping are hereby incorporated in general form as protections for all Pacifican food producers, except that all tariffs are forbidden, because Pacifica shall defend its food system by non-tariff measures, truthful labeling, enforceable quality standards, anti-fraud law, competition law, and the equal application of rules to all persons and enterprises rather than by taxing trade. Any governmental power exercised under this provision shall be justified by objectively reasonable standards, interpreted in favor of liberty, and limited to what is necessary to protect the natural rights, health, and productive freedom of the people, because in a republic the public thing is held in trust for the people and not as an instrument of control over them.
[]

No law shall infringe with the freedom of the People to be self-sufficient, and for them to grow, raise, prepare, and serve their own sources of food and resources, including but not limited to fungi, plants, and livestock, fuel, wood or artificial lumber, paper, fiber, rope, wicks, cloth and textiles, plastics, explosives, building supply or material, paint, sealant, lacquer, soap, lotion, ointment, medicine, and the great number of industrial and commercial products. Free exchange and trade of germa products including but not limited to [both viable and non-viable] spores, pollen, seeds, and non-sapien animal eggs between Persons within the Nation of [the] Pacifica [of Sovereign Persons], and those mutually consenting outside of it, is sacrosanct.

The Commonwealths of Pacifica affirm the fundamental importance of productive use of agricultural land, local community food sovereignty, and the stewardship of land as a commonwealth heritage entrusted for the public good. Each Commonwealth shall maintain a State Bank holding agricultural land parcels designated for lifetime productive use by qualified farmers. These parcels shall be granted to farmers as non-transferable, rent-free lifetime use rights contingent upon continuous productive use, including cultivation, ranching, agroforestry, or other sustainable food production practices. Farmers granted lifetime use rights shall not have the authority to sell, bequeath, or transfer these land parcels, and upon cessation of productive use or at the end of the farmer’s lifetime, the farmland shall revert to the State Bank holdings for reassignment consistent with these purposes. Productive use shall be defined as the active utilization of land for agricultural or ranching output sufficient to sustain the farmer’s livelihood and contribute to local food supply, in accordance with standards established by the Commonwealths, allowing temporary fallow periods within sustainable practices. The program seeks to increase agricultural and ranching productivity, promote resilient local food economies, foster community self-sufficiency, and preserve farmland as a heritage resource entrusted to the people of Pacifica. The governance, stewardship standards, productive-use requirements, and reallocation procedures of agricultural land held within the Commonwealths shall be administered under a democratic council of active farmers, elected by and from among those granted lifetime use rights, whose resolutions shall carry binding authority in establishing, revising, and enforcing policies governing farmland tenure and succession, and have sovereign autonomy except against the powers of the People local to each region of agriculture to ensure ecological preservation and equitable practices amoung the farmers, but not to micromanage crop or livestock allocations or to deprive such farmers of any outputs they create as property on such non-transferable lifetime usufructs. This constitutional provision is intended to empower individual farmers with free use of land under stewardship obligations, prohibiting speculative ownership, and supporting community food sovereignty through a commons-based heritage system complemented by sustainable practices.

The right to sell raw milk with informed consent shall be protected by law, but States may prescribe the necessity for which tuberculosis testing on raw milk products is provided before sale as information available on the label through lab certification of being free of disease. States may also prescribe the necessity for which explanation of the dangers of potential disease (such as tuberculosis) found from bovine dairy products that are raw or otherwise unprocessed.

In addition to the food sovereignty rights in farmers and customer consumers of their products surrounding raw dairy, the right to the sale of raw honey and other raw food and supplemental nutritional or bioactive natural ingredients shall not be infringed or otherwise circumvented, in accordance with the theory of informed consent.

Section. 3.5.

In recognition of the essential principle that every individual, regardless of their economic means or mode of payment, is entitled to equitable access to sustenance, it shall be enshrined within the constitutional framework of Pacifica as an immutable dictate that all food sales enterprises, encompassing but not limited to grocery establishments and convenience markets, are unequivocally prohibited from engaging in any form of discrimination or differential treatment with respect to the availability, pricing, quality, or provision of food products between patrons utilizing government-sponsored food assistance benefits, such as those facilitated via Electronic Benefit Transfer cards, and those transacting by alternative means; however, while such businesses must uphold this non-discriminatory mandate, they concurrently retain the autonomous prerogative to extend specialized discounts, produce and bulk credit programs, or ancillary services exclusively targeting customers who remit payment through established nutrition assistance programs, thereby fostering voluntary market-based incentives aligned with social equity objectives, and to support and amplify such progressive commercial practices, the government shall institute and maintain a legal mechanism for the disbursement of matching subsidies, capped at ten percent of the aggregate sales derived from benefits-receiving clientele, conditional upon authorization through legislative enactment and appropriate budgetary allocations, thereby harmonizing the imperatives of free enterprise, individual sovereignty, and collective welfare; moreover, this provision is adopted to reinforce the ethos of sovereign personhood integral to the Pacifican vision, ensuring that protections afforded to vulnerable populations are balanced methodically with the preservation of voluntary business discretion and economic freedom.

To uphold the dignity of all individuals, alleviate hunger, and promote responsible stewardship of food resources by preventing waste of edible food across Pacifica, all supermarkets and food warehouses must donate edible surplus food at any point in the supply chain to eligible charitable organizations or food pantries serving the hungry. The intentional destruction, discarding, or spoilage of edible surplus food by covered entities is prohibited. Violation of this provision is a civil infraction punishable by a fine equal to or above one times (1*) and not exceeding two times (2*) the fair market value of the food destroyed or wasted. The legislature of each State shall establish clear procedures for assessing market value, citation issuance, appeals, and options for corrective actions prioritizing remediation. No donation of food shall be construed as a transfer of ownership beyond what is necessary for charitable distribution. Donors acting in good faith, without gross negligence or intentional misconduct, shall be protected from civil or criminal liability arising from the donation of edible food that meets safety standards. The legislature of each State shall enact laws and procedures consistent with this provision that encourage voluntary compliance through education and partnership, imposing only proportional penalties to deter violations while safeguarding private enterprise autonomy. "Edible surplus food" means food fit for human consumption that would otherwise be discarded due to surplus, approaching expiration, or aesthetic reasons. "Eligible charitable organizations" means nonprofit entities exempt from registration as a business under applicable laws, engaged in distributing food to individuals in need. Fines collected from violations of this program shall be directed towards food security programs for Pacifican citizens in need.

The several States shall have the sovereign authority to regulate the types of food and nutritional products purchasable with governmental nutritional assistance and food benefit programs operating within their borders. States are authorized to prohibit the use of such benefits for the purchase of highly-processed or junk foods, including but not limited to soda, candy, and other foods characterized by excessive sugars or synthetic sweeteners, artificial ingredients or un-natural additives, or those lacking substantial nutritional value. States shall mandate that all governmental nutritional assistance and food benefits programs accept for purchase with such benefits: (a) raw ingredients not excluding baking soda/powder, vinegar, lemon or lime juice, extracts, spices, and natural flavorings; (b) ready-made/ready-to-eat and hot/heated food items; (c) nutraceuticals, defined as food-derived substances that offer health benefits beyond basic nutrition; (d) garden seeds and edible live plants, to promote self-sustenance, local food production, and individual food sovereignty; (e) 'space age' food items or meal replacements such as milk, protein, fiber, or collagen powders, electrolyte blends, powdered or instant tea and coffee, and freeze dried items; (f) long-term shelf-stable storable foods. The Federal government shall enforce this provision uniformly across the several States, ensuring respect for State regulations on nutritional assistance, while safeguarding individual liberty by preventing Federal overreach into States’ nutrition assistance policies. Nothing in this Provision shall be construed to restrict voluntary participation by recipients in food assistance programs, nor to limit personal choices outside the scope of government supported nutritional assistance benefits.

The Commonwealths of Pacifica recognize food sovereignty as the inherent right of all peoples to healthy, culturally appropriate, and sustainably produced food, placing food providers and local communities at the center of food and agricultural systems. Each Commonwealth shall establish market-based incentives, including vouchers for consumers and tax credits for businesses, to encourage innovation in food preservation technologies, support development of local micro-farms, and expand procurement of nutritious food from local producers. To further these goals, each Commonwealth shall empower its government to adopt tailored policies and programs that incentivize local agricultural production as well as promote resilient, community-controlled food economies while minimizing burdensome regulation. This Provision is intended to advance the Pacifican vision of a sovereign society built on voluntary, market-driven participation, and robust local food systems that enhance sustainability, economic opportunity, and community self-sufficiency.

Section. 4.

The right to acquire and hold property shall derive from the just and productive application of one’s labor to unowned or lawfully abandoned resources, and from the maintenance thereof in a state beneficial to life and the community. No person shall claim or retain exclusive dominion over land or resources that are left unused, neglected, or permitted to spoil, save where such state is incidental to a demonstrable purpose of improvement or preservation consistent with the public good. In keeping with the principle that there must remain “enough and as good” for others, property may be acquired or retained only to the extent that it does not deny to others the opportunity of similar lawful acquisition and use. Any person who, in good faith, peaceably, openly, and continuously occupies and productively employs abandoned, neglected, or unused land or premises, without substantial harm to the rights of others, shall hold a lawful right of productive occupation against summary eviction or punitive measure. An owner who neglects or abandons land or premises for a period as shall be fixed by law, without productive use or preservation consistent with this Provision, shall forfeit exclusive rights thereto in favor of the productive occupier. Disputes arising under this Provision shall be determined in a court of competent jurisdiction, which shall balance the labor-based claims of the occupier with the legitimate and active interests of the title holder, securing justice consistent with natural rights and civil order. This Provision shall be self-executing, and no law shall be enacted that unduly burdens the lawful exercise of the right of productive occupation herein guaranteed.

Section. 4.5.

Sub-Section. 1.

The People retain the right to Homestead on un-used Public Lands and un-claimed wildlands, which shall be secured and promoted by the Legislature of the Relevant Jurisdiction, and any portion of such lands which is put to good and continuous use over the course of put to use at least one-half of the year, each year, for seven years shall thereafter become their property fully clear in title and they shall retain the right forever more to dispose of such property as they see fit, within the limitations drawn by the common law right of squatting on thenseforth un-used/un-defended Property. In homesteading upon un-used Public Land and un-claimed wildland, a homesteader must not take so much property that there is not enough left over for others as well, only laying claim to that which they truly use for their own self-sufficiency and free enterprise.

Any Person may homestead, occupy, and responsibly develop unused or abandoned land held in trust or not under clear title, provided they do not infringe upon another’s legitimate claim or the rights of Nature. No law shall abridge the People’s right to establish free homesteads under equitable conditions.

Sub-Section. 2.

Any land owner who owns a parcel or number of them, or sub-divisions, that holds title to each piece of land, each one of which the size of such land parcel [on each individual title] greater than one-hundred-and-sixty acres, but for which whom has not made or who will make no improvements other than a fence and/or signage or other boundary and eminence marking/labeling, whether or not electrified, barbed, or razor-wired, with or without a gate, whether or not it is powered/motivated, and for whom has no productive use (such as useful grazing, hunting for survival/self-sufficiency and sales, timbering, farming, or mining) except to have it surveilled, or patrolled by security personnel or robotics, then, at the end of ten years, if they have still not either placed [true] improvements upon the land, or, used it to produce property by mixing their labor with the natural resources worth no less than ten silver dollars per annum in such ten year period, then the un-used portions of such land or all parcels which this applies to that were under their ownership become “De-claimed Wildlands”, and thus are a homestead-able part of the natural heritage and commonwealth of this State, and shall not be claimable for exclusionary rules [as may be directed in accordance to the constitution of this State and as limited by the federal pact, as public land may be justified rightfully by the government in pursuit fo a compelling government interest in protecting Persons, Property, Animals, and [the] Environment/Nature]; nor shall they be respected in title by the original owner, unless they homestead it. This law shall not obstruct otherwise lawfully squatting parties from staking an adverse possession claim after five years of continued residency on un-used land; This Provision shall not enable developed land (which is being actively put to use) to be de-claimed and homesteaded.

One may lawfully squat and issue a claim for un-used private property consisting of land that is not actively defended against occupation by trespassers by the Person or Company/Business possessing original title to the land; Areas not clearly marked “No Trespass/ing” with perimeter markers and/or barriers, are considered un-defended territory unless the owner uses it for their subsistence and private capital purposes, for then they must protect it from ingress and settling, or it shall be surrendered in title at the end of the term designated to form a homestead by squatting, according to the rules of adverse possession. In order to have a squatting title issued, one must have issued a notice of claim and subsequently squat on the land for no less than five years and performed upkeep to existing structures and/or formed a dwelling of their own, as well as mixed their labor with the available resources on the claim to perform labor and generate subsequent property valuated at ten  silver dollars per year.

[]
All rights in real property shall be understood as grounded in the principles of original appropriation, beneficial use, and the preservation of order, such that ownership carries not only dominion but a continuing obligation to employ land in a manner consistent with its reasonable, productive, or conservational use, and no claim of title shall be interpreted to extend moral or equitable force where land is held primarily for speculation, abandonment, or idleness beyond that which the owner can beneficially use without waste, consistent with the Lockean proviso that appropriation is justified only insofar as it leaves no injury through non-use or artificial scarcity; accordingly, in all disputes concerning trespass, adverse possession, or unauthorized occupation, the sufficiency of notice by the landholder shall be a central inquiry, and such notice shall be deemed legally “conspicuous” only where it is reasonably likely to come to the attention of an ordinary person approaching, entering, or occupying the land through customary or foreseeable means, which requirement shall be satisfied by the placement of clearly visible signs or paint blazes at intervals not exceeding thirty (30) meters along and at each corner of the property’s boundaries, as well as at all normal points of entry, access routes, gates, pathways, crossings of water boundaries, and any location where a reasonable person would expect entry to occur, including both sides of any natural or artificial boundary intersecting a public right of way;
