such signage shall be no smaller than twenty and one-half (20.5) centimeters in height and twenty-eight (28) centimeters in width, shall contain the words “Closed to Entry,” “No Trespassing,” or their substantial equivalent in lettering not less than two and one-half (2.5) centimeters in height, and shall include the name, business address, and telephone number, if any, of the landowner or authorized agent, and may alternatively or additionally consist of fluorescent orange paint markings of not less than three hundred twenty-two and one-half (322.5) square centimeters applied to posts, structures, or natural objects in conformity with the same spacing requirements, provided that all such markings are positioned so as to be readily observable from outside the boundary lines and at the point of approach; the placement of such notice shall bear directly upon its legal sufficiency, such that signs located in remote, interior, or unrelated portions of the land, or those not reasonably aligned with actual entry points or the site of occupation, shall constitute weaker or insufficient evidence of effective notice, whereas signs placed at principal entrances, immediately adjacent to occupied campsites or homesites, or at established access routes shall constitute strong evidence that a reasonable person would understand the prohibition as applying to the specific area in question; in cases of adverse possession or squatting, each discrete campsite, structure, or area of occupation shall be treated as a distinct locus requiring individualized notice, and any notice of removal or eviction shall specifically designate and be directed to each such site and, where practicable, to each identifiable occupant therein, whether named or described as John Doe, Jane Doe, or their meaningful equivalent, as aggregated by location, and personal service or direct communication of such notice shall be accorded greater evidentiary weight than posted signage alone, particularly where land boundaries are ambiguous, unenclosed, or not marked by fences, monuments, surveys, or readily identifiable natural features; where multiple access points exist, multiple corresponding notices shall be required, and all attractive features or improvements within thirty (30) meters of a public right of way or adjacent property boundary shall likewise be marked so as to prevent reasonable misunderstanding as to permissibility of entry; boundary ambiguity, while not extinguishing legal title, shall be considered in evaluating the reasonableness of the entrant’s belief, the adequacy of notice, and the intent necessary for adverse possession, and in all such determinations the law shall favor practical communication over mere technical compliance, recognizing that notice is not fulfilled by existence alone but by its capacity to inform a reasonable person at the time and place of entry or occupation, and that failures in clarity, placement, or directness may diminish the enforceability of exclusion where they create genuine uncertainty as to the scope or application of the owner’s claim.
[]

Sub-Section. 3.

Any person who is the head of a family, or who has arrived at the age of of majority or is an emancipated youth, and is one of the People retaining Jus Solis by right of birth within Pacifica, or who shall have filed their declaration of intention to become a Citizen as such, and has been granted Citizenship as required by the naturalization laws of Pacifica, and who has never borne arms [un-justly] against their State nor the Pacifican Government or given aid and comfort to their enemies [who are the enemies of the People], shall, from and after the first January, two thousand and twenty-que, be entitled to enter one quarter section or a less quantity of unappropriated public lands, upon which said person may have filed a pre-emption claim, or which may, at the time the application is made, be subject to pre-emption at ten-dollars, or less, per acre; or eighty acres or less of such unappropriated lands, at twenty-dollars per acre, to be located in a body, in conformity to the legal subdivisions of the public lands, and after the same shall have been surveyed: Provided, That any person owning and residing on land may, under the provisions of this Section, enter other land lying contiguous to his or her said land, which shall not, with the land so already owned and occupied, exceed in the aggregate one-hundred-and-sixty acres.

The homestead program will accept applicants for filing a homestead claim, after the applicant has been homesteading for no less than twenty-eight days but no more than three years; and the homesteader shall receive title in seven years from the application date for the claim after putting the claim to productive use, adding a dwelling, and making useful improvements upon the same. The program will accept single applicants as head of household, or shared titles of merged boundaries for multiple applicants in a collective with shared title between applicants and amendments to incorporate multiple stead titles into one mutual title.

Dwellings installed upon a stead may be semi-permanent or permanent installations, but they must be used at least half of the year, and actively house the occupant of the land each year for that period; They may be tents, trailers, recreational vehicle, car port, shed, or other shelter construction, but they must be structurally sound for the seven year period of time for which the stead must be operated to gain title, and must not be transferred in possessorship except by heritance or final-testament/will, without first being brought up to relevant construction code/s for any permanent structure on the land.

The person applying for the benefit of this and other sections within this Constitution, shall, upon application to the register of the land office in which he or she is about to make such entry, make affidavit before the said register or receiver that he or she is the head of a family, or is eighteen years or more of age, or shall have performed service in the State Reserves or Militia in actual time of Duty, and that he has never borne arms against the People’s Government of Pacifica or their State or given aid and comfort to its enemies, and that such application is made for his or her exclusive use and benefit, and that said entry is made for the purpose of actual settlement and cultivation, and not either directly or indirectly for the use or benefit of any other person or persons whomsoever, except for family and guests upon the same land; and upon filing the said affidavit with the register or receiver, and on payment of one-hundred dollars, he or she shall thereupon be permitted to claim and defend the quantity of land specified: Provided, however, That no certificate shall be given or patent issued therefor until the expiration of seven years from the date of such entry; and if, at the expiration of such time, or at any time within three years thereafter, the person making such entry; or, if he be dead, his widow; or in case of her death, his heirs or devisee; or in case of a widow making such entry, her heirs or devisee, in case of her death; shall. prove by two credible witnesses that he, she, or they have resided upon or cultivated the same for the term of five years immediately succeeding the time of filing the affidavit aforesaid, and shall make affidavit that no part of said land has been alienated, and that they have borne true allegiance to the Government of Pacifica; then, in such case, he, she, or they, if at that time a citizen of Pacifica, shall be entitled to a patent, as in other cases provided for by law: Being provided, further, That in case of the death of both father and mother, leaving an Infant child, or kids, under eighteen years of age or un-emancipated as a youth, the right and fee shall ensure to the benefit of said infant child or children; and the executor, administrator, or guardian may, at any time within two years after the death of the surviving parent, and in accordance with the laws of the State in which such children for the time being have their domicile, sell said land for the benefit of said infants, but for no other purpose; and the purchaser shall acquire the absolute title by the purchase, and be entitled to a patent from Pacifica, on payment of the office fees and sum of money herein specified. The register of the land office shall note all such applications on the tract books and plats of, his office, and keep a register of all such entries, and make return thereof to the General Land Office, together with the proof upon which they have been founded.

No lands acquired under the provisions of this Section shall in any event become liable to the satisfaction of any debt or debts contracted prior to the issuing of the patent therefore. If, at any time after the filing of the affidavit, as required in this act, and before the expiration of the five years aforesaid, it shall be proven, after due notice to the settler, to the satisfaction of the register of the land office, that the person having filed such affidavit shall have actually changed his or her residence, or abandoned the said land for more than six months at any time, then and in that event the land so entered shall revert to the government for other Individuals to Homestead upon.

No individual shall be permitted to acquire title to more than one quarter section under the provisions of this Section; and that the Commissioner of the General Land Office is hereby required to prepare and issue such rules and regulations, consistent with this act, as shall be necessary and proper to carry its provisions into effect; and that the registers and receivers of the land offices of the several Counties shall be entitled to receive the same compensation for any lands entered under the provisions of this Section that they are now entitled to receive when the same quantity of land is entered with money, one half to be paid by the person making the application at the time of so doing, and the other half on the issue of the certificate by the person to whom it may be issued; but this shall not be construed to enlarge the maximum of compensation now prescribed by law for any register or receiver: Provided, That nothing contained in this act shall be so construed as to impair or interfere in any manner whatever with existing preemption rights in conformity therewith: And provided, further, That all persons who may have filed their applications for a preemption right prior to the passage of this Section, shall be entitled to all privileges of this Section.

Sub-Section. 4.

The Bureau of Forest and Land Management shall open a division to deal with providing land for homesteading, and public resources for homesteaders to establish their own off-grid/self-sustenance living solutions. The Bureau of Land Management shall furnish for applicants, property to initiate their HomeSteading operation, with:
1) A Chainsaw and one extra chain as well as one chain sharpener with twenty-five gallons of fuel available on a gas station voucher/giftcard of choice as well as one chain oil and 2 bottles of motor oil mix for two-stroke GEET-Pantone-engine chainsaw as well as a sharpener for the chains;
2) An all-weather offroad-suitable tadpole trike or quad/four-wheeler vehicle implementing a GEET-Pantone 4-stroke or diesel internal-combustion-engine using the primary fuel of their choice, with a heavy-load-tolerant rugged off-road cargo trailer, with one set of tire patches and canister of sealant goop for each tire of both, a tire pump, as well as one-hundred gallons of fuel on a voucher/giftcard for fuel vendor of applicant’s choice for the vehicle;
3) 750watts of 18E-20E_volt solar panels (either crystalline or amorphous, or a combination thereof) with an MPPT/Smart charge controller with 15 customizable programmable modes that can handle up to 2.4kilowatt photovoltaic input and load at 12E-20E_voltDC, a buck boost selectable 120v@10(I)amp and 240Evolt@5(I)amp phase-locking 50Hz pure-sinewave grid-tie_capable power-inverter delivering 1.2kWatt/second, and an 8kilowatt-hour battery-supercpacitor hybrid delivery-system using 100ampre-per-second delivery 4.8kilowatt-hour 12Evolt lead-alum solid-state lead-alum-water liquid-crystal-battery and 14.8Evolt 3.2kilowatt-hour lithium-glass-battery bank with high-crank amp delivery in addition to a 15.6volt graphene+nano-cellulose supercaps for matching amp-delivery to jumpstart the provided vehicle;
4) A 4.3meter wide * 3meter deep * 2.2meter height wax-sealed hemp/canvas tent and [a] suitable GoreTex tarp/s with attachment bungee cables to fully cover the tent to shelter from rain;
5) A tactical-style military-grade survival shovel with pick and case;
6) A tactical woodcutting fireman’s timber-axe and a sharpening stone;
7) A tactical machete with saw and sheath in addition to a sharpening oil-stone with sharpening oil and diamond coarse-fine double-sided sharpening wet-stone;
8) A tactical Bowie or K-Bar styled knife with saw and fire starter ferrocerium rod in addition to sharpening rod as well as its encasing sheath with molle beltloop adapter;
9) A fishing pole, two test strengths of line as per applicant’s request in addition to tackle and bait suitable for twenty-eight days of self-sustenance fishing, or re-usable traps of equal utility and nearing in price within twelve-point-five percent;
10) And a long-gun or upper-converted pistol-carbine of the caliber specified by the applicant, which itself has built-in iron-sights, as well as a fifteen-to-twenty-five round magazine with a secondary backup magazine and a Molle-based belt-holster for the spare magazine, in addition to a shoulder-strap and telescoping and/or collapsing stowaway stock (upon preference of the recipient), a foregrip, a laser+light 14500 or AA Ni-MH powered laser-sight and tactical flashlight, long-range hunting scope, and ammunition suitable for 28days worth of peaceable self-defense and hunting activities for the Homesteader’s security and self-sufficiency.

Sub-Section. 5.

Nothing in this Section shall be so construed as to prevent any person who has availed him or herself of the benefits of the third Sub-Section of this Section, from paying the minimum price, or the price to which the same may have graduated, for the quantity of land so entered at any time before the expiration of the five years, and obtaining a patent therefore from the government, as in other cases provided by law, on making proof of settlement and cultivation as provided by existing laws granting preemption rights.

ARTICLE XVII

All debts contracted and Engagements entered into, before the Adoption of this Constitution, shall be as valid against Pacifica under this Constitution, as under the Provisional Government.

The validity of the public debt of Pacifica, government-invested-power, including debts incurred for payment of pensions and bounties for services in suppressing insurrection or unjust rebellion, shall not be denied. But neither Pacifica nor any State shall assume or pay any debt or obligation incurred in aid of insurrection or unjust rebellion against Pacifica, or any claim for the loss or emancipation of any slave; but all such debts, obligations and claims shall be held illegal and void.

No legislative act or provision thereof shall have the force of law unless the Constitutional authority for it is explicitly cited, verifiable by proving an unbroken chain of logical derivation.

No treaty, trade pact, or foreign agreement shall have legal force within Pacifica if it infringes upon the unalienable rights of the People, including but not limited to property rights, medical freedom, food sovereignty, or speech.

Any foreign law, supranational directive, or UN policy that contradicts Pacifican natural rights shall be treated as treasonous and void. A provision of a treaty or other international agreement not made in pursuance of this Constitution shall have no force or effect. All enforcement agents acting on behalf of such foreign decrees shall be stripped of their position of power within Pacifica  and prosecuted [as a traitor guilty of treason] to the fullest extent of the law..

A treaty or other international agreement shall have legislative effect within Pacifica as a law thereof only through legislation, except to the extent that the Senate shall provide affirmatively, in its resolution advising and consenting to a treaty, that the treaty shall have legislative effect.

An international agreement other than a treaty shall have legislative effect within Pacifica as a law thereof only through legislation valid in the absence of such an international agreement.

On the question of advising and consenting to the ratification of a treaty, the vote shall be determined by yeas and nays, and the names of the Persons voting for and against shall be entered in the Journal of the Senate.

This Constitution, and the Laws of Pacifica which shall be made in Pursuance thereof, but not rules, interpretations, advice/guidances, bulletins, circulars, or other administrative statement or action of any type or form, shall be the supreme Law of the Land throughout Pacifica, the several States, all territories, and any forts/installations under their Jurisdiction, as shall all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of Pacifica; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, and all other members of the public body, composing Pacifica and all forts/installations/bases erected under its authority, its Territories, and of each State or Locality thereof, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution; A standardized test of intelligence and a psychological evaluation shall be issued; but no [a]spiritual/[a]religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under Pacifica; They shall required, before taking office, to swear the following oath under penalty for treason: “I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will faithfully execute the Office [of Power] of Pacifica, Territory or State, and Locality, and will to the best of my Ability, support, defend, uphold, and enforce the Constitution of Pacifica”; and be sworn:
“
1) Not to enact or enforce any law or create or follow any order which infringes on, impacts, or otherwise impairs the sovereignty & rights of the People, including the expression of their sovereignty through the powers of the Union and the State Powers, according to the distribution of Jurisdictions as it is established through their respective constitutions, and the expression of their rights, including but not limited to: Arms, Liberty, Property, Speech, Peaceably Assemble, and to Petition the Government for a Timely and Effective Redress of Grievances.
2) Not to enter with force into any Jurisdiction, without the express consent and invitation of that Jurisdiction’s legislature and executive, revocable at any time by them or their People.
3) Not to invade or subjugate any Jurisdiction that asserts its sovereignty and declares the government to be in violation of the compact by which such jurisdiction entered into Union.
4) Not to detain any Pacifican citizen as an “unlawful enemy belligerent” or as a “combatant”, or subject them to trial by military tribunal.
5) Not to warrantlessly Search or Seize the Pacifican People, including house-to-house Searches or Seizures, or any form of inspection than under Due Process of law underneath this Constitution and any relevant Constitution within a separate Jurisdiction.
6) Not to blockade Pacifican cities, thus turning them into giant concentration camps, nor to force Pacifican Citizens into any form of detention camps under any pretext.
7) Not to assist or support the use of any foreign troops on Pacifican soil against the People of Pacifica to “keep the peace”, or to “maintain control/order” during any emergency, or under any other pretext. The use of foreign troops against the People is considered to be an invasion and an act of War against the People.
8) Not to pervert the spirit of the law and rather to act under original intent despite any subsequent court ruling, legislation, or executory edict.
“

All members of the military and law enforcement must wear their uniforms while actively on duty, including while out in a public place such as a city, town, or countryside, and any individual or group of individuals who defy this order shall be fined and imprisoned under this title, up to five thousand Pacifican dollars and sentenced up to five-years for felonious charges and five years probation, and not less than two-years without the chance of parole, with three-years probation.

All members of Government within Pacifica, including the states, and any territory or staff at any installation in any place or region under the Jurisdiction of Pacifica, including any fort, facility, or installation under Pacifica’s or any State’s or Territory's control, must be citizens of Pacifica.

Perjury shall consist of the violation of any oath or affirmation, including that made for public office, and Congress shall have authority to criminally punish it only when made in a forum of Pacifica, or by an officer or agent of Pacifica.

No provision of this Constitution, shall be construed to provide any State, State agency, or State officer with an immunity from liability for violating any provision of this Constitution.

It shall be punishable by life imprisonment without the chance of parole for any official at any level of government to violate the Constitution for any reason while within a position of government.

ARTICLE XVIII

These definitions and clarifications are written in logical order, not in order of importance, and in some cases were written directly towards a reader’s person. Understanding all of these definitions and clarifications is essential to understanding the intention of this Constitution.

In cases where a constitutional clause may appear to come into conflict with another one, the presumption shall be most lenient or most permissive in the case of the people and prescribe the least power or least restrictive capability for government to exercise or limit through law. Clauses may be interpreted additionally to each other in a way which limits government power and which removes limitations on the people, but not which cancels out the affect or intended effect of either clause [or any number of them].

This political system espouses the philosophy of national identity that: (1) Treats universal, non‑hierarchical natural or individual/personhood rights, especially to bodily integrity, self‑ownership, and freedom from initiated force, theft, fraud, or the credible threat thereof, as well as baseline protections for animals, other life, and the environment, as the foundational legitimacy criterion for all institutions;-And (2) demands root‑level transformation or replacement of any legal, political, or economic arrangement that systematically violates those rights, rather than mere reform or incremental adjustment. Ascending Sovereignty is Pacifica's founding principle: that all political power originates in, and is never surrendered by, the individual sovereign person, whose own body is their first territory, and whose justly held property extends that territory outward. Such a sovereign answers to no rule beyond the interjurisdictional law that governs the meeting of one sovereign's territory with another's, and the enumerous rights held in common by all. The same tests by which the nations of the Earth judge one another fit to be called states, a bounded domain, a self-directing will, and standing to treat with one's equals, belong, in first instance and truest form, to the person, so that no larger body may claim a sovereignty it did not first borrow from this origin. This is the ground John Locke surveyed in his Second Treatise of Civil Government: that persons exist, prior to any government, in a state of nature under natural law, already possessed of life, liberty, and estate, lacking only a common and impartial judge to make those rights secure against one another's error. Finding that want, and no defect in their original title, they consent, each for themselves, and never for another, to enter civil society, delivering up not their rights but only copying-over (not transferring) their private power to judge and punish, in exchange for a government whose entire business is to better guard what was theirs before it existed. So Pacifica holds that communities of such consenting persons govern themselves first, and only then, by their own continuing will, form social compacts to unite into wider bodies for the securing of rights and the doing of justice, so that legitimacy in law flows not from command but from just naturalism, from natural right and natural justice alike, owed in every dimension to every existence and being capable of bearing it. Power thus ascends radiatively and never descends or deminishes: from the individual, to their land beneath their feet and upon their own property or that entrusted to them, to the locality, to the county, to the bioregion, to the state, to the federal circuit, and at last to the federal government together with its district and territories, each level possessing only what the level beneath it knowingly sent upward, and possessing it always because of the individual, never despite them. This radiative ascent is bound at every step by the mutual non-aggression principle and the equal right of every other sovereign to the same liberty in their equally respected freedom of ambit, a limit that is not mere policy but the plain logical extension of human agency, which cannot rightly be made to answer for a compact it never struck. Pacifica is raised on this principle, rather than handed down [upon command {with demands}] from any armchair idealist, monarch, or capital house, because authority that is only ever lent can always be recalled, and a government built to hold nothing but what was placed in its trust cannot ever mistake itself for the source of the rights it exists only to guard: no government answerable to a free people may grow larger than the sovereignty it was built from.

Pacifica, the several States, and their lawfully constituted political subdivisions may prosecute offenses within their respective jurisdictions, subject to this Constitution, applicable treaties, due process of law, and the prohibition against double jeopardy; a person who knowingly and purposely aids, abets, counsels, commands, induces, procures, or willfully causes another to commit an offense shall be guilty and punishable as a principal for the underlying offense; two or more persons who knowingly and voluntarily agree to commit an offense, and who perform or cause an overt act in furtherance thereof when required by law, shall be guilty of conspiracy, which shall be graded according to the most serious offense contemplated, provided that sentencing may be reduced according to the defendant’s role, withdrawal, abandonment, incompleteness of the criminal design, absence of actual harm, or other mitigating circumstance; and a person who, knowing another has committed an offense, intentionally harbors, conceals, transports, finances, relieves, comforts, destroys or conceals evidence for, or otherwise assists that person for the purpose of hindering apprehension, prosecution, conviction, or punishment, shall be guilty as an accessory after the fact, punishable as a misdemeanor of equal or lesser grade where the original offense is a misdemeanor, and as a felony one degree lower than the original felony where the original offense is a felony, except that an accessory whose conduct materially enables continuing violence, escape, obstruction of justice, destruction of material evidence, or further serious crime may be punished at the same grade as the underlying offense; no person shall be convicted under this Provision upon proof of mere presence, kinship, association, knowledge, silence, or failure to report alone, but only upon proof beyond a reasonable doubt of the required knowledge, purpose, agreement, or intentional assistance; and every sentence imposed under this Provision shall be proportionate to the seriousness of the original offense and the defendant’s individual intent, role, participation, harm caused or threatened, coercion or duress, and efforts to prevent, withdraw from, or mitigate the offense.

“Rights” are the free exercise of a Person’s will balanced against the equal exercise of others’. A right is only such if, as with the rights to life, liberty, and property, a Person can rightfully use necessary and sufficient force to defend themself against interference with the free exercise of that right. Rights are NOT “Privileges” and are NOT justfully subject to license or licensing requirements. It is an entitlement to something, whether to concepts like justice and due process, or Autonomy/Independence of one’s self, and to ownership of property or some interest in ones natural powers, capacities, liberties, and guarantees, or to property, whether real or personal; These rights include various freedoms, protection against interference with enjoyment of life and property, civil rights enjoyed by citizens such as voting and access to the courts, natural rights accepted by civilized societies, human rights to protect people throughout the world from terror, torture, barbaric practices and deprivation of civil rights and profit from their labor, and such Pacifican constitutional guarantees as the right to freedoms of speech, press, religion, assembly and petition.
They (rights) are the collection of entitlements which a person may have and which are protected by the government and the courts, or under an agreement. It is that which is proper under the natural law, and is a universal system of morality and ethics. It is something which is due to a person by just claim, legal guarantee, or secular moral principle. A power, capacity, guarantee, or immunity secured to a person by law. It is a legally enforceable claim that another will or not do a given act; it is a recognized and protected interest for which the violation of such is wrong, and causes an injury to the Person, whether or not it damages their physical integrity.
It is the interest, claim, or ownership that one has in tangible or intangible property.
The term "right" denotes the liberty [protected by law] of doing or abstaining from doing an act or the power [enforced by law] of compelling a specific person to do or abstain from doing a particular thing. It is that liberty the infringement of which entitles the possessor to a legal remedy or that power to compel compliance with the assistance of the state. Rights may be classified as primary and secondary: Primary rights are those that are created without reference to rights already existing. In this class will be the right of every person of the community to life, health and liberty of action; also the rights of ownership, of contract, marriage, et cetera; Secondary rights are created or arise only for the purpose of protecting or enforcing primary rights; Thus the right of a creditor through the courts to obtain judgment and levy execution against the debtor is a secondary right. So is the right to prevent an invasion of a primary right by means of an injunction obtained from the court.
Rights may also be classified as being either in rem or in personam. A right in rem is such a right that is good against the whole world, such as a right that the owner of property enjoys to exclude all others from the same. A right in personam is one that can be enforced only against a particular person on whom there is a corresponding duty or liability. The right of a creditor to payment is thus enforceable only against the debtor and is a right in personam. Rights are also either legal or equitable. A legal right is such a right as was recognized at common law and was enforceable through common law courts. An equitable right was one recognized by courts of chancery and enforceable only in the Chancery Courts.
In the most abstract sense, justice, equity. The word also denoted, among other things, property, interest, power, prerogative, immunity, and privilege, and in law is most frequently applied to property in its restricted sense. As an enforceable legal right, it means that which one has a legal right to do. That which a person, having it, is entitled to keep and enjoy, and to be protected by law in its enjoyment; as the right of personal liberty, and other rights of persons. That which one person ought to have or receive from another, it being withheld from him, or not in his possession. In this sense, right has the force of claim, and is properly expressed by the Latin jus.
Rights may be better understood through the following:
(1) Rights are perfect and imperfect. When the things which we have a right to possess, or the actions we have a right to do, are or may be fixed and determinate, the right is a perfect one; but when the thing or the actions are vague and indeterminate, the right is an imperfect one. If a man demand his property which is withheld from him, the right that supports his demand is a perfect one, because the thing demanded is or may be fixed and determinate; but if a poor man ask relief from those from whom he has reason to expect it, the right which supports his position is an imperfect one, because the relief which he expects is a vague, indeterminate thing.
(2) Rights are also absolute and qualified. A man has an absolute right to recover property which belongs to him. An agent has a qualified right to recover such property when it has been entrusted to his care, and which has been unlawfully taken out of his possession.
(3) Rights might, with propriety, be also divided into natural and civil rights; but as all the rights which man has received from nature have been modified and acquired anew from the civil law, it is more proper, when considering their object, to divide them into political and civil rights. Political rights consist in the power to participate, directly or indirectly, in the establishment or management of government. These political rights are fixed by the constitution. Every citizen has the right of voting for public officers, and of being elected. These are the political rights which the humblest citizen possesses. Civil rights are those which have no relation to the establishment, support, or management of the government. These consist in the power of acquiring and enjoying property, of exercising the paternal and marital powers, and the like. It will be observed that every one, unless deprived of them by a sentence of civil death, is in the enjoyment of his civil rights, which is not the case with political rights, for an alien, for example, has no political, although in the full enjoyment of his civil, rights.
(4) Civil rights are divided into absolute and relative. The absolute rights of mankind may be reduced to three principal or primary articles: The right of personal security, which consists in a person’s legal and uninterrupted enjoyment of his life, his limbs, his body, his health, and his reputation; the right of personal liberty, which consists in the power of locomotion, of changing situation, or removing one’s person to whatsoever place one’s inclination may direct, without any restraint unless by due course of law; the right of property, which consists in the free use, enjoyment, and disposal of all his acquisitions, without any control or diminution save only by the laws of the land.
(5) The relative rights are public or private. The first are those which subsist between the people and the government; as, the right of protection on the part of the people, and the right of allegiance which is due by the people to the government; the second are the reciprocal rights of husband and wife, parent and kid, guardian and ward, and master and servant.
(6) Rights are also divided into legal and equitable. The former are those where the party has the legal title to a thing; and in that case his remedy for an infringement of it is by an action in a court of law. Although the person holding the legal title may have no actual interest, but hold only as trustee, the suit must be in his name, and not, in general, in that of the cestui que trust. The latter, or equitable rights, are those which may be enforced in a court of equity by the cestui que trust.
Rights are faculties of action, not permissions from the state. The government exists to protect rights, not grant them.
(7) All natural rights are absolute insofar as they are also self-regulating in their exercise by reason of natural law, nor shall they be infringed or otherwise reduced from their constitutionally enshrined status, but shall be enforceable and defensible before all courts of Pacifica. People are not morally obliged to obey governments that violate natural rights. No exigency, majority will, emergency, or competing claim shall defeat their inherent force; infringement without strict constitutional justification denies personhood itself, rendering governance illegitimate; They self-regulate through mutual recognition in exercise among autonomous beings, securing voluntary cooperation. Limitations shall arise solely through this Constitution's enumerated powers (such as to taxation or regulation in accordance with constitutional principles) and procedural safeguards (due process, habeas corpus, trial by jury, equal protection, prohibition of ex post facto laws, general warrants, and bills of attainder) derived from natural law precepts of non-aggression and reciprocal liberty. No general welfare, public safety, or collective interest justifies reduction or suspension beyond these bounds, preserving the rights' indefeasible core against arbitrary action.

State schools, state healthcare, state welfare, armament and equipping programs, State-sector internet, and other freely provided governmental goods and services are not rights, they are Privileges established through the will of 'the People' (as in "We the People") in the instrument of the social contract.

Recognizing that liberty, to possess legitimacy in a constitutional order, must rest upon conditions that render it accessible to the generality of persons rather than a privileged minority, this Constitution affirms that property cannot exist as a purely abstract entitlement severed from the social and material foundations that make its exercise possible; for when productive assets are concentrated beyond a threshold that denies a substantial portion of citizens direct or participatory access to ownership, autonomy ceases to be a universal right and transforms into a contingent privilege, thereby contradicting the very premise of liberty upon which self-government depends. Empirical history demonstrates that excessive concentration of wealth produces dependency, rent-seeking, and institutional capture, all of which suppress personal initiative and civic freedom more effectively than overt coercion. Thus, distributive equilibrium is not an ethical ornament but a structural necessity to preserve a condition of non-domination among citizens; distributism, understood constitutionally, is the rational mechanism by which that equilibrium is maintained through the diffusion of productive property, through cooperative ownership, small enterprise, and local capital sovereignty, constituting the only empirically verified mode of economic organization compatible with enduring political liberty, as it prevents the economic monopolization that inevitably precedes political servitude. Consequently, this Constitution shall enshrine distributive decentralization as a principle inseparable from the meaning of freedom itself, establishing that the just circulation of ownership is not a limitation upon liberty but its most concrete manifestation, ensuring that neither the state nor private oligarchy or plutocracy may transform the autonomy of citizens into dependence masked by the language of property.

“Maxim/s” are established principles or propositions, which are universally admitted, as being just and consonant with reason. Maxims in law are somewhat like axioms in geometry. They are principles and authorities, and part of the general customs or Common Law of the land; and are of the same strength as acts of parliament, when the judges have determined what is a maxim; which belongs to the judges and not the jury. Terms do Ley; Maxims of the law are held for law, and all other cases that may be applied to them shall be taken for granted. The application of a maxim to the case before the court, is generally the only difficulty. The true method of making their proper application is to ascertain how the maxim arose, and to consider whether the case to which it is applied is of the same character, or whether it is an exception to an apparently general rule. Alterations of any of the maxims of the Common Law are dangerous.

"Authority in law" means the lawful and legitimate capacity to speak, decide, advise, or act in matters of law by reason of actual competence, sound judgment, and juridical knowledge, such that the person or body’s conclusions may reasonably command respect or obedience. This authority may belong to public officials, private legal thinkers, self-educated persons with paralegal or greater capability, and other competent interpreters of law; however, formal office does not itself establish genuine legal authority, and official status alone does not prove legitimacy, correctness, or philosophical purity. Where title and competence diverge, true authority follows competence, legitimacy, and conformity to higher law rather than mere institutional designation. No constitution, statute, or office can be presumed authoritative merely because it is enacted or occupied; its authority is conditional upon genuine legitimacy, actual lawful competence, and consistency with natural right and the higher law of justice. Under this view, any claimed authority that rests only on coercive position, inherited office, or statutory form without real moral and juridical warrant is not true authority but illegitimate power.

“Just Naturalism” means a legal and philosophical doctrine holding that the only valid and legitimate laws are those which uphold, protect, and are consistent with natural rights and natural justice; the belief that true law derives its authority from universal principles inherent in nature and reason, rather than from arbitrary human enactments alone. Just naturalism constitutes the foundational juridical doctrine within this Constitution, prescribing that all laws, rights, and obligations shall derive exclusively from empirically verifiable principles of equity observable in natural orders of reciprocity, proportionality, and equilibrium among interdependent entities. It mandates that legislative authority remains confined to enactments which preserve the inherent balance of self-preservation capacities, ensuring no infringement upon the equal measure of autonomy accorded to each sovereign individual or collective unit. Violations thereof invoke remedial processes calibrated strictly to restoration of prior equilibrium, eschewing retribution beyond necessity for deterrence and recompense aligned with demonstrable harm. Adjudication under this doctrine interprets constitutional provisions through the lens of invariant natural equilibria, rejecting derivations from abstract ideals or transient majorities. Governance apparatuses emulate stable natural configurations, distributing authority proportionally to sustenance of individuals and communal viability against disruption. All enumerated rights, based upon life and health, liberty/freedom and autonomy/independence, self-security and self-defense, privacy, property, and pursuit of happiness, manifest as unalienable boundaries extrapolated from observable limits of organic interdependence, enforceable by courts as positive mandates binding upon the polity.

"Unassailable probable cause" requires law enforcement officers to possess a reasonable and objective belief, grounded in clear, articulable, and credible facts—not mere suspicion or uncorroborated information—that a specific crime has been, is being, or will be committed, or that evidence of such a crime exists at a particular location. This belief must be so well-supported by factual circumstances that a neutral and detached magistrate, presented with the same information, would be compelled to conclude that there is a fair probability of criminal activity or evidence. Unassailable probable cause demands that the facts and circumstances are sufficiently reliable, detailed, and corroborated to withstand rigorous judicial scrutiny, ensuring that any resulting detention, search, seizure, or arrest is both lawful and justifiable under this Constitution.

"Irrefraggable proof" shall mean evidence or demonstration so clear, convincing, and indisputable that it cannot be contradicted, refuted, or reasonably doubted by any opposing argument or evidence. This standard requires proof that is irrefutable, undeniable, incontestable, and unanswerable, such that a reasonable person would have no basis to challenge its validity, leaving no room for doubt or plausible alternative explanation.

"Malicious prosecution" constitutes the deliberate and unjustified initiation or perpetuation of civil or criminal legal proceedings by an individual or government actor against another person without a reasonable foundation of probable cause for the violation of rights or the Constitution, undertaken with malice—such malice encompassing any improper motive such as spite, personal vendetta, harassment, or an intent to cause harm beyond the legitimate enforcement of the law—wherein the proceedings ultimately conclude in favor of the accused party, thereby manifesting a wrongful abuse of judicial and prosecutorial processes that infringes upon the procedural rights and liberties guaranteed under the highest constitutional principles; this conduct entails knowingly or recklessly advancing unsubstantiated allegations or charges with the purpose of inflicting injury, damage to reputation, liberty, property, or financial standing, and is characterized by an objective lack of justifiable grounds coupled with a subjective intent to misuse legal mechanisms not as instruments of justice but as tools of oppression or coercion, thereby warranting robust civil remedies including compensatory and punitive damages and injunctive relief to vindicate the aggrieved party and uphold the integrity of the rule of law and due process protections in both criminal and civil judicial contexts.

“Due Process of Law” is a fundamental, constitutional guarantee that all legal proceedings will be fair and that one will be given notice of the proceedings and an opportunity to be heard before the government acts to take away one’s life, liberty, or property; it is also, a constitutional guarantee that a law shall not be unreasonable, arbitrary, or capricious; It is the regular administration of the law, according to which no citizen may be denied their legal rights and all laws must conform to fundamental, accepted legal principles.
All laws must be applied fairly and equally to all people.

“Public Notice” means any communication, declaration, or disclosure issued by a governmental body, public authority, or legally authorized entity of Pacifica, intended to inform persons who may be affected by a law, regulation, action, proceeding, or condition of public significance. To satisfy the requirements of Public Notice, such communication must be reasonably calculated, under the totality of circumstances, to reach the individuals or communities whose rights, duties, or interests may be directly or indirectly affected. This includes, but is not limited to, dissemination through widely accessible and non-discriminatory channels, such as physical postings in public spaces, digital publication on publicly accessible networks, and other customary means of communication appropriate to the context. Public Notice shall not be deemed sufficient where the method of dissemination is intentionally restrictive, technologically exclusionary without reasonable alternative, or otherwise designed in a manner that foreseeably prevents affected persons from obtaining actual or constructive knowledge. No person shall be bound by, penalized under, or deprived of any right, liberty, or property interest by reason of any governmental action for which adequate Public Notice, as defined herein, has not been provided in good faith. This definition shall be interpreted in favor of maximizing transparency, preserving due process, and protecting the inherent rights of all persons within Pacifica.

A "Good Samaritan" is any individual who is legally required to provide reasonable assistance to another person who is, or is reasonably believed to be, injured, ill, incapacitated, or in imminent danger, provided the assistance can be rendered without significant risk to the rescuer or others. This duty arises in emergency situations where immediate intervention can prevent harm, serious injury, or death. The assistance must be voluntary beyond the imposed duty, conducted in good faith, without deliberate or grossly negligent misconduct, and with respect for the autonomy and consent of the person receiving aid where possible. Any Good Samaritan law that has binding effect upon the people must be consented to by the same and in no less majority than three-fifths of the People it shall be so binding upon.

Admiralty maritime law may only apply in the case of the sea, and at no point shall be used upon others on the land.

The People of Pacifica are not united on the principle of unlimited submission to their Government, reserving, each to themself the residuary mass of right to their own self-governance; whensoever the Government assumes undelegated power, its acts are unauthoritative, void, null, and of no force; in all other cases, where having no common judge, each party has an equal right to judge for itself, as well as of infractions against the modes and measures of redress. Any act for which assumes powers not delegated by the Constitution, is not law, but is altogether null, void, and of no force. The words meant by this instrument to be subsidiary only to the execution of limited powers, ought not be so construed as themselves to give unlimited powers. Every State has a natural power in cases not within this compact, to nullify of their own authority all assumptions of power by others within their limits; So too the same may the People of each State nullify usurpations by their Jurial modes of review and process in ruling that an act, law, ruling, or agreement/compact was never valid. Successive acts of usurpations and despotisms, there as such constituting a tyranny, unless arrested at the threshold, will necessarily drive the People into revolution and blood; These popular uprisings will furnish new calumnies against governance of all flavours, either public, or private in character, and new pretexts for anarchy, not being secured by an instrument against a power-vacuum coalescing and breeding a tyranny rather than a liberty in the perfect state of freedom ruled by none than nature. It would be a dangerous delusion where we as a People were to gain a confidence in the Persons of our choice, that they might silence our fears for the safety and security of our rights. Free government is founded in jealousy, and not in confidence; it is jealousy and not confidence which prescribes limited constitutions, to bind down those whom we are obliged to trust with power. Let Just Naturalism, Civil Libertarianism, and Good will toward men, be a central anchor in our republic. In questions of power [however], then, let no more be heard of confidence in mankind, but bind them down from mischief by the chains of the constitution.

A “Natural Right” is anything a person may do without harming or requiring/obligating that of another person. All natural rights are sacrosanct. All natural rights are ‘negative’ rights, which means to say that they do not demand a limited resource from another Person, as well as to being unrestrained to freely do something or obtain something how they choose without any interference from outside forces but neither interfering with another person’s or a group of people’s equal right/s to the same, which rights exist within the state of nature, before humankind created societies, where they may then thereafter also benefit in ‘positive’ rights, where they are furnished with a limited resource or certain benefit, such as an attorney or Public lawyer if they are indigent, or equal access to welfare services for food, shelter, and utility assistance, under the ‘social contract’ a civil government is erected underneath. If the government is to become corrupt to the ends of preserving liberty and justice, and chooses not to protect a right or set of rights, or actively chooses to violate them, it does not signify that the People lack the right. The exercise of natural rights, and any of the liberties stemming from them, are in all cases considered just. All Natural rights are inherent and unalienable rights, and as such, are inbuilt at the most basic level/s entailed to the essential being of the entity for which they apply, in addition to being non-negotiable, non-transferable, non-removable, un-assailable, and inviolable. They are all fundamental and essential for whatever order is affected, being the environment and nature, animals, or Persons; Universally endowed, these rights cannot be justly negotiated to compromise, transferred, muted, waived, suspended, infringed, compromised, or otherwise assailed, for any reason whatsoever (except for punishment of a natural crime, within the confines of this Constitution’s principles). Rights never die, they may only be disrespected by others, whether justifiably or not.

“Rights”, as provided under this Constitution, may not be waived by the person whom they apply to, such as a defendant, nor by their by legal representatives, such as lawyers or attorneys, or advisory/co-operative council, when representing oneself in properia persona.

The law shall not defend or enforce morals except so far as the objective existence of rights and their protection, including but not limited to the right to natural Justice.

Equal protection of the laws also entails equal liability under the law, and none shall be immune from criminal or civil prosecution or suit for violating another’s or others rights/immunities, privileges, or guarantees, as provided for through this Constitution.

The Basic needs of the People shall be secured and/or promoted for fulfillment to the highest degree humanly possible, by the Governments of both the Federal and State level, such as, but not limited to: Environment, Fresh/Clean Air to Breathe, Good Food worth thanksgiving, Water, Shelter, Clothing, Rest, and Good Sleep. Safety and Security; Health, Employment, Property, Family, and Social Ability. Psychological; Belongingness, Love, and Breeding; Friend/s, Family, Intimacy, Sense of Connection. Self-Esteem; Confidence, Prestige, Feeling of Achievement and Accomplishment, Sense of Self, Respect of Others, the Need to be a Unique Individual. Self-Fulfillment; Self-Actualization; Morality, Creativity and Creative Activities, Spontaneity, Acceptance, Experience Purpose, Meaning, and achieving one's own Inner Potential to the fullest.

All public resource disbursements from the general or directed budgets, which shall also include social welfare programs, shall be subject to accountability mechanisms determined by the relevant jurisdiction of either Congress for the Federal government, or the State legislatures for their independent State governments.

In recognition that government exists by the consent of the governed and derives its just authority from the natural Rights of the People and their pursuit of universal Justice, Pacifica hereby declares that all public power is held as a fiduciary trust for the service, protection, security, promotion, maintenance, preservation, and defense of the People and their rights, and never as a superior dominion for social engineering, coercion, managed scarcity, or the suppression of lawful independence. The several programs of public support, including but not limited to income maintenance, disability assistance, retirement support, housing stability, nutrition support, child and family support, work-transition aid, and emergency relief, shall be construed together as parts of a single civil order in pari materia, so that the whole of Pacifica’s welfare law may be administered as one coherent expression of justice, dignity, and self-command. The purpose of such programs shall be to secure the minimum conditions of life, shelter, nourishment, health, and safety, while preserving the liberty of each person to rise above necessity through labor, savings, family formation, mutual aid, and enterprise. The baseline measure of ordinary public support shall be tied to the arithmetic mean of ordinary household monetary receipts within Pacifica, and the standard monthly benefit shall ordinarily approximate one-eighth to one-fourth of that mean, subject to lawful adjustment as necessary to preserve real purchasing power and keep public aid aligned with the actual condition of the People. Benefits shall be reduced only through a humane and progressive tapering schedule, so that modest earnings do not trigger harsh loss, lawful work is rewarded rather than punished, and no person seeking to improve their condition shall be made worse off by accepting labor, temporary assistance, or lawful additional income. Ordinary one-time gifts, transient hospitality, emergency charity, donated meals, brief shelter, tips, and sporadic kindness shall not be treated as durable income for immediate benefit withdrawal, because generosity is not exploitation and aid that improves a person’s life should be understood as a step toward dignity rather than a reason to deepen hardship. The State shall recognize that stable households, whether formed through marriage, cohabitation, or other lawful and committed adult association, are not burdens to be discouraged but foundations of a healthy civil society, and therefore the benefit structure shall not punish lawful household forms merely because more than one consenting adult shares responsibility, labor, burdens, or child-rearing within the same home. Children shall be regarded as persons of independent moral worth whose needs are additive to, and not offsetting of, adult survival support, because a republic that values its future must protect the stability of the family unit without converting parenthood into a financial penalty. The State may therefore provide measured family supplements and continuity incentives for households that actually sustain caregiving, but it shall withdraw only those supplemental advantages tied specifically to the existence of a stable union when that union has in truth ended, since the public interest lies not in policing private intimacy but in encouraging durable and responsible households. Every recipient shall be permitted to accumulate a reasonable independence-building reserve for housing, transport, tools, education, emergency readiness, and small enterprise, because welfare exists to create the conditions for self-support and not to trap the poor in a condition of arrested motion. Fraud prevention and program integrity shall be accomplished through proportionate oversight, targeted documentation, and fair inquiry, not through presumption of guilt or intrusive suspicion, because liberty and accountability are both served when the honest are not treated as suspects and the dishonest are not shielded by chaos. This provision is adopted not as a socialist or communist command over private life and property, but as an expression of a socially-democratic republic grounded in progressive-libertarianism and distributist-limitarianism, wherein private ownership remains real, individual agency remains primary, markets and enterprise remain lawful, and the role of government is to preserve the conditions under which every sovereign person may stand, work, save, associate, raise a family, and pursue flourishing without being crushed by poverty or turned into an instrument of the collective.

The use of an Attorney neither makes one incompetent, nor a ward of the Court, but serves to Proxy one’s statements to the Court of Law, and avoid self-incrimination or the appearance of guilt thereof. The same also applies to Lawyers. And in either case, or both, alone or in a team, whether or not it is in full, on merely advisory terms, in either case of proxy or self-representation in propria persona.

Judges shall not previously be lawyers.

“Speech” and “press” shall include the production and distribution of any communication, private or commercial, other than calls to action whose outcome provides a clear and present danger to other [innocent] People, inducement to immediately commit a crime or act of war, or to give Aid and Comfort to a declared Enemy of War.

"Content‑neutral prohibition" means any rule or statute or decision that restricts expression/communication regardless of the subject, idea, or viewpoint expressed, including time, place, manner, modality, or medium‑based bans. It is a natural crime against speech.

“Spirituality”/”religion” shall be defined to mean “a devoted belief in meta-physics, God, or other super-natural principles, or a systematized version of any of these concepts”.

“Secular government” shall mean a government operating without having any basis in [a]spirituality/[a]religion. It shall not exclude the [a]spiritual/[a]religious from taking positions in government, but their [a]spiritual/[a]religious practice, and participation in such with others, shall be limited to their private capacity, meaning that they shall not base governmental policy, legislation, or decisions and actions, upon any [a]spiritual/[a]religious principle or practice.

For the purposes of this constitution, a "Model" shall mean a structured representation that captures essential aspects or patterns of something or a system, enabling understanding, prediction, or manipulation of that thing or structure/framework, across any relevant reality or context.

Pathologizing is the act of interpreting a person’s feelings, behavior, or reactions as signs of illness or disorder when they may instead be normal, understandable, or shaped by circumstances. The term is often used critically to describe the tendency to frame ordinary human variation as abnormal or clinically problematic.
[]
Symptomatization is the process of treating an experience, pattern, or complaint as a symptom of disease. In broader use, it refers to the conversion of distress, behavior, or life experience into a symptom-centered medical interpretation.
[]
Medicalization is the process by which human conditions, behaviors, or aspects of everyday life come to be defined and treated as medical problems. It is commonly used to describe the expansion of medicine into areas that were once understood in social, moral, cultural, or personal terms.
[]
Overdiagnosis is the identification of a condition or abnormality that would not have caused symptoms, harm, or death during a person’s lifetime. The term is often used in debates about screening and diagnosis to describe the detection of findings that lead to unnecessary labeling, treatment, or anxiety.

In general, a "Delusion" may be defined as an idiosyncrazy or fixed belief, held with strong conviction despite strong reasons [to be] against it or clear contrary evidence to the contrary, especially when the behavior or belief is not responsive to correction and is not adequately supported by reality-testing, including personal or group mannerisms or beliefs when they are maintained in the face of clear counterevidence and remain resistant to revision, regardless of whether it is shared by others or reinforced within a broader social or cultural context; In clinical use, a belief or eccentric peculiarity of character is usually considered delusional when it arises in the context of impaired judgment, perception, or cognition. As it relates to government (and groups of individuals in "Mass Formation Psychosis" {or MFP disorder} and critical-mass political conformity with [irreversible] power-transfer, presenting widespread irrational behaviour and groupthink or conformity/compliance with illigitimate authority and pressuring dissenters through coercion or isolation, particularly as it pertains to being non-skeptical of the justification of authority and [concentrated or otherwise] power, as well as [general] disregard towards negative individual outcomes from interference by 'the State'), in addition to the concept of stripping rights from the people and giving power to their abusers along with pressuring and punishing those who are non-conformal, for the purposes of this definition and clarification, connected phenomenon may be described as: A form of public authority fixation, characterized by persistent and uncritical belief in the inherent legitimacy, benevolence, or necessity of centralized power structures, even in the presence of clear evidence of overreach, contradiction, or harm, and additionally as well, to pressuring others into conformity or punishing them for dissent or civil disobedience; This condition presents with cognitive rigidity, deference to institutional narratives, a diminished capacity to independently evaluate the ethical validity of directives, particularly when such directives conflict with fundamental expectations of fairness, reciprocity, and individual autonomy, and finally, using coercive means to maintain obedience;  Affected individuals may exhibit reflexive justification and individual- or group-level enforcement of coercive policies, reinterpretation of rights as conditional privileges, and hostility toward dissent that is framed as destabilizing or illegitimate; Reinforcement mechanisms often include group identity alignment, repetitive exposure to sanctioned messaging, symbolic affiliation with political factions, and ratting or snitching on innocent people who do not obey the narrative and party-line, resulting in a self-sealing belief system resistant to falsification, and all of the collateral damage and fallout that ensues; The condition is further marked by the externalization of moral authority onto institutions, reducing personal responsibility for judgment and enabling the normalization of actions that would otherwise be recognized as unjust if performed at an individual level; Progression of this social disease is associated with increasing intolerance of scrutiny, elevation of compliance as a primary civic virtue, and the conflation of systemic preservation with moral good, while remission, if it occurs, typically requires re-engagement with independent reasoning, direct evaluation of outcomes, and restoration of the principle that legitimacy is contingent upon consistent adherence to impartial standards of natural rights and universal justice, rather than asserted or assented authority.
