A “Bill of Attainder” shall consist of any legislative disablement of an immunity, either for an individual, group, or the people in general, without irrefragable proof supplemented by irrefutable evidence, decided by a jury in each individual case, that he or she has committed a crime or is dangerously incompetent.

A “Title of Nobility” shall consist of any legislated or judicially conferred privilege or immunity, not enjoyed by all, or to the detriment of others, that is not absolutely essential for the performance of legitimate, peaceable, official duties, and a grand jury may authorize civil or criminal prosecution of an official for exceeding their jurisdiction or abusing their discretion.

The term “online platform” means a website, online or mobile application, operating system, digital assistant, or online service that-: enables a user to generate content that can be viewed by other users on the platform or to interact with other content on the platform; facilitates the offering, sale, purchase, payment, or shipping of products or services, including software applications, between and among consumers or businesses not controlled by the platform operator; or enables user searches or queries that access or display a large volume of information.

The term “control”, with respect to an instrument, testimony/will, or business means: holding twenty-five percent or more of the stock of the business; having the right to twenty-five percent or more of the profits of the business; having the right to 25 percent or more of the assets of the instrument, testimony/will, or business, in the event of the mentioned’s dissolution; if the business is a corporation, having the power to designate 25 percent or more of the directors of the person; if the instrument is a trust, having the power to designate 25-percent or more of the trustees; or otherwise exercises substantial control over the instrument, testimony/will, or business.

It is the policy of Pacifica as well as the several States and Territories to recognize two primary sexes and the biological abnormality of intersex or hermaphrodite has been protected, in their default form of either male, female, or some naturally occurring combination of both. These sexes are not changeable as grounded in their chromosomal and genetic reality, and are based upon a fundamental and incontrovertible fact, that which is also necessary for reproduction and family building. The Executive Branch will enforce all sex-protective laws to promote this reality. Recognizing Women (including of single-X and triple-X chromosomal disorders) are biologically distinct from Men and intersex or double-X+Y disorder individuals, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall provide to the Pacifican government, external partners, and the public clear guidance expanding on the sex-based definitions set forth in this order. Each agency and all Federal employees shall enforce laws governing sex-based rights, protections, opportunities, and accommodations to protect men and women as biologically distinct sexes. Each agency should therefore give the terms “sex”, “male”, “female”, "hermaphrodite", “men”, “women”, "Intersex", “boys”, “girls” and "zed", the meanings set forth in the definitions provided through this constitution in interpreting or applying statutes, regulations, or guidance and in all other official agency business, documents, and communications. When administering or enforcing sex-based distinctions, every agency and all Federal employees acting in an official capacity on behalf of their agency shall use the term “sex” interchangeably with “gender” in all applicable Federal policies and documents. The Secretaries of State and Homeland Security, and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, shall require that government-issued identification documents, including passports, visas, and Global Entry cards, accurately reflect the holder’s sex, as defined under this constitution; and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall ensure that applicable personnel records accurately report Federal employees’ sex, as defined by this constitution. Agencies shall not create nor circulate statements, policies, regulations, forms, communications, or other internal and external messages that promote or otherwise inculcate gender ideology, and shall cease issuing such statements, policies, regulations, forms, communications or other messages. Agency forms that require an individual’s sex shall list male, intersex/hermaphrodite (as "Zed"), or female, based on the biological reality of their chromosomes and sexual differentiation, and shall not request gender identity.

"Sex” shall refer to an individual’s immutable biological classification as either male, intersex/hermaphrodite, or female. “Sex” is not a synonym for and does not include the concept of “gender identity", and the use of the word "gender" assumes interchangeability with the word "sex".

[]
[]"Women” or “woman” and “girls” or “girl” shall mean adult and juvenile human females, respectively, or those with only single-X chromosomal disorder of normal two X-chromosomes or triple-X chromosomal disorder. “Men” or “man” and “boys” or “boy” shall mean adult and juvenile human males, respectively, or those with either an XY chromosome pair, or a double-X+Y chromosomal mutation. "Zed" or "Z" shall mean adult and juvenile hermaphrodite and intersex people, respectively, or those who have ambiguous genitalia [lasting after puberty].[]
[]

“Female” means a person belonging, at conception, to the sex that produces the large reproductive cell. “Male” means a person belonging, at conception, to the sex that produces the small reproductive cell. "Hermaphrodite" or "Intersex" means a person who demonstrates both pairs of sexual gonads or is sexually ambiguous at birth, and shall be designated as that along with their sexual chromosomes.

The term "State" means a State, the District of Olympus, and any other territory or possession of Pacifica or the several States.

Duly issued and legitimate "World Service Authority" and "Common Law Court" passports, as a part of visitation and immigration processes, shall be accepted as an official form of international identification.

Common Era (annotated in abbreviated form as "CE") shall be defined by this Constitution in all Laws and Statutes erected beneath them, to mean the Proper Modernization of the Prior Era "After Death" (I.e. "AD").

The government is permitted to run private advertisements on free_of_cost-level services that are not supported through direct payments by customers, such as to pay for [secure, private, and encrypted] email or social media services. They are not allowed to collect information/data about customers for the purposes of providing advertisements or tracking traffic direction, and they must show the same advertisements to everybody interacting with that service at the same time with the exception that they may be translated to other languages and formats based on a user’s language and accessibility settings.

“Organic” shall mean those foods, medicines, and internal or topical chemical compounds, which are not derived through genetic modification or synthetic biology, and which themselves are “organic chemicals” that are fully naturally derived and processed, and which are free from impurities and adulterants, and those foodstuffs which do not use un-natural bio-cides and nutrients nor synthetic or genetically engineered coatings in their production process.

"Junk food" as according to this constitution is defined as food that is high in calories or sugar, fat, and salt, but low in essential nutrients such as dietary fiber, vitamins and minerals, or myco-/phyto-/bacterio-chemicals or natural peptides beneficial to health long-term. Junk food is often highly processed or ultra-processed, providing "empty calories" that supply energy but little nutritional value to support health. Common examples include soda, candy, chips, sugary cereals, and many fast foods. These foods are linked to health risks like obesity, diabetes, and heart disease due to their poor nutrient density and high content of sugars, unhealthy fats, and sodium. Coconut oil, coconut cream, butter/ghee, cream, hemp seed oil, olive oil, beef tallow, lard, manteca, as well as other natural cooking oils are excluded from the definition of junk food even though they contain high fat, and Himalayan pink salt or sea salt is also excluded even though it is high in sodium, and molasses or cane sugar are also excluded even though they are high in fructose and glucose, since they are basic food ingredients.

All federal welfare shall be grounded in a living‑cost floor that reflects the mean-averaged cost of living in each region. This floor shall represent the minimum income necessary to afford a decent standard of basic necessities, including but not limited to housing, food, clothing, personal hygiene supplies, household supplies, utilities, transportation, childcare, education, healthcare, and digital connectivity, as well as essential personal maintenance and quality‑of‑life expenditures such as mental‑health therapy, counseling, physical‑wellness activities, and other comparable services that support individual dignity, autonomy, and participation in society, all adjusted to local economic conditions. Federal welfare eligibility and benefit levels shall be anchored to this floor, ensuring that no individual falls below the actual cost of living in their area and that no uniform national poverty line supersedes the economic realities of distinct regions.

Inspectors General, federal prosecutors, and civil servants shall not be removed without documented cause approved by a bipartisan commission. Political retaliation or obstruction of oversight shall constitute abuse of power.

ARTICLE XIX.

SECTION. 1.

The Powers of the Public Administration shall be derived solely from the provisions of this Constitution, or for the States, by their respective Constitutions, and neither the Public Administration, nor any Agent or Member thereof, shall possess any inherent authority; the Public Administration shall neither have nor exercise any power other than those expressly conferred upon it by this Constitution or in their State’s, in conjunction to what is set forth in this pact.

No/ne [of the] branch[es] of government shall/may outsource its/[their] functions to another branch or department nor other entity, neither to an institution or organization, nor other external party to the government, and it shall be limited strictly to it's delegated powers as well as the limits on those powers and their execution, in addition to abiding by the purposes and virtues for which civil government is established.

All powers delegated in this Constitution are constrained to be exercised only for a proper, or reasonable, rational, and legitimate, public purpose, as a fiduciary trust for the general benefit of all the People and not for the special benefit of any part of them, partially but not completely Stated in the Preamble. No power is plenary or without limits, and no power may be extended to accomplish a purpose without amendment. Relative to the People, no branch of Government has inherent or reserved Powers, implicit or assumed Prerogatives, or pre-supposed attributes of sovereignty. Powers must be expressly granted to the government by the People, and the extent and range of such Powers shall be strictly, and narrowly construed. As a Republican principle, the government established by this constitution is meant to remain limited and subsidiary, and only to alleviate ailments or injuries against the common public good of the people at large, including the most vulnerable, and to promote their General Well-being, but not to the detriment of the remainder [of the People]. The "state" (I.e., government, public instrument, the People's established institution, [synonyms] et cetera [ad nauseam] [non-absurdum]...) should not coercively impose its view of the good but should respect individuals’ and communities’ right to direct themselves, intervening only when necessary for justice and peace, and improving the condition of people's lives without detracting from their autonomy or other rights, except as narrowly consented in strong consensus for the common good of the People [including prioritization of the most vulnerable in order to ensure a baseline subsistence above destitution and alleviating desperation at large] (with the permanent reservation of revocation by the People of those very same reductions).

The Constitution of Pacifica shall be interpreted in good faith and literally (within strict constructionism), as far as it does not produce any absurd result, with due regard to the original intention behind its provisions in order to preserve the ‘spirit-of-the-law’; in case of doubt, consideration may be given to any Statements or Notes related to the text made before or at the time of its adoption.

On all constitutional issues, Precedents shall be regarded as only perhaps persuasive and never binding. Constitutional text shall be construed only on historical evidence of the meaning of the terms for, first, their ratifiers, and second, their framers. Equity and prudential decisions shall not be regarded as precedents.

To the extent that any provisions of this Constitution are inconsistent with the provisions of any other laws of Pacifica, the provisions of this Constitution shall prevail and shall be deemed to supersede the provisions of such laws.

The powers delegated by the Constitution to the government of Pacifica, shall be exercised as therein appropriated, so that the Legislative shall never exercise the powers vested in the Executive or Judicial; nor the Executive the powers vested in the Legislative or Judicial; nor the Judicial the powers vested in the Legislative or Executive.

The several levels of Government, in Pacifica or the several States, shall not contract a service with, nor issue a deal towards, a Private entity, in order to perform a task in with which such power is vested solely in such Government, nor may a Private entity be utilized by such Government to exercise any power which is, or would be, illegal to perform, or of which is otherwise prohibited to it, nor to receive any information or data which itself is not explicitly/expressly permitted by this Constitution for it to collect, view, or retain.

No essential power to secure or enforce the fundamental rights of the People shall be delegated to any foreign sovereign, supranational entity, private corporation, or artificial legal person. The safeguarding of natural rights shall remain solely vested in accountable public institutions directly answerable to the People.

No declaration of emergency, disaster, war, or public health threat shall suspend, nullify, or limit any unalienable right guaranteed by this Constitution.

It is at all times unlawful for the Pacifican National or State governments to at any time “operate outside of the constitution”. The government is prohibited from using any other party or other form of outsourcing to achieve violations of constitution limits of power or circumvention of any rights.

Any provision of this Constitution which delegates the power which relegates the need for spending or redistribution, shall not require a good or service rendered, nor any benefit distributed, nor any guarantee or irrevocable privilege for a positive right or provision/resource, until the available funding meets the Constitutional duty of provision. From the date of ratification of this constitution, up to the first twelve years (12 annum) , which may be extended by a vote of the people, any provision which requires the government to provide a benefit or resource shall be considered inoperative until the budget provides for sufficient funding in order to continue in perpetuity or as set aside by the budget agreed to in the last fiscal term for such purpose/s.

SECTION. 2.

Sovereign immunity of a State or the Nation shall not be a bar to suit, only to execution of judgment against assets not provided by an act of Congress or the state legislature for payment of claims.

People exercise sovereignty through the Powers of the Union and the State powers, according to the distribution of jurisdictions as it is established in this Constitution and the respective States’ Constitutions. The States’ Constitutions and legislation, by no means shall challenge the stipulations and premises of the Federal pact.

The National government may neither issue directives requiring the States to address particular problems; nor command the States’ officers, or those of their political subdivisions, to administer or enforce a National regulatory program.

SECTION. 3.

Powers not delegated Explicitly to Pacifica by the Constitution, nor Explicitly prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States, respectively, or to the people thereof [from whom which powers stem], to be by them exercised. Any time that the Federal government abdigates/abrogates its duties to the States and People of Pacifica, the power to fulfil those duties rests upon the States and the People of each State respectively. Relative to the people, no branch of government has inherent or reserved powers, implicit or assumed prerogatives, or presupposed attributes of sovereignty. Powers must be expressly granted to government by the People in explicit and unambiguous terms, and the extent and range of such powers shall be strictly and narrowly construed. All powers not expressly necessary for the protection of rights and justice shall remain with the individual, households, and community. Any centralization of authority without clear necessity constitutes usurpation and shall be void.

The exceptions [to power] here or elsewhere in the constitution made in favor of particular rights, shall not be so construed as to diminish the just importance of other rights retained by the people, or as to enlarge the powers delegated by the constitution; but either as actual limitations on such powers, or as inserted merely for greater caution.

So be it said: [that] this enumeration of rights and privileges, shall not be construed to impair, deny, or disparage others retained by the People, which rights are unalienable, and which privileges shall be equally provided for Citizens upon the same terms, throughout the several Territories and/or States of Pacifica. All of those other rights and privileges, which are not specifically mentioned, or otherwise alluded to, in this Constitution, are still reserved to the People in all cases. The existence of an Individual’s rights are not contingent upon governmental/”state” recognition of them.

So be it said as well: [that] the enumeration in this Constitution of certain rights of Animals/Robots shall not be construed to impair, deny, or disparage others retained by them, which rights are unalienable. All of those other rights which are not specifically mentioned, or otherwise alluded to, in this Constitution, are still reserved to Animals/Robots, in all cases. The existence of Animal/Robot rights is not contingent upon governmental/”state” recognition of them.

So be it said additionally: [that] the enumeration in this Constitution of certain rights of Nature shall not be construed to impair, deny, or disparage others retained by Nature, which rights are unalienable. All of those other rights which are not specifically mentioned, or otherwise alluded to, in this Constitution, are still reserved to Nature, in all cases. The existence of Nature’s rights is not contingent upon the governmental/”state” recognition of them.

ARTICLE XX

This constitution and the powers within it shall apply to the specific territory of which the nation is established. In the event Psychic or Magic domains are discovered by we mere Normies/Muggles in the World of Men, the rights protected by this Constitution shall apply to all domains/places constituting Pacifica and its outposts/stations, and the Individuals/Persons within/therein and tangent.

No confederation of nations shall be formed between Pacifica and any other party, nor any international, global, interplanetary, interstellar, galactic, intergalactic, cross-timeline, multiversal, or omniversal integration or compact of powers be established.

No law or Public action shall propose, consent to, or request the incorporation of the Pacifica nation, or any part thereof, to any other Jurisdiction or Title/Power Holder; No branch of the Public Administration, nor any number of Citizens or other Residents of Pacifica, shall propose or consent to the incorporation of Pacifica, or any part thereof, to any other jurisdiction; a majority of two-thirds of the overall number of Representatives may assent to the incorporation of any new territory to Pacifica upon the request of its People or government with any status the Congress may determine.

The prohibition on incorporation of any part of Pacifica into another nation shall extend in consideration to barring foreign embassies and Military bases proposed to be established within Pacifica.

Parcels ceded to the exclusive jurisdiction of Congress by consent of a State’s Legislature must be specifically described by metes and bounds at the time of cession, and all state citizens of such parcel shall remain citizens of the ceding state for all elections to offices of the State or the Union, and no such transference shall forfeit the Private property rights of Persons, whether landholding or not. The boundaries of such parcels shall be clearly marked to give notice to any person entering or leaving which jurisdiction he or she is in.

The power of a State to peaceably secede from Pacifica, with the approval of three-fourths of the overall number of adult Citizens of that State qualified and registered to vote at the time of the last General Election of whom have been residents for at least twelve years in that State, and to thereafter obtain sovereignty and independence apart from Pacifica shall not be denied or abridged. Congress may levy additional requirements on the secession of a state with a three-fourths vote of both houses. Congress shall have the power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.

ARTICLE XXI

SECTION. 1.

The Congress, whenever two-thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose amendments to this Constitution; or, on the application of the Legislatures of a simple majority of the several States, or upon referendum or initiative [or both] to convene a delegation on and for their behalf, shall call a convention for proposing amendments, which, in all cases, shall be valid to all intents and purposes as part of this Constitution, when ratified by the Legislatures of three-fourths of the several States, or by three-fourths in General Elections by the Citizens in three-fourths thereof, as the one or the other mode of ratification which shall occur, however, a state or person can rescind their ratification so long as it or they do/es so before the amendment process has been completed; Provided that no Amendment passed which may be made prior to eighteen years from the date of ratification of this Constitution; and that no State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate nor shall a State’s method of electing Senators be changed without its consent. A Constitutional Bill proposing an Amendment to this Constitution shall be subject to the power of general veto by the Citizens as expressed in the referendum;

The President, after gaining Election to a third Term in Office, may propose Amendments that, if approved by the House and Senate, shall be placed on the Ballot of each State for Consideration at the next three presidential Elections. If two-thirds of the eligible national electorate or three-fourths of the actual voters, whichever number is higher, approve of the proposal, it shall be considered ratified and shall become a part of this Constitution;

Those eligible to vote throughout the nation shall be able to propose amendments upon signing identically-worded petitions. Such proposals shall be submitted to a national referendum. Should two-thirds of the eligible national electorate or three-fourths of the actual voters, whichever number is higher, approve of the proposal, it shall be considered ratified and added to the Constitution immediately;

The validity of State calls for an Article XXI Constitutional Convention should be determined by the most recent action of the State;

Each Convention must be transparent and not conducted in secret; All Constitution conventions must be made in full view of the public with every word said by every member scrupulously recorded, and using secure electronic means broadcast publicly for all Citizens [to be free] to observe;

Each Convention must be limited to a specific topic;

Only State or Citizens’ resolutions between all of the incorporated Jurisdictions of Pacifica, on a single topic count when determining if a Convention should be called;

The Congress, the President, and the Supreme Court shall not have the right to control a Constitutional Convention nor an Amendment Convention. They can, however, as well as Citizens, express their opinions and recommendations in the process;

Voting at the Convention must be by delegate or Citizen of the Several States, not by State or Un-incorporated Territory;

Representation at the Convention must be based on proportion to population rather than one State, one vote; and delegates should be elected rather than appointed;-And

To be deemed ratified, the results of votes of the legislature or convention in the several States shall be reviewed and verified [though not subject to approval power] by a vote of at least eighteen of a randomly selected grand jury of twenty-four from citizens of that State who are not dependent on public funds for their support; and the reports of all such grand juries shall be reviewed and verified by a unanimous vote of a randomly selected grand jury of twenty-four from citizens of Pacifica who are not dependent on public funds for their support.

SECTION. 2.

The purpose of any constitutional convention is to adopt such a government as shall, in the opinion of the representatives of the people, best conduce to perpetuating [the] freedom, securing [the] safety, and enabling [the] happiness of their constituents, in particular, as well as that of ‘the People’ of the Nation and the several States, within each and every State, in general.

The body of the convention will consist of three delegates from each State, which delegates shall be elected by the people of their State in non-partisan elections.

The delegates shall act as electorate and elect a President Pro Tempore of the convention. The president of the convention shall have the power to direct and/or intervene in the official discussions of the convention as to maintain productivity and efficiency along with timeliness. In addition to their official powers as president, they shall retain the same fundamental powers as all other delegates.

The president [Pro Tempore] of the convention shall appoint a secretary of the convention charged with maintaining detailed records of both the convention materials and of the convention itself.

Each delegate shall be free to form a blueprint, and required to provide explanations [as to the “Why?”], for the amendments and constitutions they propose or sponsor.

The delegates of the convention will be tasked with strenuously scrutinizing the interactions of power in provisions whose meaning or scope may be affected or the projected positive and negative scenarios and futures conceivable by proposed amendments or constitutions. Their inputs regarding the materials of the convention will be subject to open discourse with their fellow delegates and for that of ‘the Public’/the_People.

The People of the several States shall be free to petition the convention for considerations.

All votes cast within the convention shall be kept secret until the conventional meetings adjourn, then they shall be published Publicly in full detail.

The deadline for ratification of any proposed amendment to this Constitution may be extended by a direct vote of the People, conducted in accordance with law. Any proposed amendment that fails to achieve ratification within its designated time period may be reintroduced for consideration and ratification without restriction or prejudice. Only a direct vote of the People to strike down a proposed constitutional amendment prior to its ratification shall prevent its further consideration or ratification. Once ratified, an amendment may only be altered or repealed by the process of amending the Constitution. No legislative or executive authority shall abridge the People’s right to extend ratification deadlines, reconsider unratified amendments, or strike down proposed amendments prior to ratification.

SECTION. 3.

It is on the highest advisement that amendments be entailored and enamoured suitably for incorporation into the Previously existing constitution, unless an amendment repeals the constitution in favor of following another enumeration of civil governmental instrument. To achieve this end, ‘we the People’ encourage the ratification of amendments which themselves are fully incorporated into the constitution, and to re-ratify the entire constitution with such considered amendments incorporated as shall be found to be most suitable/proper, according to the rules for each mode of amending and ratifying such amendments.

SECTION. 4.

The total size of the RAW constitutional text will be capped at a maximum of two times the bytes in length of the ratified original as a text file without markup or scripting/macros/routines, and all markup or scripting/macros/routines added to the text shall only serve augmentative purpose, but not to be construed itself as having effect of law or authority on its own, unless ratified by the Constitutional Convention Delegates or by the People. The total size of all current Federal statutes, measured in bytes of text, shall not exceed that as of three times the constitution byte size cap, and for any act which adds text, an equal quantity of text must be repealed. The total volume of all Federal regulations, shall not exceed six times that of all statutes. For all byte limits, it will be considered of the uncompressed text. Congress shall not adopt more provisions per year than can be adequately heard and decided by jurors in the Pacifican courts within two years of enactment, and if more are adopted, the jurors in the courts shall have authority to summarily strike them. This provision may of course be modified to suit an appropriate need by and through ratification of a constitutional amendment changing such language.

ARTICLE XXII

The Constitution of Pacifica shall enter into force upon the approval of either Conventions of three-fourths of the several States or should by two-thirds of the eligible national electorate or three-fourths of the actual voters, whichever number is higher, so ratifying the same.

The Constitution of Pacifica shall be subject to re-ratification by the people every twenty-four years from its initial date of ratification. If the constitution is not re-ratified, then the same general procedure utilized for preparing and suggesting a constitutional amendment shall apply, except that the process shall NOT be limited to one topic, and shall be completed within two years from the veto of re-ratification date. Within the two-years from the denial of re-ratification, whenever the conventions of the States deems it appropriate [as long as it is on equitable terms], the new constitution shall be put up to a vote for ratification by the People. It will either be ratified, or denied, and if denied, shall be subject to revision, amendment, or completely new synthesis. If the proposed new constitution is denied, then the period for ratification of a new constitution may be extended past the period of two years to the shortest additional period reasonably possible. The old constitution of Pacifica shall be upheld until ratification of the new constitution of Pacifica, upon whereafter the old constitution shall be repealed in favor of the new constitution.

proposed amendments:

James Madison, George Washington, George Mason and Thomas Jefferson all insisted that the Constitution should be updated by future generations. Those sentiments were best expressed by Jefferson, who wrote to Madison that “no society can make a perpetual Constitution. … The Earth belongs always to the living generation. … Every Constitution … naturally expires at the end of 19 years” (the length of a generation in Jefferson’s time).

Most proposed amendments have been integrated, nearly complete now. Only micropatches remain to be discovered and integrated. This document is now superfluous.
